These are pretty small, but not teensy-tiny…about the same size as Beats Studio Buds (sound a lot like them, too; but doesn’t have nearly as much bass presence as the Beats).  The only negative I have is the “non-standard” size of the included eartip.  It’s about half the size of other buds.  And there’s only one size included (I’d estimate the size to be medium), no smaller or larger sizes are included with the package.  In summary, the A1 is a great value, good sounding option for anyone looking for decent set of backup or low-cost primary earbuds.

title: Fits over glasses frames, stays put when running
text:
I wear glasses, and these fit comfortably over my ears and frames. I don’t know how they seat and block out sound for non-glasses people, but I still have awareness of surrounding noises, which I consider a good thing. A lot of earbuds get uncomfortable fast, but the buds on these do not press heavily on my ear canals and my ears do not fatigue wearing them.

They don’t come loose when running for a few hours, and allow enough noise in that I am able to hear traffic and be environmentally aware.

Battery life seems good. I used them constantly on a 4 hour 30 minute run, and they did not die (audiobook, not music, not sure if that makes a difference for battery drain).

The on-ear controls are fantastic. I don’t like touch controls, but these are actual buttons, and are simple to operate: button on the ear pauses/unpauses, rocker button on the top of each earpiece controls volume. I haven’t used them for any calls, so I can’t say how they work on that front.

I’m really happy with these headphones. They were an impulse buy when they were on sale, but they have quickly become my go-to earbuds for running and at work.

title: Comfy, no bass
text:
Update 3/3/2023: I’ve updated to 5 stars and this why: TOZO customer service reached out and offered me 3 different wireless earbuds to choose from for free. I chose the TOZO-10 (a more expensive model than these) and they sound great, the bass is fantastic. So I will next write a review of that model. But what I really wanted to say was how incredible their customer service is. They reached out and offered me my choice of a free product, it arrived at my house within a couple days, and they followed up a few days later to make sure I was satisfied. I am really impressed. I wish all customer service was like that!! I would definitely call that above and beyond!! I do think they need to update this model (the one I first ordered and reviewed) or replace it with something else, but they have amazing customer service and I feel like they are striving for excellence so they are likely to fix any issues. Highly recommend this brand! The only thing that remains to be seen is durability.

Ok first off these were my first ever wireless earbuds, so I don’t have much to compare them to. They fit great in my ears with the smallest tip setting and felt comfy and stable in there, like they going to stay put. I love how they click back into the magnetized case and charge in there. I don’t like the tap-to-touch feature that gets triggered when you’re just trying to adjust an earbud. But the biggest issue with these is the sound… there is no bass to these. I was hoping there would be just a little, I don’t need much. I mostly planned on using them for movies, not music, but the sound is tinny and lacking. A shame, as otherwise they seem like a great product. But the sound is kind of the whole point with these, so I will be sending them back. Obviously these are also some of the lowest cost ones available (and I got them even cheaper on a Black Friday deal) so I may need to spend a little more to get what I want.

text: Ok, based on what I have read about Beats in general these are a massive disappointment. These have a lot of the things you want out of an apple product, instant reliable connection to Apple products, a nice look, good battery (from what I read) but the sound quality is very meh. Now, I will say one thing, Apple locks up EQ for its on music only, which could make a huge difference, but really I'm not impressed. The sound clarity is pretty good, but if you listen to anything other than Apple Music you're going to be disappointed. Additionally, iPhone only allows you to change listening environments not a true equalizer. Anyway, I would look at some of the other brands, even Monster the original designer, might be a better bet at less than 1/2 the price.

title: Life Changing
text:
These headphones are INCREDIBLE. You can control the volume, pause, skip, and repeat songs ON both earbuds. They have a great range and battery life, too. I can't stand AirPods because they never fit comfortably for all-day wear.

These are perfect. Figuring out how to put them in my ears took some getting used to, but the three sizes of ear plugs (provided in the box) are helpful in getting a good fit. These are not noise-canceling. Beats says they have "noise isolation," but it is still difficult to hear what's happening around you when you use both earbuds.

I bought the red ones (not sure why they have a price markup). They are orangish-red in person, so if you are looking for bright red, you'll be disappointed. My favorite thing about them was pairing them with my iPhone, iPad, and Mac. The headphones communicate with the device and basically set themselves up. Super easy.

They sound great, too. In typical Beats fashion, the bass is on point. After spending 22 years in radio, wearing headphones every day, I can honestly say these are the best I have ever used.

title: These are the earbuds to get
text:
I previously owned the TOZO T10 earbuds, which have their pros and cons when compared to these A1 minis. I definitely prefer the A1 minis to the T10 and it's a great price point for such a high-quality product.

The earbuds fit magnetically to the case, which charges them when not in use and which can be recharged using the included USB. Unfortunately, unlike the T10 model, this earbud case does NOT charge when placed on TOZO's wireless charger, which was a big plus of the T10 earbuds and I believe a missed opportunity here. Rest assured, the included USB for charging is short but high quality and durable.

The product feels well-made like every TOZO product I have bought. Sleek design, and the profile is much smaller, making it MUCH less bulky to carry in your pocket with the charging case than the T10 was - that was one big issue I had with the T10. This is an everyday, all-the-time sort of product, and is the first set of earbuds I feel I can truly replace my wired earbuds with. The quality and ease of use and easy carrying give this product an A from me.

I had issues with T10 in terms of fitting them in my ears, even when changing the mesh head, and I never could get them securely in so I always had to worry about them falling out. While they were superior in noise cancelling than these A1 minis, the bulk and in-secure fit is exactly what A1 mini fixes.

I believe the sound quality you get here is slightly less than the T10s and the max volume doesn't seem as loud. Nonetheless, these are such an easy plug-and-play and convenient set with all the volume I personally really need and you can't go wrong, especially at the price point. Bluetooth connection and setting up first use was a breeze after following the instructions in the manual.

All the "tapping" functionality works great with these earbuds - play/pause, forward/backward, volume can all be adjusted by tapping a certain number of times on the corresponding earbud or holding for volume. I felt this functionality was pretty intuitive and easy to remember.

Overall, I highly recommend these for convenience, quality, and ease-of-use. I have not tested the battery to its limit but I anticipate it will be a long time before getting these down to zero charge.

---
In full disclosure, I was offered the product at a nominal price to test, but I tried to provide the most honest review I could, as I have for every product I have ever reviewed. If you benefited from this review, please give it a thumbs up so others can benefit.

title: Nice, but not quite as advertised . . . UPDATED
text:
**UPDATED . . . Scroll down for new comments!**

These budget Bluetooth earbuds work well, and paired with my laptop without any difficulty. There is a slight delay in the audio when watching movies - not all that problematic. The sound is clear, but occasionally seems to divert from stereo to one ear or the other for a second or two . . . not sure what causes that. The silicone buds themselves are quite securely attached to the devices -- they're actually a bit challenging to change -- so no worries about the little things getting stuck inside your ears.

The antenna range is definitely limited to about 20 feet, which shouldn't be a problem if you are only going to use these with a phone and keep the phone in your pocket or purse, but if you plan to leave your phone in one place and wander around, you can't go too far before the signal begins to break up. I sometimes listen to Sirius-XM on my laptop while working and leave my desk to go fetch something from a printer or head to the break room for a snack, and when more than 20 feet from the computer, the signal becomes choppy, then is lost completely at 22-25 feet . . . once back in range, they pair up quickly.

The most important detail concerns battery life. I have never gotten close to 6 hours of listening time, which is a minor disappointment. The most I seem to get is between 4 and 4.5 hours on the first two charges and just over 3.5 hours on the third -- those recharges only add up to about 11-12 hours of listening, far short of the 24 hours advertised -- I have not been able to charge a fourth time. I don't generally need such a combination of listening time or recharges, but it lets me know that on a coast-to-coast flight, I might not get to see all of two movies without stopping to recharge the ear buds at least once. I don't know if this is a defect or the best these will actually do.

I like the convenience of wireless earbuds, but I can actually use and charge a cheap wired Bluetooth set of buds at the same time -- these have to go back into the case to charge. I don't think I'll be returning these, I just think they're a little overrated when it comes to battery life.
=====================
UPDATED REVIEW . . .

I really wanted to like these, but, alas, it's not happening. And despite my earlier comment, I did choose to return the original set for a replacement. The replacement actually did have superior battery life -- very close to or more than 6 hours on the first two charges, about 4 hours on the third, but could not get a fourth charge, so still short on the claimed "24 hours" of use -- and longer reception range by about 50%. But what I actually realized is that they don't block out external noise at all and this causes you to have to run the volume higher than necessary to hear what you are listening to when ambient sound level is average. I have a cheap wired-BT headset that I paid $7 for at Marshall's that does a superior job in all respects . . . I just don't like the wires or the extremely bright blinking LED when I use it. I replaced the first set and have decided to return the second for a refund. Caveat emptor.

title: Disappointing
text:
I had high expectations for the Powerbeats Pro, and have ended up highly disappointed.

Fit
If there's one good thing I can say about the Powerbeats Pro, is that they don't fall off like AirPods, EarPods and most wireless and wired ear buds do. The Powerbeats Pro come with four pairs of ear tips in different sizes. Too bad none of them actually fit my ears. I wish Apple would just make their current AirPods with an ear hook to prevent them from falling off our ears. Anyway, the ear tips included with the Powerbeats resulted in either flat out pain or discomfort. After trying out all four pairs of ear tips, I ended up going back to the medium ones that come installed out of the box.

Sound
Sound quality in ear buds is directly related to their fit and how well that fit can create a seal. Needless to say that I cannot get good sound with the ear tips that don't cause me pain, and I can't get good sound quality for too long with the painful ear tips. The end result is ear buds that sound like the cheapest earphones you can buy, except that the Powerbeats are not cheap at all.

Battery life
If the Powerbeats Pro are supposed to have better battery life than the AirPods, I seriously don't want to imagine how awful the AirPods can be. The Powerbeats Pro can't even stand a whole day without needing to recharge, and that's regardless of whether you use them a lot throughout the day or barely at all. Yes, even in Standby these ear buds suck a lot of battery. Don't forget to take the oversized case with you, because you are definitely going to need it before you come back home..

Pairing
Don't be fooled by the super quick and simple iPhone pairing process the first time you use the ear buds. If their batteries reach near 0%, the ear buds lose their pairing and you have to re-pair them by long pressing the pairing button on the case.

I'm seriously debating whether or not to return these ear buds. They are not worth the money I paid for them. I'm already talking to people I know against buying them.

title: Compact and as advertised
text: I have had a few TOZO earbuds and they have all been good. These earbuds came nicely packaged with two extra sets of caps and a charging cable. The case is very compact which would make it easy to just stick in your pants pocket without an excessive bulge. The earbuds themselves did not have the R and L labels, unlike the other TOZO ones I have. It was a little bit difficult to get the buds out of the case the first time, but I figured out that you have to kind of put you finger on the top part and push out toward you to make it easier to get out. The sound was clear and initially I thought it was a little lacking in bass. The cap that came with the earbuds was the largest size of the three that came with the package. But I felt there was a gap in the fit so I replaced it with a larger cap I had from other orders and boy did it make a difference! Although this earbud does not have ANC, which is as advertised as the description didn’t indicate this feature, the larger cap helped with weeding out other sounds. One thing I did notice is if I put too big of a cap on, then it didn’t fit the case properly so I settled on a medium cap (maybe I just like my earbuds to fit really snug or I have big ear holes..haha). The touch feature is nice but with the earbuds being small, it’s easy to accidentally initiate the touch function while adjusting the earbuds in your ear. I do still prefer the NC9 plus for sound quality but this one works when you want a more discreet look (doesn’t protrude from ear as much). This little bud does the job as advertised for a very affordable price.

title: My perfect…
text:
As you know, these are wireless earbuds. They are not wired audiophile headsets on an amplifier. This may seem obvious, but some folks like to take reviews as opportunities to share their “vast” knowledge of what they think earbuds are supposed to sound like. After buying many wireless earbuds specifically for working out and running, these are my perfect set. First, sound quality…. Many of the sets I’ve used can handle sound on varying levels, but start to show distortion in the lower bass levels. These are solid. I need some thumps to motivate my lifts and footfalls. This gives me what I need without sacrificing midrange and detail. Secondly, and this is an enormous one, security…. They sit securely in my ear and the hooks hold on appropriately. I have no worries at all of losing these at whatever activity I perform. Third, comfort…. They are light, tight, and all around alright. I don’t experience fatigue wearing these at all so far. Finally, functionality…. This one’s for the folks who compare these with wired headsets. These offer super quick connections to Apple devices. Within minutes I could use my Powerbeats Pros with my iPad, iPhone, and Apple Watch. I can receive calls well through these with good call quality. I can use Siri easily with these as well. I didn’t want these for the greatest sound quality available. I wanted these for the best sound quality for wireless, workout earbuds. Again, these are my perfect set.

Drawbacks? Yes, a few. A lack of a wireless charging case was an oversight that definitely shows the age of these earbuds. It’s slightly inconvenient as compared to my other devices that can charge wirelessly; however, the hours of charge and the additional charge from the case helps to mitigate the inconvenience. Also the price tag. It’s really a good product, so I get it, but I feel like the price tag is more about exclusivity and less about a fair price for the type of technology offered. On the other hand, my wife bought me these and I’ve been like a kid at a candy store since I received them… Folks they are good and if you are getting them for sound, security, comfort, and functionality, you won’t be disappointed.

title: Nice addition to the Beats wireless line
text:
These are a solid addition to the ever growing true wireless market. Although this is a Beats branded pair, it is markedly different from the Powerbeats Pro. First, it’s a smaller form factor both in the buds themselves and the case. The buds in particular are very tiny. See pic comparing to the AirPods Pro. It has no stem but the bud itself sticks out your ears a little more, so they are uncomfortable to lay on if you were to watch a movie in bed or so.
They look like bolts in your ears from afar. With that being said, they are comfortable for regular use, at least for me. Although the silicone tips are less pliant and soft compared to the Pro’s. Sound quality is where it shines, with a nice resonating low and crisp highs. Mids is where these fall short. Battery lasts pretty well, about 6 hours with ANC on, haven’t tested with them off but it claims to last up to 8 hours. Now the case I believe should have been a little smaller since it doesn’t house a wireless coil, so not sure what the large body is for. Overall battery life with the case is similar to that of the Pro’s and the Pro’s case is much smaller.
Another pro is that it works better with non-Apple devices but may be a con for Apple users. There’s no proprietary H1 chip, so you won’t get the auto-connect to all your synced devices. There’s no spatial audio for video although I believe it supports audio on Apple Music.
Now for the ANC and the ambient pass through. It’s ok, for the price point. Both pale in comparison to AirPods Pro or even other similar priced competitors but you do pay extra for the brand cachet.
All in all, nice pickup. Hopefully the successor will be more tuned towards the iOS ecosystem.

title: Think Avatar
text:
You know how in the Avatar movies the people, animals, and plants connect to each other so easily? That is how these Beats connect to the iPhone. I have an iPhone 14 Pro Max, and the connection with these earphones was perfect and instantaneous.

I have a set of AirPods Pro which also connect the same way. Seamless. However, like many of this style, they are not always comfortable or if I'm really busy (cleaning house and bending over the bathtub for instance) they can feel like they are going to fall out. I needed something behind the ear so that I wouldn't have that problem. I have a couple of cheapie behind-the-ear buds, and while comfortable, they can be a little touchy and the next thing I know I'm five songs ahead when I didn't mean to be! That doesn't happen with these. They are far sturdier than the less expensive ones, and they're actually quite comfortable for me. The attached silicone tips fit my ears perfectly out of the box (YMMV), and while it took a few adjustments for the ear wire, I finally got that dialed in as well. No pain even after hours of wear.

I listen to podcasts, YouTube videos, audiobooks, and music, of course, when I'm busy. I am not an audiophile, but the sounds have been more than satisfactory for my needs. I happily give these five stars so far, but Apple accessories have never been a problem for me, so I doubt that I will change my rating.

Oh! While the battery life is good, one pair of my cheapies can go even longer. These are nine hours, and the others are 12 hours. The difference is these feel much more substantial than the others. That being said, either pair can work fine with just one earpiece in at a time.

Highly recommended.

They used to make CD players for Pro DJs which would advance read a few seconds in to a track and play them basically in "delay" so that if the decks were jostled at all, it wouldn't matter because the laser had already read further in to the track and the computer was programmed to auto correct the skip, thereby effectively eliminating skipping on non severely damaged CDs. title: Not as good as my Airpods Pro, but MUCH more budget friendly for a backup pair.
text:
The charge on my AirPods Pro Buds doesn't last the entirety of my long-haul flights or overnight if I wear them to sleep. Buying a 2nd set of AirPods to always have a charged pair on hand seemed excessively expensive and indulgent. These Beats Studio Buds do the trick for less than 1/3 the price of my AirPods. For my purposes, the Beats Studio Buds work out great.
The sound quality and noise-cancelation features of the Beats Studio Buds are just a step down from my noise-canceling AirPods Pro Buds. With the Beats Studio Buds, I hear a little more of what's happening around me which is disappointing, hence the 3 stars. However, I wouldn't give the AirPods Pro noise canceling feature more than 4 stars. Neither brand of Buds holds a candle to my Beats over-the-ear noise-canceling headphones. For sound quality, I get some weird feedback if I'm laying down and the Beats Buds rub against my pillow, whereas I've never had that problem with the AirPods Pro, hence 4 stars for Beats Buds vs. the 5 stars I would give to the AirPods Pro. The battery life is almost identical for both brands, which IMO is subpar in both brands of Buds, so I would give them both 3s. I would rather have slightly larger buds that held a charge longer than the tiny buds I'm constantly searching for when I drop them on the floor or into various crevices.
The charge on both brands of Buds lasts about the same amount of time, which equates to about 4-5 hours of usage per set. For my very long-haul flights of 10-15 hours plus airport time, my Airpods are recharged again by the time my Beats run dry, and then my Beats are recharged if the 2nd Airpods charge gives up. Most planes have USB ports, but I have yet to find one that does more than trickle charge, which means my iPhone must get the USB port so it doesn't die when I'm watching shows, listening to music and podcasts, or reading on my Kindle app. So I can't recharge my Buds of either flavor while I'm using my phone. Fortunately, the charged-up cases get one set of buds back in action by the time the other set dies, and I can often get enough of a 2nd recharge on my Airpods to last until I reach a 'real' recharging location.

title: Avoid the reviews, buy the product
text:
Reviewing after clocking 40 miles, 30 days of use.

I spent hours searching for a earpiece which won’t keep falling off my ear during my outdoor and treadmill runs. I tend to focus on listening to my body while long distance running but felt the need for music during my speed workouts, purely for motivation.

After reading the bad reviews, I was doubtful if this Device will meet my requirements but then I decided to give it a try and not get influenced by the bad reviewers.

The battery lasts long enough and you don’t need to charge often. One full charge gives 2 weeks of full use.

The device doesn’t slide into the ear and the video clip on detail page is misleading. It does take a bit of manual adjustment to tuck it nicely in your ears but once it does, it stays there. Speed workouts or long distance, I never had any issues with the fit. You also get different soft buds to perfect it with your ear hole.

The volume buttons on the device works well but the change button is a hit and miss. Sometimes it pauses and sometime it changes the song but the mechanics of single and double click is mostly faulty especially when you are running. While walking or static it tends to be more accurate as it reads your inputs from finger with more stability.

The connectivity is simply and seamless, you open the box, connects to your iPhone automatically (except the first attempt when you manually connect the Bluetooth).

Lastly, the Bluetooth range is adequate but not great. I see the sound break as I move away from phone but no issues upto ~20ft.

All in all, I am very happy with this purchase and worth the price.

My husband has a set of these and really likes them. I should have known better. He’s not a music lover and prefers to wear one at a time. Old school. Plus longer battery life.
The main reason I tried them is they’re well reviewed for exercise and I use a yoga swing. If anything could hang on while you’re upside down it seemed like these should. If that’s all I needed them for, I’d still have sent them back.
For me, I found them painful to wear for any length of time. I couldn’t find a way to solve it. As for the tips, the problem seemed to be the angle. Then there are the loops, and that was more about finding a way to adjust them so they didn’t make my earlobes sore. I never could wear them for more than an hour without my ears aching.
Plus, since they’re so bulky, wearing both at the same time made me feel like a critter out of Star Trek.
The battery life was okay, but not great. They did recharge quickly. On the whole the battery is better than the Jabra 75t Active I replaced them with.
The final straw that made me send them back was the sound. I had a faulty pair. I got feedback noise. But I’m getting squelches and skips with the Jabras. It’s not my month.
I am hopeful the sound issue was just poor quality control. Bad sound isn’t acceptable for so much money. I only wish it had been the only issue. My old Beats Solos sound better and are more comfortable and they’re taped together. I had hoped for better from the nice folks at Apple from design to sound.
Sorry not to have better news.
I hope this is helpful to someone.

Some people I read on here talk about the music quality being poor, but I guess I'm not from LA and work in a music studio, so I thin the sound is what I would hope for from any of my music devices. If you are worried at all about these falling out of your ears (I also had trauma from the skull candies before I decided to spend big boy amounts of money on my earphones, which would constantly fall out) THESE WILL NEVER AND COULD NEVER FALL OUT, unless you somehow broke them or you have elephantiasis of the ears. I won't wear these things for more than an hour and a half to two hours, because I just want my ear canal to breathe a little every once in a while and it can get slightly uncomfortable (as would any other earphone). I use these for runs, and they are great! I don't have to hear my terrible heavy breathing, and with a Spotify subscription, these earphones, and the Mighty Vibe music player, I have already lost about 10 pounds in the last 3 weeks. I also prefer to use these when in lecture with my college over zoom sessions.

I bought the moss colored ones, and if you are at all like me and don't really like the idea that the beats symbol is too gold colored, don't even trip. They don't really show as super bright gold, and no one would see the gold in your ear anyway.

title: Nice Sound, Great Design!
text:
For the last two years (May 2019 to June 2021) I've owned BOSE Sound Sports as my ear buds that I use at the gym. Sadly I lost them recently and needed a replacement. The Beats Studio Buds looked good and were a good price point. I was pleasantly surprised that the Beats were quite a bit better than the BOSE and at a better price point.

1. Sound: Just as good as the Bose Soundsports if not better, good volume amount.

2. Button Controls: Very nice light touch buttons on both the right and left buds. Unlike some other reviews that I have read pressing the buttons did NOT push the buds into the ear. I found the buttons to be a nice lite touch when compared to the SoundSports buttons, which were about 3 times harder to press (or more, really took some pressure).

3. CASE: Very well designed case, sleek, durable. Really liked the magnetic lid and charging ports, well designed and thought out.

4. BEATS APP: LIke that the app shows how much of a charge is in each bud right and left. Useful.

5. Comfort: Felt like the fit (For me) was perfect, never fell out, a good interface with the ear. A better fit than the Bose for sure.

6. Aesthetics: The Beats do not stick out as much as the BOSE Soundsports (They really stood out quite a bit). The BEATS are much smaller and have a very nice profile to them.

Overall am very pleased with the BEATS, so much I got the white ones to! Ironically after I ordered the Black ones I FOUND my BOSE soundsports, but after using the BEATS, I found them to be superior in many ways to the BOSE buds. Sorry Bose BEATS is the new BUDS for going to the gym for me!

Update, 8.27.21

Having no volume control on the actual Buds was no big deal to me (Some reviewers really didn't like that you couldn't adjust the volume on the actual Buds). You'll always have your phone with you anyway and it's just as simple to press the volume control on your phone.

title: Get them while you can.
text:
If you lead an active lifestyle, these are king. The newer Beats Fit will fall out of your ears despite the hook, have 3 hours less battery life (9 here versus 6), have features no one needs like surround sound, and the smaller USB-C case of those does not offset these differences. Only these have independent rocker button volume controls in each side; the newer Beats Fit have awkward single button volume control which is awful. I enjoy these so much, I bought a second set. For running outdoors, I use Shokz (formerly Aftershokz) Open Move and their newest premium model since they are bone conduction. But for treadmill, weight training, use in a stadium, a loud gym, these are wonderful. I do not like active noise cancelling headphones as it’s a battery drain and, frankly, you need to hear someone screaming and sirens. These have no ANC, but have four ear insert choices to keep sound essentially out.

Nothing will top these genuine full ear hooks to keep your devices in your ears when you are sweating, hiking, bodybuilding, driving your car (unilateral), hitting golf balls and baseballs, this is the beast.

title: Noise Cancelling Makes a Difference, But Still Not Perfect
text:
I'm literally sitting here writing this review while city workers are outside my apartment jackhammering the sidewalk. The noise cancellation doesn't make all that noise go away, but it softens the noise enough to the point that it's tolerable, especially with some music on. The noise cancelling on these buds is better than my other noise cancelling headphones from Soundcore., Granted those aren't the highest end headphones but they are over-the-ear and one might assume they are more noise isolating to begin with. but they're still not as good.

ETA: After using these for a week, I don't think I can keep them. First, there are compatibility issues; sometimes when I connect I only get one bud to work and the other is on but silent. The buds don't seem to be able to remember multiple connections well, so to get both buds working I have to go through a re-pairing process. And perhaps most importantly, the button placement has proven really frustrating. These buds don't fit my admittedly-small ear canals very well, which means I often have to adjust them to make sure they're secure. When I do that though, I inadvertently hit the button either. The has resulted in several dropped calls because apparently hitting the button while on a call stops the call and starts whatever music/podcast you had going before. This is just too frustrating for me to deal with, so these buds are going back.

That said, there's quite a bit not to like about these buds. First, the case feels cheap and is much larger than something like an Airpods case - almost twice as big as my Airpods 2 case. It does have some extra battery though, which is good. The second thing I'm not fond of is the button. Unlike Airpods, it's actually a physical button and using it requires pressing hard, jamming the bud into your ear more. And trying to out the bud in or adjust it better often triggers the button. Also, the button has limited functionality - basically it can only be used to pause music, activate Siri, or turn noise cancellation on/off. No skip track, volume controls or anything else. Finally, these are not as well integrated into the Apple universe as well as Airpods. For instance, taking them out of my ear doesn't automatically stop the music/podcast. Little things like that make me miss my Airpods, but in the end the noise cancelation makes these buds the better ones for me. At least until the jackhammering stops.

title: They are decent
text:
I bought these earbuds back in 2020 when they were around $200, and while they weren't terrible, I don't think they are worth the price. If anything, I'd say these are $125 quality at best. They are still okay, but after purchasing the Sony WF-1000xm4, I didn't truly know what I was missing as far as sound quality (not just loudness)

The Pros:
Great battery life (provided you set the ear buds correctly in the charging dock and get them perfectly on the connectors). I've been able to use these things non-stop for 8+ hours.

Good bass, and pretty loud

I actually like the ear hooks. It gives me a big more security during my HIIT circuits.

The Cons:
First and foremost... the case. I understand that because of the ear hooks, the case has to be bigger, but this thing is chonky. Most of the time I just carry the buds around in my pocket when I'm not using them because you can't get the whole case in your picket comfortably.

The other bad thing about the case is the actual charging dock that connects the ear buds. It's magnetic, so you would think it would just pull the bud onto the little metal connectors, but if you don't double check by wiggling it around a bit to make sure it's on, you will end up with a dead bud when you go to use it next time.

If you are an android user, you will have constant connectivity issues and you will not be able to use certain features... at random. Sometimes I can control the volume of my samsung watch with the earbud volume controls, most of the time I can't. Sometimes I have to restart my watch or phone to get the thing to connect. Sometimes the music stops when I take them out of my ear, most of the time it keeps playing. If you're an apple user, you'll have a more seamless time with these and be able to use all the features. If you use Android, it's a crap shoot. It might work, it might not.

The audio, while loud and heavy doesn't offer very good mid-range, so there are nuances of music that are lost. If you're listening to workout music like trance, house, techno, rock, whatever... it's fine. If you're listening to these things while reading, it's not going to offer the best experience with softer, more lyrical music.

There no noise cancellation. At all.

The rubber tips that go in your ear can be very uncomfortable at any size, and what's worse is they will form almost a vacuum seal in your ear which can cause ear pressure and completely dampen the music unless you wiggle the bud around a bit. I had this issue a lot with my right ear. If you get these, buy some aftermarket memory foam tips for a more pleasant experience.

These are 'okay' earbuds, and have worked for about 2 years now, but for the price, you can get better (especially if you are an android user). You may even get better cheaper ones.

title: Not great.
text:
Got these at half off to replace my AirPods that stopped working. Overall, these weren’t nearly as good as I was hoping based on the $150 price and relatively good reviews.

Pros:
They do fit very well and stay in easily. Really comfortable to wear and I haven’t had them fall out while moving around.

Battery life is fairly good, definitely outlasts my older 2nd gen AirPods

Noise cancelling is nice, not up to par with over ear headphones but that’s to be expected.

Cons:
Sound. Out of the box these really lacked bass. Everyone has different preferences here so maybe that’s just me. Figured this would be an easy fix through their equalizer. Nope. The Bose app doesn’t support these earbuds, only the more expensive variants. Pretty unacceptable to have a pair of earbuds at this price range be intentionally hindered this way. And yes, they are sealed correctly.

Connectivity. I use these with an iPhone and getting them reconnected is always a pain taking them out of the case. I often have to “forget device” and reconnect.
They also stutter regularly (every 5 minutes or so) while no other Bluetooth headsets I’ve used have this problem.

The play button is also very easy to press when putting them in, a pretty minor inconvenience compared to the above points.

The case is incredibly cheaply made for something in this price range. Not a huge issue, but I could see the lid breaking in the future.

Really not impressed with these, I’ll be returning them. Regular AirPods are cheaper and have vastly better sound quality imo.

title: Powerbeats vs Airpods for running
text:
I wanted wireless headphones mostly for running, but also to use casually for conference calls and listening to music/podcasts. From the outset I assumed the Powerbeats would be the best for me and got those. While they are very good, it didn't blow me away. It wasn't so much better than the $30 bluetooth headphones I got 3 years ago. I also struggled to get a good fit in my one ear. What made me send it back though, was that it is just too bulky. The carrying case is huge and even the earphones without the case are big, and I didn't just want to put the headphones without the case in my denim pockets, as they have protrusions that might get damaged or break off. Bottom line, you can't just keep them in your pockets "just in case". Every time you want to take it somewhere you have to make space for it somewhere.

So I got the Airpods. I was very skeptical that:
1. They would fall out when running
2. They would not survive the sweat I generate in the Atlanta summer during 13 miles jogs

I watched some YouTube videos testing the Airpods water tolerance and I was surprised that people reported them fully functional after a wash/dry cycle (obviously not recommended). I pulled the trigger and bought it and am happy to report that they work perfectly for running. The Airpods' sound is good (not quite as great as the Powerbeats), and they don't fall out at all while running. I thought I'd might need an after market silicone casing or ear hook, but found I didn't need it.

Overall, the Powerbeats are great product, but the Airpods won me over due to their portability and the fact that I can carry them on me all the time.

title: So Close to Perfect
text:
So initially I purchased the Tozo's off Amazon for $40 just to try out and see what all the hype was about. After 6 months I decided to upgrade to the Beats. Now, after 2 weeks here are my thoughts.

The Good
Sound quality is incredible, deep bass, clear, and max volume is too much for me which was expected from Beats.

Noise canceling - when I'm listening to music I can't hear anything around me but as soon as you mute it does allow to hear your surroundings and it's not a problem to have a conversation with someone with them in.
These are much nicer to use for phone calls as well. I don't feel like I can hear myself talk.

Fitment - definitely not coming off your head even during intense activities.

Battery Life - I use these for around 2hrs a day 3-4 times a week. Earbuds don't even come close to dead and the case has around 50% at week end.

The Bad

title: Tiny and epic!
text:
I was just looking for a cheap alternative to throw in my laptop bag. My Sony earbuds have been making my ears sore from long hours of use. I had no idea how small these were, so I uploaded a photo of them by a U.S. nickel. They really are a lot smaller than every other earbud I have seen. I only use these for music and never phone calls.

Pros:
So comfortable. I wore them for a good hour and forgot I had them in, something that I would have been adjusting with the bulkier alternative I was using.
Great audio for the price! The best way I can describe it is flat and clean, a few tweaks to the equalizer and they sound great.
Decent bass, not too harsh of highs
You can't tell you to have them in, not really. They are so lightweight and fit in your ear so smoothly... they knocked it out of the park on comfort and longevity for wearing in my opinion.
The case is a great size, nice light, and compact as well.

Cons:
You have to be careful taking these out, they are so small that it's hard to get a grasp on them. I lost grip of one and it was like squeezing a wet bean or something and shot under my desk. Will take a few days to get used to it and get a routine down to get them out.
Getting the earbuds out of the charging case is a bit hard for me, I have bulky fingers. I found that if I grab and twist it towards the back of the case they come out easily.

Unknowns:
I don't know how long the battery will last. I usually have headphones in for a few hours before taking them out and letting them charge.
I am old school. I don't answer calls on my earbuds, so I have no idea what the quality would be on them. I hold my phone up to my ear so people don't think I am talking to myself or them when I am trying to have a conversation on the phone.

Should you buy it?
For nearly $20, these are a no-brainer for music. A resounding YES! Even if they are a spare for your car or something. If you make frequent calls on your earbuds, seek advice from someone else.

text:
They are the absolute worst. Biggest problem is that, while they'll pair with your phone after some fiddling, they are unreliable - the left and right buds frequently lose pairing with each other. When this happens it creates strange sounds and gaps and means you have to stop what you're doing to try to get them paired again. Try doing that in the rain when you're out running. So I gave up using them in both ears, meaning they're not at all suitable for music. I had let the return period run out, so I'm stuck with them, so now I only use them one at a time and only for phone calls and podcasts, although even for that, the max volume is variable and is often not adequate. The microphone doesn't work consistently either. Batteries don't last long on a full charge after the first month or so (maybe 30 minutes). Sound is only so-so when they do work.

Crappy workmanship - one of the earbuds on mine falls apart repeatedly, and the silicone seal doesn't seat right so it's for sure they're not waterproof.

Frankly, I have a couple of pairs of generic-brand totally wireless earbuds that cost about $30 or less (with coupons) from Amazon that work and sound much better and are more predictable about pairing, and they stay connected and hold a charge for a decent amount of time.

Another big problem is that the manufacturer doesn't seem to feel any need to distinguish among different models or updates/versions of this product. Prices online range from about $80 to $250 with no clear distinction among them to explain the differences or why the prices are different - they're all called just "Powerbeats Pro Wireless Earphones".

title: Great value buds
text:
It's hard to believe such small, inexpensive headphones sound as good as these do. I adjusted the bass response on Spotify, cutting some of the highs out of the sound -- and then they were quite good. They fit well and are light in the ear. The touch sensitive portion works fine -- the usual controls for volume up and down (right and left ear touches), double taps for rewind or skip. They connect immediately to the last device they were paired with after removing them from the case.
The case holds a charge strong enough to charge the headphones a couple times -- good enough for a full day of use. Phone calls come in clear.
There is no active noise cancellation -- just small, medium and large rubber tips to isolate exterior noise. The medium fit perfectly so I didn't mess with changing them.
The case is very small -- a great thing for pocket carry. The problem is the buds fit so well that larger fingers have difficulty popping the earbuds out of their holder -- a very small inconvenience for the comfort you experience once they are in the ear.
Can't go wrong with these!

title: Do not buy these headphones
text:
I know this sounds extreme, but these are by far the worst the worst piece of consumer electronics I have purchased.

The biggest issue I have with these earbuds is that you have to constantly re-connect / re-configure your bluetooth settings in order for both earbuds to work at the same time. 90% of the time, only one earbud connects to bluetooth upon start up. This has costed me several minutes, perhaps even hours, frustratingly disconnecting / reconnecting the earbuds before workouts. In addition to the poor bluetooth connectivity element:

- The sound quality is average at best - certainly not representative of a $200 price point.
- Support / return options are highly limited - Beats is owned by Apple; even if you're under warranty, you need to navigate the maze of Apple support resources / schedule an appointment to get assistance (virtual or in-person).

Do not buy these headphones. Spend the extra money and get a higher quality brand or go with a cheaper option / save your money.

The noise cancelling earbuds were too large to fit in my ear without pushing hard against the inside of the earmuffs, so I purchased these compact earbuds.  They fit nicely under the earmuffs.  The earmuffs along with these earbuds mechanical noise isolation do the job, and the sound quality is more than adequate for audiobooks as well as light music needs. title: Great idea- Not worth the $
text:
I had these for less than a week and decided to return them. Here are my pros/cons:

Pro’s:
-they fit great! I sweat like a mofo when I work out and they stay in great!
- they look really cool while on your head (but who really buys headphones cause they look cool?)
- the battery life is good, BUT (see cons)

Cons:
- my biggest con was sound quality. They sound quality is really not that good. I have cheaper wireless headphones ($30 ones off Amazon that sound as good). I personally thought the bass response was garbage and I the sound didn’t feel full at all, especially not for $200+ headphones
- I personally didn’t like the way you see the battery life. You could only see the battery life when you have the carrying case around. And even then you had to fiddle with the carrying case ( open and close it with the screen on your phone unlocked) for it to show up. Maybe there was another way, but I couldn’t find anything online to say otherwise.
- the carrying case is too large! I know this to be expected with this type of earbud, but seriously, this is huge and way too bulky. Not practical if you want to take with you places and take them off and on. The case was also hard to hold without feeling like you were going to drop it.
- I Actually didn’t like the battery life. I don’t like to keep my electronics on the charger, especially when they don’t need. One night I left them on my dresser overnight (8 hours or so) b/c they were fully charged and I didn’t want to leave them in the case to continue to charge. They are suppose to go into standby mode and not use up battery, not the case! When I went to use them they were completely dead.

Overall NOT worth $200+. Don’t waist you money unless $200 chump change or something, then maybe waste your $

title: After SEVERAL trial & error purchases….
text: I had to come back to review these. My beats went out on me a while back. I need wireless earbuds for the gym, but after buying beats for years, I really wasn’t wanting to spend too much. I just  wanted  a decently priced pair with good quality. I had tried several styles that I had seen on Amazon, Including different TOZO designs that claimed to not fall out. I tried different attachments and they always seemed to fall out.  Also, poor connection. Just when I had purchased and returned 5 different pairs, I found these. I read the reviews & thought I’d give it one more shot before returning back to beats or a more expensive brand. THESE WERE THE WINNER! These come with several attachments, but the original attachments fresh out of the box have been perfect. No matter how much I run, lift, do cardio, how much sweat I accrue, they NEVER fall out! (Again literally  everything I’ve tried has fallen out which is super annoying.) These are super light, sleek, and matte. They’re definitely not too bulky which was something else I noticed about the ones I had purchased. The charging case holds quite a bit of battery life. I wouldsay I’m charging the case maybe every 4 weeks? Maybe 5,  not even kidding. I go to the gym every morning (M-F) for about an hour and a half to 2 hours. When I’m done I pop them back in the case to charge. Perhaps if you use them more often than that you’ll need to charge sooner. Tip: I always make sure I disconnect Bluetooth from my phone and power them off. But truthfully sometimes I just disconnect Bluetooth and throw them in. They turn off on their own. Regardless…. Charging case keeps them charged for me. I’m never without & I’m completely  satisfied. I’m a basics kind of person,So I definitely would say that they’ve got good range, very good connection, good sound quality, super easy to connect/pair, & in my opinion pretty noise canceling. I’ve got nothing but good things to say about this product. 10/10 for me. Check them out. And of course they’re extremely reasonably priced! I don’t even think I paid 20 bucks for them .

title: Two failures in a year
text:
First of all, these were the first pair of Beats I ever owned and I loved them. Wear them to the gym and they stay in your ear, they sound great and they look good, but in the end, the unit failed me twice, I took it to Apple for them to fix or replace the left ear headphone, and two days after Christmas, just out of warranty, the right headphone is doing the same thing. It will not hold a charge.

The case is fully charged. The contacts are clean and look good. When I put it in the case it seems to connect, but who really knows. I use the unit, then put them in the case and the right unit drains to zero while the left is at 100%. It did the same thing in reverse order the first time around.

The case is another factor. My God, the case is as awkward and slippery as a greased pig. I am 6'6" tall and have big hands and the case was dropped a few times because it was so slick and slippery. I finally bought an add-on product, a cover for the case, and that gave the case tackiness. You would think for $250 headphones, they could design a case that was easy to grip, easy to load, and not act like a greased monkey.

If they didn't fail on me twice, it would have got a 4 star rating. The app is made for Apple users and Apple makes things as difficult as possible. The sound is fantastic. The microphone is wonderful and it is easy to make calls and they can hear you as well. They are comfortable on the ear.

In the end, it was money wasted. I bought a $30 dollar pair on Amazon and figure I can buy and replace these 8 times before I am up the the price I paid for these. Alas.

title: Cheap, compressed, bassless audio from a $25 pair of cheap buds
text: I am absolutely blown away at the low quality of these earbuds. I have an audio engineering degree and own some $2500 headphones including Stax headphones and a pair of lovely flagship AKG 701 headphones... in addition to Amphion & Barefoot monitors. These are by far the cheapest, most lifeless earbudds I've ever experienced and are below my $50 cheap in ear buds I replaced these with. Brand apparently means everything to half asleep American consumers because these are shockingly bad and yet they have 5 star reviews. Sheesh. I am blow away actually, at how poor the mid range and bass response on these are. Thin, hyper compressed, small soundstage, boxed in and completely lifeless. The audio is poorly compressed and missing a massive amount of frequency range needed to minimally enjoy music. I do not recommend this product to anyone looking for quality. I suspect Apple bought this company and the average unsuspecting consumer has no idea the difference between quality and "loudness" of these buds. However. title: Excellent earbuds (if you don't need noise cancellation or waterproofing)
text:
OK, so I was one of those edgelords who was cynical of Beats from the moment I first heard of them. "It's all marketing, it's a gimmick, it's not going to be up to audiophile standards, blah, blah, blah...". But I needed to buy a new pair of earbuds for running, and I saw a lot of serious runners giving this product good reviews. I figured I'd just try them out and just return them when they turn out to be garbage.

Well, this sure smacked me upside the head. The sound quality is excellent, with strong bass and clear details. Not much in terms of noise cancellation (I can hear the sound of wind when running outside on windy days), but that's a necessary trade-off for sound that actually feels expansive (as if the sound is _around_ your head rather than _inside_ your head, which is what more noise isolating earbuds like Jaybird Vista sound like). Personally, I prefer to run with headphones that don't have too much noise isolation, because the ones that do always leave you hearing the thumps of your feet as you run. You don't get any of that annoyance with the Powerbeats.

Also, note that these are water resistant, not waterproof. A little bit of rain is probably fine, but I wouldn't go out with these if it's pouring out. Great battery life, too.

Believe the hype. They're actually good.

title: Well done, Beats! I would buy again... and again... and again!!!
text:
I have had these for one day now and so far I love them. They are my first Beats and they have lived up to the name. They fit very snugly but also comfortably which has been hard to find. Sound quality is fantastic. I’m not an expert on sound by any means but I am very pleased with the sound from my music, podcasts and even phone calls.

I have an iPhone and pairing was almost too easy to the point that I wasn’t sure if they were really paired until I started listening. It also has a nice little display when you open the case near your phone that shows battery level of the earphones as well as the case. (The case charges the earphones when they are in place).

They feel very well made which was to be expected as they are Beats (Apple) after all. The case is also very nice. It’s slightly larger than expected but it could easily fit in my jacket pocket so I’m not complaining. The case has a high quality feel to it with one exception: when fully opened, the lid seems to wiggle as if it were a little loose. This was definitely not a deal breaker for me considering I didn’t buy it for the case, but rather the headphones. Just something to be aware of. When you close the case, it resumes the nice feel with a sort of snap that I’m guessing is from a magnet.

As I said before, the earphones are very comfortable. I could wear them for hours and not get sore ears. I am not an athlete but I am constantly moving around the house and leaning over etc. and they will stay in until you take them out. Another benefit is that if you slightly twist them forward on your ears, it breaks the seal so that you can hear what’s going on around you, but you can still hear your music etc. it would have been nice if they had integrated the transparency technology that uses the microphones for you to hear through the actually earphones what’s going on around you but this feature works just as well.

In the booklet, it mentions adjusting the “around-the-ear” hook but it seems like it just bends to different angles. My only complaint about this product which isn’t really by fault of the beats is that the hooks rub against my glasses a little. It’s not enough to make me return them and I only notice it sometimes. It’s really just a minor nuisance, but if you’re the kind of person that would be bothered by that, don’t get ones with ear hooks.

It comes with 4 sets of in-ear rubber pieces. One of them on the earbuds and the other four in the packaging. So far I haven’t switched them out because they felt just fine with the ones that were already on.

This brings me to packaging. I thought the packaging was excellent. Again, I expect this from a product made by Apple and I was not at all disappointed. It felt like opening a very intricate gift.

Overall, I LOVE this product. I was hesitant about the price to begin with but after having them, I realize it was well worth the sale price of $170. I would even pay the previous price of $200 for them. I would absolutely recommend these! text:

I have terrible insomnia, and I hate laying in bed staring at the ceiling fan. Preferably I would turn on a Bible reading channel or a history documentary and set the sleep timer. Usually that relaxes me and I drift to sleep again. That causes a big problem for my husband who needs to go to work in the morning. If I turn on the TV it keeps my husband awake. To fix that we decided to try headphones. They work nicely, except I wear an O2 assist CPAP and the headphones added to the other tubing caused really bad headaches from the weight and the size.
During Prime Days I asked how my sweetie liked his earbuds & he let me try them. I thought I would hate something stuck in my ears, but I loved them. These were so inexpensive & with the Prime Sale I spent less than $18.
We were afraid I would have trouble using them because they are so small & I have significant trouble w/ my right hand, but I can usually manage these myself. I use them all night sometimes & they still have a charge for the next time I need them. I have had them on for 6 hours & used them the next night for another 3-4 w/o any battery trouble.
At first it was hilarious to hear a Chinese accent in my ear, she was telling me that my earbuds were on and were synced to the TV or computer, but it's not a big deal.

text:

At this price I did not have a lot of hope for battery life so I bought two sets. Surprisingly I have used the same pair for over 12 hours at a time, using one at a time with the charging pod fully charged. The range is also excellent, better than one of the $70 pods that I still have left. I only listen to pod cast, etc. not music, with my buds. I am aware there is a different set of criteria for this purpose, but for my needs they are more than adequate.

The one issue I did have was that they are so smooth that combined with the magnet they were very difficult get a grip on. Even with the indentations, the charging pod was also a little challenging (for me) to get a grip and open. I solved this by ordering a set of "Dragon Grips" from Amazon. Placing small pieces strategically, as there are touch controls on the ear buds, I can now open the pod and the pick up the buds with no issues at all. Very impressed.

title: They are Bluetooth
text:
UPDATE: I finally found the brand I had been looking for and bought a second set. The quality is great and the battery life is about eight hours. Even so, this isn't about those ear buds, it's about these TOZO buds. Not long after I left my original review the company reached out to me and presented an offer to make up for my opinion of their ear buds. (My previous review below included only three stars, I would like to note that I know how this update might look considering what follows, but I assure you I am not bought, I speak my real mind in truth. That's just how I was raised. In any case, just read on and decide for yourselves.) They really like their product and wanted a second Chance to get a better opinion from me. Perhaps the pair of ear buds I originally got from them were just a bad set, I don't know. Anyway, they offered to replace the set I bought for free, also they offered a different set for free if I didn't want to try the first set again. I thanked them for the offer, but I found the original brand I'd been looking for (as noted below/above) and didn't need any more ear buds. However, about a week later they again reached out with the same offer adding that they really just wanted to make things right because they work hard to make sure all their customers are satisfied with their products. In truth, it seems their customer care services are very motivated, they do go out of their way to satisfy their customers. By my wife's suggestion I took them up on their offer for a different pair, the TOZO model T9. Instead of being small and hiding in the ear, these have a tail that resembles some Apple brand buds. Once I received them I charged them up and tried them out. They were much better than the first ones I bought, sound quality was very clear, I could even understand the voice in the buds telling me when they were connected. Most impressive though was the length of time the batteries appeared to last, I started using them about 12:30 p.m., and they finally ran out of juice at around 10:30 p.m. That was with non stop use! So I would like to add two things here. First, this company really prides itself on taking care of their customers. Second, I am especially glad my wife talked me into taking them up on their offer, because these second set of ear buds really met the great reviews that convinced me to try these in the first place.

(Previous review:)
I had bought a different pair for about the same price as these and was so impressed that I decided to buy a second pair. Since I couldn't find the ones I was looking for I decided to try these based on so many positive reviews. After receiving these, charged them up, set them up, used them for roughly four hours and the right ear bud ran out of power fallowed shortly by the left one. The other brand I used might have spoiled me a bit since they easily last a full eight hours before needing recharged. These also do not have the sound quality as my other pair even though they both were under $20. Finally, the announcer on this pair that tells you when you've hooked up to a Bluetooth connection, or when the ear buds need recharged is really hard for me to understand. Sorry but the accent is simply too distorted to make out clearly. I'll use these as an backup set for now, but I'm really going to look harder to find the brand I originally purchased since, for about the same price, they are far superior in every way.

Your milage may be better than mine, but I won't be buying these again.

title: Not as good as T6, but has its own advantage
text:
I bought these and the T6's, which are only a few dollars more if you catch a coupon or sale. The T6 is hands down better in every way, especially sound and build quality.

However, the A1 has a place for me. I ride motorcycles and usually wear ear plugs due to wind noise, which can damage hearing. The A1's have two distinct advantages when used this way:

1. They are lower profile (don't stick out of my ear as far) so when I put on my helmet, it doesn't knock them out of my ears. It's a little trickier when removing my helmet, but I've adapted.

2. They are smaller and lighter so they stay in my ears like earplugs. With the T6's I occasionally need to push them in to keep them snug.

Wearing on a motorcycle allows me to do 2 things that are otherwise difficult to do while riding:

1. Listen to music or use an app like Google maps or calimoto for navigation.

2. Answer phone calls. These things work pretty well for that.

My only complaint is the audible notification when Bluetooth connects. A female voice with a thick Asian accent says "Your headsets is connected." But that's to be expected for a Chinese product. The T6 does NOT have this same voice, btw.

I am keeping them since I got them on a Lightning Deal; the price I paid pays for the battery and portability, but definitely not for sound quality.

title: Major design flaw- drains battery while in charger
text:
[[VIDEOID:643941e6d721df978307d44025e7e221]] Edit: I returned the first one and my second pair is having the same problem. This is clearly a major design flaw in which: 1) they don't seat in the charger properly and 2) they may still be running when in the charger.

As this is my second pair I'm paying close attention to the battery. Yesterday evening I listened to Audible for 30 minutes (on full charge) with just the right earbud when I went to the store quickly just for stamps, leaving the left bud home in the case. When I got home, I put the right bud back in the case, closed it, and left it for the night. In the morning, I opened the case to listen to a podcast. I popped in the right earbud and got the battery drained be-doop-doooo sound. Looking at the iPhone widget, sure enough, the right one DRAINED FULLY WHILE SITTING IN THE CHARGER overnight and the left one drained about 2/3 of the way despite not even having been used. (see photo- right one dead and no "lightning bolt" indicating charging)

Maybe I'm spending more time than is warranted to troubleshoot, but my best guess is that it's running while in the charger. Also I note that unlike my AirPods, sometimes it says on my apple watch "phone call" when running audio apps- these things, despite being apple devices, may bot be programmed right. Looks like sometimes they may treat apps as phone calls and not hang up properly when I'm done using them? Could explain the dead batteries. Either way, I'll be returning these. I just want headphones that work,

Original pair review:
These are great headphones, when they work. My issue is battery drain and ineffective charging. I use these for running, 45 minutes to an hour tops, and give them a wipe and promptly return to the charging case. Usually well within the advertised battery life. Sometimes I listen to audible on my couch with just the right ear bud in, and again, return it to the case after no more than an hour of two of use.

Yet oddly, I typically find the left earbud battery fully drained. Is it running when I’m only using one ear bud? And not even that earbud!

More problematic however is the charging adapter. I have to set them in the case just right and poke them about until I hear the click of the magnetic pins- otherwise they look like they are charging but really are just sitting in the case. Lately I’ve taken to using my iPhone widgets to monitor both earbuds’ status when placing in the case, taking extra care to make sure the lightning bolt shows up indicating charging.

Another problem is that when you close the lid, it pushes the ear buds. Now I’ve noticed that the act of closing the charger lid moves the left earbud off the charging connection while the right one continues.

This is a shame because otherwise I like the headphones. They have good sound, block ambient noise, and fit nicely. Just the charging case is garbage. Do yourself a favor and either avoid these until they get a better case, or just be extra careful to monitor charging status and location so they don’t get bumped and disconnected from the charger.

title: Good, if you don't care about sound quality.
text:
If you want over-the-ear buds that have physical control buttons with great battery life and easy connectivity, then these are great.

If you're looking for top notch music quality, these are not it. I can't really recommend anything else since I haven't found anything else that actually has an ear clip with good battery life, or easy connectivity to your devices.

If you're like me who hates regular ear buds with a passion (they fall out too easily), needs something that isn't headphones for portability, and needs it to "just work" without stupid bluetooth shenanigans, then there's no other good option than these sadly.

The sound quality of these are pretty terrible, but it is something that can be fixed with a sound equalizer. On your computer or android device, a system wide sound equalizer that reduces the highs/treble and boosts the bass will make these sound like the proper ear buds they need to be. I don't have an android so I don't know the latest and greatest at this time, but for your windows computer, Equalizer APO with the Peace Setup works pretty well. On Apple, there is no system wide sound equalizer without jailbreaking, so instead use a music player like Spotify to get around this.

title: Best gym earbuds I’ve ever had ...
text:
It is impossible to explain sound by using text, and sitting here and saying “good sound quality, amazing sound, bla blah” Doesn't mean anything. The best i can do is compare these to headphones and earbuds I already have, from best to worst this is my list

Again, this list goes by what headphones I have tried and own myself...

1. SONY 1000XM3
2. Audio Technica M50
3. Bose Sound true wired earbuds
4. SONY XB900N
5. Bose 700
6. A tie between the Bose QC35, airpods gen 1, Beats Studio 2.0 and these, the powerbeats Pro.

Yes , I said it, the Beats Studio and Powerbeats sound as good as the QC 35 which are overrated. The QC35s sound flat and non exiting , it makes music feel bland. Even airpods sound livelier.

However I come from an era where $10 earbuds where good enough, and $50 earbuds are expensive, so for $250 you would expect these to blow your mind which they won’t.

BUY THE POWERBEATS PRO IF...

- You want EASY CONNECTIVITY with IOS, it is literally addicting to connect these things to my phone, very easy and seamless. No hassle.

- YOU CARE ABOUT LOOKS, these are the coolest, nicest, most aesthetic fully wireless earbuds I’ve ever seen, you can literally wear these as a fashion accessory.

- YOU WANT PREMIUM QUALITY, from the case to the earbuds themselves these feel premium, they have a weight to them that makes it feel like “dam, this is worth $250”.

-YOU WORKOUT, I wear these on my 2 hour gym sessions, 1 hour runs, 30 mins stair-master intervals, jumping, dancing, walking, hiking, I don’t care what you do, you can put these on and you can forget you even have them on.

- YOU CARE ABOUT COMFORT, the most mind blowing thing these earbuds have is the fit, these literally feel like they have been tailored to my ears, they fit snug, not loose or shakey. Once you put them on you don’t have to fumble around with the ear clips, I felt them comfortable but I wouldn’t recommend them for sessions longer than 4 hours. Basically don’t buy these if you plan to wear them in the office for 8 hours at a time.

- YOU CARE ABOUT SOUND, you can’t expect these to sound like Bose 700s or Sony 1000xm3s, and you can DEFINITELY find other earbuds with equal or better sound quality, but these definitely do not sound bad at all, think of it this way. The powerbeats pro sound GREAT, but there will always be something better.

To wrap things up, if you workout, you don’t want to fumble with bluetooth settings, you want to listen to music with good quality, and you want to look good while doing it, the powerbeats pro are a must.

If all you want is music and don’t care how it sounds, then get something else.

*Note*
An important thing with these earbuds is that picking the right size of ear tip is crucial to getting a good sound. At first I used the default ear tips and was satisfied but decided to switch the the “double” eartip that comes with the headphones and man what a difference does this make! It makes them sound like over the ear headphones.

*** 3 Month Update ***

Well these have become my absolute favorite pair of gym earbuds, I cannon imagine myself working out with anything else. They stay in place and look good, bluetooth pairing is also amazing and battery life is basically infinite lol. To put it into perspective I workout about 4-6 days a week for 2 hrs. I have charged the case to full about 5 times ever since I got these.

My only gripe is that there is no noise isolation as many people say, you can basicaly hear everything with these on. Imagine airpods but a little more isolating

title: Great sound quality, some dated design issues
text:
The sound quality of these ear buds is excellent, as with other Beats products the bass response is superb, which is lacking in the AirPods, IMO. Understandably, it's difficult to pack a lot of bass amplification into a tiny set of wireless ear buds, but Beats managed to do so. They also work with my iPhone 12 Pro Max as seamlessly as the AirPods.

The fit is nice and they stay in my ears better than AirPods; however, I do NOT like the physical buttons being directly on the outside of the buds, opposite your ear canals. I often have to adjust my ear buds and push them back in my eyes to optimize sound because they tend to move around, and this pauses the sound every time - SUPER annoying and dated design flaw. Also, the noise cancellation is pretty lame - not nearly as good as the AirPod Pros. I can hardly tell the difference with it on/off. Lastly, I'm not a fan of the lack of magnetic charging - it is USB-C only. As much as I would love for everything to switch to USB-C, Apple seemingly refuses to let go of their Lightning port, so I still have mostly Lightning cables and thus it would be nice to have magnetic charging instead of just USB-C.

All in all, this a great product at a good price, but if noise cancellation is important to you, you might want to spend the extra $ on the AirPod Pros.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

So, I work at a warehouse and music keeps me going through the shifts. These are by far the best headphones I've ever own. The touch controls are a very neat feature if you're on the move and don't have time to look at your phone. You can play and pause music or videos, skip music, rewind music. You can even lower your volume and raise your volume just by holding down on the buds. These headphones even let you switch between three modes, noise canceling mode, transparency mode and normal. Personally, I try not to use the modes because it does drain the battery a bit faster on the headphones which makes sense cause you're either using the built in mic for transparency or blocking out sound with noise canceling (which I DO NOT RECOMMEND when working around dangerous machinery) trust me you will not hear anything, so either use transparency mode or stick to using one headphone to stay safe. Always be aware of your surroundings with these because the sound quality is just that good. Overall the battery lasts me about 4 or 5 days and that's me using it consistently for about 4 hours a day, so these buds last a decent amount of time. When speaking over the phone, I get no complaints of sounding muffled so the mic works good too. The headphones are easy to connect and is best if you get the beats app so you can set up the headphone controls to your own personal liking. For me, I opt in for the volume control for the buttons. It comes with three different bud sizes for ear adaptability, and that's the only area where I have trouble but I'm certain it's just my right ear being a jerk and refusing to accept music. But overall, I'd recommend these to anyone who is looking for some seriously good headphones but again brand choice is up to the buyer.

APP:
The app as mentioned before has some great features but if you lose your headphones, good luck finding them. I lost a single headphone in a warehouse and the app really didn't help none. I was lucky that someone else found and returned it to me. Just be mindful where you are at because finding them when out of the casing is hard.

title: Didn't work for me ... returned.
text:
I pre ordered these from Apple and received them on May 10th. Spent about a week at the gym using them and after the second day I knew I was returning them. I've listened to so much hype and even now that they're out almost all reviews are saying to "throw out your AirPods" .. these are superior. I was dumbfounded when I first put them in my ears and started listening to my music. I really thought something was wrong because I had it cranked all the way up and it wasn't that loud .. at all. Louder than AirPods? No way! The reviews also said that it has that Beats "bass" that made them famous but that wasn't there either. Now I own the PowerBeats 3 wireless headphones which are pretty much these except for the cord attaching the two and I never had a problem with them and even those sounded better than these. I'm not saying the sound is terrible, it's actually pretty good. There is a lot of treble which I like. The mids are a little muddled as even some reviewers have said. But the overall sound, in my opinion, doesn't justify the price. I did have a good seal with the tips that came with the phones but even when I pressed them into my ears I wasn't getting that good bass that the PB3s have. And I found myself constantly adjusting them after every set working out because they sometimes lost the seal. And when that happened, they sounded no better than a cheap $10 set of phones. I mostly listen to metal and hard rock and I am subscribed to Apple Music so the real test for bass would be house music so I tried that .. and still not much. And for volume, I switched back and forth from my AirPods to the PowerBeats Pros playing Metallica, Sabbath, Slayer .. etc and the AirPods were noticeably louder.
This review is just my opinion. I'm not saying they're terrible. The sound is good, but not great. They will stay on your ears whatever you're doing but they did start to bother my ears after about an hour and a half at the gym. The pairing was seamless and the Bluetooth never lost connection. Having buttons and volume knobs on both sides is great. But for me, I'm sticking with my AirPods and PowerBeats 3 wireless for now. My advice would be to try them first to see if they work for you. If you're buying them for the convenience of having stable phones that won't fall out of your ears and are ok with less than "audiophile" sound, they might be for you. But for me, my AirPods in my ears with a slight twist forward sound better, as do my PowerBeats 3.
