title: Runners, beware; expensive piece of junk
text:
I paid $249 for these from Target in mid-June (didn't purchase through Amazon this time). Target's return policy is 30 days for electronic products so I'm past the return point there. I bought these because the first review of the product in Runner's Magazine said they are great for running, sweat-proof, great battery life, etc. I run every day, so I've been looking for a great pair of wireless earbuds. I balked a little at the price point, but figured, what the heck, Apple makes good products, why not? I've had these for just over two months, and they are junk. Here are the problems:

1. The biggest issue, by far, is the battery life. For a product marketed as having a great, strong battery, you'd think it would last for a couple of months. It doesn't. I've had problems for at least 3-4 weeks, with each of the two earbuds dying out almost immediately, even right after being recharged. I've taken to leaving the battery case and the earbuds connected to a charger, and then double-checking them each morning before my run to make sure I can actually use them for a whole 45 minutes! Not a great routine.

2. Apple's "warranty" process. This was the most stunning to me -- for a company that charges a significant premium for its products, it sure screws over the customer when it comes time to honoring the warranty. I called to report my issue on September 2. I was told that I couldn't exchange the product at a local Apple Store. I had to wait for them to mail me a box, at which point they'd likely replace (rather than fix) my pair with a new out-of-box pair. I was told two business days for the box. Waiting, waiting, waiting. Today, Sept. 9, I called Apple again after not receiving the box. I was told (and I'm not kidding about this) that "we ran out of boxes" and Apple has NO IDEA when they'll be getting additional boxes, but when they do, they'll send one my way so that I can send them back my 2.5-month-old $249 pair of defective earbuds. I was so stunned by this, I asked for a supervisor, thinking that there's no way this can be a real policy! But, indeed, it is. This is literally Apple's policy. The supervisor (the "highest" level I, as a customer, am permitted to speak with) confirmed that they don't make exceptions to the policy that defective earbuds purchased by consumers can only be serviced once boxes become available. And Apple is all out of boxes! No kidding. I suggested that, given the situation, I should be permitted to exchange my earbuds with new buds from the Apple store 10 minutes from my house. I was told no, because they are not going to give me new buds; they are going to give me "refurbished" buds. So, essentially, all of the information that I was given last week is wrong. So, here I am, sitting around waiting for a box to be made available to me so that, perhaps, my earbuds can be exchanged with old (but "like new!") earbuds, after 2.5 months of usage. Nice, Apple.

3. The sweat factor. These things aren't even close to moisture wicking. It may be that they are sweat-proof, in that the sweat while you run doesn't destroy them (but it may NOT be, as, see above, mine don't work!) -- but I am regularly getting sweat under the earbuds that cause a popping noise while I am listening to music, which drives me crazy.

4. The sound quality. Great or not good depending on the source of the music. When I listen to the music I have on the phone, I can adjust the quality of the speaker, and the quality is quite high. When I'm listening to my Peleton app (or another app where I'm playing music) you lose the ability to adjust, and the treble is simply too high. I'll call this a wash, because the sound quality is actually very good when you can control the source.

Bottom line: I own a $40 pair of wireless headphones (not Apple, obviously given the price!) that has served me better on my daily runs than these overpriced junk earbuds that Apple clearly doesn't stand behind. Do yourself a favor -- buy elsewhere. From now on, I certainly will.

Update (Nov. 2019): after weeks of arguing with Apple, I finally found someone helpful who replaced my earbuds with a new set. New earbuds, same problems. I’m on month 2 with the new pair and they have the same issues. On my morning run I’m listening to my iPhone speakers half the time because one of the damn buds is never charged, despite always carefully positioning them in the case and charging the case far more than should be normal. Bottom line - these are junk, and it’s a design issue. Apple forums have now caught up — many complaints, but no action from Apple. Do. Not. Buy.

title: Much Better  3.5 Stars [previously rated: "A Disappointment" 2.5 Stars]
text:
29 July 2019 - Hi there. After a day with my first pair ofPB Pro's, I quickly shuffled them off to Amazon for a refund. Once the refund was posted, and very quickly I might add. I ordered another pair. It was my hope that I initially received a defective unit that slipped through the QC inspection at the factory.

Verdict: The second pair sounds way better. There is bass, which the first set did not have. More importantly, there was a lack of overbearing harshness to the mids and ear-splitting shrills to the treble. However, they still fall short in sound quality to the Powerbeats 3. Too bad. Not sure if I'll return them. I will give them a try for a a couple of weeks or so and decide before the 30 day return period expires.

Downfalls of PB Pros are a lack of a mobile app to allow for sound quality settings. Stuff like EQ settings and soundstage modes, i.e., stadium, rock concert, jazz. Presets I guess is what you would call them. Also a mode to maybe check to see if there are any firmware upgrades, revisions. I wonder if there will be any?

My recommendation? Well, I say give them a try. It's my subjective guess that the quality control of the builds for these may be lacking. I'm not overblown like many of they reviewers are on YouTube. Many whose recommendations haven't failed me. Importantly, make sure you buy from a seller who does have a trustworthy return policy.

My Advice. If you do buy these, keep the package intact as much as possible. If you have an IPhone or other Apple mobile device that has a Fire connector, use that to charge your case up [another quibble of mine] That way you don't have to unpackage the included connector that comes with the PB Pros, therefore, not putting at risk your return for damaged packaging.

The lack of wireless charging is bummer too. Just my thought. Good luck if you go with these. :)

Previous Review >> As an intro my review, let me say that I am a happy owner of the Powerbeats 3 wireless earphones. They were definitely a step up over the Powerbeats 2, which I still have and I do like as well. They both represent the music I listen to very well with little or no distortion. My taste runs the gamut from a classical to jazz to Kpop/Jpop. All over. They both do very well. I've never caught myself critiquing them for getting in the way of the music I listen to.

Now to the Powerbeats Pro. I think this is a wonderful concept. It was what I had hoped for, a dongle free earbud setup with a secure hook around your ear.. My like of the Powerbeats 2 and 3 were the ear hooks. Very little chance of them coming off in most activities. 5 stars to Beats for this!

But, these Powerbeats Pro sound extraordinarily horrible. The tapping of the high hats, the cymbal tapping, the one and three beats of most pop music, all sound sickly distorted. Not crisp, sharp and more importantly, discernible as an instrument. It's like when a recording artist doesn't use a an "s" shield on the microphone. You get that sharp distorted staccato of a sudden hissy hit. It's the only way I can describe it. I'm disappointed.

There is a maybe. Maybe the one I have is part of a production run that is below spec and wasn't caught to be rejected? The go to review sites and Youtube reviewers I follow had good things to say about these. I am in agreement with about 70 percent of their reviews of what they reviewed and what I bought based on those reviews. Your ears won't lie to you. So what I am saying is that for me, this particular set is lackluster not worthy of keeping. I'm going to return it. I still want to give them a shot and will buy another pair from a local electronic boutique. This way I can open it up and try it out on the spot. If they pass, the they will be a go. If not, then an on the spot return with refund can happen :)

Oh, one more thing to be aware of. The extra earbud tips that come with these only go up to about a medium/large size. I had to take the x-large tips off the Powerbeats 3 and put them on the Pro's. It helped with the sound a bit, letting be captured fully in my ear canal.

A great effort by Dre Beats that fell short of my hopes and expectations, for now.

text:
I got these mostly as a replacement for the Jaybird X2 headphones that I'd been using at the gym. I really like the Jaybirds, but I wanted something that was truly wireless, and I also like using headphones with the W1 chip so they work seamlessly with my devices.

My primary concerns were sound quality and comfort. I'm pleased with these in both areas. I wore them for about 40 minutes and they felt great; I'll have to get used to having earhooks (the Jaybirds don't have them), but they weren't uncomfortable, just different.

The gym is kind of loud, with music playing as well as a lot of fans going full blast. The seal created by the rubber tips effectively blocks out all of that. They're not noise-canceling as such, but they do a great job of keeping out excess ambient noise.

I will say that I got noticeable lag when I used them with my MacBook Pro. I did not, however, when using them with my iPhone, iPad Pro, or Apple TV. I'm not sure what's up with that, but I may ask next time I'm at an Apple Store. I'm not going to use them with my MBP or Apple TV regularly, but I wanted to put them through their paces.

Anyway, these are great, especially if you're in the Apple ecosystem. They're comfortable, the sound quality is very good, and they're very user-friendly.

title: Sound is very average. No bass. Terrible battery life
text:
Update: now that I have had these for over a year I can tell you that the battery life is abysmal. You do not get more than a few hours out of a full charge. And the worst feature is that you can fully charge the device, use it for only an hour, and they will be dead in a few days if you set them on the table and not back in the charger case. In other words, they will not hold a charge for more than a day or two sitting out even when barely used. Awful product.

As far as fit, comfort, and function these are great. They have a lot of excellent options integrated into a small package. And all of the functions seem to work as described. Accessing and controlling the headset is very easy. All in all these are great headphones from a build perspective and I want to love them.

However, for a price that is much higher than almost all competitors, I expected way more from the sound quality. These are not any better sound quality than my $60 plantronics sports version. The sound is very tinny and the bass is almost nonexistent. It touts that you can just wear in one ear but that makes the sound really awful. So for me that’s not even an option. I think maybe the problem is that they try to build it so that you can wear it in just one year and push the same sound to each headphone instead of making a true stereo experience like you would across two earpieces. So even when you were both earpieces you get the same dull sound and no true stereo affect. I could have bought three or four cheaper headsets that serve the same purpose and have equally good sound for the price I paid for these. Very very disappointed.

title: A serious step up from Airpods
text: First, the most important stuff.  Sound quality is very good 8/10, the bass is slightly less than Powerbeats3, but way more than Airpods give you.  The treble in my opinion is too high though, and makes listening to many songs at high volume impossible because it gets piercing.  Mids are pretty much lost in the mix.  Its a shame Apple doesn't provide an Equalizer so we could adjust these settings.  Battery performance is amazing, I keep them in the recharging case whenever not in use and they last DAYS (used during gym, subway commuting).  The case is big, and not pocket sized but that's OK because I carry a backpack always.  I sweat alot and haven't noticed any issues yet.  In terms of connection quality, over the past week of use, they have had blips twice...nothing noticeable or really noteworthy. They are a little harder to insert into the ear than the Powerbeats3, because the design is meant to put the sound stem deeper into the ear.  After a few days of use though I got used to it, and can put them in very quickly now.  Ive heard complaints about sound isolation, and for me these are perfect because I need to be somewhat aware of the sounds around me during a busy commute or at the gym, just from a safety perspective.  Overall very happy with the purchase and hope they last a few years!  250$ though is STEEP!  would be better if they were $199 and Airpods were $149.

title: What do you need AirPods for? Lmao
text:
I’ve tried lots of different earbuds, and I’ve even tried some AirPods, but I like these the best. They come with instructions for use with IPhones and Android products, and they also come with different size ear inserts. I saw a lot of people complaining that the noise cancelling is trash, and that the earbuds kept falling out and stuff, but both of those are adjustable features and can easily fit the tastes of the majority of people.

You can change the noise canceling settings, which is really cool. I don’t really use noise cancelling, but the noise cancelling on these earbuds is totally worth the price if that’s what you’re looking for.

Also, When looking for a pair of headphones or earbuds, I’m always looking for something with good bass. These don’t have the best bass I’ve ever heard, but I’ve adjusted some settings on my Iphone, and am ultimately satisfied with their bass. I’ve definitely had cheaper headphones with better bass, but the noise cancelling settings can also help with that. On their basic settings the treble is a bit loud for my taste, but I’ve managed to adjust that in my phone settings as well.

The battery life is good, and they pair really easily to my phone. As I mentioned earlier, I’ve used AirPods before, and I don’t know if the pair My brother and I had were especially jacked or something, but they weren’t nearly loud enough and had no bass. These Beats are definitely a much better option, especially since these were only like $120, and AirPods are around $200+. I mean, if AirPods are your thing, you do you Boo. But these little Beats have made me happy, and they made my wallet happy, too. :)

text:
Listening to these right now ATM. Genuinely really good sound quality without having too much bass, just the right amount for my ears. Good spectrum between both joined together. Had it paired within 2-3 seconds and they worked immediately. Had to press the outside right one to get both on at same time. I'm completely new to this tech.
Came almost full charged and only took about 2-3 minutes for full charge. Tested it out with spoken voice first, very good and now trying it out with music (Grand Funk Railroad I'm You're Captain) really great sound quality. Good signal for up to about 20' which is plenty enough for me. Better than my Razer gaming headset! Better sound quality too and for half the money. Fully waterproof as well, tested them in my sink. You really don't even notice they're in at all. Used the earbuds that came installed originally and they fit perfectly even with rigorous activity they stay put which I absolutely appreciate.
The charging case is super small which makes it very convenient and fits in any pocket pretty comfortably sort of about the same size as a set of keys. Very lightweight too which makes long-term carry time even better. The only thing I haven't tested yet is the call features which I'll try later but that's really not what I bought these for but is a nice additional capability. As far as noise cancelling they're actually great too without having to pump the volume to ridiculous levels.
Comes with two small booklets, one for quick operations and one with details for music use and call use. If you prefer a lot of bass these may not quite be for your taste but given the cost they're tough to beat. Higher volume than say what you'd normally hear in a room you get a bit of clipping and distortion for music. For voice, you can turn them up pretty loud.
No question about it for me, they're definitely worth the money and will serve my needs for a very modest price!!! Definitely recommend these!

title: Not As Described
text:
I wanted to love these. I preordered from Apple, they arrived Friday and I immediately put them to use. The first issue is the design. They're a little difficult to get a good fit in ear and the instructions on inserting and twisting are confusing.

The second issue and most important to me is... These are nothing like Powerbeats Pro where you get all day listening and talk time (I get 8-10 hours. And I use them ALL DAY). These have the listening/talk time of AirPods.

After the first use of the Beats Studio Buds I had to swap them out after about 3 hours (I wear one at a time) and they were basically just sitting in my ear. I didn't use them much. I talked on the phone for a little while and listened to a few songs but that was it... To get more hours of use you must turn off Transparency AND Noise Cancelling. If you have either of those on the listening/talk time is TRASH!!! Also, even though you can turn the transparency mode off it seems to come back on automatically after charging. If you want to extend your time of use, you have to remember to turn transparency off again...

And for these 2 reasons they're going back to Apple. These were an epic fail for me!!

The case is a good size compared to the Powerbeats Pro but I rather have a huge case that I won't even have to touch throughout the day (because the listening/talk time is ALL DAY) than a small case that I have to keep up with and carry all day because the things will be dying soon...

Also, when talking on the phone people said the sound on their end was amazing but the sound on my end was just ok. I did miss not being able to adjust the sound from the earbud. I originally didn't think that would be an issue but the feature WAS missed.

Maybe the next generation will be better but for me... I'm sticking with the Powerbeats Pro.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

HOWEVER, I tried to pair them with my Oculus Quest 2 VR headset for a workout (I like to have music loud and if I am not using the earbuds my family can hear it). These would NOT pair. They were discoverable, but when I tried to connect them it wouldn't. I spent 30 min going back and forth trying to figure out what the problem was since my older TOZO earbuds (model T10) worked great. Finally I googled it and apparently some earbuds do not work with Oculus. So I ordered more of the T10 - which is fine with me since they are easier to handle and remove and put in the charging case. The case is smaller so for those who don't mind fuddling with them to get in your ears and out of the case or correctly placed in case (that is another strange design) they are OK.

The pics show the difference in case size and also the actual earbud size. In reality the earbud size if just about the same. However, the design is more kidney bean shape and I think that is a reason it was awkward getting them to fit comfortably in my ear and also getting them in and out of the case to charge. title: Great headphones overall.  Very good battery life.  Just wish they supported a mute button.
text:
I bought these for cycling. I wear one in an ear at at a time and it gives good sound and is able to switch to mono automatically when paired to an Apple phone. I switched from a previous much cheaper earbud previously that claimed a 6 hour battery but barely every passed 4 hours. So far, I have done several hundred mile rides and have never had it lose charge. So I don't know if it really gets 9 hours but it definitely gets 7+. If I needed to do 120miles or more I'd probably bring both earbuds just to be safe - although there really is no way to turn them off outside of the case so I'd guess the entire case would be required for this which is kind of a bummer now that I think about it.

I really like having the over the ear bracket for riding. My previous earbuds would fall out every once in a while and it eventually made me fairly paranoid about tilting my head which is not something I want to think about during a ride.

There are two improvements that could be made to this device. The first is for taking phone calls on it. The unit has a rocker button for volume, and a multi-function button that can be used to pause/play, go forward, or reverse the track depending on how many taps you do. For phone calls it can only pick up or hang up the call. I occasionally like to take calls while I am riding and I would appreciate the ability to mute/unmute. I don't see why they can't just change the function for a phone call so that a double tap allows this. But they haven't.

The second improvement would be to include this device in the Find My App on the iPhone like the Airpods and Airpods Pro support. This unit has the right chip to support the feature and there's no good reason for Apple to not include it other than pure laziness.

I'd still choose this again out of all the available options on the market with these shortcomings. But it loses a star because of them.

title: Stable Bluetooth connection, powerful touch control, good sound quality
text:
I own a T10 over 2 years and use it almost every day. It is a well-built earbud. Recently, I bought the new A1 model. I see the improvement instantly.

Highlight of the A1 earbud
• Very small case and slightly smaller earbud
• Touch control
• Good sound quality
• Bluetooth 5.0 long range connection.

The earbud is lightly smaller. To someone, it may be nothing significant, but to me, it is a big improvement. This small earbud fits my ear much better. Even after 2 hours of using, my ears did not feel anything uncomfortable. The bulky earbud will cause my ear pain after using it for over half an hour.
The case is about half the volume of T10. It has indicator showing remaining energy. Tozo did a good job.

Touch control is very easy to use, especially when you are using the earbud. Just a few taps, you can play next/previous music or video, pause and play, volume up/down, phone call answer/hangup. I tried all of the features, impressed. On the other hand, I barely used T10 control. It is so hard to push the buttons.

Sound quality remain high, no significant difference to T10. I turned on AAC audio and did not have compatible issue.

The Bluetooth is better than T10. I walked around the house while leaving the phone on the desk, I got stable connection and consistent sound quality. The improvement is obvious.

On the negative side, I noticed one minor issue. The case can only be opened 90 degree. That makes taking out earbud a little hard. I can see it is a tradeoff of minimizing size of the case. But usability should take higher priority.

Overall, it is an improved high-quality product. I recommend it.

title: Jammin with an actual button
text:
The Beats Studio Buds are a tight built power house. Replication of my favorite tunes was fantastic. Base and high pitch tones never had issues or max vol distortion.

These things stay firm in my ears and passed the shake/run test.

A HUGE plus is that the buttons to active play/pause etc actually have a click to them. Some unit it’s a tap a sensor deal and I am always accidently setting them off (or on). Nice job.

The case is compact but has magnetic grips the buds when storing/charging so that you know you have them in place. I tested with some foam tips which can add to the ear seal and help with noise canceling. small and medium named and knock off brand foam tips did store in the beats case and charged, while larger ones had trouble getting contact going.

Let’s get back to noise canceling, these are top of the charts. The app has limited button settings but 3 modes for ANC (see capture). Even without foam tips the AC and ceiling fan was undetectable. Outside nose was significantly muted. With the foam tips on and my ear size, I was able to take a nap I mean test laying down and had no discomfort to my ears  Results may vary!

Some of the tunes tested with a rank when played on these buds:
Enya: Memory of Trees Instrumental (great dual channel soothing sample) 4/5
JT: LoveStoned (great opening base but when you get to 0:48 kicking in full bloom is crit) 5/5
Miles Davis: So What (you got horn on the left and front center, riding cymbals back right, incredible listen on these) 5/5
Maroon 5: Wait (check out bounce from L/R in opening on your buds and compare… then groove at 0:23) 5/5
Nipsey Hussle: Blue Laces 2 (Slide into the bass carefully!) 4/5
The Weeknd: Blinding Lights (bro told me to start using this tune to compare, highly synthesized song from the 80s? (laff) but great tones up and down the chart) 5/5

As we are finding with many buds, if you don’t have a boom the mic pick up can be challenging. Callers said at times I was slightly muffled and others asked if I was on a speakerphone. Not enough to dock a star but not blown away with the recordings I did either.

Overall a premium experience for music.

title: Really enjoyable and easy to use.
text:
I have been having so much fun with my Tozo A1 wireless earbuds. They are straightforward to use. There are also instructions online if you have trouble reading small print instructions. I really like the sound of these. I am sure I could have spent upwards of $200 on some fancy earbuds, but I've never owned a pair before. After reading many positive reviews, I thought this could be my first experience with wireless earbuds. I am so happy I made the purchase for under $20. In fact, I can't believe they are so inexpensive.

The microphone and call answering and talking all work great with this device. When you have both earbuds in, you can't really hear anything else. I don't believe they advertised noise canceling, but the sound is really immersive when both buds are in and you can't hear much else.

The only thing that might be an issue for some is that the bass isn't very heavy. The base is decent, and the sound is well-balanced. I haven't found this to be a problem for me.

The fit in the ear is really nice. I don't have anything to compare it to, but I found the fit to be very comfortable. I guess I average sized ears.

Overall, I recommend these earbuds. I absolutely would buy them again. They are a great value for your money, and I'm having a blast with them.

title: Pretty much perfect.
text:
First, let me humbly say that I am a recording engineer at a professional studio, and have produced and recorded a lot of records so I have some pedigree in this realm. I purchased these beats for two reasons: because I wanted something that stayed in my ears when working in the yard, and when working out - but also so I can test my mixes on earbuds that have a modern eq profile to make sure they will sound good when people are listening to them on bassier buds.

I’ve only had them for 12 hours. But at this point I can say that I love them. They totally work - the connection is solid, the soundstage is wide and clear, they sound great, they actually reveal quite a lot of detail, they are VERY comfortable (and also the arm is adjustable by bending it so if it doesn’t fit your ears exactly you can make them fit better).

They are a TAD bit bassy. But probably on the order of about 3db hot below 100 Hz. Listening on Spotify if I cut just a tiny bit, they seem pretty flat to me. But I turned off the eq because I really don’t think the bass is as overblown as some say. If you are an audiophile who has a collection of tube amps and high end headphones, you will likely say that these are grievously bassy, but remember that folks like you are focused on a level of detail that most listeners are not even able to hear without formal listening training.

Personally I find that with the right earbud tips these buds sound phenomenally good, with a little bass bump that sounds and feels really good to me - especially at lower listening levels when we want/need more bass anyway because of the physics of sound (Fletcher Munson curve).

So - I’m sold. These are sweet. They sound awesome, I’m not missing any mids, not getting too much bass or highs, and they just go with you wherever you go - comfortably and reliably.

The ONLY think I don’t love is that they are just a little bit tricky to put on, especially with glasses. But I think I’ll get the hang of it as I get used to them. title: Better than past Beats buds?
text:
It’s been a while since I tried any Beats Brand headphones or buds, and the truth is that I was never impressed by the sound quality and value. Leaving all that behind and going in with fresh expectations, I will share my experience so far.

I appreciate the white Studio Beats case design. The small footprint, oval shape, feels good in the hands and fits flatly in almost any pocket without being too bulky. There’s only the Beats logo, one USB-C port, and an LED status light. The white plastic finish seems well made and can resist smudges and fingerprints but may be susceptible to getting dirty fast. The lid opens easily and shuts down with a snap satisfyingly. Along with the buds, the top is magnetic and stays in place securely -maybe too securely as it can be difficult to take out the buds sometimes.

The buds have a similar matte white finish on the casing, but the front is glossy. The shape of the buds is quite interesting since they resemble some sort of handle. This shape allows them to be placed and adjusted easily. Using the large gel tips, they fit very comfortably in my medium-sized ears. I was able to wear them until they ran out of battery, about 5 hours without any discomfort or issues. I did find that when exercising, they can shift a bit. It’s a good thing they are rated IPX4 so a bit of sweat or rain won’t be a problem.

Now, these are interesting because they are Apple products, but do not include any Apple chipset. However, the Bluetooth (class 1?) is fully compatible with both Apple (natively) and Android (app) and connects seamlessly. The connection is stable even at a good distance. I did not notice any lag when watching videos or playing games. There’s also full integration with any voice assistant.

The battery is decent. They last about 5 hours with ANC and 7 hours with ANC off at 50% volume. The case adds 15 to 24 hours. They also feature a quick charge where 5 minutes in the case adds 1 hour of playback. Unfortunately, the case does not support Qi wireless charging, which is disappointing at this price range. It is also strange that a USBC to USB-C cable is included instead of a USB to USB-A, which is most common.

The noise cancellation is decent, albeit not all that impressive. Aided by good-fit ear tips, they are adequate enough to drown some sound, although I was still able to hear my loud central air system. The ambient sound mode is also good enough to become aware of my surroundings and is certainly welcome.

The Studio Buds feature button controls and I actually like them. Typically, button controls tend to push the buds deeper into the ear canal making them uncomfortable. They are very responsive. In fact, adjusting them can sometimes activate them. One big issue I have is that there is no volume control. You either must take out your device or tell the voice assistant to do it for you. Sadly, there is no automatic pause when taking them off, but you can take one out and still listen to the other if that’s useful to you.

I was surprised by the sound signature. This time around, Beats opted for a more restrained bass response. It is pronounced but not overbearing. It is a bit lose but enjoyable. The midrange is noticeable, but it is brought into the background somewhat. Thankfully, the treble is well represented, adding much-needed clarity. The soundstage is not that great, but the channel separation is well implemented. While they are definitely designed for audiophiles, I found them enjoyable, nonetheless. By the way, having ANC on or off does not change the sound signature.

The call quality is very good. Although you still hear the wind and background noise, and people can tell that you’re on wireless, my voice came in clear without hiccups.

In the end, I like these buds. The design is unique enough without being pretentious like previous Beats offerings. The sound is fun, and they fit well. The lack of volume control, wireless charging, and just “good enough” sound may not live up to other similarly priced buds out there. Still, I recommend them because all of these nitpicks are subjective and I think most will still enjoy them.

title: Uncomfortable to the max — Not a replacement to the Airpods
text:
TLDR: I’m just OK with these. I love the battery life and integration with the Apple ecosystem but they’re super uncomfortable for all day wear. And no, these are not a replacement to Apple AirPods. The AirPods are your jack of all trades while these Beats are more geared for specific usage.

My rating: 2.5/5

Note: Dear Amazon — Sound cancellation and noise isolation are two different things. This doesn’t have noise cancelling. It does have noise isolation with the right sized earbud tips.

Comfort
————
I love my Apple AirPods and would consider myself a hesitant Apple fan girl. I know other people have had issues with trying to keep Apple AirPods in their ears. It’s the unfortunate nature of one size fits all. However, they fit me — so lucky me!

With these Beats, you get the ability to change the eartips out. That’s very helpful for comfort and sound quality. However, the base of the earbud makes it super uncomfortable. And ultimately, this is what kills it for me! Unfortunately, it’s just too big that it makes my ears sore after a half an hour of use. So — unlucky me, this time!

Sound Quality
——————-
When you put these on and compare them to AirPods, the AirPods do sound very anemic. Everyone asks if these are replacements to AirPods and my answer is no. AirPods are not meant to take you away from the world with your music. By design, they don’t have a seal to isolate the sound. When you put on any pair of “normal” headphones, the cushions that touch your ears help with comfort, yes. However, their primary function is to create a seal. That seal helps with sound tremendously! Also without that seal, bass is non-existent.

These Beats offer a nice selection of four different sizes plus a fifth size that’s cone shaped (that one’s intended to not create a seal so you can hear the world around you). It’s very easy to establish a seal that provides a nice degree of sound isolation and bring out the best that these can offer. Regarding the sound profile, these headphones have a less aggressive but similar EQ profile as the rest of the Beats line. I’ve tested these on Tidal against various master quality songs of different genres. These Beats are really meant for a certain branch of music but kind of fall flat outside of hip hop, R&B and dance music. And yes, there’s no midrange at all. It’s true!

Overall
———
In the end, I still prefer the AirPods because they’re so much easier to put back in their case. The case itself is smaller. The Beats case is massive comparatively. In addition, the Beats are so bulky with putting them on and off, putting them back in their case, and pressing the buttons for adjustments. For me, the touch feedback of the AirPods doesn’t require you to push into you ears like these Beats do. The Beats requires a little more heft with pushing buttons. It’s neat that you get to have all this functionality and extra battery life. title: Charging issues and poor user interface ruin the great sound quality
text:
Pros: These sound great. They're a definitive sound upgrade over my old workout earbuds, especially for the bass. I love listening to rock music while I run with these. They're pretty comfortable, though I don't think I'd want to use them continuously throughout a 2 hour workout. They also look great, and so does the case. Build quality of both also feel solid.

Cons: After about one month, the right earbud stopped charging inside the case. It has become my pre-workout ritual to open the case, put in both earbuds and find that only the left one connected. I have to disconnect and reconnect them about 2-5 times on my iPhone 7 before it will finally show me the charge level for the earbuds and the case. I then have to leave the case open as the right earbud charges. This is where fast charge should save me, but I've found I need to charge them for about 10 minutes to get 45 minutes of playback, well below their advertised "1.5 hours on a 5 minute charge".
The interface, at least on the iPhone 7 is a pain. Once I finally get the charge level to show up on the screen, there's no way to get it back once I move away from it. So my phone has to sit unusable while I wait for the earbud to finish charging.

I have to assume this is a quality control issue, and it's really disappointing because these cost a lot of money and the problems only started right after the end of the 30 day warranty. Will be going back to a cheaper pair of workout earbuds next time to avoid paying so much money for a broken device.

title: Better for running/workout than Airpods Pro
text:
I bought a pair of Airpods Pro from Apple. First time out, I found that they felt very insecure in my ears while running and working out and even fell out a time or two. Changing the ear tips did not help much. So, I sent them back and bought these from Amazon, because of the behind-the-ear clip. It was a good move. I've worn them running on a trail and doing a weight workout. They feel absolutely secure and can't fall out.

The sound quality is about the same as the Airpods, maybe not quite as good, but that's hard to tell. In any case, if you want top sound quality, you have to use big headphones, not earpods. There's not a whole lot of bass, but you can't really expect that from such a tiny device. I like that there is a volume control + a function button on each earpod--but "Hey, Siri" works great for changing volume etc. Battery capacity appears to be quite large. Like airpods, they charge from the case and you charge the case when needed. After a 45-minute run, the earpods were only down about 5%.

title: Great battery and sound quality, OK fit, NO noise cancellation
text:
These headphones have no noise cancellation at all. Even considering the earpiece is similar to an earplug in that it blocks your ear canal, it's only a thin piece of silicon/rubber, and even with music at a comfortable level, you can still hear your surroundings. You can drown out your surroundings as these headphones are plenty loud, but unless you're willing to damage your hearing, expect to be able to hear your surroundings. This is good for when you're running and want to hear cars driving by for safety, but quite irritating when you're on the plane and the only way to even hear your music / video above the plane noise is to blast the volume past a comfortable level.

The battery is stellar. They claim 9 hours on just the buds, but I've never gotten there as who wears headphones for 9 hours straight without putting them in the case? As soon as you put them in the case, they start charging up again, and the case probably has another 1.5 to 2 charges on it. Absolutely amazing battery life.

My favorite part of these compared to other true wireless headphones is that each bud is completely stand alone. They have a volume rocker on both buds, and the multi-function button has the same function on both buds; effectively they're two standalone buds that work together in perfect harmony, or individually. Using them individually doubles the play time, so I find myself wearing one at a time and going nearly a week without needing to plug in the case.

They say the ear hook is adjustable... I haven't found it to be adjustment friendly, but I also haven't tried to force it. They fit ok, and would fit even a larger ear than mine (although mine are already quite large). I don't think they'd be as well suited for smaller-eared people. They certainly stay in place, but depending on your ear shape, they may cause a little discomfort as the earpiece (not that goes in your actual ear canal, but just the plastic that sits inside your ear) is quite large, and for me at least has a tendency to put pressure on my ear, which does get uncomfortable after extended periods if it isn't adjusted right.

The case is also pretty stinking large; doesn't fit in a pocket very well at all, but you can stuff it in one just to get from A to B if necessary.

Overall I'm pretty happy with these, but I will likely end up trying to find another pair that actually has some noise cancelling features, be it active or passive, as these have no noise cancellation.

title: Not good for my tastes/use
text:
I purchased these through Best Buy and decided to return them for a number of reasons. I got them for the gym, exclusively, so things like battery life and case size weren't huge selling points. I wanted good fit, ease of use, and at LEAST "good for what they are" sound.

I'm an Android user and the lack of any equalizer, which I knew going in, ended up being a big deal. I tried using my 6th generation Ipod Touch, re-subscribed to Apple Music, thinking that might make a difference. The "equalizer" on that device, at least, is basically choosing from presets rather than independent values. When the latest ios installed, only one piece paired and I found that irritating. I'm not an Apple fan, to be fair, so might be quick to write them off if things aren't smooth (and suspect Apple loyalists are quick to praise because they're ready to love anything they make).

Getting them on is kind of a pain, but something I'm sure you get the hang of after finding the right technique. When I did work out, the stability was definitely great and worked well in that regard. But the sound? Surprisingly underwhelming. I didn't notice much difference between my Ipod (with preferred sound stage setting) and Android; I even tried ordering different tips to get a better seal, but they just sound so average.

I drove myself nuts reading reviews because they're basically mixed on every one of the premium options, so I just asked the guy at Best Buy for his opinion. He recommended the Jaybird Vistas, based on my use, which I TRIED reviewing on Amazon, but it won't let me because of "suspicious" activity (or something). Because I appreciate recommendations when the reviewed product doesn't work well for that person, I could not recommend them more! For my taste, every single thing about them is superior. Right out of the case, they fit excellently (the standard "medium" with other options if that doesn't work). And the sound really, really surprised me in every possible way, not just "good for what they are," but actually good sound (again, for my taste). I had similar opinions of the Jaybird X2s I owned in the past, and REALLY liked their equalizer app., but just didn't like the tethering between the two ear pieces. Even though the equalizer is still available for this set, I haven't bothered messing with it because I like the sound just the way it is, out of the box. And even though the case size isn't a big deal to me, I do appreciate how tiny it is, in comparison, to the Beats, something you could probably hang from your key chain. When I finally did start working out with them, I was fully sold - they stay in no matter what I do, the connectivity is strong (some issues getting too far away, but I figure that's standard; but I have never completely lost connection), they block out ambient noise very well, and the controls are tuned well (something you can change in their app, I believe, eg which clicks do what).

So...Beats may be superb for batter life, phone call clarity, etc., but I couldn't find anything redeeming for the way I used them, especially for the top-end price (for a sport set, anyway). And since I can't review the Jaybird Vistas, PLEASE give those a try if you're in my position!

title: Constant connectivity issues and now battery issues
text:
I purchased these in February. I had been purchasing cheap workout headphones for years, but just got tired of the horrible sound and them easily breaking. I did a ton of research and decided to pull the trigger on what a lot of people (and publications) deemed the best workout headphones available. When they first came, I had trouble connecting the left ear piece, I was able to reset it and then it connected. The sound was awesome. Not true noise cancelling, but easily the best for any workout headphone I've ever tried. Then the issues started to arise. The left headphone had to be paired over and over again for them to work. After a few months, it's to the point now where it takes 5-10 minutes for me to get both headphones to pair. In addition, the left headphone doesn't charge correctly. So essentially, it's a very rare occurrence where both headphones actually work. They may be the best sounding workout headphones, but it's completely irrelevant if they never work.

Pros:
- Sounds great
- Noise cancelling is pretty good

Cons:
- Large case
- Connectivity issues
- Charging issues
- If something goes wrong, expect a long battle with Apple for repairs or replacements

Just to note, I purchased Apple Care for this product. I usually never purchase warranties since they are mostly a complete waste of money. I had heard good things about Apple Care, so I decided to pull the trigger. I contacted them about replacing the left ear piece and they said it would cost $100 to replace. So basically, you pay $250.00 for headphones that work for 3 months, then you have to pay another $100 to replace them.

title: As good as I could've hoped from Beats for $100
text:
If you like the look, the brand, and the price, then you'll be satisfied by these. If you're okay with spending more on a more reasonably priced brand and getting more for it, I'd go that route instead.

Sound quality:
- It's fine. They sound terrible until you get the right sized tips for your ears selected and then they sound fine. My ears are still slightly too big for the biggest included tips so it's hard for me to get these to sound their best, but not impossible. They're not the best but there's nothing that they do a bad job at. The bass is nice, it isn't overly boosted and manages to extend without sounding too flabby.
- The overall "fidelity" is noticeably low if you've tried anything better. There isn't a ton of depth or clarity but its still better than baseline.

ANC and pass-through:
- 3.5/5? The vast majority of the noise cancellation comes from earbuds plugging up your ear canals, and if you hadn't tried these with ANC before, you'd think it was on as soon as you put them in your ears because of how much noise they passively block. Pass-through works somewhat but everything still sounds muffled, more expensive tws earbuds can make this work good enough to forget you're wearing them but these beats definitely cannot (though I wouldn't expect them to at ~$50+ less).

Usability:
- They're easy enough to use. There was a bug on the Android version that would send you a notification every time the battery percentage went down 1% but it looks like they fixed it. They're easy to pair and theres always a battery life indicator in your notifications to glance at.
- The buttons on the sides are easy enough to press but you have to test and memorize which setting of ANC you're on as the sound cues aren't the best.

Would I recommend these? I'm not sure. There's plenty of similar anc tws earbuds around this price that I haven't tried and the only ones I have tried are $50+ more and all sound/work better, but are still all $50+ more. I daily drive the Bose QuietComfort earbuds which cost twice as month, but the ANC, pass-through, and audio quality are miles beyond what these buds can offer. If you're not an audiophile and want simple tested "default" earbuds, these will work fine. If you want to do some research on lesser known brands around this price point, you can probably find something better. If you want higher quality and are okay with paying for it, there's WF-1000XM4s and QuietComfort earbuds that will blow these out of the water. In the end its up to you

title: Good airpod pro alternative if you're willing to give a few things up
text:
These are nice sounding and well fitting buds for me. As with all earbuds that depend on an eartip/eargel to provide a good seal, sound will be bad if the seal is poor. For me, the medium and large tips both work, but the medium are more comfortable.

If you're willing to give up "hey siri", the great microphone of airpods pro, the wireless charging case, premium feel of the case and charge via USB C instead of lighting, these can be good alternatives which save you $100 at MSRP, but we all know airpods pro no longer cost that, so your savings is more along the lines of $30. For me, I'd rather have airpods pro.

The things I really like:

The buds are lightweight and you hardly feel them.
The sound is quite nice, with good bass.
Lightweight buds.
Fit well.
Really good noise cancelation, better than airpods pro.
Really good hear through/ambient mode with no hiss.
They are smaller than airpods pro, and should fit smaller ears better.
No lag with videos, but none is to be expected.
Really good battery life at a rated 8 hours. Most I've used is 4 and were still going strong.
IPX4 rating.
Look good.

The things I don't like:
The buttons on the buds are too sensitive. While not touch buttons, they are too easy to press when adjusting the buds in your ears.
The case feels kind of cheap, like thin but not too thin plastic, which is what it is.
The microphone - you sound really, really distant and faint on phone calls.
They start slipping out when active (running, jumping).

Overall, these are good buds for listening that fit into the apple ecosystem well, but there are better options at lower prices available from other manufacturers. You're paying for the name and post purchase support should things go wrong, and that's worth something to some, but many other manufacturers also have great warranty support. Why four stars? Because overall they are really good sounding buds that are well made, and what I consider shortcomings others may not.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: Excellent Sound, can be tricky to charge
text:
Overall I really do like the Powerbeats for their sounds, longevity and compatibility. They have a few quirks to get use to, but no technology is perfect.
Pros:
Great sound for music and voice. Holds up well to sweat during workouts. Syncs well with all my devices (Mac, iPad, iPhone, Windows. Long battery life that will last most of the day on a single charge and quick to recharge. Can use them together or just one, which is especially important for one of my one complaints. I really like to over the ear clip, which keeps them in place for the workouts and outdoors use and is comfortable for me even with glasses on.
Con:
Can be tricky to properly charge. The earphone charge by two very small connections on the bottom that magnetically connect to ports in the case. If you don't get the connection just right they won't connect and charge and in fact drain down since they aren't charging. There is an indicator light on the case that tells you if they are connected and charging however it seems the light comes on even if just one is properly seated. There are times I have taken the earphones out of the case thinking they have had a long charge only to find one is critically low and have to re-seat it to charge while using just one that is charged (that is the pro, that one will work alone). I am trying to be very meticulous about seating to charge which has helped some but still not always perfect...works about 60-70% of the time. Reading elsewhere, outside of Amazon, I've seen others have a similar issue. Since they do have this quirk but last a long time when charged, I only took 1 star off battery life for the quirk.
They are also sometimes tricky to connect/sync both earphones. When I take them out of the charger or switch devices, both earphones do not always connect to the device on the first try (at least one of the two does) and I have to put them back in the case and reconnect to the device. This happens about 25% of the time and a second time usually does the trick.

title: Don’t compare to Sudio
text:
I bought the pink and purple ones and they are SUPER cute…but that’s literally the only thing they have going for them. I’ve heard good things about Beats, and after my beloved Sudio earbuds crapped out (they lasted a few years of literally daily use though) in the middle of a work day, I ordered these on a whim immediately. I’m a dog groomer and it is LOUD in the shop so I can’t live without noise canceling earbuds.

Well, color me disappointed. They cost the same price as the cheapest pair of Sudio earbuds and do not hold a candle to them. I feel like you’re paying for the branding because these were really expensive trash. Before Apple did away with their headphone jacks I used SkullCandy and those old $20 earbuds have way better sound quality than these $100 ones. The quality wasn’t poor, just disappointing for the price. But the noise cancellation? Terrible. Sudio ANC cuts out the obnoxious barking and loud force dryer so that I can listen to audiobooks while I work. With these, even with it turned on I had to crank the volume up so high it was distorted and painful to be able to hear the words over my dryer. They’re not comfortable, either. If I pushed them farther in they sorta cut out the sound but it hurt my eardrums.

Yet another downside? They’re shaped super awkward. Hard to get in and out of the case, hard to put in your ear (I dropped them about 8 times in the first hour), and the button is terribly placed because every time I went to adjust it in my ear I would bump the button and stop my book/music. Super annoying.

Don’t buy. Get Sudio instead, I promise you won’t regret it.

title: Excellent Battery Life and Great for physical activity
text: Sound quality of the Beats Pro Wireless Headphones is better than their previous generation, but not as good as the over the ear Beats Studio3 or the Sennheiser HD series over the ear headphones.  The design is great for working out, going on runs, or other physical activities without worry about the ear phones falling out/off of your ear.  When I go running with my partner, my Beat Pro wireless headphones stay in my ear during the whole run and my partners' Apple Airpods tend to fall out at least once.  If wind is significant during outdoor runs, it does overwhelm the noise cancellation feature where you can hear the wind noise.  Overall, sound quality is good, battery life is good, charging time is very good, noise cancellation is pretty good, mic is great for phone calls, easy to pair with iPhones, and build quality is excellent.  Only issue I've had with the headphones is that you need to ensure that the headphones make good contact with the recharging case otherwise the headphones may not recharge properly leaving you with only one head phone working during your workout.

title: Good for teaching yoga/ fitness classes but hurt my ears and not great sound quality
text:
Pros: I chose these earphones after doing a ton of research for the best wireless earphones for teaching yoga online. I wanted something that would stay in my ears even while upside down or while moving through power flows, and that I wouldn't have to stress about. I wanted to be able to be heard clearly and hear clearly, without having a mic piece that could get in the way while on my belly in floor poses. These absolutely met those requirements, and the choice of multiple sizes for the earbud, along with the ear hook, ensured they stayed in my ears.

I also loved how when I took one earphone off and put it down, my macbook air paused the video I was playing until I put it back in. The Apple compatibility is amazing. They were so easy to connect to my iPhone. When I said "hey Siri," I got this very lifelike "Hmmmm?" in a sexy female voice that my iphone has never done before, and it kind of creeped me out. But she immediately got my commands to play spotify and skip to the next track.

Cons: But I also wanted versatile earphones that I could also use to do work calls, and listen to music or podcasts while doing housework. I found the hook on the earbud really hurt my ear after just one hour of use. I wore them for 3 hours yesterday, and my ears are still a bit sore a day later! I don't think I have weirdly shaped ears or anything. I was also quite disappointed with the sound quality, to my surprise, after reading so many positive reviews. It's not very rich, and the bass is minimal. I switched to my apple airpods to compare the sound and it was a world of difference.

Comparison to other options: I didn't choose earbuds that don't have a hook or wire because those easily fall out of my ears when doing yoga or fitness workouts online. I also tried a friend's jaybird earbuds that have a wire connecting them, but are bluetooth. Those actually had way better sound quality than these Beats earphones and are 1/10th the price. But they jaybirds also fell out of my ears. Thankfully the wire meant I could find them easily mid-teaching my class and pop them back in, but it did distract me. I even tried bobby pinning the wire to my pony tail, but the wire fell off and stayed around my neck.

I am returning these and getting the Bose wireless noise-cancelling earbuds instead. They have a wire connecting them and no ear hook, but the reviews say they stay better in your ears.

title: OVERPRICED.  Issues all around with sound quality, charging, weak volume and reliability.
text:
LOOK ELSEWHERE. This is a competitive market and these are nowhere near worth their price. I have several pairs of these, and several similar earbuds from other brands. Of all the brands I have, I regret buying these and have no regrets with all but one of the other brands I've bought. These are overpriced, they are not in the same league sound wise as AirPods, not close. They don't sound as good, charge as well and aren't as reliable. Here are the issues I have experienced --

Below average sound quality -- I have $25 earbuds that sound much better. I have $35 ear buds that sound much better, and all but one of the other pairs of earbuds I have sounds better than these PowerBeats Pros. Not by a little either but by a lot. Compared to similarly priced Apple Air Pods and Air Pods Pro, which I also have, Apple's sound is much, much better. But you'd think these buds could beat out budget competitors on sound quality. Sadly they don't.

Fit/Stay On -- Apple's issue is they don't like to stay on during vigorous exercise, which is why I bought these in the first place. These do a good job, mostly, of staying on during exercise.

Volume - Maybe the company nerfed the volume to avoid complaints and lawsuits, but the result is noticeably lower volume levels than any other earbud I have, including Jabra, Apple, and a few others as well. You cannot crank these up, the volume is noticeably muted compared to other brands. Disappointing and again, performance well below the price point.

Charging -- A bit of a crapshoot to get these to charge reliably. Charging by the case is glitchy and finicky. You may close the case and the tiny contacts are ever so slightly out of position. You pull these out of the case the next day and OOPS, you have to pull another brand out (one that actually will charge reliably) because these still need to be charged. This happens frequently. The charging overall is not well thought out. The product cost is high, and they seem to think the case is a bonus. It is not. More basic, charging by cable would've been better. The case has a built-in storage battery, hooray, but so what if it won't charge reliably when you want it to.

Reliability -- Poor. One of the single buds I had stopped working completely. I was left with sound from one side only. No thanks. At this price point, should one side completely stop working after 6 months? No.

With so many brands and models to choose from in this competitive space, keep walking. Do a side by side on sound quality and volume issues and you won't buy these. Couple it with the charging and reliability issues, moves the needle way past NO in my book. I'm sorry I bought several pairs of these, I won't repeat the mistake.

title: Good earbuds, bad charging case
text:
Overall, these are good earbuds. Build quality, comfort, volume, and sound quality are all great. I primarily use these for biking and for office use, where the fit and battery life make it a great option. I primarily use them on an Android phone and there is no compatibility issues, the app is able to show battery life and control everything. Other than the occasional one-bud pairing requiring re-inserting and removing the other bud from the case, they work without a hitch.

The main thing holding these earbuds back are the case. Issues include:

* Too bulky to comfortably carry in your pocket. This is largely a consequence of the size and battery life, but keep this in mind compared to regular buds (e.g. pixel or airpods), you can't just slip these in your pocket and forget about it. This encourages leaving the case behind and leaving them around the house, which is risky.
* Not water resistant. This further adds to the incentive to leave it behind.
* Only supports proprietary Apple charging solutions. No USB-C, no Qi wireless charging. If you don't own an iPhone, even if you own a MacBook, you'll need dedicated chargers for this case just to use these earbuds.
* Does not lock earbuds in place when closed and doesn't provide clear feedback if only one is actually charging. You need to physically ensure each earbud is properly magnetically engaged before closing or risk having a dead earbud at worst, or having your phone continue playing music into your charging case at best.
* Does not have any indicator to see battery level of itself or the earbuds. It's so massive yet a simple multi-dot LED apparently is too much to expect and instead all you get is a single dot LED with limited information.
* Does not have any "find-me" functionality built into it.

At the end of the day, the earbuds are the main product, and they're good enough to make up for the case for me. But the case itself would get 2 stars from me.

title: Great Battery life, decent noise cancelation.
text:
The case reminds me of an altered pixelbuds case. It's a great case to reference for the design and materials used. This case opens from the side however, and the buds stay securely inside while the case is at the bottom of a backpack. It's great that they will stay in place even if they aren't in a pocket.
The case is a tad large for most Pants pockets but it will fit if it's necessary, except for in the smallest of pockets.
The buds are small and designed so that getting a good fit shouldn't be difficult for many, even if you need to use 3rd party tips.
The noise canceling is not on the level of the Airpods pro, but can effectively reduce the level of environmental sound you hear around you, especially with lower rumbling noises like those on a plane or train.
The Studio Buds are capable of android fast pair, available on many Android phones, but they curiously lack an H1 or even the previous generation W1 chip found in Airpods and other Beats products.
That said, pairing the beats is not at all difficult.
The Beats Studio Buds support the AAC Codec, but not APTX for android phones.
While I got a very low volume level when pairing the Studio Buds to my LG V60, the sound was nicely balanced. Bass was quick and linear, with matching mids and complementary treble. it is a clean all around sound that many users would enjoy. While I wanted more than the 15% volume I was getting from these, the sound was consistent and enjoyable. it didn't matter if absolute volume on the phone was enabled or disabled, nothing would raise the volume level. Not even a factory reset of the buds themselves.
When pairing to my iPhone 11 Pro Max, by default, the Studio buds were far to loud for anyone to safely listen. The noise level rivaled standing in front of a giant Speaker at a concert.
Once I'd recovered and adjusted the volume, to my surprise, even at the lower volume levels, the sound signature I enjoyed from the V60 was non existent on the 11 Pro Max.
The mids were shouty, treble was uneven and veiled, and the entire bass region was sloppy and lacked good texture. It was like listening to a poorly tuned passive sub woofer, though all bass notes were audible and the level didn't drop off for any key changes.
In both cases the eq was set to flat.
This really surprised me. Not because Beats is owned by Apple, but generally speaking, apple implements the AAC Bluetooth Codec very well, and it often brings out the best from headphones that use it. AAC is usually not as well implemented on Android devices, but APTX usually provides a better sound on Android.
Wireless charging, great design, well built and decent noise cancelation are all positives for the Beats studio Buds, but the vastly different sounds I heard from an Android vs iPhone, not to mention the stubbornly low volume level I got from android, make it hard to recommend these.

title: Excellent value and great noise canceling/sound
text:
[[VIDEOID:affa7daba5b949379437125cb0fd1a03]] First of all I have 3 TWS. AirPods Pro, Sony Wf-1000xm4 and now these.

Comfort
These are probably the most comfortable. They are light and have a small profile. They seem to stay in despite much movement.

Case
These are probably the biggest. It’s not by much but definitely bigger. Also the case is very slippery.

Noise Canceling
I was pleasantly surprised. I read and saw online reviews saying the AirPods Pro were better but I have to disagree. I could never get a good seal with the AirPods Pro. With the beats I get a good seal and the noise canceling was considerably better in my opinion. This will depend on your ears. The Sony’s are definitely the best at noise canceling, but not by a huge leap.

Transparency mode
These are third place for that. It’s not very clear. It sounds somewhat muffled. The AirPods Pro are definitely the best and more natural.

Sound
These sound really good. I would say it kinda of sound like the AirPods Pro but with more bass, mids and a little narrower. It still has a nice clean sound. It doesn’t feel too warm, you still get some nice higher frequencies. The Sony’s sound the best IMO.

Connectivity/App
These connect very easily. I tested them with Android and Apple. Unfortunately if your in the Apple ecosystem you don’t have the H1 chip. That means no iCloud pairing or Spatial audio for Movies. The app is pretty barebones on Android.

Battery life
Pretty good, probably in the middle. More than AirPods pro but less than Sony.

Overall I think these are an excellent value and fully recommend them if you don’t need the H1 chip for the Apple ecosystem. Perfect for Android users.

title: Generally poor, even compared to 1st gen airpods
text:
Updated: For the first few weeks I thought I'd gotten a bad pair. After 3 months of using them, multiple frustrating experiences with Apple support and several weeks waiting for them to be repaired, It seems clear that these just aren't very good.

Sound quality: it's not bad, it's probably the best thing about the PowerBeats Pro headphones. It's about the same as airpods but maybe a little heavier in the bass and you get better passive noise cancelling with the rubber tips.

Connectivity: TERRIBLE. Not a day goes by that they don't disconnect, desync (where one side gets ahead of the other and plays everything just a little bit sooner), or have one side disconnect while the other continues. Sometimes pressing pause and play again fixes it. Sometimes I have to put them back in the case and close it and open it and try that 3 or 4 times to get them both connected. Sometimes I have to completely unpair them from the device and re-pair them. Sometimes I have to do a factory reset to get things working. That's just daily life with these things and I've resigned myself to carrying the case everywhere so that I can go through all the standard troubleshooting, which is a shame because the case is huge. iOS gets the advantage with these but still doesn't work reliably. Macos seems to be pretty mediocre and usually that's where I have issues first with them. Android works just about as well as iOS, minus the on-screen battery life notices.I've given up on using them with Windows because they just disconnect from anything else I try to connect and reconnect with the Windows machine.

True-Wireless features: Taking them out of your ears does pause music, but not reliably. Sometimes it pauses but then plays again immediately, or if you take one out it pauses but then plays and refuses to respond to pressing the pause button. It does depend on if you cover the little sensor that it uses to determine if they're in your ears but that is incredibly finicky. The charging case is huge, which gets good battery life but it's not going into a pocket, that's for sure. And the extra battery life, well...

Battery life: great in theory, terrible in practice. It would be great if the headphones would charge in the case reliably. It is a regular occurrence that I take them out of the case only to find that not only has one not charged, it remained connected to my phone while in the case, completely draining whatever charge it had. The contacts in the case just don't make contact very well. I've gotten to be very conscientious of pressing them in and double checking that they've made contact with the charging nodes in the case but they must flop around in the case too much to maintain contact. I may have to tape cotton to the interior lid or something to use up the empty space.

Bottom line:
I wanted "true-wireless" headphones to go over my ears securely when working out. I got hosed. For $250 these are more hassle, less reliable and have only marginally better sound quality than my old $70 pair of Plantronic Backbeat Fit bluetooth headphones. The true-wireless doesn't really work, the things won't charge reliably and the connectivity is atrocious. If you want a good pair of headphones for working out, these are probably the worst option and cost over 3x more than more reliable headphones for "true-wireless" features that don't really work.

title: Great design and excellent sound. Not much to complain about.
text:
This is my review after using them for a couple of weeks. Background information: I’ve used the Jabra 65T, Jaybird X3, Havit G1. I’ve also reviewed headphones (both wireless and wired) for Sony, Sennheiser, AKG and Beyerdynamic, among others.

- Sound is great, better than Airpods and any of the wireless earbuds named above. I'm sure the earbud design plays a big part, but it's not only that. I tested the Airpods 2 + silicone earbuds with these and sound is still noticeably better.
- They are **not** as bass biased as previous generations. actually, when compared with the Sony WH1000X3 (I know, it's not an apples to apples comparison since the Sony are wireless headphones), I think the Sony headphones are way more bass-heavy than the Powerbeats Pro (I wear the Sony headphones on a custom profile that brings down the bass a little).
- They have bass super powers, but they are just summoned as needed and do not overpower other parts of the spectrum. For example _Seven Nation Army_ by the White Stripes sounds beautiful (Mids and Highs are still excellent), heavy bass as intended. However, Jazz and Rock (e.g. Foo Fighters) sound excellent too, Mids and Highs *are NOT overshadowed* IMO (as opposed to what has been indicated on some online reviews).
- They don't feel like other earbuds because they seem to allow some outside sound in (it doesn't have to do with earbud seal, I think it's by design, as there are some small openings on the back). That helps improve their sound-stage. Still, I don't need to crank up the volume on noisy environments (like I need to with the Airpods 2).
- Make sure you try several of the included flexible tips to find the ones that provide the best ear canal seal. I found out that on the Powerbeats Pro, the larger tips provided the best fit for my ears, which is strange as I use medium-sized tips with other earbuds.
- Comfort is excellent, I’ve used them for hours without any ear fatigue.
- As expected, integration with the Apple ecosystem is amazing, just like with the AirPods.

Still, quality wired earbuds might sound better... but not by much.

title: Better than AirPods in some ways. Depends what you are looking for in a headphone
text:
I own first gen AirPods since launch. Love them. Use them everyday. ALWAYS scared one will fall out of my ear when I least expect it or that I will lose them in the small case. I've been using the Powerbeats Pro and the AirPods back and forth for a few weeks now. What I can say is that they are great for different things.

Powerbeats Pro > AirPods in these ways:
-actual button control opposed to "tap" functionality that never worked for me when I wanted it to. I use to NEVER use the touch controls on my AirPods because I could never get it to work right. I would activate it ALL THE TIME by accident, though... ended up turning the settings to OFF. The button is much nicer to use in practice.
-I never feel like they are going to fall out. This is perhaps the biggest plus for most people.
-Battery life is pretty great.

Airpods>Powerbeats in these ways:
-So light that I often forgot they were in my ears. Powerbeats Pro will weigh on you after a while.
-Can actually hold a conversation with someone while I have one in. Even with no sound actually going on, having a PowerBeat Pro in my ear significantly impacted the quality of conversation I could have with someone even standing right in front of me. Annoying to have to take them off to talk to someone. With AirPods I would just pause my music and chat when necessary.

I use them in different ways. When I am on the train for my morning commute, I use the Powerbeats Pro because I don't want to hear anybody. When I am in the office listening to podcasts while I work at my desk I will usually stick in a single Airpod because it is slightly less obvious than the giant black thing hanging over my ear and I can also hear people around me better with it in. I love mowing the lawn with the Powerbeats Pro because I am not as concerned with sweat, and the noise blocking is a boon. Having both is great, but obviously not everyone can afford $450 in wireless headphone options. Look at your use case scenario and make your decision based on that! They are both great, you just have to decide which ones will be greater for you!

I consistently experienced intermittent connectivity issues with my music cutting out, and speeding up to catch up to its original spot . This was the weirdest thing I have ever experienced with a pair of wireless headphones. I originally thought maybe my sd card is acting up, so I switched to using one of my music subscription music accounts via wifi and got the same issues. I was like (insert expletive). It got so bad that I left the gym and went home to troubleshoot the issue. Got home and they worked fine. I don't know if it was due to all the metal causing interference in the gym or the H1 chip going nuts due to being around a bunch or iphones or what. All I knew was that the main reason I purchased these was for gym use and I couldn't keep a consistent connection without my listening experience being interrupted repeatedly due to my music dropping out. title: Decent sound, but not worth $200
text: I have a few issues with these headphones.  They sound decent, though bass heavy, which is to be expected from the Beats signature sound.  As a result, the treble is a bit muddled and the mids somewhat exaggerated , sounding woolly.  It's acceptable to me because I use them for mainly working out.  The rubber ear piece design works well for most ear shapes, though for me, the left one is not as snug.  Just keep that in mind.  I don't run but I do bike and lift weights, therefore I'm not sure how secure they would be jump roping or sprinting.  They are secure for my low impact activities.  The one problem is that you have to make sure the phones are securely attached to their recharging receptacles which are these little pins.  It's hard to tell because there's no solid "click".  As a result, there are many times when the one side may not be charged at all, muted.  Unfortunately , there is no left/right light indicator to show full charge for both, although bringing my iPhone close shows the percentage.  All in all, these are as good as it gets for wireless sport headphones.  I think a fairer price would be $120 or so but knowing Apple has tinkered with the design and ownership of Beats, it's not a surprise.  Only time will tell how long they and the charger will last

title: Strange audio processing - right side louder than the left
text:
At first, these seemed great. Though as time went on, I noticed that the right ear was louder/more dynamic then the left ear.

I tried all kinds of different troubleshooting steps (hard reset, different devices etc) but it was the same. If I manually adjust the balance from 100% right to 100% left, it sounds identical to me. So something with the way this device processes audio is off. If you listen to any podcasts, it feels like the person speaking is constantly on your front right.

The best way I can describe it is if you have a 5.1 system, the F/R & Center are in the right ear, then the back surround L/R are in the left ear. It seemed like this happened after I got a firmware update notification, but not sure if that was a coincidence.

It's honestly very annoying/distracting when working out. I keep adjusting my left ear thinking it's off centered and the soundstage is projected more on the right. So it's disorienting.

I think I may return them for this reason, but I want to have something on or in my ear and forget about it to focus on my workout.
