title: Excellent for Gym Use with Android phone
text:
I've been looking for a good pair of workout wireless headphones to replace my cheap Chinese-made wireless ones with cord connecting them. I knew in advance that I would not have the same ease of use with my Galaxy s10+ that others have with an iPhone and the PBP so no surprise. It took me a few minutes to figure out how to pair them since I had already paired them to an iPad but they show up now with no issue.

I've worn them to ride a stationery bike at the gym several times. No issue at all with them falling out of my ears -- which has been an issue with my usual Bluetooth earpiece from Plantronics. Initially, I kept the default tips and found that the volume was too low - likely because I didn't have a good seal. Today I switched to the largest tips and the sound was great - loud but not overly bassy. I also found that I have not had the dropouts from Amazon Music and Pandora that I previously had with my cheap Chinese headphones. Hopefully that is due to the higher quality components here.

The only wish that I have is that they would easily list the battery meter on Android as it does an iPhone. That would be helpful for me.

Update: They have died on my constantly despite being fully charged with latest firmware. It's a real shame since they fit well and the sound is good. Die in the middle of phone calls such that I have to pull it out of my ear and use the other one. Epic fail.

title: Not impressed. Overpriced! Paying for the name.
text: I'll start by saying I've tested numerous TWS earbuds dating back to the first ones to be commercially available (Earin) including the famous brand names, not so famous brands, and the no name brands available for $50 and under.  I'm by no means an expert but I generally look for good sound, fit, durability, connection, battery life, charging case, and of course price.  I recognize that big brand names are often more expensive (sometimes significantly) since they are genuinely higher quality products backed by quality companies with a loyal brand following. Customers tend to trust that products by Beats or Apple will be superior to whatever else is out there, but I'm sorry to say that hasn't been the case with TWS buds.  In my opinion AirPods are built well, stay connected, and have great battery life. And of course are backed by a company with solid product support.  The Powerbeats match up pretty well in these areas.  As far as comfort, I would say these are far more comfortable and practical than Airpods. So now to what arguably is most important... the sound quality.  Sorry to say that just like Airpods, these are average at best.  I'm not impressed at all. The sound quality just isn't good enough for what you're paying considering I have multiple sub $50 TWS buds that sound superior, with more volume, cleaner and punchier bass, and better distribution between highs, mids, and lows. So if you're looking for a well known and respected brand that effectively suits its purpose and you're less concerned about the sound quality, then these will certainly do the trick.  But if you're looking for buds that make you say wow when you first hear them, then you may need to look elsewhere.  Since sound quality perception has a lot to do with the fit of the buds, I would recommend testing a variety of buds and their ear tip options to determine which fit and sound the best in addition to meeting whatever other requirements you have based on how and where you intend to use them.  What works for some won't necessarily work well for others.  That being said, I was unable to get these to sound "good" enough to justify the price tag.

title: Comparison of my top 3 favorite
text:
Comparison of my top three favorites:

Bose SoundSport free have Bluetooth 4.2, so there’s video lag, making then unsuitable for live listening. For music, they have good bass compared to AirPods, but the mid and hi frequencies tend to be slightly muffled in comparison to the other two. And they cannot be used individually. Fit is great. Calls are mono but quality is decent. Overall, they rank third.

Apple AirPods PRO (2019) have Bluetooth 5.0 so they are very suitable for live listening. For music, they have very crisp mid and hi frequencies compared to Bose, but ever so slightly less bass than PowerBeats and Bose, but overall they appear the most natural sounding. They can be used individually. Fit is great with silicone tips. Call quality is great. They rank second, from the sound quality standpoint but they’re the winner if active Noise Cancellation and Transparency mode matter to you equally.

PowerBeats Pro have Bluetooth 5.0 so they are very suitable for live listening. For music, they have just as crisp mid and hi frequencies compared to AirPods, and the most punchy and tight bass response of the three — and not in the usual negative way that older Beats products are often described as. They can be used individually and the fit is great with extra security with the hooks although violent shaking of my head sometimes brings the right one out but that’s just my ears and for most people they’ll fit very securely. Call quality is great. They are the winner from the sound quality standpoint. And they rank second if you value active noise cancellation and Transparency modes matter to you.

If you’re wondering where Jabra 65T series sits, they are between rank 3 and rank 2 from a sound quality standpoint and on par with 1 for call quality.

title: Work well with an Android phone but, to use them to their fullest, they need an iPhone
text: I bought these from the Amazon Warehouse and was pleased with the wide variety of options it offered.  I had previously bought a pair of Jabra waterproof earbuds for my work iPhone and intended to use these PowerBeats earbuds for my personal Android.  However, after learning just how much more functionality the PowerBeats have when paired with an iPhone instead of an Android, I had to swap them around.  It quickly became clear that, while they functioned with an Android, they became fully integrated only with the iPhone.  One simple but critical difference that made me swap them was the fact the Android required both earbuds to be used ... whereas the iPhone just needed one.  I could definitely see the 2-earbud requirement making sense if I was at home and just using them to listen to music or watch videos.  But, for talking on the phone ... or using them in an area where I didn't want fully noise cancelation ... having just the single earbud was what I needed.  While the over-the-ear clip design still takes work to get into place, once situated, I've been happy with how firmly it remains in place so that I can still easily move around and work while talking.

You have to have the bulky case in order to repair, so I went back inside and went through several iterations of pairing and resetting. The audio would play through the music app, but any attempt to start a workout on the watch would immediately cause the sound to cut out. Based on reviews here and on the apple forums, sound and connectivity issues seem to be fairly common with these. I ended up sending these back.

However I do need the volume function to work while buds are in my ears. Sometimes it works, but most of the time it just powers off and then back on again when using the function to increase or decrease volume. With a fully charged case the battery life is great!

*** 7/5/22 UPDATE TO THE ABOVE
Upon the above review seller reached out to me and deemed the earbuds damaged - offering to replace them with my choice of the T6 or T9. I chose the T6 as they were basically an upgrade from the A1. I'm happy to report that the T6 is a champion ear bud set, and like the A1 the battery life using the charging case is top of the line giving upward to 30 hours of battery life. MOST EXCELLENT CUSTOMER SERVICE! Because of this I'm changing my rating to 5 stars!

Thank you Amy for making sure my TOZO experience came to a happy ending.

title: Wonderful Upgrade to PowerBeats3
text:
So far these little guys are a great upgrade from the PB3.

Likes:
- great sound quality
- fits ear nicely; I have small ears and all too often wireless earbuds fall out. These do not - they secure nicely and there is no discomfort
- pause / skip button on both ears
- volume button on both ears
- can still hear road noises around me (I use these for running so I don't want complete noise cancellation)

Dislikes:
- none yet

Verdict is still out on:
- battery life. Right now its great because they are new. I get a full charge and they will last quite a few longer runs w/ active use (volume / song skip use).
- case is nice. It is sleek and I like the way the contacts are visible and can be cleaned (unlike Apple EarPods), but I feel as if it will open up in my gym bag if I don't buy an aftermarket case to prevent accidental opening. I haven't traveled with them yet, so I don't know if this will be a problem
- longevity. So, I have been an avid user of Powerbeats for running. I love how they have the bendable pieces that secure around the back of the ear...that is amazing for stay-put power....but, I will be darned if my Powerbeats were not breaking at least once every 9-12 months. It was insane. I had, literally, 4 pairs of PB3 - and my last pair I had the longest w/o issue = 2yrs. I would think for $$$ one would get a quality pair of earbuds that wouldn't need replacing every year (which ended up being the average time for my earbuds). I am an avid runner, but I take care of my items - therefore, it is hard to believe an item marketed for workouts/runs won't hold up for longer than 1yr. So, I am cautiously optimistic that these new headphones will provide me yearS of enjoyment...but we will see in 6-9months.

title: High quality earphones... NOT!!!
text: I had posted a review of these headphones when I had first purchased them praising the quality of the headphones.  However I have had a change of mind regarding them since I am now having issues with the left earbud charge dying quicker than the right one.  I have tried forgetting/re-pairing the earbuds, and letting the charge run down to 0 percent.  Neither solution works for me unfortunately.  I go for long walks and cardio in the gym.  There is nothing more annoying then the left earbud dying on my favorite song/album and I do not have the charging case with me to quick charge the earbud that mysteriously lost it's charge while the right one is just fine.  Yes I can carry the case with me and charge the depleted earbud and carry on (which I have tried & no... charge still dies again shortly afterwards smh), but it is cumbersome when I am out for about 2 to 4 hours and I do not want to carry that bulky charging case on my person.  I tried searching online for possible solutions and I see that there are an overwhelming number of people with the exact same issue - the left earbud losing charge much sooner than the right one.  It is a defect in the product that should have been addressed by Apple.  I can no longer recommend these earbuds as they are not reliable.  For anyone looking to pick up a pair of earbuds with around the ear hooks for those who are active, look elsewhere.  You will be pleased with them at first, but eventually you will run into this very same issue.  I wish that I knew this before purchasing them before...

text:
This is actually the second Tozo Bluetooth earbuds I ordered recently. The other was the T6. I HIGHLY recommend spending the few extra dollars and get the T6 instead of this. Like BAD moldy not just "off". The next closest sizes (at least it came with 5 extra sets of small to large sized) have a weird chemical smell.

And finally the sound quality is about equal to a cheap set of wired earbuds. The T6 had better bass response. I will keep this handy for those times I cannot find my better pair. In fact I plan on ordering another T6 shortly so I can leave one set at work. Also unlike the T6 it uses the really old artificial voice for "power on, power off, etc" you get with the cheapest Aliexpress bluetooth devices. That's just annoying.

title: Glitches galore
text: These were the only in-ear earphones compatible with Android that actually fit me. I'll give the product credit for having a very stable fit that doesn't fall out or dislodge easily. But the audio problems make it almost useless. Most of them happen when I want to listen only with one earbud: volume will fluctuate dramatically, audio will skip or drop, and often it will just disconnect entirely. It works much better with both earphones on, but I live in an unsafe area and need to stay aware of my surroundings. I would also say the audio quality is not good for music, especially classical, but that is pretty typical. I wish there was a way to turn these off without placing them in the charging bay/case so that they don't drain battery while I'm not using them. Furthermore, there's no way to pair these with a new device without the case. In other words you need to carry around the case with you if you want full functionality, and it is kind of bulky so it won't fit in your pocket. The fast-forward and rewind buttons on each earpiece are difficult to press while you're walking. Overall I cannot recommend these earphones because of the number of audio problems and awkward functions.

title: I am picky about anything sound, and I love these!!
text:
I was born a musician. So anything having to do with sounds, I tend to be BEYOND picky about. I will scrutinize an item that omits sound considerably more than I would anything else because my highly trained ear is very sensitive to sound.

That being said, these ear buds aren't perfect. In fact, they're a little bit snuffled sounding, like there's a blanket sitting over a mic during a recording session. But it's a pretty thin blanket, so most of you won't hear it. Plus, there's the added benefit of being able to fix the sound in the equator function of the app you're using to listen to anything, more than likely. So, even if you do hear it, most of you will be able to get past it with little to no effort with that function. I certainly was able to get it pretty close to it that way; though, sadly, I would need a much more intensified equator to fiddle with to get past that muffled sound altogether.

While I'm sure I could find one fairly easily, it's such a minor issue at this point that I can't justify to myself wasting the time to go that far now. In other words, unless you have an ear as intensely tuned to sound and mine is, you won't notice it at all to begin with, and if you do (probably only because I brought it up to begin with), you'll be able to easily work it out with your app's sound equator function. So, it won't be an issue at all for you. Even I've been able to work out that little kink almost completely. At this point, if I weren't listening specifically for it, I doubt I'd be able to notice it anymore at all, myself.

So, with that issue eradicated, I haven't yet found any other issues with this set of ear buds, and I am VERY pleased with my purchase. I doubt I'll be looking to replace these any time in the next few years, unless they come up missing like my last set did. Yay!!

title: Battery level and recharging
text:
Apple/Beats cheaped out in two significant areas on these ear buds.

1. First, there's only a single LED on the front of the case. The inside of the case is designed in such a way that you can place an ear bud in the case for recharging but it won't make contact or, for some other reason, won't recharge. Because of the single LED, you can only tell that something (one or both) is recharging. You can't tell for sure that *both* are recharging. Usually in 1 out of 3 runs I go out to find that one of the sides is non-functional. Other times, they seem to get in a mode where they're micro-seconds out of sync so it sounds like reverb.

2. Second, if you're not using these with an iPhone, you can't look at your Bluetooth devices and see the battery level (like with every other modern Bluetooth device on a modern Android phone). This is absurd cost cutting (since it's a limitation only in firmware in the ear buds themselves). This should be fixed with a firmware update.

Overall, sound quality is good (though to be accurate, I only listen to podcasts, not music). There are times when you put the ear buds in your ears and because of the first issue above, you're only listening to one side. Just bad design which is not typical for Apple traditionally.

They require a Lightning connector to recharge but if you're in an Open household (that is, not using Apple products), the supplied cable may be the only lightning connector you have.

Someone up in the Questions asked about its noise cancelling feature because they were concerned if they were out running whether they'd be able to hear what's going on around them. I have small ear canals and use the smallest silicon tips and these earbuds have NEVER been noise cancelling. Most of the time, the cars/trucks going by are louder than what I'm listening too. If they're noise cancelling, I've never experienced it. I am more used to earbuds that come with an app that allows you to configure features on the device; you *may* be able to do this on an iPhone but not on any other device - a shame.

title: Good product, good price
text: These are simply wireless earbuds. They function just as well as every other brand or better, and though I haven't used other brands, this has served me well. It connects easily and it even connects automatically to my phone now, although I honestly don't know how this happens and there aren't any settings for it to connect automatically. I use them every day at work and I've found that the earbuds can last continuously without charge for about 4 hours, so if you use them one at a time and switch them out regularly, they will last an entire day. The noise cancellation is very good, although it only really works if something is being played in the earbuds, but white noise works just as well as heavy metal, so it should work fine no matter who you are. Be careful when using both earbuds however, since you literally can't hear outside sounds if you have both earbuds in and noise cancelling, so if someone is trying to get your attention, you probably won't notice unless you can see them. If you have noise transparency on and both earbuds, then you can only understand outside language on low volume, but can hear more than with noise cancelling. Overall, noise cancelling and noise transparency aren't incredibly distinct, and it will mostly depend on how many earbuds you're wearing and how loud your audio is. Most of the time, only wearing one earbud is better because you can still interact with people and the battery lasts longer, but you can get better sound quality with two earbuds. You can still get audio if the source of the audio is across the room, in another room, or in a pocket, but if there are too many or too thick obstructions, they won't work. If you drop them, they will scratch, but almost definitely won't have their performance affected. Overall, the earbuds work great and they're worth it to get.

title: AirPods Pro Replacement (Missing a Few Features, But Still Worth It)
text:
So, my wife bought me Apple AirPods Pro for Fathers Day this year, and I was so excited. They sounded great, the spatial audio on videos was incredible, and the noise cancellation was top notch.

The problem was, I couldn’t wear them longer than 10 minutes…They hurt. They fell out of my ears. I tried every tip. I even bought replacement foam tips because I wanted them to work. I finally came to the realization that I had to return them and I was bummed.

By chance, I stumbled across these Beats Studio Buds. Apple owned them. Beats has a good reputation. I was willing to try.

I’ve had these for a few weeks now, and I feel pretty confident in my thoughts.

It took some time to find the right “fit”. At first I just popped them in my ears and they felt nice. After a few days, they started to hurt. I tried another tip. And another tip. I was scared I was going to have to return them too. The secret is, you have to give these a slight “turn” (it’s even pictured in the packaging). Once I perfected the slight turn, I’ve been nothing but happy. They stay in when I exercise. They stay in at work. I’m happy.

The noise cancellation/transparency mode are somewhat better on AirPods Pro, but what good is that if I can’t use them. I can use these.

If your ears aren’t made for Apple AirPods Pro, definitely give these a try. They are still an Apple product and work perfectly with IOS. Some features are better on AirPods Pro, but the Beats Studio Buds simply work. I am a happy customer.

title: I am conflicted ....
text:
I originally bought these for my youngest child. I have offered to buy her higher priced earbuds before, but she has always said "No" because she was afraid she would lose them. So she gets wired ones instead. And she is very particular about how they fit in her ears. I saw that these were on-sale & were recommended by a YouTube presenter I follow, so I thought I would give them a try. She put them in her ears & immediately said "NOPE !" because she didn't like the way they felt in her ears. So I decided I would give them a try ...

Now, I have NEVER been a fan of earbuds either. Mostly because I don't like having anything IN my ear & have preferred on or over the ear headphones instead. But it had been getting to be an issue carrying my Koss UR-40's with me to work. So I was hoping these would be a suitable replacement.

Early observations ... they are not UNCOMFORTABLE. I did change the ear tips out for a slightly looser fit. But I am still getting used to how MY voice sounds when I have them in (I am using them for conference calls over my MacBook.) The sound for a teleconference is perfectly fine. There is a definite lack of bass, but that is okay for what I need. One thing I am noticing is a slight lag in getting the audio to my ears. Not sure if that is the earbuds fault, or my Mac Book. Will give them a longer tryout before I make my final judgement.

On the plus side the RANGE of the BlueTooth on these is really good. Not that this would be an issue in the office, but at home it's nice to follow a conversation if I need to step away.

I will say this, for the price these are a pretty good value. The sound quality isn't the best, but at this price you can't expect THAT much. And they were a breeze to pair which was always the problem I had with other "cheap" wireless buds.

Bottom Line, I won't make my final judgement on keeping these until AFTER I use them in the office a few times. If they do okay there, I will keep them. If not, back they go. Either way I will update this review accordingly.

UPDATE: They are going back. I was dealing with having things in my ears, and they were performing just fine - actually BETTER than they did when I tested them at home. But I hit a deal breaker. I used them from 8:00 AM until 11:30 AM, charged them from 11:30-12:30, and started using them again .... and I got a "Battery Low" message at 3:15 PM. I need them to last until 5:00 PM or at least CLOSE to that. If I have to use wired headphones, I might as well use my "Good" ones.

title: Nice alternative to Apple AirPods Pro
text:
Dear Beats,

I bought this headset for my wife in black. It was easy to pair and you can use either the left or the right earbud by itself which is nice because when one earbuds runs out of battery you can use the other one for a few hours. The case takes a lightening adapter and charges fully regardless of what kind of power brick you’re using. For the price these are a good deal. Pairing was as easy as open the lid next to your iPhone and then follow the on screen steps. Charges fully in about a couple of hours and will last you 20+ hrs with the case. The only thing I wished it had was qi wireless charging ability otherwise, these are nice for the price.

Almost a month later… I am using these headsets for my M1 MBA and my iPhone 13Pro. One nice thing about this is that you can switch devices within a matter of seconds and a push of a button either on your iPhone or your MacBook. Second nice thing is that you can use the headset individually. One earbud could be in your ear and the other one in the case. It doesn’t matter which on you use first but I’ve been using the right one, depleting it, and then put it back into the case to charge when I’m not using it and switch to the left one. The case holds a good amount of charge. With average use, the case can charge the earbuds fully about twice before everything needs to be charged. Tapping on the earbuds pauses whatever you’re listening to or watching. The right bud is for increasing volume and the left bud is to decrease volume. You have to push and hold down for the volume to change. It charges via usb c which is nice. It also sound pretty good when just using it for talking. Overall, I am happy with the headsets.

title: A Long Suffering Runner Finds a Solution
text:
I run marathons and train in the swamps of central Florida. Between April and October you live with near-100 percent humidity any time of day, 80 degree mornings rising near 100 by the afternoon, and almost guaranteed afternoon rainstorms. That's a long way of saying that I need headphones that can survive being damp almost all the time and drenched quite often too.

After trying some Ankers that quickly died, I found some success with a few sets of Plantronics Backbeat Fits. Don't get me wrong, these are perfectly fine headphones, but I felt like the price has kept on rising from about $40 to near $100 these days, based in part on their high ratings on Wirecutter and other review sites. I liked that they don't fully seal your ear canal, allowing you to hear some ambient noise like traffic behind you, but the sound quality is pretty mediocre. After the last set of Plantronics I had stopped working (insides ended up being fully rusted), I decided to check out a higher tier of options.

First, I bought the Bose Soundsport on runner recommendations on reddit and elsewhere. These have incredible sound quality when I use them when not exercising. But they have a true seal of the ear canal, and when I ran I felt like I was in a vacuum--the seal seemed to amplify my own breathing, footsteps, and heartbeat--and I couldn't hear any traffic of anything around me. The sound quality also became muffled due to the seal. In addition, after about 30 minutes of running, the sweat and moisture in my ear meant that the bose earphones repeatedly slipped out, despite trying all different sizes of tips. Back to bose they went . . .

Next, I pulled the trigger on the Powerbeats pros. These were a game changer. The adjustable hooks let me decide if I want them fully inserted and sealed, or if I want to just partially pull them out to allow me to hear traffic and ambient noises. The sound quality is up there with the Bose. But really it's the functionality with my iphone that I love and some of the apple touches, like the fact that they turn off when removed from my ear. Time will tell how they hold up to the sweat and rain, but after a month they are doing great. Battery life hasn't been a problem as long as I remember to put them back in the case after every run.

title: Do NOT buy if you plan to listen to Apple Music
text: I am echoing what other reviewers have said about the poor sound quality. I also have issues with the sound only coming through one ear. On a very rare occasion, I have heard excellent, full acoustic sound range in both ears, but I can count these times on one hand. The absolute worse thing about these is they do not maintain volume when I am listening to Apple Music. Just google “power beats pro volume issue” and see all of the people complaining and zero support from Apple for the ongoing issues. The software on mine is current and yet, while I am biking, the volume will continue to ramp up every few seconds until my ear is blasting. Then I have to pull off the road, open the tool bag under my bike seat, grab my phone and adjust only to have it happen again in the next song. I have even tried to find “child safe volume setting” on my phone, located in the Apple health app, to try and stop my ears from getting blown out. If I ask Siri to lower the volume while riding, Siri tells me I have to unlock the phone. So I usually shut off the earbuds and ride 25 miles in silence. I will never buy beats audio devices again. This is an Apple supported device with zero support and they are not cheap. Do yourself a favor and find another option. After 18 months of frustration, this is what I am doing.

text:

Same for as the Powerbeats 3 but don’t have the chord connecting them. Honestly I prefer the chord. These coke with a pretty big charging case as the headphones can’t be plugged in to for charging they charge via the case.

The biggest issue it the headphone don’t have a power button. They have to be put in the case to “turn off” and when you take them out they automatically turn on. I hate it. Instead of just hitting a button to turn them off, you always have to carry this case around. If you go for a run they will be one until you get back inside and put them in the case. If you wear them before bed and take them out when you half asleep, they will be left on all night until you return them to the case. Seems like a pretty stupid design. I burn through these batteries light years faster than the Powerbeats 3.

So 2.5 stars. Not the easiest things to use.

title: Powerbeats pro!!! The yays and the nays.
text:
First and foremost. I love my pair Powerbeats pro. Yes I did my research before I bought it. I knew it wouldn’t have the bass like the other beats headphones does but for the battery life the quality, the connectivity, the range, the snugness, durability of it. These true wireless headphones are number one.

However!!!!!!!
If you’re running/jogging. It won’t cancel outside noise. If you're flying it won’t cancel out outside noice aka the engine of the plane. If you fall asleep while listening to music and have the headphone against something the buttons are extremely sensitive and your music will stop or you will end up calling someone. Suggestion wear a beanie to add to the cushion you’ll still chance it but at the right position you’ll be fine.

Also I can’t wear these for a long period of time. The ear hooks IS NOT a soft rubber. It’s hard and will hurt your ears after 4-5hours Of having on your ear!

For $250 dollars. The case is NOT wireless charging compatible, which really is a let down and the case for the Powerbeats pro is extremely big. Definitely something I would not carry in my pockets. And I wear loose breathable clothings. The case for my Powerbeats will always remain in my backpack home or in my car.

These ARE shower proof!!! Rain proof sweat proof NOT Swim proof.

However for music and calls. These headphone do sound amazing. Phone calls are clear music is clear. “Please don’t expect a normal beats headphone bass sound” but they do deliver great music.

I love my Powerbeats pro. Even with the cons. If I could afford another pair I’d buy it with no questions.

title: Great customer service
text:
Edit:

After working with the companies customer service department, they were able to get me a new set of earbuds that do not seem to have the same issue. Based on this I’m updating my review to a full 5 stars.

I am honestly loving the size and form of these. They fit well in the ear. The case is super tiny compared to my other headphones. I want to love them so much but I am hitting a huge snag. title: Comfortable with quality sound
text:
I bought these after initially buying and returning the ‘beats pro fit’ which advertised basically everything these do with the addition of the silicon piece to better secure the earbuds in your ear.

I returned those because that piece made them uncomfortable to wear for more than half an hour or so but their sound quality and especially their noise cancellation were phenomenal—they sounded a bit better than these do. Not by an extremely large margin but especially in regards to the active noise cancellation, the Pro Fit did it better and I’m not sure why since they’re nearly the same product but perhaps they have more differences internally than I realized.

I’m tempted to return these and re-order the Pro Fit and just trying to find a way to make them tolerable to wear because I miss the level of noise cancellation they achieved.

Alas, these are still great earbuds and I’ll need more time with them to make the decision of whether or not to keep them. From only a day’s use I can say that they’re far more comfortable to wear for extended periods and the charging case they come with is of better quality than that of the Pro Fit’s (which isn’t saying too much to be fair).

I’ll update this after I’ve had a chance to use them at the gym a few times.

Music is paused / played by one tap of the ear. 2 taps skips a song & 3 taps plays the previous song. I found that other ear buds would NOT do the previous track function. Why the *#&! not? Doesn't make sense to me. When I'm jamming to that one song that gets me AMPED when I'm running, sometimes I wanna hear it again. I went with the ivory color since most of my electronic gadgets are black. Cool color & glad I did that. Pairing is a breeze. title: Charge doesn’t hold up
text:
I have two sets of these headphones. Obviously I was satisfied, but now I’m just getting irritated. These sound great, but they die sometimes after just 2-3 hours. Many years ago I got into the horrible habit of keeping my TV on all night. I cannot sleep in a quiet room. Now I’m getting older and my hearing is going a bit. I have a roommate, so if I have the TV on so I can hear it, she can hear it from her room - and, my luck, she can hear a pin drop in the next apartment. My solution is to use ear buds.

However, lately they are only holding a charge for 2-3 hours. Of course I wake up. That’s why I bought a second pair. She gets up extremely early to go to work, so my ear buds are necessary from about 8 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. so all night I am constantly changing from one set to the other. So on any given night I’m switching 3-4 times. Whichever one I’m not using at the time is always plugged in, so charging is not the problem. I really hate to complain, but the charge time is just too short. It would be normal to have to switch once, but not 3 times in a 9-hour period.

So buyer beware. The sound is extremely good for such low-priced buds. They just don’t hold a charge well.

text:
I LOVE the way these feel in my ears! They are sooo comfortable and secure. They have never popped out of my ears. They are small and extremely light weight, each bud weighs 3.7 gram, vs 5.4 g for Airpods Pro and 9 g for Tozo T12, which I also purchased on Amazon. I can wear them for hours and not even know they are there. However, the sound is not very good. They are clear, a bit tinny, with no bass, slightly worse than listening to my iphone 11's speakers. The Tozo T12 sound really good, and only for a little more money, but they were not nearly as comfortable, especially when locked/twisted in, and popped out too often when not. And the reality is that after 5 minutes, I forget about the audio quality...and that the A1s are even in my ears. The comfort and security are even better than the Airpod Pros.

The sound quality of voice is also tinny, but clear. The microphone works well for calls, at least in a home or office environment. I have not tried them outside in the wind and background noice. They are so small, I can lay on them in bed, ear to a soft pillow, to listen to TV in bed when my spouce falls asleep. And unlike my Airpod Pros, I can control the volume when paired with my streaming FireTV Cube.

If you want earbuds to listen primarily to music, these are not the best option, but as inexpensive "mini" earbuds, they are terrific and worthy of my 5 stars. They well suited for listening to pod casts, talking on the phone (indoors?), listening to TV shows, going for a job and anything the requires keeping the buds in your ears for extended periods.

title: Athletes- this is the one/ Audiophiles- move on
text:
I have been looking at these for a while, and when Amazon took $50 off the regular price with same day delivery I figured I would give them a shot. $250 for headphones was a hard pill to swallow, since I already have a pair of Bose for travel. I was looking for something to replace my failing ipod headphones. I have seen quite a few critical reviews of these, so I was skeptical out of the gate. Let me get a few things out there first. The AKG chorded headphones that came with my Samsung phone sound significantly better than these, and the Bose headphones are leaps and bounds better. And when I move behind a few walls on the other side of my apartment they lose connection. So if you are wandering 75 feet away from your device and want concert quality sound these are not for you.

That being said....I didn't buy them for that purpose. I am a runner, and I wanted something without a chord that would stay put during an extended run, or a good workout at the gym. I took them out on a trial 5 mile run this morning, and I have to say that they excelled at exactly what I bought them for. They fit perfectly and stayed put the entire time. In fact, they are so comfortable, I forgot I had headphones in at all. They stayed in tight and delivered a sound quality that was absolutely acceptable for a morning run. I had my old ipod in my back pocket, and never lost connection once. For the purpose I bought them for....5 stars. If I were looking for the best sounding headphones on the market? Well I would have been a bit disappointed. Figure out what you are buying these for, and make your decision based on that. If you are active and don't want to worry about losing an earpiece, these are the ones. Once you get them in, they stay in.

title: Premium headphones with intolerable charging and app issues
text:
I've had these headphones for a bit more than a month now. I use them almost exclusively for long aerobic workouts (running, elliptical, hikes, etc.).

PROS:

- Fit is excellent. Unlike past wireless headphones I've owned, these do not come loose even with high motion workouts. This alone earns the second star in the review.

- Sound is ok, but highly dependent on the fit and choice of ear tip. Keep in mind that these are primarily workout headphones and are not intended to compete with audiophile cans through a headphone amp.

- Battery life is fine when the headphones charge properly, which brings me to the CONS:

CONS:

- Controls don't always respond on the first press attempt. It's almost as if the first press is a "wake up", and then the controls work as advertised. This is minor.

- MAJOR ISSUE: I'm using Android, and the BEATS app seemingly only does two things 1) manages the connection, and 2) reports and manages the charge levels. For #1, you often have to open the app, open the case with headphones seated, press the button, wait, rinse and repeat to make a connection. This is vintage 2010 Bluetooth behavior. For #2, the app often reports erroneous charge levels. For example, in one moment the case is reported at 0% charge, and in the next it's at 100%.

- SHOW STOPPER: The headphones won't charge properly on a regular basis. Literally about half the time I open the case all ready for my workout, either the left or the right headphone is fully drained. I am very careful to seat both sides properly in the case and keep the contacts clean, yet this problem persists. Others seem to be reporting the same issue. After fiddling with the seating for a few minutes I can eventually get them to charge (while looking for my old Plantronics headphones to use as backup)

The CONS above are bad enough for any true wireless headphones, but keep in mind that this is a BEATS/Apple product that retails for $250. A product at this price point should not have these sort of issues. Unfortunately I am outside of the return window.

title: DON'T Trust Apples Warranty
text:
My review is for a heads up on Apple's Warranty. My Pro Beats had connection and charging issues straight out of the box. Basically, 50% of the time they would not connect and 50% of the time they would not charge- even when making sure they were seated just right in their charging case.
Finally, after months of them just not working well, I decided to send them back to Apple to fix. Apple told me they would take back the defective Pro Beats I had and simply send me a refurbished replacement.
After sending them back, I got a message from Apple basically saying I can pay $250 for them to be fixed or else they would just send the defective pair back to me.

After phone calls and talking to at least 5 customer service reps, the last supervisor I talked to said that Apple was voiding the warranty due to liquid damage- by the way, first I had heard about liquid damage.
I said there was no way there was any liquid damage as I treat my products very carefully and that there was no way that I had damaged them. This supervisor basically said they are damaged and therefore the warranty is void. I said I did not damage them. And that's it, a stale mate. Apple claims there's damage and the warranty is void. I know that I did not damage them, but had a defective pair of Pro Beats. There's nothing I can do and there is nothing Apple will do at this point.

My WARNING is, just beware that it can be very likely that Apple will not honor their warranty and quite possibly make up 'damage' in order to void it.

-P.S. I had bought my wife another pair of Pro Beats, shortly after I bought mine. Her Pro Beats work as advertised. Just beware that Apple's integrity as a business is very questionable.

title: Nice set of wireless earbuds but wait for a sale
text:
First, there are a lot to like about these. They are well made. As do all Beats they pair easy with iDevices. The sound is fine, if not spectacular. Noise cancellation is excellent and there are three levels (full, pass through, none). The case is compact and fits easy in a front pocket or whereever. There are also a lot of hard shell and silicon cases available on here and elsewhere.

My favorite aspect of these: the form factor of the buds themselves. These ‘screw’ into your ears for a comfortable and secure seal that doesn’t come out and is inconspicuous. Easily, they’re the most secure earbuds I’ve ever owned. And, for phone calls and Zoom conferences where you only need one bud they’re great. Overall I think they compare, well, to the early iterations of the AirPods.

That said, and above all, keep in mind this is basically an entry level product. The sound is good, but will not blow you away. Spotify (even at high res) is just OK; Apple Lossless is good but will be better on upgraded buds The firmware functionality is very limited; you can either control noise cancelling or volume, but you can’t do both. For some people battery life may not be all that; I find it fine. How these will hold up in intense workouts I don’t know; but I mowed my lawn with these and they were fine. Also, for whatever reason I found these cut out every now and then when I was mowing the lawn, but I don’t know why.

The four star rating above is based on full price. I got these for a third off and for that price I’d give these five stars, easy. And, if you can get these reconditioned, all the better. But if you’re looking for something that is more powerful, go a level up.

UPDATE 8-13-2022: Affirming my earlier review. I really enjoy these. The sound is great, noise cancelling works great, they’re secure. And they’ve held up.

On a few phone calls people have had a hard time hearing me with these but not always and it may have been on their end. Bottom line: I still say at 149 these are four star, 99 or below five star.

Update 2-19: These are still great. Very comparable to AirPods. They don’t fall out, compatible with iPhone and Apple devices. Again, wait for a sale and/or check out used ones. Like I said, at $149 these are 4 star, $99 or less five star.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: Underwhelming, with connectivity issues.
text:
I'm not an audiophile. I was also hoping that these lived up to the hype. Unfortunately, at least for me, they didn't.

Sound: Very clear treble and mids, poor bass (more powerful on the sony's and enacfire's). Poor power; I had to increase the volume 3 times past the orange mark (usually too loud) on my cellphone to be able to have comparable output to much less expensive brands.

Comfort: Ok for me. Choosing the right size of the earbud is paramount. This is not a deterring factor when scoring these earbuds, as it depends on your anatomy, so you gotta try and see if it is comfortable for you. Used it for 2 hours with minimal discomfort.

Hardware: The buds themselves look and feel premium. The case is flimsy, with a cheap plastic feeling despite being a premium brand. Silicon is comfortable on the ear. The buttons are where these earbuds shine the most; quick, responsive clicks allow you to chase different functions and you can do it with either earbud so you are able to use one if needed and you will have all the functions.

ANC: Ok, not groundbreaking. It muffles lows very well, but mids and highs go through easily. It is comfortable and allows you to hear the music in a more intimate manner. Apple AirPods pro remain a much better choice (tested my wife's) in this respect as it feels more natural and drowns the outside noise much, much better. Transparency mode is good, similar to Airpods pro.

Calls: Surprisingly good. No complaints from callers.

Battery life: As stated per the manufacturer, so read the descriptions.

Connectivity: This is by far the worst. I have not had this experience with earbuds costing 5 times less. Choppy connection in wide spaces where you are expecting to have interference. I tried with cheaper earbuds (enacfire H1) and I had no issue with Bluetooth connectivity whatsoever. The phone was in my pocket.

I am not an audiophile, again. But for this amount of money you expect something closer to premium brands. I would spend my money somewhere else. Returned.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: Noise cancellation is perfect!
text:
I wanted noise cancellation earbuds so I can watch my shows on my phone while in the same room as the family who watched another program on the tv. I did not want sound competition in my own house. I also wanted have the flexibility of walking around freely without my phone & a earbud cord.

I wear them when I walk my dog and the transparency mode keeps the podcast sound directly in my ear, but I am aware of noises in my surroundings —a good thing for night walking; there is tracking in case you misplace an earbud. These are perfect!

Sound quality is excellent, battery life is six hours plus- at least- And the fit is really comfortable and snug. You get three sizes of silicone tips to fit your preference; pricing was under $125.

I agree with another reviewer that putting the earbuds back into their charging case takes a little bit of getting used to as the shapes /slots are a little funky. Charging cord only fits a computer port so a wall adapter may necessary.

My only complaint would be that the instructions are not exactly detailed on how to access all the uses; I stumbled upon a skip feature & I have not quite figured out how to access the microphone to take phone calls;

I am fearful I will misplace either the case or lose one of the buds just because of a busy lifestyle, but I would buy them again. The noise cancellation was the priority and these have it!!

text:
There's nothing worse than putting these in your ears and only having one play. This would be a design flaw with the charging case. I only use these when my PowerBeats3 and PowerBeats3 reconditioned earphones are re-charging. title: They're trying too hard
text:
Good overall. I haven't called with them to verify voice, just voice mail but mostly want them for music anyhow. Oh, & I bought a pair as a gift for someone who loves them.

They do a lousy job connecting to my older phone that I use as a player, so that sucks. They do better with the newer phones. They are alright on the computer as well. The pick up is pretty decent, albeit a bit tinny. Be sure your files are top notch, or you will hear those tiny imperfections. So good there. Cd rips, wavs & wmas are the best, & a joy to listen to.

The range is pretty darned good too! Certainly better in the computer, pushing high volume, but I can almost walk around the house which is WAY better than those Lab buds I had! There are very few wireless/blue tooth bumps or rebounds with the Tozo ear buds. I like them so much, I am gifting a couple pair to friends.

I find them too sensitive to touch, but that happens with all of these new generation of ear buds. You want to get them in your ear, not change songs or answer the phone.

Charging in the case is nice, & convenient. I would like to see an on case USB, but they use any 9-11 pin old style micro (phone) connector, so that's fine. Seeing that they hold a decent charge, I haven't had any conflicts with other items.

That's about it. They hold up, & don't really discharge too much between uses. I did a full charge at first, & haven't charged them again, for about two weeks. They get their juice form the case, & pretty quickly turn off or go in stand by.
I would have liked to seen a better manual off, than tap or hold. Sometimes I just want to stick them on the side for a bit, not in the case.

Bottom line. I like these Tozo A-1 ear buds over many, many others (see my reviews). I have been trying & returning a whole bunch of (other) premium buds of late. All kinda super lame-0. These are very good. I really don't like they are so sensitive to touch that putting them in or adjusting them changes things-ANNOYING.

title: Beats The Competition (In Some Ways)
text:
The Beats Studio Buds are a polished, well designed pair of earbuds with an excellent soundstage, even if they are a little on the quiet side.

Having just come off another review of the competition (good stuff) I wasn't sure what to expect from Beats latest attempt. Throughout the years I have heard the Beats brand both scorned and longed for. A sign of quality or of overpriced brand-loyalty. This is my first foray into their world of sound.

I am left reconsidering what is possible with earbuds.

Simply unboxing these was given every consideration. There is a pull tab to remove the adhesive smoothly. Like opening a file cabinet you are then presented with a number of tabs inside the small box. Attached to one of these is the pill-shaped buds case containing your new pair of beats. There is another tab/card with alternate rubber tips (if fit is a concern). There is also a quick start card, a USB-C to USB-C cable, and few other offers and paraphernalia.

The quickstart guide is astoundingly simple. It says to simply open the beats case beside your phone. Right. Is it really that easy to pair these bad boys?

It is.

Upon opening the case a small dialogue was presented on my OnePlus 6t asking if I wanted to pair and download the Beats phone app. This is an Android phone. Beats is owned by Apple. I had no right to expect this level of ease.

Upon pairing I removed the buds from their case. The angled 'handles' serve multiple purposes. They house the single button on each bud (top portion, away from the "b"), and the twist the buds into a more locked position within your ear.

I have not felt any concern over whether these buds will stay in my ear.

The ANC (Active Noise Cancellation) was immediately apparent. I had not counted on it being active right from the gate, but the shroud of silence they provided was functional and adequate. These aren't world class noise cancelers, but they do add a nice layer of isolation to your music.

The music itself is shockingly crisp. The Beats Studio Buds seem to excel at bringing individual tones out of a song and making them pop. They are also located all around you. You can space out instruments, voices, sounds. The soundstage on these small, small speakers is wide and engulfing. It is engaging.

The soundstage doesn't assist as much if you are listening to a single source of audio, like a singular cello.

These Beats don't quite have the edge on battery life, promising 8 hours per charge and something near two additional charges within the case. This totals 24 hours. That's some good listening, but less than half has much as some of the competition.

These buds pair at around 50% volume on first connect. I am happy they seem to remember my desired volume on subsequent connections. However, the initial setting is near where I needed to keep it for comfortable listening. These buds run quiet. As reference I find I may only need 20-30% volume with a competitive pair for a similar level of volume, giving me more headroom should I need it.

I have experienced a few stuttering glitches with the left bud, but this may be due to my phone or location. I will be sure to update this review if there are any unforeseen failings that become clear in time. For now, however, I can close on a happy note.

These buds are musical fun. I find myself wondering how things will sound on them and looking forward to using them on my commute.

Given my initial impressions I can easily recommend them. The Beats Studio Buds are a polished, pleasant experience right from the start and straight into listening.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

text:
There's a reason things are on sale sometimes.

First - I'd return these for AirPods, but I have teenagers, and teenagers "borrow" your AirPods after they have either blown the speakers in theirs or lost them. Or given them to their now ex-girlfriend, whom neither of you wants to deal with.

I wouldn't buy these again, but for the reasons stated above, I'll be keeping them.

They have buttons on the ends of them to answer calls, hang up, pause the music, etc. But they're placed in a way that 1/3 of the time I hang up on people when trying to put them in while on a call. When pushing them into your ears, you're also generally pushing the buttons. I'm guessing they let an intern design that feature.

When I am on a call and lose wifi - for example, if I'm on a call and take the dogs for a walk - the connection between my earbuds and my phone drops, leaving the person on the other end listening to my pocket. Or me, half shouting at them from the handset while I swear at my earbuds and try to reconnect them.

Besides that, these are comfortable and sound good enough. I added memory foam ear tips to improve the noise cancellation. They charge fast enough. They're an Apple product so they pair easily and switch between my laptop and iPad seamlessly.

But bottom line, I wouldn't buy them again. If a friend asked, I'd tell them to keep shopping.

I then had to take the earbuds out, try to resync them with the phone...nope, I had to press the button on the case for five seconds and have my phone recognize them again. title: I just got them, and I'm in love...........
text:
I have used Bose Quiet Comfort for decades. But, they are just too bulky now on airplanes. I got these Beats Noise Cancelling Ear Buds just for air travel. I wear hearing aids that stream music and phone calls, so I only need the Beats for air travel. I take my HA out and put them in the little travel carrying case, and put in the Beats. See the picture for what I was traveling with and what I am now.

I tried another product and it went back the same day, as it kept cutting out and the noise cancelling was not very good. That one had an app I used on my iphone. Beats arrived today. Where's the app? No app. When I paired it with my iphone, the entry for Beats in the Bluetooth part of the phone's settings automatically updates with all the Beats controls! However you control your music volume playing on your iphone, that's how you control the volume on Beats. Tapping the ear bud pauses, forwards, skips the song.

So, I tested these against my Bose. If Bose has a score of 10 for noise cancelling, then Beats is an 8, which is really good I think. Of course, when you've got music playing then the noise cancelling seems even better, because you are only listening to what you want to listen to. These will also work great for streaming news videos, movies, and TV programs, while on flights.

There is no user manual, but you can find more detailed instructions by just searching online. If you find yourself pushing and twisting to get them in your ear, switch to the small tips. Medium is installed, and small and large are included, too. I had to switch to small to get a snug fit. The snugger, the better the noise cancelling effect.

Sound quality is excellent! I played one of my softer music playlists from my phone to test out the noise cancelling and quality. Excellent!

Final thing: THERE'S NO USB C WALL ADAPTER INCLUDED for charging, so buy one. I got one for $10 on Amazon that included a 5 ft cable. USB C slots are not like the regular USB slot on a wall charger we are all accustomed to using.

I am gonna love these the next time I fly!!

title: The most useful and durable bluetooth earbuds out right now
text: I have owned the Powerbeats Pro since 2019 and use them quite often. Although pricey, they are well worth buying because of their durability and how useful their functions are. The Powerbeats Pro offers a great way to listen to music while doing physical activities. I highly recommend the Powerbeats Pro for someone who is looking for earbuds for working out and physical activities. The Powerbeats Pro are extremely durable earbuds. This is because they are water resistant and have helpful accessories. Having water resistance is very helpful while working out or doing physical activities. However, water resistant and waterproof are two very different things. If a person submerges their earbuds in water they will break. The Powerbeats Pro, being water resistant, means that if the owner begins to sweat or it is raining outside, and the Powerbeats Pro gets wet, they will not break.  Although the Powerbeats Pro are more expensive then the next wireless earbuds, like Airpods, they are better quality. The Powerbeats Pro are more stable than the Airpods because the Airpods can easily slip out of your ear. In this product, there is a plastic hook that goes around the ear. This hook allows the earbud not to fall out of the ear when a person is participating in physical activities. On the other hand, the Airpods can easily fall out and then break. The Powerbeats Pro also comes with different sized buds for different sized ears. Buds from the speaker are interchangeable so people with bigger or smaller ears can wear them. Airpods on the other hand, only have one size that does not fit everyone's ear. Therefore, Airpods can break because they are too loose and fall out. The Powerbeats Pro, unlike Airpods, have multiple color choices to choose from. So instead of having plain white, people looking to buy Powerbeats Pro get color choices such as green, blue, pink, red, black, and more. The Powerbeats Pro is not only durable, but has unique, useful functions. For example, to stop a song, all you have to do is press the Beats logo once. To skip a song, press the Beats logo twice. To go back to a song, press the Beats logo three times. This makes it very simple to adjust music. Another aspect that the Powerbeats Pro offers is that your music will stop if one of the earbuds gets taken out. The Powerbeats Pro has Siri installed and can talk to her through the microphone in the earbuds. When the Powerbeats Pro is in the ear, hold down and ask Siri a question. I have found this to be very helpful because it allows me to ask Siri questions like, “What is the temperature?” or “How much time is left on the timer?” While I could use my phone to look up these questions, the Powerbeats Pro makes it so much easier. Adjusting volume on the Powerbeats Pro is as easy as one click. Instead of having to stop a workout to adjust the volume, just click the top button on the Powerbeats Pro and finish the workout. The Powerbeats Pro also has chargeable cases. These chargeable cases allow for charging the Powerbeats Pro when there is no outlet or while on the go. The charging time of the Powerbeats Pro is amazing in itself. When fully charged the Powerbeats Pro lasts nine hours before it needs to be charged again. Plug it back in and it only takes five minutes of charging time to get one and a half hours of listening time. Overall the Powerbeats Pro’s durability and useful functions make them a great way to enjoy music. Not only is it a great earbud, but I highly recommend it for someone who loves listening to music while doing physical activities.

Sometimes both earphones don't connect right away. Ever so often I have to put one back in the case to reconnect. All in all I love these headphones. As an extreme music enthusiast, and getting voice lessons, I love these soooo much. Thanks beats for the headphones my soul needed❤ I would get these in every color if I could... Get these headphones, they are built to last and be the solution you need to get through your workout, travel, studying with ease and joy!

title: Best completely wireless earbuds out there. Work great on Android too.
text:
I bought these directly from Apple a little while back. At the time I purchased them I had the iPhone XS along with my iPad Pro and Mac. Since then I have moved to the Google Pixel 3 Android. Everyone is aware of the chip set which has some added benefits when using on the Apple ecosystem. It does work very well. With that said...they work excellent on the Pixel 3 too. One time connection was easy. Now when I put them on they automatically connect to my phone without ever having to select them. Funny, but many times I still had to select them on my iPhone XS.
These are extremely comfortable. Very light and just fit well
So what about the sound? Are they better than higher end wired headphones? No way. Are they the best completely wireless earbuds? Absolutely. If you get the correct seal (this cannot be over stated) they sound great. I am not a fan of Beats heavy bass, but these earbuds do not have that. Too me that have the bass that the writer/singer mean for the song. Highs, mids and low sound great without any muddied songs.
One thing that always bothered me with wireless headphones is the top volume. Years of working in a noisy environment took a toll on my hearing. These headphones have the volume. On the iPhone I used Apple Music. I now use Google Play Music. The volume was very good on the iPhone. It is actually louder on the Pixel 3. I believe this is due to Google averaging out to a high dB level with their songs.
Two last things. All controls work on Android. Play/pause, FF, Rew. Obviously you cannot say “hey Siri” Well...I guess you could but nobody is going to answer.
The Bluetooth connection is really good. I have a couple of outdoor spots that cause interference with many BT headsets (skipping, static etc). I have yet to experience any of this with these headphones.

So..simply put they are excellent for what they are. I use them every day at the gym, outdoor tracks and on occasion at home. If I lost them I would rush out and get another pair. I am that impressed.
**Some say the case is too big. Meh...it is fine. The magnets are a nice feature to assure the headphones are in place.

Issue easy enough to observe, contacted Apple customer service and was told to mail in the headphones. Very next day was told the issue could not be duplicated so the phones would be sent back. As soon as I opened the box and put it to charge, same image right there. Took pictures and contacted Apple again, providing images and, per their request, access to my phone logs. Contacted again and was told there is nothing they can do. Complained to BBB. Response is that the case is closed for them and nothing will be done. WITH PICTURES, LOGS, everything. text:
Man.. I was pretty excited to get these because the only pair of Bluetooth wireless headphones I've ever owned were $18, super uncomfortable and got me about 90 minutes of play time.

The good:
- Sound quality is awesome. I'm not a headphone snob but I tried it on several gentes: alternative, folk, pop, R&B, country and was satisfied with all of them. I think the bass was appropriate. Occasionally the poppy stuff felt like it had more treble and as if the vocals were being pushed way out but nothing super crazy.
- noise cancellation is pretty good. I don't need it to be 100%, or even 90% for that matter. I have kids and for some reason they keep needing me to take care of them..?? Weird. Anyway, I like to be able to hear if someone starts crying if I need to. However they do block out most of the play fighting noises from the hallway outside my bedroom while they're on, even while they're in the same room as me if the volume is up enough.

The kind of bad and only reason they get four stars:
Comfort- they are quite nice to wear, I prefer the wrap ones versus the ones that sit just inside the ear as I occasionally wear them resting in a car and I've had others fall out of my ear. However, I have a conch piercing and it turns out, that's wear the end of curved piece sits. If I turn the piercing completely backwards and face it down it doesn't push on it so much and I can get them to rest where I need them to, but I can see how it may get uncomfortable after awhile.

Things that still need updated:
-- Length of actual battery life. I took these from the package with 74% and have been wearing them for about 30 minutes and they've dropped to 72/73% respectively. Unsure if I'd ever wear them long enough to test the 9 stated hours but so far they seem like they'd hold up.
-- charge time from empty to full
-- call quality
-- comfort from longstanding wear

I'll try to update if I remember. But the moral of the story is: they're pretty great and I don't think you'll be too disappointed 💛

title: A1 and NC2 UPDATE
text:
UPDATE ON SECOND PURCHASE:

The old adage is true, "Fool me once, shame on you, fool me twice, shame on me."

A few days after receiving the latest set, I'm only getting about 3 1/2 hours of charge out of the right earbud. The irony is, if it was the left earbud, I could combine both sets to make one working one. Now I have to print out a return label and drive to a return center. I wouldn't recommend these earbuds to anyone.

UPDATE:

I wrote a review that never seems to have gotten posted; I now have an update.

Originally, I purchased 2 sets of A1s and a set of NC2 earbuds. I had some tip issues and it took many emails to tech support to get a response and then I was asked for a 5 star review.

Moving forward a few months, I have left one pair of the A1s plugged in at an airport waiting for a flight and the right earpiece of the second set has lost almost all volume. I have cleaned it repeatedly but it does not help. Meanwhile, the NC2s are working ok, about what I expected for such a low cost. Actually, much better bass than I expected for the money.

Even though I've had trouble with the first set, I've recently purchased another set of A1s and hope they will last longer than the first. Here are my reasons:

1. They are very inexpensive so worth giving it one more shot to see if they hold up. Also, not TOZOs fault I was rushed having to change gates and forgot one pair charging.

2. While they were both working, they were excellent for making and taking calls. I was clearly heard and had no problem hearing the caller, much better than the NC2s. I had to swap the NC2s on calls so often that the A1s became my go-tos for everything but music.

3. Excellent for audiobooks, podcasts, streaming media (not great for music as bass response is not great, the NC2s are really much better for music.)

4. The A1s fit my ears, and more importantly, they stay in for their charge cycle! This is quite important because I've wasted a lot of time on buds that don't fit my small ear canals.

So, why only 2 stars for now? Tech support was very hard to reach, and then asked me to post a 5 star review in response to sending me out a set of tips (which turned out to be for another style), and because the right earbud dropped to about 10% of max volume about 6 weeks in.

But like I said, I'm willing to gamble another $17 because there are the first buds to actually fit, stay in and be comfortable all day. If these last for a few months I'll purchase another set so I have all-day coverage for calls and use the NC2s for music in the evening and night.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:

They are decent for the price, I purchased 3 sets but I need more of the smallest eartips they supply. I have written support a few times to purchase them but no response. I can't agree with the posts that talk about "excellent technical support". The buds are fine until you need more tips; I've already wasted the cost of a new pair of A1 buds trying to find the correct tips on my own.

title: Compared to 4 other Earbuds...
text:
I bought these earbuds along with 4 other pairs, with the intent of comparing them over a couple weeks and returning all but my favorite. Here were the results:

Beats Fit Pro - https://www.amazon.com/dp/B09JL65GNM?psc=1&ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_product_details
Pros – These buds had some great base, and the wingtip gave them a fit that made them refuse to fall out of my ears. But the best feature? Physical “clicky” buttons on each one of the buds. You press in and hear/feel the click, rather than relying on a touchscreen-like feature. No need to guess if you tapped them once or twice, you will know.
Cons – The wingtip gives a very sturdy fit, but not the most comfortable. I wouldn’t recommend to anyone with smaller ears. The noise canceling was solid, but nothing special. And this may be picky, but I didn’t care for most of the color schemes available. I prefer my earbuds to be hard to notice, and even the black ones have a bright red letter “b” in the middle.

Beats Studio Buds - https://www.amazon.com/dp/B096SV8SJG?psc=1&ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_product_details
Pros – Very comfortable with the same great physically “clicky” buttons as the Beats Fit Pro. Noise canceling seemed slightly better than average. Great base. Classic look.
Cons – Tested during a workout, a little bit of sweat had these sliding right out of my ear. The case for these earbuds also was the flimsiest of any I had tested, with a very weak hinge that I was scared of breaking off within the 2 weeks of using.

Samsung Galaxy Buds Pro - https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08MWZHHKP?psc=1&ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_product_details
Pros – A neat feature that I noticed only in these earbuds was that it had noise amplification as well as noise cancelation. With one swipe in the app, the surrounding sound was actually louder and clearer than it would be without the earbuds in. Great if you are hard of hearing, or just enjoy snooping on conversations out of reach.
Cons – Similar to the Beats Studio Buds, these didn’t stay in during a workout. They were usable, but every 10 minutes I found myself pushing them back into my ear. And this is an opinion, but these are the ugliest earbuds out of the bunch. The shiny black gleam made it look like a large beetle was hanging out in my ear. No visible brand placement either, which makes them appear cheap and generic rather than the quality Samsung they are.

Samsung Galaxy Buds Live - https://www.amazon.com/dp/B09TBM1L3S?psc=1&ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_product_details
Pros – Cost effective! I added these to the test group because of the unique shape, and for that they are worth giving a try. If you have small ears and do not like the rubber insert that is standard in most other earbuds, these may be perfect for you.
Cons – Poor fit for large ears. These were tested the least of all of the buds, because the fit was so bad for my ear shape that they wouldn’t stay in if I turned my head too fast.

Bose QuietComfort - https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08C4KWM9T?psc=1&ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_product_details
Pros – Bose noise canceling is unmatched. If your primary use for earbuds is to cancel out that background white noise, this is the pair for you. The sound quality is great, not too heavy on the base. The case for the earbuds stood out from the rest as the only one that impressed me. Felt very study, and I had no worries tossing it into a gym bag or cup holder. The only case with a button latch to make sure it doesn’t open accidentally.
Cons – This was the most expensive pair of earbuds by a longshot, and there were still some things I felt could be improved. The rubber inserts had more of a “flayed” shape rather than the “rounded” shape that is standard. My guess is that this was by design, because the earbuds were also slightly heavier than others and may need that extra in-ear grip. The flayed shape did make them sturdier, but at the cost of them being uncomfortable in an active situation. They were also the largest earbuds, and stuck out from the side of my head further than I would have liked.

My favorite? The beats fit pro! While I wouldn’t recommend this pair for everyone, it was perfect for my routine. My music taste benefits from the boosted base, and the wingtip shape was perfect for any workouts. The feature that really convinced me was the physical buttons, something that I didn’t realize how desperately I needed.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

text:

Luckily I have a stash of other eartips and found a pair that provide an acceptable sound. It took a while to find tips that both fit my ears and still fit in the charging case. Even so they will never be bass heavy so Bass heads don't bother. There's decent detail but I can't recommend these if you need loud because they still emphasize the upper registers and could get fatiguing. With good eartips they're pretty comfortable and at modest volume can be worn long term. These are cheap, disposable and OK with reservations. I have other Tozo and Soundpeats earbuds that cost not much more and I think are worth the extra.
UPDATE: After living with these buds for a while with decent eartips I think the sound is better than first thought so I upgraded my overall rating. But my original observations still stand. If you can't get a good ear seal even at $16 you'll wish you opted for something else.

text:
I wrote one review previously, but then I deleted it when I thought I had figured out the secret to getting them to pair with my device. Apparently there is no secret way to get them to pair to my device.

After wanting these for a few months, I was delighted when they finally went on sale, and I bought a pair. I have a pair of beats headphones, which I love, and they have never given me any trouble at all. They are a little tight on my head, so I thought that a pair of beats ear buds would be the thing to get so I didn’t have to deal with that issue.
The problem is that I could never get them to easily pair with my device.

I would open the lid and they would appear to be connected and then I would put them in my ears, and nothing would happen. So then I would check the audio connections and apparently the sound was still selected for my iPhone, and selecting the earbuds didn’t really help. Sometimes they would connect, and sometimes they wouldn’t.

Today I decided to go for a walk, so of course I wanted to wear my earbuds. After 20 minutes of trying to get them to connect, I gave up. I did get them to connect a couple of times, but the left earbud wasn’t playing any sound. So I got my device to forget them, and then re-connected them and they wouldn't play at all. So then I turned off my phone, and turned it back on and then the left wouldn’t work but the right one did. And I got so frustrated that I decided just to return them, which I did, and I still haven’t gone for a walk and now it’s been about three hours.

I don’t understand how the headphones can be so trouble free, and the earbuds were the biggest pain in the butt ever.

title: I would save money to purchase AirPods
text:
Here are the major points:
-no matter what sized ear piece you use, it continues to pop out of your ears.
-when using the “noise transparency” setting, if it doesn’t know how to read a certain sound the earphones burst into a cacophony of screeching eardrum bursting high pitched frequencies. They will continue to do so until you reset the ear buds.
-the bass reading is very low and I wouldn’t say it’s the highest of quality sound performance.
-the charging chord comes as a “C type” as opposed to a “usb”, meaning you have to either buy an entirely new chord or an entirely new wall plug (assuming you don’t already have a “C type”.
Minor side notes:
-the case feels like a very low quality plastic
-it picks up dirt, oil, and fingerprints like a magnet and is hellish to clean.
-it’s very difficult to find aesthetically appealing cases, due to the odd shape.
-when using it without a case, it is extremely difficult to refrain from dropping it. It’s like carrying one of those cylindrical water tube toys, designed to give you the “dropsies”.
-the earphone is so small that once it does slip out of your ear, it’s like needing to conduct a police investigation to find a needle in a hay stack.

-One positive is that the battery life is quite adequate
