title: READ THIS
text:
This review is written by a semi-active (I haven't been going to the gym as often as I should've lately :( ) 34 year old adult who has owned regular AirPods for over 2 years. Like many of you, before buying AirPods I highly considered these. I must say, besides the much higher price tag back then, I was highly intimidated by the size of the case. I thought, "there's no way I'm going to carry that around in my pocket" and then of course, the style. Yes it's more likely to stay in your ear, but will it bother me after extended periods of time?

Well, let me say, after owning AirPods for 2+ years and loving them, there's major flaws. You already know the pros of them so I won't get into that.
1- they're small. and even though that's a pro, it's also a con. I'll later explain the reasons for losing AirPods but this is one of them. I once left my left AirPods in my pants pocket and didn't notice when I put them in the hamper. I'm sure you know what happened next. It was thoroughly washed. (and I left it out for one week so it can thoroughly dry and fortunately it works! but still, maybe I was lucky). They get lost because they're so small. More likely to fall into cracks in the couch, or in the car. I've spent well over $250 replacing either single AirPods or the whole set because I've lost them so many times.
2- they don't easily stay in your ear, especially my left ear. my left one dropped while mowing the lawn once, Never saw it again :( You can purchase rubber covers for them to create a MUCH BETTER FIT, but still, that's something else to purchase, and carry around with you, therefore the smaller size of the AirPods case isn't as attractive anymore. Also, I've lost so many of those rubber earbud covers. I've spent about $35 over the last two years because I've had to replace them so many times.
3- the battery doesn't last as long as I'd like therefore you're forced to keep the case with you at all times. more on that later.

Now on the Powerbeats. They fit so nicely. I was afraid it would be bothersome but I don't feel the back side of the Powerbeats pro on my ear. I know it wraps around the ear but I don't feel it. That rubber tip fits perfectly and doesn't come off. Yes, the case is huge, but because the battery lasts so much longer I leave the case at home when I go out and just leave one of them in my ear at all times. It's not annoying, I still hear what's going on around me with just one in my ear. Because I'm way less likely to lose them, and because they have a perfect fit in my ear I know I'm now more likely to save money on replacements and rubber covers. These will cost me less in the long run, I KNOW IT.

Ah, before I forget. IT HAS BUTTONS! Which is fantastic. I have better control of what I'm listening to. It was never a deal breaker for the regular AirPods, but this is much better. Oh, and these seem to be smarter about when they're in my ear and not. The others were a tad weird about that. Sometime they'd be playing music when they're not even in my ear, just in my pocket.

Overall, I can't think of anything in particular that makes AirPods a better choice. I obviously can't speak for the pros, but I went with these because they were $50 less than the pros.

Oh, before I forget. I went with the red, I love that color and think they look super cool. Maybe consider going with black or ivory so they match better with what you're wearing. Red can clash if I have a purple or orange shirt on (which coincidentally I have lots of those) But I don't particularly care much if my Powerbeats match my outfit, you however might.

Talking through the mike is fantastic. maybe a tad better than the AirPods but not a reason to pick one over the other.

Seriously though. Don't be intimidated by the large case. just put it in your ear and leave your case in your house, or in your car. The battery lasts a while and they do charge quick.

title: Really Good Ear Buds...with some flaws
text:
These are really solid. I bought them on sale at $130 which is definitely better than the $150 they are normally at. The first day I honestly thought they were terrible and wanted to return them, but now i'm on day 3 and they honestly are sounding better by the day. I'm used to over ear headphones which obviously are far superior to any earbuds so I think I had to adjust to that but for earbuds the sound is really good. I was worried about the volume for calls because that was a pretty common complaint in the reviews but people have no issue hearing me on calls and I can hear them pretty well even when outside walking around. Before purchasing, I was also a bit concerned about the fit, but they come with 3 sizes of the buds included the smallest ones work best for me and they actually fit surprisingly well and feel super comfortable, but these things fit everyone differently so your mileage may vary in that regard. However, I don't think I would trust them when working out unless I wore like a headband over my ears or something, but overall I feel confident walking around normally without being worried about them falling out. I am a bit disappointed in the battery on the ear buds themselves they seem to drain fairly quickly but the case seems to give me a recharge I could probably get like 20 plus hours out of these with the case recharges which isn't bad. I'm less sold on the transparency mode than I am the noise cancellation. The noise cancellation is pretty good once you get use to how it works with ear buds, again, for me I'm used to over ear head phones that do everything better than buds and the adjustment takes a little time, but for buds, the noise cancellation is very good, as for transparency mode I could take it or leave it, it's nothing to write home about.

I am #TeamAndroid so I was never going to invest in glitchy airpods but I have zero issue pairing these with my Galaxy phone or my Ipad so that is a super plus for me. If I am only reviewing these and not comparing them to anything else, I'd give them a very good to great 8 out of 10 overall (or for Amazon purposes 4 stars). Maybe even a 8.5. As for my complaints, would have loved wireless charging and for transparency mode to actually matter plus it would be great if this thing had sound and EQ controls available on the app, as it stands the app is pretty much pointless. But otherwise, for me, this is a really good and in some ways great product nd i'm happy with the purchase, not lets see how long they last lol I've been lucky with my beats products in the past they lasted for 3 plus years with heavy use in the gym so i'm hoping for that streak to continue.

title: Totally unreliable, but nice when they work.
text:
When these work, I've really liked them. The sound is reasonably good (a bit low as others have noted), they fit well and stay on while working out. Having volume and play controls on both earbuds is also a good feature (that the competition does not have). The complete absence of wires is great for exercise.

The thing is that they are totally unreliable. That's why as I type this, they are back at Apple for a 2nd time to try and get service. The first time they sent them back to me with the same problem.
The problem is that the charging system (via the case) is totally unreliable. Over and over again I go to use these and one or both of the earbuds is at 0% charge. This is after leaving them in the case, which was charged so they should be fully charged.
I don't know what the problem is and neither does Apple. But if you read the comments here and elsewhere, you'll see that many people have the same experience.
This complete lack of reliability makes them highly problematic - because every time I want to use them, I have to remember to check whether they are charged at least an hour before to then charge them if they're not charged.

Overall extremely frustrating and what seems to be a not-ready-for-primetime first generation product that is being sold for a ridiculous amount of money based on the Beats and Apple names.

title: Faulty charging system makes them obsolete
text:
Pros:
- Sounds just about as good as Airpods
- Fits nicely and no issues of falling out while running
- Looks fairly nice

Cons:
- Doesn't sync at times
- Only one ear will register about 50% of the time (my experience)
- Doesn't charge both earpieces and doesn't register them as being housed even when firmly connected

I get it-- these are great and what I have been waiting for. I myself wanted something that'll easily connect to my iPhone XS Max, and immediately I was somewhat unimpressed with the sound; however, I realized that the angle of the buds in my ears was a bit off. Once that was fixed, they sounded great. I worked out, then left them off the charger, and did another work out the next day. No issues. I charged them, and only ONE charged, despite the magnetic force in the casing being made specifically to put them back on the charging part. They started to work after my workout and I thought maybe I just didn't secure the buds in the fully charged case. They worked again, I was happy. Charged them again after a couple of workouts, no issues again. Today, after they were charged, only the left earbud decided to work. I played with the casing and housing for several minutes before giving up-- I'd have to work out with one earbud or no earbuds. I left both buds out of the case for about an hour. Magically, they both were recognized and worked.

Contacted Apple and they told me to contact Amazon, because I bought them here. Amazon's chat person asked for my number just in case we got disconnected, then decided to leave the chat after not addressing anything and just thanking me for being a Prime member. I had to contact them despite giving my number a second time, and this individual did take care of the issues. Returning!

You might just luck out and get a good pair. I liked them when they worked, just not worth keeping if the whole point is to have an easier time connecting at the gym.

title: 1st gen product bugs. Great sport earbuds when they do work.
text:
They are great when they work. Going completely wireless is a great and liberating experience once you try it firsthand. I was on the fence about getting any truly wireless earbuds because I thought it was all hype. I settled for these because I am an iPhone user.

Not all is great though. These have had various connectivity issues. Issues such as
•an electronic buzzing sound that comes from either the left or right earbud and it gets louder when you actually touch the earbud with your fingers. This never happens to both at the same time, but each one has had this issue. When this happens no music or any sound comes from the affected earbud. Just the buzzing sound. This can be fixed by resetting the earbuds (put them in the case and hold the button for 15 seconds) however the most recent time this has happened it took several resets to get them working again.

•synchronization issues. Often times the sync goes out of whack and everything just sounds like an echo in a cave. This has a much easier solution of just taking them off, waiting a few seconds, and putting them back on.

•another issue is when you bend the ear hooks to fit to your ears, the hooks might interfere with each other in the charging case and prevent one earbud from making proper contact and not charge.

I would recommend to but the wired ones or Powerbeats 4 as people tend to call them. You save $100 and it’s still better than a wired connection for the gym.

With that being said I still use these all the time. At home when cooking, right before bed, the gym obviously, and during lunch break. I’ll definitely get another pair if and when they release a second gen product once they have ironed out the rest of the bugs.

title: Clearly a step above the AirPods and a Great Pair of Workout Earphones
text:
My first impressions is that they are pretty fantastic and I own AirPods as well as Beats X. They also fit very well too and I wear glasses most of the day. Having interchangeable ear tips is a total plus too. I've worked out with these yesterday and this morning and it's almost impossible to get these to fall off my ears. They only way I see these falling off is if someone wears these while they are boxing lol. Other than that, I'm going to have a tough time transitioning back to my Beats X for working out.

As far as sound quality goes... they are definitely a step above the AirPods and I believe how they fit in my ears contributes to that as well. Bass is strong and if you like your eardrums taking a Beat-ing then you will definitely love these. Listen to Pop, rock, piano solos etc... they all sound great on the PBP. I sometimes watch YouTube videos or binge while I work out on the treadmill. Movie / speech dialogue, explosions, cars screeching and dragons roaring on videos are above satisfactory.

I'm having a tough time trying to see if there is a difference in sound quality between the PBP and the Beats X. Also for people who don't want to spend the $250, the Beats X is a great value which you can find under $100, they fit well, you don't have to worry about losing them if the buds happen to fall off your ears and they are pretty compact.

Making phone calls on the PBP is incredible. I'm walking through a sidewalk with cars zooming buy and the wind blowing, shopping center or crowded area and people can hear my as if I was indoors in a quiet office. With the AirPods, it does pick up some noise around you and oops... it falls off my ears while doing something as much as a slight jog.

I only have a few gripes with the PBP... The case takes quite a bit of space for an everyday carry bag and I wouldn't mind the size so much if this thing at least have wireless charging. For a gym bag, obviously there would be no issue. You can forget about pocketing this thing if you are wearing anything besides cargo pants and gym shorts with big loose pockets. What does make up for the large case is that 9 hour rated battery life. If you are going out and about, you can buy a $5-$10 pouch on Amazon to carry this around in your pocket and leave the case at home or in your car.

My other issue is after about an hour an a half or longer, these are a strain on the ears. AirPods, while working on a desk, taking calls and walking around the office, I can wear these all day without any issues - except I have to pop them back in the case because battery life on AirPods are crappy.

I'm hanging on to these PowerBeats Pro for now. They are a great workout companion and I need more time to decide if this would replace my AirPods as an everyday carry. Before the PBP, I was pretty satisfied traveling with my Beats X as they were great for flights and I didn't have to worry about losing them and they are great for the gym as well and cost less than half of the PBP price tag. If the PBP were $199 instead of $249 it would be a no-brainer for anyone. However, that $249 does give you a great true wireless experience and Apple's H1 chip / pairing capabilities.

title: Got more than expected
text:
Came for the extreme reliability, stayed for the incredibly sound quality. It never sounds like an earbud is producing all the sounds, but that you're actually there in the movie, in the game, and the sounds are coming from all around you, from 10 feet away, from an inch away. You can hear the difference. It's shocking, for people that never had it before. People that say they don't enjoy music just need to get off their cheap antiqued earbuds.

Still, the extreme reliability is the selling point. Can't possibly fall off and go missing. Waterproof enough to take a shower with. Incredible battery (are you sure it's just 9 hours?). Can do independent ear listening, which effectively doubles the battery life. Plus elegant, beautiful case that recharges 90 minutes worth in 10 minutes. Therefore, performance is guaranteed at all hours, a trait that is look for even in business tech. Yes, I do believe these sports earbuds are good enough to sold as businessmen earbuds.

The natural passive noise canceling is a little much sometimes. It's a bit bothersome to need to take one off every time you need to have a conversation, but whatever. It's actually somewhat strange to wear in public, because at this price point, I feel like I had to be on guard in worse neighborhoods, but then you look over and see someone holding an iPhone X in public... oh well.

Update:
After over a month of use, am feeling more like these are still great, but not perfect, and therefore might not be worth over $200. I bought these for their reliability, but putting them on and having them connect is the one area these have trouble with. They HAVE to connect to bluetooth while in the case, which makes them a hassle to put on in public or while driving. And sometimes, only one side connects (sometimes only the left, sometimes only the right). However, a few repeated presses of the play button on the nonresponsive side gets it to come back to life. Did not expect this of an Apply product.

The other thing is... I actually don't get to workout with these on as often as I thought. In the gym, I'm talking to my buddies and need to hear them talking, plus actually feeling a little conscious about wearing a pricy set around them. While running, I tend to have my own thoughts anyways. Still I use them... half the time.

They are a great replacement for the broken overhead headset I originally had for sitting down at a desk :P Two in one?

Didn't expect the $50 off to be permanent. I suppose Apple were trying to sell them all off before the 2nd and bigger shipment of the Sony WF-1000XM3 came out (which I personally would not have bought because it's a new and therefore untested product).

title: Long term review: I'd buy something else.
text:
I purchased my Powerbeats Pros in December 2020. I know technology evolves quickly but these earbuds are becoming more and more glitchy.

Here is what I don't like: after every use, I have to fight to get the earbuds seated properly in their charging case. They will click into place but don't actually disconnect and charge. Beats states that the case design sometimes knocks the buds lose which disrupts charging. 2-3 times a week I play the "are they charged or not" game. The app will say they're at 100% but upon removal from the case, they show 0% charge. Or one will be 100% but the other is 0%. At least twice a month I have to delete and re-download the app due to connectivity issues. I've used Beats products for years but these will be the last.

If you're still reading, here is what I like: sound is decent but noise canceling abilities are better. Volume and control buttons work very well. The design is comfortable for long wear (3+ hrs on flights with no ear discomfort).

All in all, these get 3 stars. When they work, they work well. But at least 3 days a week I have to fight with them to get them to work properly.

title: Super cool features, such as answering the phone without having to touch anything
text:
I have some beats studio over the head earphones which are absolutely amazing, & I wear them every day, however I don’t like driving with them because they are so noise canceling that you can’t hear sirens. They’re wonderful to mow with, so that’s what I’m comparing these too.
Although these are not a soundproof as my over the head beats, that’s kind of what I was looking for. Something I can wear while driving in my car and still hear the sirens, or people talking. I wanted something less conspicuous when I go into a store as well. These check all the boxes! The sound is great when talking on the phone, but the sound with music is not near as good as over the head beats. They are still good though! I do love the extra added features such as when somebody calls, this headset will tell you who’s calling, and ask you if you want to answer it. You do not have to touch anything and just tell it whether you want to answer it or not. When you’re done talking you can just tell it to hang up! I love these hands free features. I don’t have to touch anything when I tell it to play certain songs! You can also tell it to turn the volume up without touching anything. That’s super nice when you’re working outside & your hands are dirty! I can wear these for hours and they are very comfortable in my ears and I don’t ever lose them, like I have with so many earbuds! I think having the clip around the back of the ear makes all of the difference in the world and these are quite comfortable! One thing I am a little disappointed on is the battery life. It’s not a major issue, but my beats over the head earphones last several hours longer than these, but I can still get 4 to 5 hours of continuous playtime/talk time with these so I’m not complaining too much.
Overall I would absolutely buy these again! This is a great product!!

Not sure how many hours they play, but when the battery gets low, a pleasant voice warns you "Battery is Low" several times over 5 minutes before announcing "Battery is Low. Turning OFF".

title: BE WARNED: Used earbuds sent instead of new!
text:
The Powerbeats Pro Earbuds were purchased as a gift and upon registering them noticed that the serial numbers on the units did not match up. We also experienced some difficulty pairing the devices. After contacting Apple, we were informed that the warranty had been activated months ago. The "NEW" ear buds that were purchased were in fact NOT "NEW" but rather returned, repackaged and sold as "NEW". I am appalled at the false advertisement and embarrassed that I gave these earbuds as a gift and now have to exchange them. I can only hope that I actually get a new set. I will not give more than a single star due to the misrepresentation by the Beats Store. The more I think about this dishonest business practice the more frustrated I am as a customer.

I encourage anyone purchasing anything from the Beats Store to be sure to check the items and register them immediately. Verify the serial numbers and, if necessary, contact Apple to be sure that the items purchased are new. The "remedy" that Apple offered was to reset the warranty to the new purchase date. This is a ridiculous offer. I would not want to stick some earbuds in my ear that some stranger has already had! COVID or not...that is GROSS!

Given the popularity of the Beats brand, I have no doubt that many others have been tricked into thinking they were purchasing new equipment at full price and were actually getting returned, repackaged and possibly refurbished items.

EVERYONE BE WARNED! Apple...as a company, you should be better than this!

title: Bad reliability; Design issue
text:
Unfortunately the bad reviews on lack of reliability are true.

I bought my first pair from Target, and was initially was happy with the headphones. Then a couple of months later the left earpiece started to give problems. It wouldn’t charge reliably. Luckily I was under extended return period and returned the headset. I really liked the headphones otherwise and I figured I had gotten unlucky and so bought a second pair a month later. The second one started to have the same issue after a few weeks of use. I just lived with the issue initially. Did a headphone reset a couple of times. Yet slowly the problem started deteriorating. I’ve had this second set for 4 months now, and they almost unusable. Every time I open the case, the left earpiece is discharged. I have to push it down, make sure it’s charging and then check it every so often to confirm it’s still charging. And then even after it does, if you open it the next day it’s again discharged. It doesn’t show battery indication as reliably as the AirPods. You have to open and close the case multiple times for it to show. Luckily the battery widget works well. even when fully charged, every so often there won’t be any sound on the left headset when you start using it. You have to put the left piece back in the case, close it and pop it out again for it to work.

Finally I gave up and called Apple today. They said repair is the only option. They’ll ship me a box and have to ship these back. Considering this is my second set and going by other reviews of people who got it fixed only to have the problem return, I’m not too optimistic.

The headphones clearly have a bad design. Notice that most of the bad reviews mention the left earpiece going bad (though I’ve read some with the issue being on the right one). Some think that the pins on the left side are not too long. Some think the magnets are weak. Some think it’s a firmware issue. Not sure what the issue is but it’s definitely something the worsens over time.

title: Good quality sound, decent comfort, excellent price
text:
I've had mixed experiences with Bluetooth headphones in the past (esp on regards to audio/video sync) but given that I was just looking for something to listen to music and podcasts while working I wasn't too worried. I saw these earbuds were highly reviewed and on sale, so I decided to try them out.

All in all, I've been pretty impressed with these little guys. I haven't had any issues with sound quality, and the batteries seem to last several hours (I can usually make it through most of an eight hour shift with one earbud active before it dies, at which point I swap the other one out of the charging case and continue without an issue).

The only things I'm still adjusting to are the comfort of the earbuds and the touch controls. The flat surface on the outside of each earbud serves as a touch pad to play/pause (and some more specific commands depending on if you're touching the left or right earbud), and there's been a number of times I've accidentally paused it and/or taken several attempts to get it to start playing again. The rubber buds themselves are also not the most comfortable, but unfortunately they won't fit in the charging case if I swap out my usual rubber buds from my wired headphones. It's not the end of the world, but they'll occasionally get a little irritating or uncomfortable.

All in all these were definitely worth the price, and while I have a couple complaints they aren't bad enough to not make them worth using. If they wear out or I lose them I may compare this brand's other options, but I'd be willing to buy these again in the future for their price.

title: Side-by-side comparison with Air Pods
text:
I bought Apple's air pod wireless ear buds as well as these Powerbeats Pro for a side-by-side comparison of not only sound quality, but functionality throughout a normal day as well as workouts.

Sound quality: Beats wins this contest hands-down, but with a large caveat. While the air pods sound no better than the standard wired ear buds that come with a new phone, Beats has phenomenal sound quality. The bass is not overwhelming, but definitely noticeable and very rich. The caveat is that the sound quality is only superior while you are at rest. I noticed immediately that when I began running or doing anything physically active, the seal in your ear that provides the superior audio quality is slightly compromised and results with a sound that is hardly distinguishable from the air pods. This is a big issue for me, as using them during exercise was one of my main use-cases for them.

Fit: The Beats have a wing on them that hugs your ear to keep them from falling off during exercise. I literally couldn't do anything to get them to fall out. The air pods don't have a wing, but don't really seem to need one. I was also able to run and exercise without worrying about them falling out, but the Beats do feel much more secure.

Usability: The air pods can be tapped pretty much anywhere with your finger to skip songs. The Beats, however, have a small button that has to be pressed to register any action. So for example, while I'm running with my air pods, I can easily reach up and double-tap either ear piece to skip a song. But with the Beats, I found myself having to come to a complete stop, search with my finger for the tiny button, and with more effort double click it to skip a track. It was MUCH more cumbersome to operate during an active workout.

Various issues: Within 5 minutes of receiving the Beats, I put them on to try them out on a walk around the neighborhood. I put on my hat, and immediately realized that the wings that wrap around your ear also rub against your hat and transmit that awful scratchy, rubbing sound straight into your eardrum. If you wear a hat, this will be a constant issue. I almost returned them for this reason alone, but my wife who doesn't wear a hat hardly ever ended up taking them.

Bottom line: I don't feel the Beats are worth the extra hundred bucks or so if you're looking for wire-free ear buds to work out with. If all you're going to do is lie around the house, you'd probably be better off with over-the-ear headphones anyway.

title: Good, but not $200 good
text:
Original Post:
Simple overview of the pros/cons in my opinion:

Pros:
-Nice style
-Good sound quality
-Good battery life

Cons:
-The headphones are always on (there is no way to turn them off), so the battery is constantly draining even when you're not using them.
-At this quality for $250 - you're paying the Apple price that doesn't match the quality.
-The portion of the headphone that wraps over the top of your ear is more fragile than one would expect at this price. I gave my headphones to a friend to try on, and naturally he pulled on this portion so that he could fit it on his ear..and the material completely bent out of shape.

Also I honestly don't see any benefit to the H1 chip apple is boasting about. It gives a cool little graphic when you first set up your headphones, but if you don't use Siri it seems like there is zero benefit to it.

If you can get these headphones on sale ($150 or less) its not too bad. I got them on a black friday sale for $200 and feel like I paid a little too much for the quality...but not the worst thing in the world :)

Update: So I've had these headphones for over a year now. There is one design flaw that has really gotten on my nerves: the charging. You charge the headphones by placing them in this awkward case. The problem is, the left headphone has stopped charging unless I place it in and out of the case multiple times. And the only way to know if it is charging is to check on your phone...there is no indicator on the case to let you know.
So ill plug in my headphones all night expecting them to be fully charged and one is dead because it didn't place it in the case properly 2-5x (note: the issue never happens to the right earphone).

title: Expensive and great when not glitchy
text:
EDIT: I've had these for a few weeks now and overall the review below stands. However I've been noticing some glitchiness in the headphones. Like sometimes if the headphones are out of their case for a while, one of them will be nearly dead while the other is at a reasonable charge level. Sometimes I lose pairing to one headphone or the other. Today I went to the store, took my headphones off for 30 seconds or so, and when I went to use them again they wouldn't pair.

It feels like something that a firmware fix would solve, but no updates are available right now. When they work properly I like them though. I'll update this in the future if things improve.

---
I've long struggled with finding good quality earbuds. Part of the problem is that one of my ear canals is not the normal shape and so standard earbuds do not necessarily stay in and almost universally sound crappy because they don't seal correctly. For a while I was using the Blue Ant Pump headphones which were cheap, decent quality, and comfortable. My most recent pair was falling apart after much abuse and so I decided to see if I could find something better.

After a couple weeks with these I'm really impressed. Initially I had some discomfort with the way the arms were pressing on my ears, but after a little finagling to get the right positioning they've been good since then for hours at a time. The headphones come with an assortment of silicone tips and unlike my last earbuds these stay on snugly.

The sound quality is excellent. An earbud is never going to be as good as a good quality over ear headphone, but for earbuds these are remarkable. I was listening to some music the other day and was a bit surprised when some bass kicked in and it came through so clearly. I've never had earbuds that were capable of that.

One nit to pick is that the the earbuds assume you are going to put them in the case when you're not using them. So they remain on once they are out of your ears and the battery will continue to drain. This wouldn't necessarily be an issue except that the case is pretty large and not really suitable for carrying around in a pocket. The battery life is really quite good if you're actively using them, however. They also charge very quickly so even if you drain them accidentally it's an easy fix.

The biggest downside of is that these are very expensive. The quality is definitely high enough to justify the cost, but I will say that I'm definitely more nervous about losing them than I was with my $30-40 pair of earbuds. At this price they feel like more of an investment than I'm normally comfortable making in a couple tiny bits of plastic but they seem well built. So hopefully they hold up over the long haul.

title: Disappointing ‘Apple’ product
text:
For an Apple product, I am very unimpressed, and I feel wronged for the price tag.

Pros: sound quality, and YES, ACTUAL VOLUME BUTTONS.

Rant: I am SHOCKED and insulted that Apple product designers STILL decide for AirPods to have no physical volume buttons. CLEARLY they’ve never used headphones in a human society.... Just imagine this ludicrous scenario, where one may need to quickly turn down their headphones.... such as, say, getting into an elevator, without wanting to yell “HEY SIRI, TURN DOWN THE VOLUME” like a complete and utter .... you fill in the blank.

Cons:
(1) The charging case design is literally unforgivable. It’s bulky and ugly (okay fine big deal), but impossible to open without fake finger nails or a screwdriver.
Much worse: if one headphone is not VERY carefully set, (no magnetic docking), it will not charge. And you have almost no way of knowing. You must slowly set them down, one by one, and wait for the tiny single little pin sized case LED to pause and blink red , to acknowledge that one is charging.

(2) The biggest slap in the face: Apple product, but you cannot use the “find my” app to ping the headphones as you can with AirPods. —— As an AirPod user, this was unbelievable when transitioning to these.

title: Mostly Good
text:
I purchased these ear buds after losing my Powerbeats3, so I knew what I was getting into for sound.
Beats have a slightly exaggerated bouncy sound. If you care a lot about the mid range tones on your Led Zeppelin albums, don't get Beats. I like the fantasy-bass sound. I also am fussy about my ears and Beats have always been the most comfortable for me.
Initially, I had a little problem with one of the ear buds coming un-paired. I could get them to re-pair but it was a pain. This was until I realized that sitting in the open case IS when the ear buds pair. Giving it a 1/2 second between opening the case and pulling out the ear buds fixed the un-pairing issue for me.
I don't love the case as a charging middle man. It is necessary with the delicate nature of the ear buds and it is the way the technology is going. No stars taken off, but I like to complain and I'm going to here. I wish I could just charge the ear buds. Battery life is better than the Powerbeats3. I'll give them that.
Color choices are awful and for that: I did take off 1 star. I was trying to hold out on purchasing these until better colors were available, but after losing old ones, I wanted something. So I tried not to fall asleep when picking a color and I got black. Where are the shock colors? Yellow? Green? Electric Blue?

title: Excellent for durability and weather resistance
text:
I bought a pair almost 2 years ago and it was one of the best decisions I've ever made.

I'm a mail carrier. I spend long hours either walking around in crazy weather or driving an incredibly loud LLV (those old school mail trucks). I put one of these bad boys in one of my ears and I'm good to go. I alternate which ear each day.

The noise cancellation is definitely noticeable, even when I have nothing playing, I can clearly hear a difference between the ear with one in and the one without. I only have to keep my phone volume at around 60-70% to clearly hear most things over the sound of the truck.

The battery life on these things is amazing. I spend 6-10 hours a day listening to audiobooks and podcasts at work (and then even more time driving home and the grocery store). Even doing this an average of 6 days a week for just under 2 years, I can still go 10+ hours before I hear the bloop bloop sound signaling that my battery is low. This is straight run time, without switching earbuds or putting them back in the case.

These are comfortable. I was wary as, up until buying these, I have absolutely hated the feel of earbuds. These are the first pair that I've found that I could wear and then "forget" about. The over ear hook is adjustable, and they do not fall out of your ears constantly like other ear buds do.

They really are sweat and water resistant. After experience rain, snow, wind, tree branches, summer heat and sweat, these bad boys are still going strong. They're also easy to clean and care for, as I just grab a baby wipe and wipe them off.

I would 100% recommend them to anyone. I wish anything else that I used for work held up even half as good as these. They're an amazing product, and they're definitely worth the money.

title: Very good, with some quirks
text:
They are solid headphones and I use them for pretty much everything. I think the sound on them surprised me the most. The bass response is good, without being muddy over overpowering. The high end is slightly recessed in some cases, but I am ok since I treble really bothers my ears.

Comfort wise is really going to depend on the person. For me they are perfect and feel very secure when I work out. But I think with different ear shapes it might be different for some people. The case, though great that it charges - is just way too big. You cant really fit it in your pocket and it still uses lightning instead of USB-C, which is getting ridiculous at this point.

The main knock on these is that when putting them on sometimes, one of the earbuds wont register with my phone or laptop. title: Decent bass heavy sound, uncomfortable design
text:
Sound -
The sound of these headphones isn't terrible. Being simple they do what you would expect beats do, handle bass well. While they never felt quite as full as a set of over or on ear headphones, they get the job done. they seems to sound dull though for non musical productions though, as I noticed Youtube and other video sources sounded duller then I expected, especially compared to my Bone Conduction headphones which is saying something. That is to say they live up to the beats stereotype.

Comfort -
Comfort is where they let me down. The tips are limited, and since they only use the in canal tip and by design put all the weight on the lower parts of the ear. I honestly found this discomfort from this to be annoying and returned them mainly for this issue. I know not everyone has these kind of issues, but if you find Apple iPod headphones from the 00's uncomfortable, I don't think this will be for you.

Performance and Other notes -
A few days into trying this out, playing with tips to try to find some comfort the left headphone refused to connect, with no quick fix I could see. I also had sync issues between the left and the right, and some static break into the headphones. I know this isn't the rarest issues with true wireless buds, but I had these for 2 days and experienced a lot of issues for that time. I have had much better experience with $50 and under headphones and these cost $150 ($100 on Black Friday). All around they are simply disappointing. They are wonderfully simple to use, the simplified design from using a single touch button on each bud is nice (though more control over the button would also be nice). I wanted to like these, but Apple/beats failed to deliver with the product.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: Best Workout Headphones Available
text:
These are designed to be the best possible headphone that you can buy for workout/sports, and they absolutely are. The batteries (earphones + case) last for an entire week if you use them for a few hours a day, they are IMPOSSIBLE to shake out of your ears and manage to always keep a good seal, they're sweat/rain-proof, and the controls use real buttons on both ears so they're easy to find and manipulate.

I've put these through a lot and never expected them to be this good at every single thing you would want in a workout earphone.

A few downsides that I won't take any stars off for, but some buyers may want to know about:

- They never really turn "off" unless you keep them in the case. Made the mistake a few times of taking them out of my ears and just leaving them on the table overnight outside the case and they were totally dead the next day. This seems like it would be avoidable with better software/firmware to power down after long periods of no motion, but oh well.

- The audio quality is surprisingly good, but nowhere near what you would get with a pair of "hifi" IEM's or headphones. You could buy a pair of low/mid-range Shure IEM's for the same price as these that would blow the Powerbeats Pro out of the water with sound quality, BUT with these you are paying for wireless, durability, fit; it's a tradeoff. This isn't worth removing a star since they certainly sound good enough for their role as workout headphones. Coming from listening mostly to super flat pretentious hifi speakers and headphones, I have to say the sound profile on these is actually kind of fun with all the punchy tight bass. (this is the first Beats product I ever bought).

Hoping they come out with a 2nd generation of these that can handle staying outside the case and have slightly improved sound quality, but these are great already.

title: Terrible Charging Pin Design Kills The Product
text:
These headphones seem like a decent value when compared to other headphones with similar features, particularly when you consider they're "backed" by the Beats and Apple brands. However, they are comprised by a serious and unforgiveable flaw - the charging pins in the case and the pods themselves very quickly become corroded, damaged, or fouled so that the pods don't charge when you replace them in the case - you will find yourself fiddling with the pods in the frustration so you can seat them JUST RIGHT in order for them to charge. The case itself is designed so that when you close it, it jostles the earbuds out of the position you just spent ten minutes getting them into! The end result is you will often break out your ear buds only to find they're dead.

Save your money - look elsewhere.

title: Great for trail running
text:
Update after a few months of ownership (5 stars to 2): I returned the first pair after a month due to the left earbud not charging while in the case. The second pair I received had the same issue after two months. These sound awesome, battery life is great, and they stay in my ears and are comfortable. However, 90% of the time they won't charge properly. I have to go through all sort of trouble to get them seat in the case properly and charge. I've tried resetting and all of the other common fixes I found on the Internet. It's just a poor design. So I have to constantly check them hours before I go on a run to make sure that both buds are charged.

I bought these because my Bose Soundsport Free earbuds sound great but they always get jarred lose when I trail run. The most important earbud factors to me were that they stay in place, are comfortable, sound good, and have good battery life. The Powerbeats stayed in my ears during a three hour trail run in the mountains over very rugged terrain (lots of jarring impact); they were comfortable, I didn’t notice them at all; they sound about 90-95% as good as the Soundsports; and the battery life is twice as good. I’m glad that bought them even though I have a good pair of earbuds. They are exactly what I was looking for while trail running.

text:
I'll start out by saying that there's no way I would shell out the money for these if I didn't have an iPhone. The totally wireless aspect is great, but not THAT great.

As far as the headphones themselves, the sound quality is great for wireless earbuds. I don't understand the 1 star reviews for audio quality. These are NOT marketed as audiophile headphones, and I am not sure what people expect from wireless earbuds make for active individuals. One review said they would be sticking to AirPods, but these definitely beat those out in terms of audio quality.

The case is a bit bulky, but it's a great feature and gives these an amazing battery life. On the subject of battery life, these will get you through any given week of regular workouts or long trips on one charge! Strangely enough, the right earpiece seemed to drain faster the first time I cycled them to 10%, but I have not had these long enough to test the consistency of that occurrence.

Finally, in terms of comfort, the earbud size these come out of the box with seemed best for me versus the other options that come with these. These really bothered my right ear every time after a few minutes of wearing them, but I discovered the the base of the ear hooks were adjustable, which lead to both earpieces fitting like a glove!

The A1 chip makes these work just like AirPods. Pairing is a breeze, visibility to battery life is easy, and the ear-sense technology makes pausing for conversation seamless. Connection distance is also superb compared to standard bluetooth headphones I have had in the past. Cannot recommend these more to anyone who is active and has an iPhone.

P.S. I am not a verified owner because my girlfriend surprised me with these from her own account.

Last thing, sound quality isn't as good as previous versions either.  I have to turn the volume up louder just to hear it. The the audio always ends up not synched with the video. title: Update: broke twice in 17 months- Great features, Astoundingly bad audio quality
text:
Update at the bottom- I have been using I have been using Treblab Bluetooth earbuds for years because the reviews talked about how they had good audio quality and the battery life is phenomenal. But I had a little splurge money and decided to try to upgrade so that I could have one earpiece in at a time. Some thing these Beats pro earbuds are able to do. I was immediately impressed with how easily they sync right up to my iPhone, you can tell they’re built for one another because of how seamlessly they work together. I love that I can have one in and leave the other charging. I do this for work and at home for a leisurely listening to music or podcasts. So I have one on almost all day. I don’t have to pay them off or get them to connect. They recognize the iPhone and just connect on their own. I don’t have to pay them off because it soon as I take them out of my ear because to sleep. So I just raise it and put it back on my ear when I’m ready and it’s already on and ready to go. I love the convenience!
They recognize the iPhone and just connect on their own. I don’t have to power them off because it soon as I take them out of my ear because to sleep. So I just raise it and put it back on my ear when I’m ready and it’s already on and ready to go. I love the convenience!

That being said, because beats is a larger audio company I was very surprised at how bad the audio quality is. I’m coming from my regular wired headphones that come with my iPhone, and the Treblab Bluetooth headphones. Both of these sound great. They have rich warm sound. These beats earbuds are mostly tinny with highs and absolutely no warmth or bass. Often times they come off painfully piercing. It was almost enough to return them but as I said I wear them one at a time casually to listen to very quiet music all day so the convenience outweighs the terrible audio quality. But I think anyone who is looking for these is going to really want that audio quality so I should leave an honest review.

Update- After nine months the beats stopped charging. I had tried all troubleshooting I could find and nothing worked. I finally had to contact beats for a service request and they confirmed I had to ship them back have them repair them and then shipped back to me. They did so stating they found a hardware problem and had to replace the buds. So basically now I have brand new hardware and start over. Nine months later same problem. I contact service again and they told me now that it’s out of warranty I can spend $100 per bud to have them replaced. Which is almost as much as just buying a whole new set and case. Problem is, seems like I will be doing this every few months! Definitely not worth it. I think I’m going back to my cheap $40 headphones that sounded really really good.

title: Very good wireless earbud for those of us with small ears or small ear canals
text:
I have been looking for quite some time to find wireless earbuds that are comfortable. I have normal sized ears, but very small ear canals. Even with the extra small earbud caps there has been some discomfort. Not so with the Tozo A1 earbuds. I have paired them with earbud caps from Earphones Plus as shown in the photo. The photo from left to right, an earbud cap right out of the package, then one whose middle section I have folded back over the smaller section. I carefully cut off the earbud cap stem as close to the middle section as I can, then place the cut off middle and small section on the Tozo A1 as shown.

This is the only set of earbuds and caps that have fit me comfortably. I have used the same earbud caps with the Tozo T6 & T9 and I just can't get them to seat fully and comfortably in my small ear canals. I don't know what made the difference with the A1, but it works!

The A1 as well as the the T6 & T9 all have great sound & function as described. There is a slight learning curve with the touch buttons, but now that I've mastered it, I really like it. The A1, T6 & T9 all function beautifully. Pairing with my Android phone was simple and without issue. I like that the case of each of them can recharge the earbuds several times before the case needs recharging. But the A1 is the clear winner for me. For the price, these are exceptional wireless earbuds. Thank you Tozo!

title: Good product for the price
text:
You can spend well into the hundreds for some bluetooth earbuds and live in fear of losing one or both or you can go for something like this. These work perfectly for podcasts, audiobook, phone calls, and even music (which will not likely be super high bitrate anyway if youre listening on a mobile device.)

Ballpark 3+ hours playtime per earbud per charge and the earbuds can work independently so if you only use one at a time and one is charging while one is playing youve got something on the order of 24 hours of continuous playback without having to plug into a usb.

Every year or so I get the latest version of this type of product and every year theyre better, these are no exception.

If youre on the fence just buy them. You might regret an apple or bose purchase at $100+ but at the price these things are selling for you really cant lose.

title: Disappointed - lots of treble, drops connection
text: I found one of the three supplied ear cushions to fit perfectly.  I was amazed how slick and easy they paired to my iPad.  I just held them up to the iPad and it was automatic.  Sweet.  Then I tried to pair them to my iPhone.  Unlike Apple pods they can only be synched to one device at a time.  So I had to press the button on the case and hold it to disconnect from my iPad then connect to the iPhone, which it did without carrying forward my preferred settings.  Not a terrible hassle but not the Apple ecosystem I pay a premium for to enjoy.  The settings and equalizer settings are several clicks away in the utilities app.  Every time I bounce between my devices I have to re-pair them.  Then at the gym, no matter which of the three ANC (automatic noise cancellation) settings I chose I could not hear a difference.  It’s easy enough to switch by pressing on the stem of either bud.  You might hear a difference but I couldn’t.  Then while on the cross trainer watching music videos it would stutter in the left earbud if I turned my head to look around.  It was sitting on the cross trainer 2 feet in front of me, but I don’t know if the cross trainer’s electronics interfered.  I found the bass to be lacking no matter which choice I made in the equalizer.  Finally, these things are held strongly in the case with magnets and the stems feel like they’ve been coated with Pam!  Getting them out is really a challenge.  So I bought the new iPods 3 and gave the beats to my son.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: Waterproof and Durable!
text:
I've had a pair of these for well over a year and they've done a great job at keeping up with heavy use. I use them in my nightly run and will jump in the shower with them right after. They're pretty loud and great at keeping the noise of the outside world away. I actually like that I can toss them around and even accidentally step on them, then clean them off to use again.

When they're wet, the water can make the volume controls a little wild and they might turn down or even pause what you're listening to.

As long as you care for these and clean them every so often, they'll handle a good beating. I finally have to replace these because I threw one out the shower to dry when some water got in them, even though it did still work just fine. It landed near my dog and he took it to the couch to chomp on the. The rest of the time I was in the shower, I could hear the music pause, volume up, and volume down as he chewed it. I know the ear bud is still alive somewhere in my house but I can't seem to find it!

These are a 10/10 for me.

title: Pros:
text:
Noise cancellation was a distance thought in this product's development. In addition to it not screening much sound out, the overall speaker volume seemed to diminish after using these for less than 1 week.

The headphones would randomly unsync themselves to my phone. Which requires you to place them back into the case. Forget the device in your Bluetooth settings, then go through the repairing process all over. Mind you, this doesn't take a huge amount of time, but still very inconvenient, especially seeing how they are now just over 2 weeks old.
The band that wraps around your ear is much more firm than cheaper brands which offer the same function. Due to this stiffness, ear fatigue started setting in within a 1-2 hours of use, until I acclimatize to them.

The plus side is that they have no problem staying in, no matter how intensive your workout might be.
Also, the battery is great. I only really have to change them every other day after using them for 4-5 hours a day. Also, the rapid charging case isn't a false claim. When the battery was low,15 mins of case time was more than enough to get me through for another 1-2 hours of use.

title: Can't believe I spent 200 bucks, but these work great
text:
I am never one to pay 200 bucks for headphones. I like music but not enough of a audio expert to every care about the difference between $30 headphones and these $200. However after trying 4 different pairs and all of them sucking (that's a word right) I bought these.
My requirements were to have full control in either ear as I bike and only wear the right ear. That pretty much eliminates any that just sit in your ear as you need both for full control. I have weird shaped ears anyway and those anyways fall out. So an earbud with an over ear band is what I needed.
Not only did the other brands I tried not work but they fit terrible. Well these fit incredible 5/5. I will never have to worry about it falling out while riding at 30 mph!
Sure connection is supper easy if you have an Iphone, but to be honesty I have never had issues with any bluetooth. So while these are faster - that was not very important to me. 5/5
Most headphones use the volume controls to skip forward or backwards. So if you hold the volume too long it skips. Well with these the skip control is from the main button. I like this as I can now hold down on the volume instead of multiple pushes. Also the main button barely requires much effort 5/5
I rated noise cancelling as 3/5 as they do not seem to cancel outside noise very well. I however like that as I use them while running or cycling and the music is just background noise for me. Being able to also hear around me is important. Seriously I pass a lot of walkers/runners while on the bike and have to scream ON YOUR LEFT because they didn't hear me the first 2 times. Nose cancelling outside your home is not safe!
I did not rate sound quality because again, while I like music I am probably tone deaf and am not sure what is good quality.
My biggest fear is losing these. I have never paid so much for headphones, but so far they are great!

title: Basic headphones at an astronomical price
text:
You are paying for a label with just about every cent of these. They function adequately as basic head phones, that is about it. But you can also get sub $30 head phones that do that so there really is no point to these. Received as a gift and should have immediately returned them.

1.) Sound quality is average but is not mind blowing by any means.
2.) The wireless charging for the case does not function with either of the different charges we already have, maybe it works if you have a special apple or beats branded charger but if you have any universal wireless charge its a no go.
3.) Only wired charging option is a apple firewire, which is all well and good if you have apple products but a complete pain for me since it will be the only device requiring that connection standard.
4.) I find them rather uncomfortable to wear especially if paired with glasses. The over the ear hooks don't fit right if that real estate is already taken up by glasses. I have changed the ear pieces to get a little better in ear fit but even that is only average.
5.) There is no active noise canceling despite what you may expect from $200 head phones.
6.) The buttons are finicky, sometimes being so sensitive that just wearing a stocking cap over my ears will randomly stop music or end calls I am on. Other times they are completely unresponsive. I have joined a couple of conference calls while biking into work and had them hang up 3 times in 10 minutes on the very first call.
7.) Battery life, especially given their size is pretty abysmal and the charging case appears to lose its charge quite quickly even when they are not used. A week of less than 30 min/day round trip bike commutes will have the entire system depleted and they give no warning before just shutting off.
8.) The reliability and clarity of the BT connection is on par with cheap off brand speakers/headphones. Moving the wrong way will cause them to cut out. On one walk I was unable to look to my right or my podcast would cut out as pressure from my hat/scarf would cause the headphone to freak out. It is nothing like the connection quality I get from a JBL speaker.
9.) In-ear recognition is sporadic and even at one point mine kept playing music after I put them back in the case.

Overall, yes they are a pair of ear buds that does basic ear bud things... but at 5-6 times the price of other quality earbuds for completely average performance I don't know who these are for, other than someone who absolutely must have a b in their ear or loves proprietary expensive stuff.

title: Finally the headphones I’ve always dreamed about!!
text:
I pre-ordered these headphones before reading any reviews because I have been so desperate to find good headphones to run with. In my nearly 30 years of existence, I’ve never been satisfied with a pair of headphones. I probably have the weirdest shapes ears ever because nothing fits them. Either they slide out or hurt, or both.
Day 1- FINALLY THEY’RE HERE!!! 😍 I charged them while finishing my work day up (I think they came pretty much charged because they were at 100% within 5-10 minutes) then eagerly headed to the park for a test run. The temp has reached the 90’s here in Mississippi so it was inevitable that they would be receiving a sweat test! After 3 miles (41 minutes, let me mention I’m a beginner runner) I realized I never had to adjust them or push them back into my ear, not ONCE! I’m thinking this is too good to be true! I had forgotten I even had them on, other than the fact that I had a clean crisp bass playing in my ears. I also own a pair of Studio beats, and honestly these ear buds sounds almost as good... which is pretty awesome to not have to wear something so bulky but still have the noise cancellation and sound quality.
Overall, it’s only been one day but my first impression is absolutely amazed.
Side note, these were shipped in a box big enough to fit a baby heifer and it looked like it had been thrown off a mountain. I could almost remove the tiny product box through an opening of the baby heifer shipping box. Not sure if Amazon or UPS is to blame for that, but it definitely wasn’t the headphones fault.

title: Fiddly, and a Fail for Android
text:
Perhaps I'm a Luddite, but I can't get these to behave on my Android phone. Much of the site is Apple-centric. Even the Android app has an Apple logo on it. I don't know if this product was tested on Android phones, but it leaves much to be desired.

The app continually prompts you to turn location on, and that's a battery drain which I refuse to leave on. Bluetooth should be all that's required. For the sake of getting through this process, I left location settings on, to see if I could get it to behave.

Volume when listening to YouTube was low. I found out how to disable the "max volume protection" feature in Android by going into the Developer Options. No change in volume after this hack.

My voice quality on the phone was reported to me by the listener as sounding distant and somewhat muffled.

Oh yes ... how about a decent manual that a human can read without a magnifying glass? After some searching (through Google, not the internal search function on the Dr. Dre site), I finally found instructions.

All in all, a fiddly fail, a waste of an hour and a half, and I'm returning these.

title: Secure fit and ok sound, but wouldn't buy again
text:
After using these headphones regularly for 3 months, I can only rate them 3 out of 5. They work well enough and I will continue to use them until they wear out, since I paid quite a lot for them. But, if I had known what I know now before purchasing, I would not have bought them.

Pros:
1. Secure fit: My top reason for choosing these headphones over other true wireless options was the ear clip. I have very small ears and there is no way airpod style earbuds would stay put, especially while exercising. These headphones are very secure and have never fallen off, even while running or doing yoga.
2. Comfortable: The ear clip can be molded to your ear shape, and the material is very smooth and comfortable to wear for hours at a time.
3. Stylish: Nicest-looking of all the ear clip headphones I've seen. Looks as stylish in person as in the pictures.
4. Physical buttons: The buttons are easy to control, even while running, since they are physical and not capacitive.
5. Battery: Lasts longer than expected, especially since you can always use them one at a time. Also charges up extremely quickly, which is very convenient.

Cons:
1. Weak Bluetooth: These headphones have a very short range before cutting out (less than halfway across my small apartment). They also have a weird directionality, so they lose connection if I turn my head certain ways. This is mainly a problem if I'm wearing them while doing yoga, which is frustrating because this was one of the main reasons I wanted to purchase true wireless headphones in the first place. They also have a hard time reconnecting after I remove them from my ears and put them back in again. At other times the Bluetooth connection just drops randomly.
2. Poor sound quality: Not a big audiophile here, but I do notice some real distortion in music and spoken audio when wearing these headphones. I expected them to be light on the lower tones due to their small size, so I wasn't too disappointed to find that was indeed the case. However, they even distort the voices of my favorite podcasters, making them sound nasal and grating. This is a pretty big drawback in a product this expensive, since even my most basic cheap headphones do not have this problem.
3. Fuzzy microphone: When I'm talking to friends on the phone through these headphones, they tell me my voice sounds muffled and muted. They also say ambient sounds, even quiet ones like my footsteps, interfere a lot with the sound. In fact, friends have such a hard time hearing me that I have decided I can't use these headphones for work calls, since the poor microphone quality is just too frustrating and unprofessional.

Overall, these headphones are functional and have a nice-looking and secure design, but they are not at all useful for taking professional calls (mic too fuzzy), wearing during certain exercise or wearing while walking around the house while my phone is charging (Bluetooth too weak). They make my favorite songs and podcasts sound distorted and tinny to the point that they are unenjoyable to listen to. I really wanted to like them due to the useful and comfortable ear clip, but sadly there are too many drawbacks and I cannot recommend them.

title: decent for a while, then sharp decline in functionality; ed: new ones work better
text:
I've had these for about a year now. They were fine at first-- decent sound, okay range, very acceptable battery life for my needs. The touch controls were always a little finicky and I think never quite worked like they were supposed to, but I chalked that up to the fact that these are decidedly not high end.

Now, after a year, the touch controls are completely nonfunctional. The only way to stop/start music, change volume, advance tracks, etc is through the computer or phone the earbuds are paired with. There are also some signal issues, where I can be sitting right next to the device the Tozos are paired with, and there is still occasional skipping in the audio, like they're struggling to maintain a consistent signal. I've reset them multiple times, but the issues persist.

For the price, it's not the end of the world, but it's still pretty upsettingly wasteful to need to buy a new set of earbuds after just a year. Unfortunately, I guess you do get what you pay for.

edit: originally posted Sept. 2022, updating Jan. 2023
Tozo reached out to me to apologize for the fact that my A1s had lost so much functionality, and to offer a free set of comparable earbuds (I guess the A1s were not available?). I ended up with a pair of T6 Tozo bluetooth earbuds, which are similar but not exactly the same. The earbuds themselves are slightly larger than the A1s and the case is a good bit larger. I have small ears, so the size difference does matter for me, but for adults with more normal-sized heads it probably won't be a huge issue. The controls are largely the same, although the touch responsiveness on the T6s seems to be a lot better than the A1s out of the box. The range seems similar to that of the A1s when I first got them, maybe a little bit better. The T6 case charges much faster than the A1 case did.

As with the A1s, the sound is not superlative but it's fine. They plug your ears pretty well so there is a bit of a mechanical noise cancelling thing going on, which can make them unpleasant to wear for any uses where you have to be speaking (since your own voice sounds super weird when you're wearing them). They are relatively inexpensive bluetooth earbuds, they aren't going to win any audiophile awards. But they are totally fine for my needs, which is just listening to music or podcasts while working around the house.

So far, the T6s work. All the touch controls are functioning and the blipping out of range is not nearly as constant and disruptive as it was when the A1s started to die. I received them in either late November or early December '22 and it's now January '23, so only time will tell how they hold up. But my initial experience with them is positive and I am very happy with Tozo for reaching out to at least attempt to address a product failure.

title: Buyer Beware - Lots of Connectivity Issues - Apple Can't Fix and Won't Replace
text:
I've had issues with the right earphone not charging properly. It was an intermittent issue, and of course, when I had them sent into Apple Repair, they said there was nothing wrong and sent them back.

Fast forward to month 10 after purchase. Now I can't pair my headphones at all with my phone or any other device. It's giving weird messages and errors. I setup a repair with Apple for the connectivity issue. I get an email saying I need to contact Apple because they need more information. Apparently, when trying to clean the earwax off of the earbud tips, the toothpick I was using tore the mesh/foam outside layer. So now they will not fix the connectivity issue until I pay $99 + tax out of my own pocket to replace the foam....That is an ABSURD price to pay to replace a piece of foam.

When I ask if they can just fix the connectivity issue and ignore the foam, I don't really care about that, I just want my headphones to connect like they are supposed to, they refuse saying, since they cannot guarantee the work on the connectivity issue without replacing the foam, they can't just fix the original issue under warranty. This is HORRIBLE customer service. If they cannot guarantee a perfect repair without replacing the torn inner-ear foam, I should be able to sign paperwork accepting that the repair for the original issue is no longer guaranteed given the customer's decision to forgo a separate issue. Just fix the original issue that I sent them in for, a piece of foam has ZERO impact on the connectivity issues I've had before and again now. A 10-year-old can figure out that the issues are unrelated.

I will NEVER buy any Beats product from Apple again since they have not worked properly from the get-go, creating an intermittent known issue that many others have reported through various online reviews, forums, and news articles. Time for me to switch back to Bose since Apple can't do a repair that is covered under warranty without trying to rip me off over a non-related issue.

text:
I like listening to audiobooks and calming music as I fall asleep. And I was using my AirPod Pros (AirPods Pro?), so I don't disturb my wife. That presented two problems. Firstly, AirPods are expensive, and I was always worried I would lose one or both in the bedding while traveling. Secondly, as nicely as they fit, they were a tad uncomfortable when I tried to lay on my side.

These earbuds address both of those problems. They are cheap enough that I only care a little if they get lost. And they are small enough that I barely notice them even when I'm lying on my side. So, for falling asleep, they are fine.

They are not as well suited for general use. The fit is good but not great and not nearly as great as my AirPods. Similarly, the sound could be better. That goes for playing stuff and using the built-in microphones for calls or audio recordings.

One thing I did like about them was the selection of included tips. You get five pairs total in different sizes and shapes. I used two slightly different size tips to accommodate my somewhat different size ears.

Finally, one big annoyance is how you control things like pause/play, volume, and other functions. Each earbud has a flat panel that you tap and press in various combinations. However, they don't work reliably, resulting in having to bop the side of your ears repeatedly until they eventually do what you want.

In summary, these work fine for when I'm going to sleep. When they inevitably break or get lost, I'll replace them with something the same size and perhaps a bit higher quality.

text:

I always hated when the wires would touch my skin when I worked out. It made it hard to wipe sweat off with the wires there. Also the controls are the same on both earbuds so you can use one earbud if you want you and keep the other in the case. I do this so I can here what is going on the office. There are sensors in the earbuds so it can detect which earbud is in your ear. It will only play music in the earbud that is placed in your ear! It will also stop playing if you pull the earbud out of your ear and will resume once you put it back in your ear and hit the pause/unpause button. I like this feature a lot!

They are not noise cancelling earbuds but if you want to, you can drown out the sound by turning up the volume.

The sound is way better than AirPods... hands down! The sound is very clear and clean. I would recommend these over AirPods any day. The only thing is AirPods case is a lot smaller. The beats earbud case is huge compared to it.

title: You Get What You Pay For
text:
Pay cheap, get cheap. First, I am surprised at all the purchases and positive reviews on this product which led me to purchase these earbuds.

The battery life on them is reasonably low compared to my other Bluetooth earbuds (AirPods and HiFuture). The case battery certainly drains faster than the other earbud cases.

I am unable to answer or hangup a phone call with these earbuds. It does, however, pause and unpauses my music. That's the only function touching them does.

When I have my earbuds already in my ear and I receive a phone call, the Bluetooth connection drops when I answer my phone. This only occurs with these earbuds. When I am on another phone call, and I receive another incoming call, the voice on the earbuds repeatedly states "Incoming call" while I'm in a phone conversation. It blocks out the sound of the person I'm listening to on the phone.

The fit on these is quite comfortable, and I like the compact size of them. However, I need the functionality to be there.

title: (Updated Review) Great physical design, terrible sound
text:
(Update after deciding not to return. Original review of complaint below the update):
After shopping for different headphones and seeing how many people were singing the praises of these Powerbeats Pros, I played with ear canal pieces and ear hooks, I finally got to a position eventually that gives me a fuller sound. So if anyone is upset with a thin sound with little bass, keep at it and you will probably be able to get it where you're happy with the sound. OK, so now I think I'm happy. For the rest, you can read my original mostly bad review below:

(Original Review):
I'm confused. I'm not an audiophile, but I notice and care about sound quality. I love an old pair of Powerbeats Wireless 3's I've been using a long time, but I was interested to try some new, supposedly improved headphones with some sweat and water resistance.
First, I got the new Powerbeats High-Performance Wireless. They seemed like the new and improved version of what I already had. I got them, and I couldn't believe how bad they sounded in comparison to my Wireless 3's. Returned them immediately.
I had it in my head that maybe it was just a bad pair or something, so I was considering trying buying another pair, but then I saw these Powerbeats Pros were on sale, so I figured it would be nice to go completely wireless and have maybe even better sound.
But they sound exactly like the other ones I returned! It's not just that I need to change the fitting. Even when I press the buds into my ear canals, it's terrible. Bass is weak, high end is unpleasantly tinny.
Yet these headphones are getting rave reviews everywhere--and not just customers, also tech websites. What is going on? They sound terrible! I switched right back over to my Wireless 3's to make sure I wasn't crazy or that my hearing wasn't going bad. They sound great. Rich, deep immersive sound. Switch back the Powerbeats Pro: sounds thin and terrible!
On the positive side, the design is great. Really comfortable in the ears. I love the buttons, way easier to operate than the Wireless 3's. The case design is nice with easy charging. Pairing was easy. The sensors that know when they go in and out of your ears worked perfectly.

They sound terrible!

title: There are very little things I hate more than these earbuds
text:
I bought these earbuds exactly 11 months ago, since I bought them they have been a complete disappointment, I felt a little pressured to like them just because of the brand and the amount of positive reviews they have, but I gave them 11 months of my life and I'm still giving them more time because of how expensive they were, but without a doubt, a complete waste of money.

1. It is noise cancelling, HOWEVER, the mic is actually noise enhancing somehow, so people can never hear me when I'm using them, my husband has a similar pair and being with him on the phone while he's just moving around or doing very minimal activities is headache inducing because of how much they enhance the background noise. I can't even walk by a bag of chips while being on the phone because the person on the other end of the line might pierce their ear drums!

2. The app is useless! Does nothing for the background noise situation.

3. They aren't consistent, they disconnect and reconnect and disconnect and reconnect, for no reason, doesn't matter what device they are connected to.

4. The sound quality is OKAY, just okay, definitely not worth $150. I've had $50 skull candy earbuds that sounded the same.

5. The battery life used to be okay, but now 11 months later. Its horrible, I have to charge it multiple times a day, and the battery life it reflects on my phone isn't always accurate, so I definitely thought they gave up on me a few times because it didn't show that the battery was low but they weren't working.

6. They are always falling out, its annoying but honestly its not the biggest gripe I have with them!

7. They break up, whenever I'm talking to someone or listening to something I just kind of hear it skipping, so if I'm face timing someone I can see their lips moving and sometimes can't hear them, again this is over multiple devices so its not a connection issue or a phone issue its an earbud issue. It does the same thing with videos as well. So it gives me raging migraines if I'm using them for too long.

In conclusion: I 've been annoyed by these earbuds for 11 months now, they felt like a bad purchase the second I bought them and I should have just returned them right then and there, but lesson learned! Just because its a big brand and is expensive and 'looks' like its worth the money, doesn't mean it is.
