title: Directions are included - don't miss them!
text:
There are a number of reviews complaining about inability to turn off/on the headphones without putting them in the case. I think probably those reviewers did what I almost did - threw out the directions. There is a small pamphlet tucked into the packaging and it is really easy to overlook. But it has all the shortcuts to do stuff!
1 tap on either headphone = pause/play
double tap on left = go back a track
double tap on right = skip to next track
press and hold left/right = volume up/down
press and hold when no music is playing = turns off (or on) that headphone (you need to do both sides)

I got these so I could listen to music while mowing my lawn. I have a lawn mowing headset (that does not play audio) to muffle the sound of the mower, but I could still hear the mower pretty loudly and was hoping that I wouldn't have any problems hearing the music over my riding mower. I don't! The music comes in loud and clear, and the only problem is that my mowing lines aren't as straight because sometimes I do a little seated dancing while I mow if a particularly good song comes on.

title: Good Value if They Last
text:
$250 is the obvious deterrent to these headphones. Are they a good value?

Summary: you're basically pitting them against the Airpods if you're an Apple user and want that convenience, so I'd say there's a good enough sound and battery improvement to justify the premium in that comparison. They also don't have that "There's Something About Mary" look to them. Some of y'all will get this.

Sound: They sound really good, but they're not the best in-ear headphones I've heard, and some over-hear headphones blow them away. They're equalized quite well and I don't find them to be bass heavy. In fact, some of my favorite guitar solo playlists have really shined with these for the high notes. Very good range even if the mids are sometimes lost.

Comfort: Strange to get on and off at first, but I haven't had any discomfort for long-term use. I forget they're there easily. Stay in extremely well.

Battery: best I've ever used. Have only charged up the case three times in the month I've had them.

Case: it's pretty big and at first felt like cheap plastic. I think the hinge is where it just feels cheap. It has grown on me because it makes a wood knocking noise when you close it so if it wasn't for the hinge I'd actually think it was a premium build now.

Features: I use hey Siri and love it. The easy pairing is great and switching between devices is great. The range is spectacular. I can leave my phone inside and wash my car outside with no hiccups all while taking calls via SIri. The mic works well and I've heard no complaints about wind etc. There is no companion app or dedicated equalizer which seems a bit lacking.

Gripes: don't try lying on your side with these. At one point one earbud became unpaired and I had to do the non-Apple pairing of holding the button with them both in the case to pair them. Once you've switched it to a device once it'll assume you want to transition to it all the time. Say you're jamming on your phone and want to watch a video on your iPad sans sound, like Twitch etc., it'll skip you on over interrupting your music.

Value: wow, these are expensive. They're ALMOST class competitive in sound and the hands-free voice assistant for Apple was a must when I shopped headphones this round. I'm very much enjoying them and if they're going strong in three years I think they're absolutely worth the premium over Airpods. If you don't use hey Siri your mileage may vary.

title: Worth every penny -- best investment of 2020
text:
I hesitated A LOT about purchasing these because the price is obviously high. Yet, having invested on my beloved Beats is a redeeming quality of this year of awful. I previously tried about every wireless earphones in the market, from low to high price. They all let me down one way or another--bad connectivity, poor battery life, ear pain, wind murmurs on my music, poor grip, too much grip, less than great sound. And, VERY important for runners, these high-quality beauties give me the best sound without falling on the overrated obsession with noise cancellation that has made many earphones feel too tight and painful (like bursting something on the ear canal when they come out) and it's quite a dangerous feature if you run in a city (or anywhere where cars and moving creatures exists), as I do regularly in NYC.

In summary:
--Best battery life, haven't run out once in 8 months and I wear them daily for hours of music and podcasts outdoors and indoors.
--Gorgeous, ergonomic, comfortable design.
--Amazing grip that never feels tight and never lets down -- can run, jump, bike, do HIIT, barre, Pilates, etc. and never fails.
--Wonderful, smooth, crisp, warm, involving, impeccable sound that doesn't fall for the noise cancellation fad and allows for safe running, walking and commuting (remember when we commuted?) anytime anywhere.
--Easiest device to set up, if such a seamless minute can be called "set up".
--Solid fast charging box -- could be a nicer color frankly, design-wise not my favorite element, but it's solid (it felt a couple of times and nothing outside or inside changed) and the charging is absurdly fast.
--Perfect for calls, never loses the connection, the sound is great both ways -- or all ways if in a group video call.

En fin, if you can make the effort, these aren't going to let you down. Stay well and safe!

title: Absolutely horrible sound. So disappointed.
text: I was really excited to receive these headphones because of all the positive reviews. I have several different wireless headphones ranging from Bose, Beats, AirPods, etc....I also own a pair of powerbeats3, which I don’t use at all due to the fact that they’re extremely uncomfortable. The powerbeats Pro are not only just as uncomfortable as the powerbeats3, but the sound quality is absolutely laughable. I’m not sure how there are so many positive reviews for sound on these headphones, because the sound is awful. I literally get a better sound profile out of a $20 pair of Sony headphones I bought for my son at CVS. Either people don’t actually know quality sound, or this is their first pair and they think this is what quality sounds like. Without writing a long essay, the two main things that are wrong with the sound are: absolutely no bass, and very low volume output. I agree with some of the other reviews that state these were rushed to market. I firmly believe that. I mean I own about 10 different pairs of higher end headphones, and these BY FAR are the worst. It’s not even close. If you actually own any other wireless headphones that are in the same price range as these, you will be SEVERELY disappointed with the sound quality. About the only positive aspect of these headphones is the battery life.....they do last quite a bit, and the new chip in them, makes connections very smooth and seamless. I was really hoping these beats would be good as I need a reliable pair for riding bike, that won’t keep moving around on me, and these were definitely secure, but I just couldn’t get over how awful they sound, and how uncomfortable they are. I literally have to take them off after 5 mins because my ear is killing me. These sound like a $20 pair, not a $250 pair. If you have AirPods already, trust me, stick with those as they are far superior. If you don’t own AirPods, I would choose them over the beats pro any day of the week. Guess I’ll keep using my AirPods and beats x for now....

text:
I bought these a few months ago and after about 20 minutes I knew I was going to write a review but wanted to wait a bit to get a good handle on them.

I've logged hundreds of hours now and it seems I continue to like these more and more.
Audiobooks, podcasts, or YouTube videos make up 99% of what I listen to through these.
Turning off and on automatically when you pull them out and put them in has lead me to realize that I don't like power buttons. I've always been one to truly value when companies remove needless steps between me and what I'm trying to do as I am a very impatient person. These feel so streamlined, If I want to listen to something I just take them out of the case, insert them in and hit play on either bud, after that they pause and resume on their own on removal and insertion and it works flawlessly.
Battery life is outstanding, they claim up to 9 hours, I work a 10 hour shift and these have never even once died on me before my shift was over, hell, I think I've even gotten 11 or 12 hours out of them. But music does tend to consume more battery than what I listen to so that's probably why I get such good battery life. In any case, these charge so fast it wouldn't matter anyway though. The battery life and charge speed of the case are amazing as well.

text:
I bought this mostly so that I could go work out or go running without getting tangled in wires. To that extent, this works great. Fast charge and it has a great battery.

However, the cons to this are vast and I think with the price they're charging, they should have made a better product.

The audio quality isn't great as there really aren't any lower tones or ways to adjust the sound quality in the earbuds. I'm assuming that they sacrificed that so that you can use only one of the earbuds similar to an earpiece when on the phone or driving. For any sound that is in the talking range or higher in range, the quality is decent. An example would be if you were listening to Ariana Grande, you might find the quality of her voice the same as if you were using other headphones but you would definitely notice the erasure of the bass/percussion in the background.

The other thing is that it hurts. I agree with the reviewers that say that putting the earbuds on it definitely required a period of adjustment even with the smallest bud. The way it's curved is really meant for a bigger ear and sometimes the plastic components do sort of scrape against the ear. I have gotten used to it and it no longer hurts but the first 3-5 times I put it on, I definitely immediately wanted to take them off.

And the last thing -- I don't think these earbuds were made with glasses-wearing people in mind. There's simply no way to adjust how it fits onto your ear and this fits really close to your head which means that I have had my glasses fall off or had to constantly adjust my glasses. Or I have had to adjust the earbuds which sometimes means it fitting really poorly.

Overall, this product can be improved. Would I recommend you buy it? Probably not. There are or should be better options out there at a lower price point.

title: Good, but has its pros and cons.
text:
UPDATE: Second day, I had connection issues in my right ear. I noticed it stopped playing at the grocery store. Had to go home and put them back in the case to reconnect both headphones.

I’m giving a fair review on several areas that matter to Bluetooth headphone lovers. I’m basing this on other beats products I have owned in the past (Solo and Urbeats). I am also comparing this to first impressions from opening the box to using it. I will update if changes occur.

Opening the box:
Box was simple to open.

Rankings:
-Battery life 10/10: The battery life on beats products are usually amazing. These are none the less. Compared to other Bluetooth headphones I’ve had in the past, the battery will last you awhile.

-nose cancellation 10/10—I couldn’t hear the cleaning crew come in and vacuum our hallway in our apartment. Once I took them off, I remembered they were there.

Phone calls 10/10–I FaceTimed my brother and he said he headed me clearly without turning up his audio on his end. He also didn’t hear any static noises or background noises. This was an issue I had with the Beats Solo wireless I owned.

Comfort 5/10–I had to change the silicone to the smallest ones. After two hours of use, the wrap parts began to feel like they were pressure on my head and irritated my ears.

Durability 10/10-I tried moving up and down, jumping jacks, and shook my head. They won’t come off!

Portability 3/10–I wasn’t expecting the case to be as bulky as it was. This will not fit in average size pockets (for women, not sure about men). Best to leave it in a bag or a jacket pocket.

Music sound 3/10–this is where I was disappointed the most, considering I owned other products. Usually you hear the bass and sound on the lowest iPhone volume. I have to turn this up to halfway to even get wind. Pretty shocking. I’ve had cheaper headphones that got sound out better.

Specs 8/10 Truly Bluetooth. Love I can remove it and music pauses and it syncs with my iPhone. What I don’t like is that the headphones have to be in the case to connect. I can’t just take them out and connect them. Something I’ll had to adjust to.

Was it worth $199 + tax ($220)?

text:
I've had quite a few different true wireless earbuds. I started with the Jlab Air and then the Galaxy Buds. I really liked both but was looking for something with better bass and a clearer, louder sound quality because I listen to music all day at the warehouse I work at.

Powerbeats Pro sold me on the amazing battery life of 9 hours. I was a little worried because they are designed for iOS. I didn't want to lose a ton of features on my Galaxy 10. I did some research and a few sites said that the ear detection for pausing when taking out the buds was lost on android, that single earbud listening was available on iOS only, and that general connection issues were present on android.

I've found none of these issues. The ear detection is better than what I have on the Galaxy Buds which are specifically made for Galaxy s10. These are quick to pause as soon as one is removed and start right back up when replaced. I can listen with a single earbud which was super important for safety in my warehouse environment. Connecting to the bluetooth was a breeze and as easy as connecting any other device.

The Beats app for android doesn't offer an equalizer but it will tell me what battery level my case and buds are at, separately.

Sound is better than both the Jlab Air and the Galaxy Buds in general. The Powerbeats Pro feel more secure than both of the previous ones I've tried. My Jlab would fall out often, and while I never had a Galaxy Bud fall out, they still felt looser than the fit with the Powerbeats Pro. They charge pretty fast too where the others took quite a bit of time and didn't hold as much of a charge as the Powerbeats.

Overall, I'm very pleased with my purchase and how well they work on android for me.

title: More of a 4.5 than a 4
text:
Short Version: Not the greatest sound but they fit amazingly in my big ears for working out.

Long Version: Have had these for a bit now and I can say that these deserve more of a 4.5 than a 4 but I’ll give it a 4 since I can’t do half scores.
I bought these when I started working out and notice that my AirPod Pros were not able to stay in my ears at all when running, jumping, lifting, etc. My ears are fairly large so that might have to do with it… anyways. I did the whole “buy attachments for the AirPods” thing but it was becoming a hassle taking the attachment off putting it back on and it was just a pain.
Setting these up was painless with an Apple device: Open the case and put my iPhone right next to it and it immediately recognized it. I had these out of the Amazon box and in my ear in 5 minutes and it can be an even shorter time if you already know how to put these on your ear (note: I didn’t know so it took me a minute).
First impressions playing music: Not as good as Airpods audio wise. Airpods sound more balanced and on Beats the bass sounds overdone. Messing with the EQ fixes this but still Airpods sound better.
If you’re looking for the best of noise cancelling, you won’t find it here. I could here gym equipment, people talking, slightly hear the gym music in the background, etc. Audio controls on the earbuds themselves are what you’d expect from a modern audio device (one click pauses, two skips, etc) but nothing super innovative. The case is a bit bulky too so it’s gonna be difficult to fit in jean/pant pockets compared to a pair of AirPods or something.
These Beats almost made my return list… until I worked out with them.
The fit is phenomenal. They don’t move. I jump rope often for 10 mins and they won’t budge. Running fast on a treadmill won’t make them move, putting my head sideways, up and down, left, right nothing. They work exactly how I needed them to. Plus they are water-resistant so sweat doesn’t affect these at all.

Sound on these Beats may not be phenomenal or life changing but for people with bigger ears or ears that don’t fit loose buds like AirPods, these are a necessity and you can’t go back once you start wearing them. Sure you could get headphones that will stay on and sound better but I like the convenience of having these in my gym bag ready to go. And the charge lasts long. I only use these for working out so they’ve lasted me 2.5-3 weeks without charging.
I recommend these for people who find tradition buds won’t fit your ear and want something reliable. I don’t recommend this for someone who wants the best of the best audio quality and who has the option to have other well fitting earbuds.

title: 5 stars in 4 areas of importance - GREAT product
text:
I did a lot of research before purchasing these. I read all of the bad reviews first, then worked my way up to the good reviews. I have owned several pairs of Bluetooth earbuds and these by far are the best. I have now had them for just over 30 days, and I intentionally waited to post a review until I had plenty of data.

Features that were important to me were: Comfort, ability to pair each bud separately, range, and most of all battery life.

As to comfort, I was worried about the eat loops at first as I saw mixed reviews, but to be honest, I love them! They stay in place without falling out or slipping. I wear them for 8-12 hour shifts and they don’t bother me at all.

I only wear 1 at a time because I have to talk to customers from time to time, so being able to pair them separately is a plus.

The range is far better than any war bud I have owned prior to this. I can walk to the back of my store and not lose signal.

As to battery life, this is the best part. In a 10 hour shift, I don’t have to change or charge my ear bud. I’ll even have roughly 20% left at the end of my shift. When I do have to charge the bud, it’s really fast. I can go from 20% to full in just over 30 minutes.

I’m VERY happy with this purchase. I highly recommend this product. They were worth the $ I spent on them.

title: Best Beats yet
text:
I work out a lot. When people ask me what is the most important piece of fitness equipment, my ranking is 1) shoes, and 2) Beats wireless.
I’ve used (and completely worn out) Powerbeats 2 and 3 and these ones are my favorite so far. I have a hard time finding earphones, most kinds either don’t fit securely in my ears or they chafe. I originally tried Powerbeats because I wanted the over-ear hooks to hold them in place. These work great.
Big upgrade from the last model as well: I love being truly wireless. The wire between the previous Powerbeats would catch on my hair or clothes, sometimes enough to pull one of the earphones out. Not anymore!
I also like how they power on and pair automatically instead of doing it manually every single time.
The only possible negative with these is that they don’t block out all ambient noise (although that may be because I use the tiniest rubber tips, YMMV). You could probably wear them jogging outside and still hear the traffic.
Overall I’m thrilled with the purchase. Definitely worth the price.

title: Sound great but charging is a nightmare
text:
I love the sound quality, but keeping them charged is a huge hassle. If you don't seat them perfectly within the case they don't charge, and any movement - for example, gently picking up the charging case from the kitchen table and setting it down on the counter - can break the charge connection.

This problem is exacerbated by the headphones' "always on unless charging" setting, which means that as soon as you break that headphone-case connection (again, maybe by picking your charging case up from the kitchen table and setting it down somewhere else), the earbud boots up and starts drawing power. So when you pull out your headphones some morning to work out, you find that one of the two was on all night and is now at 2% power. This has happened to me at least 75 times in the year and a half that I've had mine. In fact I'm writing this review now while I wait for one of them to charge up.

I suspect I have a lemon and that others aren't as finnicky, but apple told me they were working perfectly when I tried to get them to repair my set.

People speak highly of the AirPods but I hear they can be uncomfortable and there isn’t much noise cancellation, so with that being said the Beats Powerbeats Pro are the way to go. title: Wow..Tozo has done it again. This time for a price that's a no brainer...Love this  unit...A++
text: I was looking at the Bose quiet comfort brand and earbuds  until I got the Tozo. Bose had lots of issues with pairing, connectivity, not a great fit and hardly any customer service to fix issues. Just read all these reviews on Amazon and you will be upset after spending two hundred bucks. Now with Tozo, these guys have mastered the headphones. As soon as you open the case and remove them, they literally pair and then connect to the computer or phone. It's almost instant. title: Pretty Incredible All Things Considered
text:
Immediately stunned by the sound quality once I got a good fitment.
That is absolutely the key. Get a good fitment. Sometimes it takes two different tips, one for each ear, in order for you to get that fitment. But just put the 2 minutes in and do it.
Secondly. Garbage in = Garbage out.
Get some good MP3's, Wav, or HD FLAC files, a good DAC and your ears will reward you.
I'm amuzed that I'm able to get this kind of quality for under a Jackson.
It's dumbfounding. But you need to appreciate how technology has taken that kind of leap in the last 15 years or so.
Bluetooth has made leaps and bounds in reliability and sound quality from where it was even 6 or 7 years ago.
Now these aren't the be-all-end-all by any means. There are going to be better IEM's of course. But I'm listening to an 8 year old iPod Touch Gen. 4 with a 2.1 codec that I just today found in my basement, and these very inexpensive buds right now. And you know what? It sounds great!
I'll hook these to my S22 Ultra as well and see how well it works with the new 5.3 Codec and PowerAmp Pro. I'm sure with the additional EQ features, extremely high playback rate encoding and 64bit processing as opposed to the 32 bit processing and no music player other than the default (and no EQ possiblities) available on the iPod, I'll be even more impressed.
Look, these are very lightweight to the point you'll maybe even forget you have them in. They are probably easily lost, so pay attention. They also won't have the battery life and next tier sound quality that you might expect by jumping up another $100 or so. But in this bracket, you really can't complain.
With this many satisfied users (nearly 70% 5 stars) , you either have a bad set, a bad fit, bad playback equipment, bad reference tracks, or bad ears if you can't get a nice sound from these.
So for anyone so cheap as to be contemplating taking a chance on these, just do it.
You'll be rewarded far beyond your investment. How often can you get anything these days that brings you even 1 hour of happiness, let alone the lifespan of the product (that remains to be seen) that has a warranty anyway.
Do it.

title: Constant connectivity issues
text:
I've had these for over 8 months and constantly use them for around the house and intense sweaty workouts in the gym.

When I first got them after wearing them for very long periods of time (over 2 hours at least) my ears would hurt and I'd have to take them out, but after a few a week or so this went away.

They stay on very well and overall fit is decent, there may have been a few times they "fell out" of my ear if I was at an awkward angle cleaning or something but they sometime have to be adjusted but 99% they're sturdy in that regard.

The BIGGEST issue with these is they connectivity is garbage. For mine, I have to put on the left earbud on FIRST, wait to hear the connectivity noise, THEN put on my right earbud. If you put the right one on first, sometimes the left one won't connect and you have to put them back into the case. Wait a few seconds and retry, sometimes this would take a few tries which is just annoying as this happens at least once or twice a day since I bought them.

Also, when I'm cooking, idk if there's radio interference or something but occasionally in the kitchen it'll just pause my sound or disconnect completely. I'm not super knowledgable around the science behind it but I imagine whenever I'm cooking my electric oven, microwave, and other equipment is interfering with the Bluetooth which is super annoying.

Why I'm writing this review is one day I was pretty far from my phone and put my earbuds on and they wouldn't connect so I tried putting them in the case. It still wasn't working. So I tried a full unpair and repairing (going into Bluetooth settings on my iPhone and pressing "forget this device") as I've done this at least once or twice before. Guess what, NOW IT WON'T CONNECT TO ANY DEVICE. I've tried EVERYTHING short of contacting Apple Support/taking to the Apple Store (which I may/may not) so now the case just blinks white and doesn't do anything. I reset it, I cleaned the connectors, I've reset my phone, everything. No other device will even notice it.

These could've been great headphones but they've been nothing but an expesive piece of junk. One problem after another CONSTANTLY. Also, the case is HUGE. I thought it was no big deal bc I'd use it mostly at home and maybe the gym. No, they're bulbous and such an awkward size. And if you clean out the ear tips you may damage the earbud itself. Waste of plastic and electronics.

title: I had hopes
text: So let me start by saying the build quality of these in ears and their case are top of the line. They feel and look very high quality. The tactile feel of the buttons are perfect. The position of the buttons did not, however, work for me. This is not a critical comment but merely a statement of fact about what I needed. I often wear my in ears when I am sleeping and I am a side sleeper. When your head presses on the pillow it activates the buttons leaving you with either full volume or no volume(if that is how you set up your button functionality). Again, not a negative comment, just a limitation for how I use mine. Now, to why I only gave them two stars for sound quality. Some background. I own a pair of over the ear Sony WH-100XM3 over the ear headphones. I also own an old set of Skullcandy Method in ears and Raycon Everydays. These are what I judge these Beats against. First of all, nothing comes close to the sound quality of the Sonys. They are a phenomenal set of headphones with a very robust supporting app and I recognize that and take it into account when looking for new in ears. When I first received the Beats I downloaded the app and updated the firmware so everything was up to date. When I played them they were very flat in bass response. Almost tinny if that makes sense. As I dug into the app I noticed they were in noise cancelling mode so I turned that off. Marginally better bass response. So I dug around in the app to try and find an equalizer to adjust. Nothing...So I went into Apple Music and attempted to adjust the equalizer and didn't have much success making the sound better. I was so disappointed I went out and bought a pair of Skullcandy Indy Evos to see if I could get better sound out of a set of in ears half the price....and I did. They were much better sounding. Nothing approaching the Sonys but much better than the Beats. The reason I bought these was to replace my Raycons that I dropped on our wood floor making them sound like they had blown speakers(guess I jarred something loose inside the buds.) I loved the Raycons but that was the second issue I had with a set of Everydays so I won't buy the brand again. I'm too hard on them. With that said, I believe if I would have dropped these Beats I don't think it would have affected them at all. The build quality is very good. They feel incredibly solid and the case feels the same. Unfortunately their sound quality just isn't what I(and I stress the I here. Many people have given these high ratings) would expect from a $120 set of in ears. I hope this helps someone. Again, these Beats have received high ratings so maybe I am just the outlier. Good luck.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

To start the noise cancellation is not very good. You can hear hissing that’s no bueno, the transparency mode is even worse it sounds like you’re hearing the world through a really old speaker and it’ll make you dizzy.

So I use these in normal mode. That being said the sound is nice, not impressive but nice. They’ll sit kind of snug when they’re in your ear but the buds are huge! They’re heavy so they’ll fall/slip out of your ear if you walk, talk, chew, run, exercise or they’re in your ear for longer than 5 minutes.

The charge time is not very good. I find myself having to recharge the case even after minimal use. Unfortunately I have not tracked the usage/batter life very closely but compared to AirPod pros it’s significantly less. The headphones and case combined.

Putting them in is a small nuisance because the shape of the case and the headphones aren’t very pronounced. So I find myself sticking the headphones on opposite sides.
Maybe this is just me not playing with blocks enough as a kid.
I got these for about $100 on sale. I can’t imagine paying more or full price for this. Simply not worth it. They’re wish headphones with a premium logo.

Remember this brand is owned by Apple and they will not compete with their own products so just buy the AirPods. It’ll be worth it.

title: Almost useless....
text:
I will start with the positive because there is a big one. The sound quality on these headphones is phenomenal. Rich, full sound only interrupted by Siri and that's easily muted. The sound quality is fantastic on these. I wish I could review these on sound quality alone because if I could, they'd be five stars. Sadly, I've had these for a while, and after some actual testing in real life exercise environments I can give a true review and it ain't good.

First off, let's talk about the housing, it seems neat, and compact, but, the way that the earbuds sit within the housing means they are constantly touching, and with nothing to charge them but two chintzy prongs per earbud, it means your earbuds aren't charged a lot. Which, leads into my second gripe. The battery life. The battery life on these are not great, as a distance runner having your earbuds start dying after a pretty quick 10k is less than ideal and not quite as advertised on these earbuds. That's IF the earbuds are charged in the first place which, 6 out of 10 times they are not, or the left one is charged but the right one is dead, and there sadly, is no alternative method to charging your earbuds except to place them in their housing and pray they don't shift at all and the chintzy two prongs stay connected to each earbud long enough to charge them. For earbuds pushing $300 to have the whole ensemble derailed by poor charging design is pretty unfortunate. It's gotten to the point I hardly use them because every time I get ready for a run I go to grab them after charging the housing, and one of the earbuds is dead from not charging. This upsets me not just because of the price point, but because the sound quality is phenomenal on these and I do enjoy using them on the rare occasions the stars align and I am able to use them. Beats fooled me years ago with overear headphones when they first came out and were overpriced junk, they got me again with these unreliable earbuds. Will not be buying Beats again and I cannot in good conscience recommend these to anyone.

title: Always be on guard
text:
1. I was the guy that always mocked others for buying Beats because of the price.
2. AirPods were always good enough for me.

With that outta the way you now know where I’m coming from. I don’t like spending a ton of money on headphones. Heck, spending $150 on my AirPods was brutal but overtime I saw the importance of convenience. I quickly became hooked and took them with me everywhere, wore them through just about every activity I did, and quickly realized their long term value.

Over time I would accidentally wash them and with enough accidental spin cycles they eventually bit the dust and stopped working.

This brings me to these Beats. For the longest I was trying to find a cheap alternative on amazon to my AirPods. After a few cheap buys ($30-$50 range) I concluded nothing will quite match what I had. The convenience, the sound, the comfort, the seamless integration of Apples software communicating between the AirPods and my phone. Then out of the blue I see a YouTube video unveiling these new Powerbeats Pro. I instantly became hooked! I had to have them!

They were everything I was looking for in an upgraded version of AirPods. I’m a runner and when I’m not doing long workouts I’ll do short high intensity workouts from sprints to Olympic lifting. My AirPods held up just fine and always stayed in place. So upon seeing these Beats that was my first concern. Then I noticed they have a loop around them that sits over your ear. If your into high intensity workouts this is exactly what you need, a sense of security. AirPods design were perfect in that they weighed themselves down which never allowed them to fall out. So in order for ear plugs like these to successfully stay in place, you need a loop to hold them around your ears.

I just went for my first jog with these and let’s just say they’ve exceeded my expectations. They felt firm in place the entire time. Not once did I have to adjust them. The sound is so clean and crisp you almost get lost in your own world. Which brings me to the title of this review, always be on guard.

With AirPods they weren’t plugged into your ear canal therefore you could still hear a small amount of wind/ambient noise to maintain a sense of awareness with your surroundings. With these Beats you can’t hear any wind, any ambient sound, nothing! Only music! This can be both good and bad. The good is the sound quality that I previously mentioned. The bad is you need to be extra, EXTRA, aware of your surroundings so that nothing happens to you or others. Now, instead of hearing your surroundings you have to constantly be aware of your surroundings because you WON’T hear the dog coming, nor the car coming, nor the person behind you or in front of you. You’re sense of awareness will now be cut short by one of your primary senses (hearing).

All in all just be smart with every activity you do and you’ll enjoy these as much as I do. As for the price..if these last anywhere near as long as my AirPods did (minus my accidental spin cycles) then I’m ok with spending $249 because I know they’ll last the long haul.

title: One of my best purchases
text:
I had a bad experience with the original Powerbeats, but found myself drawn to the Powerbeats Pro. I contemplated getting either those or AirPods. Despite many people saying it wasn’t a problem, I didn’t like that the AirPods simply went into my ear without any way to secure them. I lift weights, and the last thing I wanted was for one of them to pop out at an inopportune time. I also didn’t like the fact that there was no volume control on the AirPods. The Powerbeats Pro allow me to adjust the volume from BOTH earpieces. That way if my right hand is occupied, I can adjust the volume with my left hand, or vice versa. Here are my pros and cons.

Pros: #1 These headphones last a pretty long time on a full charge. They don’t last as long if you’re using them for a phone call, but if you’re simply listening to music, you will get 5+ hours out of them. #2 Again, I love that I can adjust the volume, start, stop, repeat or skip a song directly on my earpiece, rather than having to reach for my phone, which is often buried at the bottom of my bag. #3 I’m sure the AirPods do this as well, but I love how the Powerbeats Pro integrate with Siri once you allow the right settings. I don’t even need to touch my phone or my earpiece, I can simply say “Hey Siri” and ask the time, the weather, what a word means, have someone on my contact list called or messaged, etc.

Cons: #1 I wish the earpieces were truly adjustable. They don't come with different sizes of inner-ear pads, and the over-the-ear hooks don’t adjust as much as I would like. At times they can feel uncomfortable and somewhat painful. #2 I learned the hard way that despite it being an added burden, it might be a good idea to take the charging case with you when you leave the house. I’ve been out while all of a sudden, one of my headphones stops working despite having a substantial charge. The only way to reconnect both pieces is to place them back in the carrying case and re-pair. #3 Sometimes if you don’t sit the headphones onto the charging prongs correctly, one (or both) might not properly charge. That can be very frustrating when you’re ready to use them. When you go to Bluetooth settings on your phone and first connect them, sometimes a box will pop up letting you know how much power is left in the case, as well as the charges on the earpieces. If you pull only one of the earpieces out, it will tell you the charge of each piece individually. Unfortunately I don’t always receive that dialog box, which is very helpful.

Overall, I absolutely LOVE my Powerbeats Pro, and they are certainly one of my favorite and most satisfactory purchases. In fact, I love them so much that I own two pairs of headphones and alternate between both. I like throwing one into my gym bag as a backup, just in case I need it.

title: Excellent for listening to music, but not great for talking on the phone
text:
I read multiple reviews and questions and answers before I purchased these.
The sound you hear is excellent. Ear fit is really good and adjustable. They don't look stupid and they stay secure.
Now on to call quality. Like I said, what you what you hear is excellent, but what your end caller hears is a different story. Slightly muffled, a little like being in a tunnel or having your mouth slightly covered when you talk. You can still be heard but for the price you pay for these I'm surprised its not better. I am on multiple conference calls a day, and if that is your life too, you know its hard enough to be heard when people are talking. I have a cheap Jabra that I current use and the call quality is 100 times better. HOWEVER, the Jabra constantly disconnects from my IPhone where the Powerbeats stay connected. So take the good with the bad. If you are ok that you sound slightly muffled on a call, then these are an excellent choice for you. I am still currently deciding if I am keeping them or not. I did contact Apple and walk through the support of these. They tried a couple of tricks of disconnecting and resetting, but the sound stayed the same. title: They hurt my ear
text:
I’ve loved beats since they came out years ago and have been a customer since. I upgraded my Powerbeats 3 to these pro models because I wanted the latest and greatest and my AirPods don’t stay in my ear when I’m working out so naturally I figure these would do wonder for me. The sound quality is good and I love more bass in my music which is a personal choice. The downside to this however is the design so let me explain.

After the rubber tip that goes in your ear there is a hard round piece. This is the part that hurts me. Comparing them to my Powerbeats 3 which still work for me these pro models hurt a lot due to that design. It may be my ear which is why I’m not complete bagging on them but it hurts having them on for at least 10 minutes let alone an hour for working out. If you have that problem I would consider looking at other options or maybe some AirPods Pro. I’m bummed that I won’t be keeping these because I was excited to use them and have a pair.

Update:
I really liked these powerbeats so I loosened up the ear hook to see if that would lessen or take away the pain I was feeling in my ear. So far that seems to have done the trick but I will update once I do use them for about an hour or so. Fingers crossed!

Final update:
I got them to work for me! Turns out I had to loosen up the ear hook so that it wouldn’t hurt my ears and I’ve been using them the whole week with no issues. Great but. The only reason I gave it a 4 star was because I wish Apple had included more bass in them like the Powerbeats 3. You can still hear bass but not like the Powerbeats. They still sound good but I’m more of a bass guy but it’s not terrible and would recommend these for working out. I use AirPods Pro for daily use.

title: very good but not perfect
text:
These are slick and robust but flawed, too.

I use wireless earbuds for very sweaty and reasonably intense exercise. I mountain bike and an earhook design was important for me. I don’t want to be looking for a tiny earbud out in the woods.

Previously I've used the various super cheap offerings here on amazon. They’ve performed reasonably well but never last more than a few weeks. But they’re cheap and easy to replace.

This time I decided to take a chance and splurge on a premium product. The beats are definitely expensive but looked to be exactly what I needed.

They indeed exude quality. Pairing with iPhone seamless and fast. Fit comfortable and secure. Connection stable. Sound a little tinny at first but improved dramatically with better sealing ear tip. Overall they sound pretty good, considering what they are. My ears and jaw start to get fatigued after about 2hr. They don’t block extenal noise very well. Siri usage and phone calls very pleasant experience. Most importantly they felt and sounded great during an extended run and biking in the woods.

Here is what ruined it for me, though: the charging dock is finicky. You will think the earbud is seated and charging but it's not. And the battery drains mysteriously. So on two occasions I went to use the buds and found one or both too depleted to use. Fast charge gave me enough to get by, but it was aggravating nonetheless. Perusing the help forums this seems to be common and maybe even expected.

These are slick, but honestly you get 80% of this performance (but none of the robustness) in a $20 pair of buds.
For this price point I expect perfection so I'm sending these back.

text:
The fit of these Beats earbuds are about the best thing going for them unfortunately. They do not slip or fall out during the most vigorous activities. The sound quality is decent, but there is no active noise cancellation which diminishes the overall "feel." The fit and sound quality merit about half the monetary asking prices for these earbuds (well below my expectation of an Apple product.)

The biggest negative of these earbuds is the charging. They are intended to charge when inserted into their case. There are magnets that attempt to seat the buds into the correct charging position. This is a great concept, I suppose, but the execution does not meet expectation. I have to seat and re-seat the earbuds each time I place them back into the dock. It takes several attempts to get both buds charging (and if you so much as bump the case, you risk unseat one or both.)

I cannot recommend the earbuds, and I would suggest looking at another model and/or brand.

title: good but lots of cons
text:
These are the best earphones I’ve ever tried, including more expensive Bose earphones. But there are definitely many cons.

-I agree with those who say the midrange is lacking in quality.
-As with most earphones, the sound quality decreases dramatically depending on what size ear cups you use on the earphones. The powerbeats pro totally wireless come with about 4 different sizes, but, personally, only one makes these earphones any good in terms of sound quality, i.e. the largest size.
-I find these hard to put on. Part of the reason why this is the case is because the buttons that control it are pretty much all the places you want to put your fingers in trying to put these on your ears. It’s very hard to try and put these on without accidentally pressing a button and music starting to play prematurely.
-I had read before receiving these that they do get uncomfortable after a while, and they really do—especially in one ear (for me, it’s the right ear). My ears will also start itching after a while, and I have to take these out to scratch and then struggle to put them back on (see my previous point).
-You better stick with and use your case with these, because these could be really easy to lose and the ear cups can easily come off if you are very mobile. I have to fight the urge to just place these on my bed sometimes, knowing they can easily go bye bye that way. I don’t love the idea of always needing to carry a case around with these or always leaving them in my ears just to make sure I can keep up with them. This is where wired earphones that don’t have changeable cups are better.
-Because they operate via bluetooth, often when you go to the next song the first second or two of the song is cut off. I have the same issue with some other bluetooth speakers, and it’s something that caused me to stop using them. Very annoying.

Those are my biggest cons with them, although there are others that are probably more specific annoyances to me.

Pros:
-If you have an iPhone or iPad, it will show on the screen how much charge your case and your earphones have. Love this feature.
-The charge is pretty long-lasting for both the case and the earphones. Have not had to charge the case since getting these a few days ago, and that charge is still well over 50%.
-Best bass in a pair of earphones, if you have the right size ear cups on.
-Easier to pair with your devices (and easier to use) than most of the cheap wireless earbuds I’ve seen, but especially if you have an iPhone or iPad.
-Overall, the sound quality is good, especially for earphones—it’s just the mids that are not perfect, but it seems like no earphones are perfect unless you’re the type who hates bass...in that case, you can find many “perfect” earphones.
-They do stay in place, unlike other earphones. Very big deal!
-The controls do a lot and are fairly easy to learn and to use, although not totally perfect.

I do want to caution that I order from Amazon a ton, and when I ordered these for a Christmas present for myself (someone else paid, so it was really a gift from them), Amazon’s delivery truck “lost” them after showing my house was the next stop for them to deliver these. I have never had a lost package from Amazon, especially when UPS or USPS delivers. I had to order from Walmart before getting my Amazon refund to get this by Christmas. I just think it’s odd that the first time I order an expensive, popular electronic device and it’s Christmas time, Amazon’s drivers suddenly lose my order on the way to my house. So beware if you’re thinking of ordering these Amazon Prime Fulfilled By Amazon...

title: Most dysfunctional piece of tech I've ever used
text:
Absolute garbage is the best way to summarize these. They look great, they're fairly comfy, sound quality is good enough, and then you get to the connectivity issues, charging issues, app issues, and finally you realize you payed $250 for earphones that don't even work. I'll just list the many issues I have.

When I get more than 5 feet away from whatever device the earphones are connected to, the sound quality turns to trash and sounds like the headphones automatically added a reverb to the music. The only way to fix this is to disconnect then reconnect. As for actual range, I get a maximum of 10 feet before the reverb thing happens.

This same sound quality problem also occurs when someone who has Bluetooth activated on their device gets near me; however, both these issues are inconsistent. Sometimes you get lucky and nothing happens, other times you're forced to reconnect.

Then you have the only-one-side problem. The buds frequently only connect one earphone, while the other is totally silent. The only way to fix this is to reset the pairing with your device, which requires the charging case; so, if you leave your case in the car while you're at the gym, and then you get the one-side-only problem, you're forced to go back outside, get the case, disconnect the earphones and unpair them from the device, then pair them again, then connect again and pray they work, which they often don't.

The app. The useless app. At first glance it seems quite nice, you get to see the battery percentage of your earphones and you get to manage your beats devices; then you press a button that leads you to a page that has nothing but a picture of a person and says "Help Connect", even though I'm already connected to the Beats. There is no way to get out of this page and just get back to your device management, unless you reset the app entirely. So again, you're forced to reset something just to get it working.

The charging mechanism is very flimsy. Just 2 days after my return window for these closed, I come to find out the left side of my charger has broken, so now only one earphone works, if I can even get it to work, and the other won't even charge. I've had these for one month and the charger already broke.

These are branded as Beats but they're made by Apple. They're exactly what anyone with tech knowledge would expect from an Apple product. They look great, feel good, are heavily overpriced, seem to work just fine for a week, then everything falls apart and you're left wondering how you can get your money back.

title: Difficult to adjust for proper fit!
text:
After trying all of the 4 different rubber earpieces, I settled on the largest size. For my left ear, adjusting the band was easy - I’m able to put the earbud on, repeatedly, and it “just works.” The right side, however, is a problem. My ears must be different, because no matter what rubber earpiece I use, no matter how much I adjust the band, I just cannot get it to fit properly. It always feels like it is going to fall out (never has, though) and as a result, the sound quality suffers. Additionally, as other reviews have mentioned, the huge ball on the earbud is pressing directly on my ear - after three days, my ear is now painful to touch.

Another issue is the battery life. Not sure what I’m doing wrong. I made sure the case and both earbuds were fully charged, then went on my ~1 hour run. Came home, set the earbuds on the counter, and turned Bluetooth off on my phone. The earbuds are supposed to turn off automatically after 10 minutes of no Bluetooth connection. Yet, the next day, the left earbud was at 33% and the right at 61% - WTH?

The final annoyance is that once the earbud bands are properly adjusted, the lid of the battery case will not close!!! Forcing it closed means that the ear bands move slightly, ruining the fit I spent so much time perfecting. Quite annoying.

There are too many problems with these earbuds to warrant a $200 price tag. I will be returning them.

BT connection drops between R or L piece even with 100% battery and your charging box near, and it can be very choppy at times. If you are trying to connect to your smartphone and then switch and connect to your computer ... forget it, you will have to reset it a bunch of times and if the connection gets lost you have to do it again.

Inside the charging box the positioning of the R and L pieces is not ideal, and you can find yourself at times with 100% battery on the R ear piece and 0% on the L one.

title: You'll find better for much cheaper
text: I had recently been using some $30 bluetooth earbuds up until I lost them, so I decided to finally use some higher quality earbuds. In terms of sound quality, these are solid. Comfort is pretty good too. But whoever designed these headphones screwed up BIG TIME. You can't turn on the earbuds without removing them from the case, and they will constantly remain on until their battery life is drained unless placed back in the case. There's no way to increase volume from these headphones. The noise cancellation is terrible. The battery life is pretty pathetic (usually 2-3 hours) especially in comparison to other earbuds which can get you 6-8 easily. Also, when the case runs out of battery, you're screwed. Even if the earbuds themselves have battery, you can't actually turn them on unless the case is charged. On top of this, when the case isn't charged, everyone near you will get constant unending notifications on their phone about how the case isn't paired with a phone yet. It will drive you and everyone else mad, because you can't do anything about it. The button to pause on the headphones is so sensitive, even adjusting them in your ear will set if off. Honestly, save yourself some time. Buy some earbuds that can turn on and off with the earbuds alone, last longer, have volume control, and don't constantly cause problems when the case is out of battery. Before these, I had enacfire E60's, which I dearly miss. Very similar sound quality, and had every feature you would expect and want on earbuds.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: I give up, DO NOT BUY THESE
text:
I would give these a zero if I could. I use earbuds exclusively for running and walking outside. I had a "wireless" pair of Bose Soundsport earbuds that had the connecting wire between the two buds. The sound quality was amazing. My only issues with them were the wire between the buds getting caught on my running hat or sweating neck, and the fact that I felt like I had to keep pushing them in my ears during my runs.

Enter the Powerbeats Pro. I liked that they had an over the ear component. I figured they were a Beats product so the sound quality had to be good, right? (Disclaimer: I am not an Apple Products Person. I have all Android items and always will). I read reviews exhaustively, and they were all glowing (at first). There were a couple at the bottom that mentioned connectivity issues and issues with earbuds not charging correctly. But only a couple. I figured, every product has glitches I am sure that was an isolated incident.

Oh how wrong I was. From the very first use of these earbuds, I have had numerous issues. You cannot connect the buds to your phone unless you have the charging case with you. So if you are out on a LONG run and suddenly the buds disconnect, you are out of luck until you get back to your case. I did not carry it with me as it is bulky and I really don't have a place to put it while I am exercising. This issue happened at least once a week.

Then, my PowerBeats would be in their charging case all night and I would wake up early for a run and weirdly either one or both earbuds would be at 0%. At first I figured it was user error as the buds have to be seated "Just So" in order to make contact with the charging contacts. Eventually, no matter how I placed the buds in the charging case, one of them would be at 0% in the morning. It alternates which bud it is. No matter what I do now, one bud is never fully charged and this is happening consistently for at least a month. I have read countless reviews now of others experiencing this same issue and it seems that Apple doesn't really do much, if anything, about it. I don't want another pair of Powerbeats earbuds...I want the pair I own to just work. At least the Bose Soundsports were always charged and ready when I needed them to be. They also had better sound quality. I have tried all the tips and tricks (disconnecting and resetting the case, etc.) and sometimes that works and sometimes that does not. I don't feel like wasting 15 minutes of my time at Zero Dark Thirty trying to hack these earbuds into working properly.

I have owned these for almost a year and I regret purchasing them. They are worthless for what I need them for, and after I receive my Jabras (thanks Prime Day) they will be relegated to connecting to my work phone where having only one earbud work at a time is not that big of a deal.

Save yourself money and time and find other earbuds.

title: Good but a couple minor changes to design could make them so much better
text:
I've had these for about a week and use them daily during workouts and general usage around the house and while working.

Cons:
- To get good bass quality you have to really shove the in-ear piece far into your ear canal which actually cause discomfort over time. A simple change to the angle of the speaker "hole" to direct it down into the ear canal would make a world of difference. If you look closely the speaker is currently directed in the opposite direction of your ear canal.
- There is no way to power them off, so if you need to disconnect them from your device you have to either disable your bluetooth, un-pair them from the device, or insert them back into the case and close it, which eventually depletes the charge in the case as it re-charges the headphones. This ends up with either the headphones needing daily re-charge, or the case needing daily re-charge. All other bluetooth headphones I've ever owned could be turned off then stored for several days or even up to a week if needed before having to recharge.
- Positioning of the headphones inside the case is awkward; it took a few days to remember how to do it and stop fumbling around with placing them back in the charging/storage case

Pros:
- Long battery life; one day I had them on for about 10 hours without recharging; total usage about 5-6 hours of phone calls and music playback
- Instant pairing to phone; as soon as I remove them from the case they are linked up with my Android phone
- Very rarely lose sound or bluetooth; I only lost sound once and all i had to do was put them back in the case, close it, wait a few seconds for the light to go out, and take them back out again and they started working; have yet to have issues with loss of bluetooth connection except when too far away from the paired device which is normal
- Comfortable to wear for long periods of time (see first "pros" comment above)
- So far no issues with sweat, discomfort, or with them falling off during workouts; I've used them running, rowing, and weightlifting daily with no problems
- The Beats App for Android devices allows you to see how much charge is left on the headphones when in use, and when in the case (with the lid open) you can see both the headphone charge and the case charge levels. The app also provides periodic updates to the firmware and uploads them to the headphones.

title: Most Likely Worth It
text:
Well, just got them in. I'll have an update out in maybe a month.

- Paring them with my One Plus 7 Pro was simple and straight forward, no problems. I've experienced no lag between video and audio when using YouTube so I assume it's good for other video players. However... I get the feeling the sync up isn't quite solid? It works but I feel like it could just as easily not? Not sure why.
- I can see why people might complain about discomfort after extended use, make sure to adjust the stems as needed. The best ear tips I've ever used so far are from the plantronics backbeat fit but these are okay. They fit very snugly though, so don't expect these to fall out unless you... well... I'm not sure what you could do to make them fall out actually... maybe by rolling? There's a trick to getting them on your ear, you need to turn it sideways and then slide it in by turning it upright in place.
- Sound quality doesn't seem to have improved much over previous versions but it's certainly not bad and most people should be quite happy. Maybe I got too used to the beats series. Audiophiles be warned, you likely won't be impressed. Other people are right, the sound isolation isn't the best, Mainly it lets in higher or sharp sounds.
- Battery life is fine for now. People complain about the case but my pockets are almost always big so I don't have a problem.

I got these for the shape since they're usually more comfortable to wear and not as easy to fall out, especially when working out. Cordless is awesome! Not worrying about catching the cord and accidentally yanking out the buds is a weight off my shoulders and should make sure these don't break as quickly.

In short, if you've got money (or credit) to spend and want nice fitting headphones with decent sound you might enjoy these...

title: Good cans
text: Most things I get on Amazon but these were way cheaper on eBay when I wanted them.  I bought them because Beau hates the design. They are good! Worth every penny. They do the trick for what I need. They could also be better. They are better then just about anything else in the class. Sony makes a great one and Jabra and a few others round out a newer segment of higher end multi purpose in ear experience. I say multi purpose because every company has a different goal. This is clear from an initial comparison of the category. When I scanned reviews I kept noticing patterns of complaints and compliments that could be traced back to the end user’s main application and if they had chosen one that compliments that. I say this because to nit-pick new tech and ask too much is setting it up for disappointment. The last 7 years of wireless has been that. Recently a few have become useable. Most of those are above the 300 tag. And they all sit on your head and surround your ears. I wanted a set of workout headphones. I have been using wired because of sound and sound and also the sound. Those three main factors have caused any wireless for workouts to be sidelined. I needed something that has no trace of digital compression. I know I’m gonna get colored sound. Very colors win the case of these.  But I need it to play very loud without degradation during stress. Both the beats and Sony’s sidestep mainstream algorithms to utilize their own chip. Must be nice to have such a company and to be able to tune it to the hardware and to a listing type. Is it crystal clear. No. But it also doesn’t digitally stumble. More like a tape vs a record. The bass can hit low while delicate female vocals are aloud to move freely. I mostly listen to vinyl. No noise at high volume. End to end clean with very good speakers that are well placed and matched to the amp perfectly. A lot of music also gets pushed from a pc though a good dac and into that amp. So I need a portable option that approximates this listening environment. In that light. These are just awful. Good bass should hurt your teeth and anger the neighbors. These are earphones. The sound is fine. It pairs with the phone w/o issue and turns on and off as I take them on and off. I am simple, I won’t call anyone with these. That’s weird. People need to stop doing that. Can I get some public in my public? Anyway they are comfortable and don’t bleed sound too much. I bought some aftermarket foam tips that are good. Beau hates those also so…double bonus. They Do help the sound and comfort. Find something that works before writing them off. The style might not be for you and the features may be a different set from yours but if those align then these sound terrific.

title: Thoroughly disappointed (Overpriced)
text:
After reviewing multiple earphones and deciding on the Probeats I've come to the following conclusion.
Sound: I had issues with my left ear getting a good seal to really get the best sound so I decided to purchase some comply foam pieces which helped tremendously. The sound is good but not great. in fact, I had purchased a cheap china version a year previously and they sound just as good as these. The problems with the cheap version is the battery and looks.
Pairing: The pairing with an iPhone is extremely easy and the distance you can walk away from your iphone and still get a connection is amazing.
Price: to me these are overpriced. I would think $150 is a good price for these but $250 is just too much.
Aesthetic: They appear well built and stay in your ear very well when exercising.
Overall: They worked well during exercising but not very well when you're trying to keep noise out (like mowing). Less than an month after receiving these earphones I started having problems keeping the right earpiece charged. I originally thought it was the comply ear foam so I had removed them which this didn't help. if fact, a few weeks later the right side earphone doesn't keep a charge at all and will discharge the case entirely. After speaking with apple support I was supposed to receive a return kit in 2 days. Unfortunately, this hasn't happened even after waiting a week now. My second call to Apple support is they informed me they are short on return kits for this type of earphone which tells me this might be a bigger problem. I wished I had returned them within the month but I wanted to give these earphones a good try.

text: These are the best wireless headphones I have ever had based on their sound quality, battery life and fit. Unfortunately, there is something wrong with the plastic material apple used. The headphones cause terrible rashes and allergic reactions on the inside of the ear resulting in painful irritation and a flakey discharge. There is a forum on reddit and apple with hundreds of people having the same complaint. It took several months before this state to happen and once I figured out it was the headphones I stopped using and the condition healed within a few days. I cleaned everything thoroughly and swapped the tips thinking they were too large, but within a couple of uses the condition returned. There is a chemical that people are reacting to from the headphones. I am currently waiting for a resolution from Apple as more people report this issue. There is something wrong with the materials they used to make these headphones.

title: Excellent earphones that do not come off
text:
So since the virus lockdown I have been on a quest for the perfect wireless buds that will stay in when I work out (and I work out hard!). I used to do jiu jitsu (no headphones allowed!) but with the virus I have taken up circuit training and elliptical and running, and the buds I was using (jabra 65t) were fine for hanging out but not vigorous work outs. The Jabras kept falling out. I do have a deformity in my right ear from wrestling so nothing works as well in that ear, but even the left Jabra bud would fall out when I ran. Otherwise they are very good buds. So I bought Jaybird Vistas to try next. Jaybirds come with a wing tip that I thought would solve my problem. So here are the pluses. Excellent sound and base (better than Jabra)! Rapid and reliable paring. Excellent case with good size, feel and function. Class 7 water proof. Excellent companion app that controls EQ and also button function (super useful) These buds are sturdy, light and function extremely well. Here are the down sides. When they are in place they really seal the ear canal so that every step is an internal thud in your head. With sweat the seal is even more annoying. Because of this when someone talks to me I want to take the bud out and it does not have a proximity sensor so it does not automatically stop. I have to take the extra step of pushing the pause button. Not a deal breaker at all, just saying. But I still could not get the right bud to stay in when I work out. The left was always fine but these are proprietary wing tips that function as one unit and only come in small medium and large. They do not allow separate adjusting of the bud portion versus the wing tip (which can be found in other devices such as the much much cheaper but very good wired anker soundcore spirits). The rubber is also thick and not as comfortable as other tips. So if you have weird asymmetric ears these may be a problem for you. If you want some ambient noise or venting in your ear canal these may not be right for you. But if you have normal symmetric ears and have never had a problem with ear bud fit these are awesome buds.

So next, I returned the Jaybirds and tried the Powerbeats Pro as well as the Master and Dynamic Go buds. Both of these have crisper all around sound than the Jaybirds but maybe less powered base. The Master and Dynamic Go buds have excellent battery life, a good case, good connection and very nice sound but also don't have a proximity sensor and their take on wing tips to maintain fit sucks. They just don't stay in when I work out, even my good left ear. They came up with a proprietary wing that seems like a good idea and is separately sized than the tips, but they just don't work that well compared to normal wings (which Bose has been doing for years).

The Power beats pro are the best of those mentioned above. They have excellent sound which is extremely crisp (though the tip size needs to be experimented until they create a good seal-this is important). The base is not overwhelming and the sound is as good as the Master and Dynamic buds (which are famed for their sound). They are vented so that sound filters in and I don't have that trapped in my own head feel. The buttons are identical on both sides and easy to use. I am an android user and they still work and pair extremely well including with voice activated google assistant (versus Siri). Most importantly they completely solve FOBFO (fear of buds falling out). Its like being an insomniac for all of your life and taking an ambien for the first time! They do not budge no matter what exercise I do. They have a hook that slides around the whole ear so they are more obtrusive and are quite visible. They are also not the most comfortable (the master and dynamics won that). Down sides: They have a lousy companion app that does not enable fine tuning of equalizer settings and the case is ginormous! There is no way I am carrying that thing around in my pocket. Purse or backpack yes, but not pocket. Fortunately they have 9 hour battery life so I never take the case with me.

Finally: I was getting used to my Powerbeats when I read about the new Sony wf-sp800n buds. As my return date ticked closer on the Powerbeats I went ahead and ordered the Sonys. OMG these win. Same battery life as Powerbeats (9 hrs). They have wing tips that work so they fit in the ear and do not fall out even when I am running or doing inverted sit-ups. They are water proof and they have BASS to die for or from! Sony super bass just totally outdoes any of the other buds I have used while maintaining crisp mid and upper tones. Really there is just no comparison. They have a very good companion app which allows for changing the designation of which bud does what (very useful) and a good equalizer. Powerbeats has a lousy companion app which barely does a thing. Finally they are noise cancelling! It is real and it works. When the buds are placed appropriately they do seal more than the Powerbeats and thus you feel more like your are thudding around inside your head, but they totally cut out backround noise. The case is cluncky but not as bad as the Powerbeats case and much easier to use in regards to getting the buds in and charging fast.

Conclusion: 1) Sony wf-sp800n 2) Powerbeats Pro 3) Jaybird Vista 4) Master and Dynamic Go buds 5) Jabra 65t

title: The noise cancelation on these is a joke!
text:
Because these earbuds have three options for noise settings, it makes it really easy to A/B the noise canceling mode. There's NC ON, NC OFF, and a third setting for monitoring sound around you. The third setting is mostly to assist in conversation without having to remove the buds.

These buds do a really good job of naturally blocking out unwanted sound with high quality in-ear pads. This has nothing to do with noise cancelation technology though. When I A/B NC on and NC OFF, there's (very little) to no affect at all. I think the buyers who think they are getting great noise cancelation, don't realize that most of the noise blockage is unrelated to NC technology. I think these are a bad value across the board. title: Distance Runner
text:
I run half marathons and needed a new pair of headphones. My previous headphones (pictured) were the JBL Reflect Contour which lasted about 3-4 years before 1 side quit working and the battery life was declining. I opted for these Powerbeats Pro after reading about them in an online article for running headphones. I specifically need a style that wraps around the ear as any ear bud does NOT stay in my ear - even if I sit perfectly still, they still fall out.

PROs
- there's essentially no set-up. These automatically connected to my iPhone straight out of the box. This smart, auto-on feature is very convenient (when it works properly).
- snug fit, the "arm" that wraps around your ear has some flexibility to it so I squeezed it down for a tighter fit. These headphones stay put for my 90+ minute runs. They do not cause any discomfort. They do not interfere with my Oakley Half Jacket sunglasses.
- fast charging, 40% charged in about 10 minutes after they died overnight from not returning them to the case.

CONs
- there's no auto-off feature and I learned that the hard way. When you take them out, you HAVE to return them to the charging case to power off. After my first wear, I took them off and set them on the counter thinking they would automatically turn off in the same manner they automatically turn on. I came back to the headphones the next day and they were completely dead.
- the sound quality is lacking, particularly on a windy day. These aren't noise cancelling in the slightest which is probably a good safety feature while running. But my previous headphones (JBL Reflect Contour) were noise tight.
- sometimes only 1 side connects. When this happens, you have to return both ear pieces to the charging case, "forget" the Bluetooth device on your phone, turn off your Bluetooth, and hard reset the headphones by long pressing the button on the charging case for 10-15 seconds. This entire process is highly inconvenient, annoying, and frustrating. I have only had these headphones for about 2 weeks now and have already encountered this process twice. I am not looking forward to constantly having to reset them.

I will keep these headphones and continue to use them throughout the duration of their lifetime. However, based on my experience so far, I would NOT repurchase these in the future nor would I recommend them.

title: Quite surprised, in a good way
text:
I will start by saying that I hate in-ear headphones. They move around and are all around just annoying. I really like the apple style earphone. However, I wanted wireless and but not the price of AirPods, so I decided to give these a try. I must say, I am quite surprised by how comfortable they are. I forget I even have them on. I also really like that I don't have to worry about them falling off. They stay perfectly in place. Which is great for not only comfort but also sound!

Now, on to the things that matter to everyone (as comfort is different for everyone). 1st, battery life. A solid 3 hours of nonstop playback, and they charge in about 20 minutes to 80%. Takes about an hour to get to 100%. 2nd. Connectivity. Simple. Not airpod easy, but close enough. 3rd. Wireless charging. No, unfortuantely. 4th. Sound. Once you get them set correctly in your ear, wow, they sound fantastic. Not audiophile, but dang good for a $20 set of wireless earbuds. 5th. You can do everything with the touch buttons. Volume, skip track forward and back, siri, take calls (deny calls). Everything you would expect, and it's pretty intuitive. It comes with a cheat sheet you can keep handy until you get used to the gestures.

Overall, I am extremely satisfied with these headphones. I would recommend these to anyone.

title: Super Lightweight & Super Streamlined!!!
text:
At the outset, let me say that I am a TOZO fan to start with. I already have a pair of T12's that I love - great sound, comfortable, great battery life. I purchased the A1's specifically to try when running and working out. I am so pleased with these - they fit very well and are designed to be small and tuck inside the ear. Their sound quality is amazingly good for a small device. Two things that really impressed me: they do not fall out when I run or jump rope, and the touch controls are easy to use with a simple tap. To be clear, these are not Noise Cancelling and are not advertised or marketed as such, but because of the fit and the seal, I find that these A1's are better at noise cancellation than other 'regular' earbuds. They certainly stay in place better than the regular (original) Apple AirPods and are much more comfortable and have better sound. I been wearing bluetooth headsets for music for quite some time. I usually prefer "over the ear and behind the neck pads" since I wear headsets many hours on a daily basis. Anyway, I find the audio with this set quite good. There are a few adjustments I make depending on my application such as pulling out the bud slightly for listening to ambient noise. I saw some reviews where others were earing a smaller bud to do this, but I just back it out of each ear slightly for the same effiect. When I want full bass and quality, of course you can just put them back in for a better seal. I used to do this with other buds that had no ear hook. Of course walking or exercising would result in frequent drops but not with the ear hooks.

Overall I love these and wear them all the time. Like with any audio device, audio quality is subject to the seal to your particular ear.

I would encourage anyone to purchase these if its in your budget range. As much as I use headphones, I didn't mind the investment, especially with the great battery life.

text:
I bought these headphones in person when they were released at an Apple store. I was really excited to get them.

Unfortunately, they are unreliable and I wish I got something else. I can not recommend that you purchase them.

First, about 20-30 % of the time the only one of the two earbuds will connect. So you end up only getting sound and control from one earbud. You have to reset the headphones and it's a major pain. This happens to me once a week at least and I dread it.

Second, there is an issue with the earbud not sitting flush with the charging pins inside the case. When it does not sit flush the earbud does not charge. So you will open the case grab the earbuds and one will be at 100% and the other at 0%...

If you can live with those two issues then it is a pretty solid product. For me personally, those two issues make it almost useless. I do not recommend this product.
