title: Can't beat these for this price!
text:
Case: Nice n compact. Love that the earbuds magnetically snap into the case when charging. USB-C and charges fast. Battery indicator is useful.

Comfort: At first when I put the earbuds in my ear, they were uncomfortable. Felt like the rubber was gouging my ears. Once I swapped out the rubber ear thingies it was comfortable and I could wear them all day. I have no fear of them falling out.

Call quality: Earbuds seem to be hit or miss in this department. I've recorded myself and I've asked my call participants to tell me how I sound and they all say I'm coming in loud and clear and crisp. Similar to my wired headphones which seem to have the best call quality. So these pass the test.

Audio quality: Bass is a little boomy on some songs but overall the quality is excellent.

Battery life: so far has been excellent. I work in headphones all day and haven't had any issues with battery life. I typically use them for a few hours in the morning, put them in the charging case for lunch, then put them on for a few more hours in the afternoon. Haven't died on me yet.

Overall, you really can't beat these for the price. I've bought wired headphones for more money and these would top them in versatility and quality.

title: Worth the money!
text:
I've tried a number of different wireless earbuds and they all have fell short of expectations either due to fit, falling out of the ear, or audio quality. These Powerbeats Pro, while slightly more expensive than other offerings, really hit the mark on everything I needed.

FIT: My primary use was for running or going to the gym. The earhooks are adjustable and should fit any ear type. Included are also 4 different sets of earbuds so you should be able to find the correct fit for your ear. Once adjusted, they were comfortable for all sorts of activities and I barely noticed they were there.

AUDIO: Not the boomiest bass that you come to expect with the beats label, but clear audio throughout which I prefer. The earbud provides good sound isolation from the outside world but if biking or running, the earhooks allow you to wear them a little looser to get ambient noise for safety.

BATTERY: Since the case acts as a charger, I haven't noticed any drawbacks to the battery life. I simply put them in the case when I'm not using them. I typically use them for 2 hours at a time and lately with the work-from-home stuff going on, I've actually used them for upwards of 4-5 hours without the need to charge them. They state that 5-minutes of charging will get you 1.5 hours of playback in a pinch. Good to know in case you had an all-day event.

MICROPHONE: While I didn't purchase these for their microphone capabilities, I've found that the mic on them is actually better than previous earbuds that I've tested out. I always do a sound test before a conference call and the quality on these were more clear than the airpod type earbuds. Will it beat the onboard iPhone mic or an actual headset with a mic sitting in front of your mouth? No, of course not, but for ambient mic on earbuds, it does better than most.

Overall, I'm happy that I splurged a little more for these. I was getting tired of buying and returning many other brands and types of earbuds due to them not meeting my needs. I will be keeping these and using them daily.

text:

The sound quality is so mediocre, especially for something costing $179. The sound is hollow, flat, and tinny–absolutely not the full rich sound that I was expecting! I put the largest eartips on hoping that might do something, and I tried every single setting in the Music Settings EQ to see if it might help at all. I finally settled on the “more base” setting, but it honestly didn’t do much. SIGH! All of these reviewers raving about the sound quality obviously don’t know how music is really supposed to sound (and feel!) Take it from someone who has been truly devoted and passionate about music their entire life–listening to music on these headphones just made me sad. A major disappointment!
UPDATE: I tested the sound quality of these (as it pertained to MUSIC only, not phone calls or voice clarity) compared to a pair of “Enacfire E90” earbuds that I had been using as a replacement for some lost Apple AirPods. As I suspected, the Beats failed and the sound of the $30 Enacfire E90s was actually much better! After that I knew I would probably be sending the inferior PowerBeats Pro earphones back (in spite of some of the great features that drew me to them in the first place, like the great external ear hooks), but there was one more test I wanted to do first, just to be sure. To replace the disappointing PowerBeats Pros, I chose the $149 Bose Sport Earbuds. Although the Bose earbuds don’t have the Beats innovative ear clips, and the battery life per charge is shorter than Beats, all of the other features are comparable, with one major exception: The Bose Sport Earbuds provide the listener with a deeper, fuller, and richer sound that surpasses the tinny, hollow, and flat sounding Powerbeats Pro, and for most people that should be a dealbreaker.

title: I didn't know a product could be so poorly designed.
text:
This is a review for use with android and macbook pro

TLDR most glitchy product i've ever had in my life. Updates are few and far between and bring new glitches. Most common glitch is sound going out of sync between left and right resulting in delay, and feeling of echo in the audio: it's infuriating and requires disconnect and reconnect: sometimes with waiting in between or having to repair from box which makes the big bulky charge box a must carry everywhere: can't exactly go ona run with that thing.
Imagine having to interrupt your sports routine 2-4 times to get these things working, does that make you want to work out more or less?

Since i first bought them, they have been nothing but glitchy, and it took two months to have them replaced on apple care (because apple after sale service is a joke) so i made a glitch diary over the past few weeks to write this review.

Android: many of these glitches are not android dependent but rather location/movement dependent, or where you put your phone dependent, or what your phone is touching dependent or next to what appliance you're standing dependent and sometimes audio app dependent (switching apps resolves the glitch).
Glitches are "seasonal" they come and go, though some are constant. But there's always something new.
-Worst and by most common glitch: the earbuds often go out of sync resulting in an echo (bc of the delay btw one ear and the other). This one is infuriating/maddening: happens everyday many times. Sometimes i just live with it because i don't want to go through the motions of disconnecting/wait/reconnect but the sync keeps drifting and it gets jarring/disorienting after a while: like chinese drip torture.
- powerbeats connect, sound still comes from phone speakers
-“skipping sound effect” from the connection faltering
-sometimes nonstop struggle to stay in sync, stay connected
-Sounds cuts in and out repeatedly with random intervals (on... off........ on.... off... on........ off...)
-put them in a box and close it only to realize they’re still connected and the sound is coming out of the box still, but sometimes the opposite problem occurs: i'd be listening from macbook speakers and they. randomly connect to the laptop and start playing from within the box, and pause playback. Must turn off bluetooth on device to recover sound from speakers.
-sometimes resumes all audio app after you pause and play (eg pause podcast, hit play, youtube, podcasts, audible all start playing together at the same time)
- Different buttons/functions cease to work, sometimes all buttons won’t respond (sound plays buttons unresponsive), sometimes just some buttons, just volume or play, or just one earbud.
-Sometimes buttons work but no sound (can see the app play/pause on the screen)
-Sometimes connects (as confirmed by connection sound and bluetooth menu on phone) but no sound and buttons unresponsive. Sometimes no sound though buttons can play/pause
-lag between commands and response (btw hitting play and music playing, pause and music pausing)
- often disconnects from phone after a call: when you hang up sound resumes from phone speakers
-sometimes disconnects during call making me run back to phone to continue call on phone
- sometimes one of the earbuds "forgets" its charged straight out of the box, putting it back in the charge box "reminds" it it's actually full (goes from 0% to 100% immediately): imagine you put them on step out of the. house and realize one of the earbuds is acting dead, now you have to go back home, stick it in the huge box you don't want to carry around and. then g et back to your run/bike/routine
-rarely, one earbud "dies" and needs to be placed in charging box for a long while before it comes back to "life"
-updates few and far between and bring new glitches
- EVERYTIME I ride (bike) through specific intersections it "slices" the connection: audio goes out though the app continues to play and the connection is still established in the bluetooth menu.
Recently (new "seasonal" glitches since last update ):
-just doesn't automatically connect when i open box and put them on, I have to manually connect them from the bluetooth menu, sometimes i have to repair them from the box.
- one ear starts playing immediately, other earbud takes 6-9 seconds to connect, during which you're standing there. waiting to see if it's this glitch or the one where one of the earbuds thinks it's empty and needs to be put back in the box to remember it's full.
-earbuds connect but they don't make the connection sound so you don't know if they've connected or not without playing something
- entire volume range is on the bottom three increments of the volume bar, goes from no sound (one volume click up) 50% volume (one volume click up) 100% volume and all the rest of the range no matter how much you volume up/down, remains at 100% volume.
Macbook pro
-refuses to connect/reconnect to macbook pro, no idea why, requires a factory reset and re pairing
-randomly switches to another device mid use (from phone to macbook pro or vice versa)

Sound Quality: bass ok, HIGH TREBLE many podcasts sound like there's a hissing in your ear when they pronounce the letter S. Overall sound is good but the hissing from the high trebble is annoying: one solution to this i found was to use biggest size rubber buds and shove them well into your ear: enhances bass and mitigates treble.

Customer service: took nine days to ship them back to some facility to have them "looked at" decided they were fine within twenty minutes (i know this because they have a link to a tracker) and returned them to me (they had to overnight ship them when I blew a gasket at the store when i realized the confirmation email after nine days was just for their receipt of the product at the repair facility and not that they were done and ready for pickup: nine days, just to get from the store to the "repair" facility).
Had to return twice more and both times same thing: they receive them, immediately decide nothing wrong with them, return them: spent the whole summer without the product i had bought SPECIFICALLY for that summer. In the end some "genius" i paris told me it was because they were labeling the problem as "permanent" as opposed to "intermittent" (permanent means it's always there and so it should show right out of the box)

Please comment if you've been having any of these problems.
thanks
100% would not recommend

title: The culmination of Beats' Vision - From Various Perspectives!
text:
These are by far the best Beats yet! Beats have been classified with several key values in the audio devices category: High-bass, hard-hitting, high-quality sound, great for workouts, stylish (both for their subtlety and their loud, "look-at-me" color palettes).

These PowerBeats Pro buds feel like the culmination of lots of R&D, and as the culmination of the brand - available in a subtle, stylish black matte finish, they are professional and low-profile. In their Ivory, Moss or Navy schemes, they are still subtle but have that stylish flair typical of Beats industrial design.

The fit is spectacular. I have ears that work with lots of earbuds, but my wife does not - She's been forced to stick to over-ear and on-ear headband design headphones for most of her life - AirPods dont work and most earhook headsets are just incomfortable for her. My former PowerBeats headphones were OK but even in my very flexible ear didn't have the best "stay put" feel. My wife refused to wear them, citing painful pushing of the inserted bud into the walls of her ear canal. Conversely, we now fight over the PowerBeats Pro - She's going to have to get her own pair! They are not only more comfortable for those with picky ears, but they sit much lower in profile, allowing for more subtle use... The first time I saw myself wearing my 2nd generation powerbeats I was a bit embarrassed. With the PowerBeats Pro, they appear flush with my head shape and sleek in appearance.

The audio quality is excellent. I'm a purveyor of true wireless headsets. I've been fortunate enough to own most of the current A-list of true wireless, including the Bose Soundsport Free, Jabra Elite 65t, Apple AirPods (1st generation) and these PowerBeats Pro. The PowerBeats are the ones that only leave my pocket or "go bag" to charge a few times a week at night when I'm not using them... The sound quality is excellent, with strong bass that doesn't muddy up the highs and mids of more sophisticated tracks, and yet hits with enough range that it feels immersive rather than just deep. In some ways, the PowerBeats Pro have replaced my Studio Wireless cans as well for at-the-desk listening due to just how good they sound, and how much more comfortable it is listening without covering my ears completely.

Add to that the modernization of the industrial design - Support for Lightning charging (Studio and Solo have no excuse left to not support this) and the nice, albeit large, carrying/charging case, and these are going to be a HUGE hit for a long time. I dont even know where they'd go from here. They leave me wanting nothing, and just completely enjoying my music.

title: Not bad but maybe not worth $200
text:
I'd been using cheap $20 bluetooth headphones for about 3 years before buying these. The cheap ones would stop working after ~4-6 months and I'd just get a new pair. I wanted to stop being so wasteful so I got a pair of "good" wireless earbuds... the Powerbeats Pro. Thankfully I only paid $150.

I have now had these for about 8 months, and they are still going. I mostly just listen to podcasts and audiobooks so I can't say whether they hit the highs and lows like they need to for audiophiles, but they get the job done. The main thing I like about them is that they have volume buttons, which are surprisingly hard to find on wireless ear buds (though I wish they had made better use of these buttons by integrating long presses for skipping forward and back rather than having double and triple taps on the main button), and they don't have that annoying blue flashing light that a lot of cheaper bluetooth headphones have when they turn on. I also like the ear hook.

Things that could be better:
- when you put them in the case to charge, the ear buds don't always connect, so when you pull them out one bud might have 1% battery. So you have to make sure they are charging instead of it being more carefree (this is a problem I would have expected from a pair of $200 ear buds)
- the charging case is quite large and is not comfortable in your pocket (unless you have some baggy cargo pants)
- when you take them out of the case, they don't always connect to your phone. So you have to put it back in the case and then bring it back out in order for the ear bud to connect (this happens maybe 5-10% of the time... so it is quite noticeable) (again, another problem you wouldn't expect from a pair of $200 ear buds)
- I flew on an airplane recently and found that the main button kind of got sucked tight onto the ear bud (due to changes in air pressure) such that pressing it only resulted in a long press result (Siri in my case) and didn't have the tactile response of pushing a button. It got back to normal about an hour after I landed each time. This is the first time I have ever had any issues with any electronics buttons on an airplane.
-Update: the microphone has also gotten terrible. On half the calls I take, the person on the other end thinks I sound muffled.

These are fine, but for the price you pay, they should be way better.

title: Worth the money?  Maybe not.
text:
Had these for a couple months. Thought Beats brand would provide great sound and Apple device connectivity and be worth the money. No so much. The bad—music sound quality is not very good. I’m no great audiophile, but there is hardly any bass. Volume is either too loud or not loud enough. I generally like over the ear fit but they are fairly rigid. My ears occasionally hurt, but you can kind of rotate them, if that makes sense. On phone calls with both in ear, the sound is great, but the microphone doesn’t pick up your own voice, so you sound muffled from them sealing your ear. All people on other end say I sound good. Once you get used to being a bit muffled and trust they are picking up your voice, you’re good. The good—audio for the spoken word is excellent. Phone conversations or listening to spoken stream is great—with one or both in ear. Midranges and highs are solid and crisp. These pair very easily with Apple devices (couple phones and iPad). I have even paired them with my LG TV. They switch very well on Apple devices.

For the MONEY, I don’t think they are worth it. Maybe if they were half of the price. I bought Concour brand of similar design on Amazon for like 30 bucks. I see they are 21 now. Music sounds much better with good bass (not great). Those aren’t as great for highs and midranges (a little blaring) but they are also more comfortable and flexible. They pair fine but you have to be more deliberate with connecting and disconnecting, if you go from device to device. Don’t buy the hype of these Beats. If you want very good EarPods for spoken word, then these are great if you don’t mind the muffling of your own voice. If for music, save your money.

text:
I originally ordered Bose Soundsport wireless ear buds and was disappointed with my purchase - they were bulky, did not fit well in my ear, and had terrible noise cancellation capability.

4) Appearance- these things look sweet. I got the Navy but the Camo green look cool too. Beats always knocks it out of the park with their designs
5) Price- they're less than AirPods 2, and come from the same company (basically). If you're active and want something other than AirPods, these have to be your go-to choice.

title: Good for sports, but poor recharge connections
text:
I bought these wireless earphones after going through two pairs of Bose Free SoundSport wireless earphones. I really like the Bose earphones, but they very easily fall out of your ears, especially when taking face masks on and off - which I do frequently when out trail running. The Powerbeats Pro earphones have a much more reliable design, with little arms that hold the earphones in place around the back of your ears. This is a much preferable design for running and other training activities. They also connect easily to my iPhone, can be used to take calls, and have easily accessible volume controls that work. The sound quality is terrific.

That is, when they are working. I have had these earphones but about 9 months. Over the last few weeks the charging connection on both earphones has become unreliable. Following advice on the internet and the Apple support pages, I have tried cleaning the two tiny metal connections with a toothbrush, and have tried to clean off noticeable debris on the tiny metal connectors with a plastic toothpick. What is really frustrating is that frequently only one side will charge - in this case the charging light will go on, but then later when trying to use the earphones only one side will work. I have fiddled with this endlessly and cannot find a way to get these earphones to reliably charge.

The Bose SoundSport earphones have four metal connectors for each earphone, and in the case there is a separate indicator light for each earphone letting you know if it is charging. The PowerBeats only have two smaller connectors on each side, and only one light. Moreover, while there is a magnet the holds the earphone in place to charge, feeling the magnet pull the earphone in place does not mean it is charging. Often it is not.

I really like the Powerbeats Pro headphones, but given these issues with recharging I have a hard time recommending them.

title: Perfection for working out
text:
A couple months in, and they're still a delight to use. I listen to a mix of audiobooks and music, and these perform splendidly for either. I thought I'd NEVER buy a Beats-branded product (their typical headphones sound like someone playing music through a steel garbage can), but I can't deny how great these are.

These are among the best sounding ear buds I've ever heard. I haven't tried a ton, but they are far above the quality of normal ear buds of any brand. That said, getting the most out of these requires using the proper fitting nubs. Four sizes are included and I needed the smallest. Once on, they fit snugly in my ears and the sound was great throughout the spectrum. If the nubs don't sit IN your ear, you aren't going to get full range audio (or not the highest possible quality experience).

But you aren't considering these ear buds for sound quality primarily, right? (you'd be buying some Sennheiser cans if you were) The true wireless nature of these headphones is the stand out feature. I LOVE them. No cables, no neck bands, nothing. I can run or hike for hours and hours, take my shirt/sweater/sunglasses off, put them back on, and never worry about getting tangled or putting something in my pocket.

As these were made for exercise, I'm not at all worried about normal levels of sweat. I clean them every time they go back in the case, and that's that. The case is not enormous as others have claimed. Maybe 3 or 4" on a side, and 2 or 3" thick. To me, the case is tiny. My wife will be getting the blue ones when they're available.

title: Truly an Air Pods Pro Lite version
text:
I started off giving these earbuds 4 stars, and then realized that I was unfairly comparing them to Air Pod Pro's that are over $100 more expensive. For the relative value, these earbuds fit the bill.
Feel: These earbuds are a bit slippery, and with the squat design it makes them a bit hard to grab. However, they fit snug into my ear so I don't have to over handle them much anyway. It takes getting used to putting them back into the case correctly.
Looks: I like the variable colors. I bought these because I misplaced my tiny white Air Pods Pro case (whose last location deleted after 24 hours because Apple is a money monger). This red case is bigger but not cumbersome.
Interaction: I don't like the button on the outsides of the buds. I wish the button was on the bottom with more of a squeeze function. To click the button, I have to essentially jam the bud further into my ear to get it to press. I also like to lay down with my buds in, but if I turn my ears against the pillow, the button is constantly pressing. A button positioned on the button (or top) would be way easier to pinch when on purpose without accidental clicks. At least clicking it doesn't pull the buds out of my ear; an issue I had with the lever arm of the APPs.
Sound quality and connection: Good enough for me. Calls connected and sounded just fine. I don't need my phone calls to have live orchestra quality. The music seems good too. Not overly bass forward but crisp.
ANC/Occlusion: The occlusion effect seems slightly worse than the Air Pod Pro's but no where near as bad as the Jabra's and other brands. I can sometimes hear my stomping on pavement but I don't hear my blood flow or anything. The ANC/transparency is also relatively equitable to the APPs, of course slightly not as significant in quality because these buds are much cheaper. It does seem to smartly block out certain sounds; i.e. my HVAC, while letting through someone calling my name.
Haven't really tested the battery life but supposedly they're better than APP. Again, these are solid buds for the price. You get what you pay for, and these buds seems to prioritize what I actually care about so you don't have to pay $250 every time your APPs or Bose go missing.

title: Could Be an Amazing Product, If Not For a Couple of Issues
text:
First let me say that these are the third pair of wireless earbuds I've purchased (The other two being One Plus Buds, and a pair by Sony at a similar price point). As far as audio quality goes, these are definitely some of the best, if not the best, pair of headphones I've used. If that were the only factor, they'd definitely get five stars.

There are two main problems with these that bring that rating down. The first is battery life. Out of all the wireless earbuds I've owned, these definitely have the worst battery life. Not to say they die quickly, but they just don't last as long as the other two pairs I've had. If it weren't for the second issue, I'd still probably give them five stars in spite of the battery life.

The second problem is issues with connectivity. This problem actually IS terrible. I frequently have issues with the buds either not connecting to my phone, or not disconnecting when I put them back into the case. Quite a few times now I've had to manually go into the settings and disconnect the buds to fix it, turning what should've been a few seconds of popping them in into a few minutes of troubleshooting. When the buds work they're great, but this issue is such a headache that I'll definitely be looking for a replacement pair.

title: Better than AirPods
text:
I am not an audiophile. But I spend a lot of my time on the go for my job. So having a pair of good wireless headphones with microphones to take and make calls is a must. I originally bought a pair of black wireless PowerBeats Pro back in June. I have nothing bad to say.

The only minor downside is that these do pinch your ears. But unlike my Beats Solo 3 headphones, the hooks are adjustable so I can wear them for long periods by moving the hooks if they pinch.

Powerbeats Pro Wireless are better than AirPods in terms of value for the money and sound quality. I bought a pair of AirPods after briefly losing my Powerbeats in an Uber. (Bought a case with a clip after that. Highly recommend!)

I kept the AirPods around after getting my Powerbeats Pros back. A couple of weeks ago, I decided to get another pair of Powerbeats because they went on sale and I originally wanted the navy ones. I sold my original black pair thinking I would get my new ones in a few days. They ended up getting lost in transit so I used my AirPods for a week and here’s what I learned.

AirPods are just ok. Yes, they are small and convenient and a little more comfortable to wear. But the battery life on them sucks compared to Powerbeats. Yes, they charge fairly quickly but I was losing 30 percent of my battery in about two hours. Not great for days where I’m busy and want to listen to books or music in between.

The sound quality isn’t great if you’re anywhere with noise. I had to have the volume turned up most of the time which I’m sure didn’t help the battery life. The ultimate test was being on a BART train and the noise of the actual train overriding the audio unless it was turned up.

Lastly, AirPods don’t fall out of my ears as easily as I thought they would. But they still do. And it happens when you least expect it.

I did a lot of research before buying my Powerbeats and they are worth the $250 price tag to me, though a sale never hurts. The large case is a negative to people but it has a battery that gives 24 hours of charge. No one had a longer battery life and a decent charge out of the buds I looked at except Beats.

text:
Absolutely love these headphones! I came from Airpods, then Airpod pros, then Beats Studio Buds, and now these. These are on a level of their own, they're so great.

PROS:
- The battery life. Each headphone lasts me an entire shift at work (8-9 hrs) with zero interruptions. The case itself charges very fast, I'd say in about 1-2hrs, is a full charge. And the case does not die that easily, lasts me a couple days.
- The sound quality. These are Beats headphones so of course the sound quality is top tier. Beautiful lows, and beautiful highs.
- Durable. The build on the case and the headphones themselves are a nice and clean finish, and are made of great durable material. They are not flimsy whatsoever. I absolutely love the wrap-around design. It is impossible for these to fall out your ears which I love the most about these. That was the main reason I kept changing headphones in the past.
- The case is not needed if you have one headphone on you. For example, some days I would accidentally leave my case at work, but still have one headphone on me when I get home. That one headphone would still work without the case in range, as long as your phone is in range.

CONS:
- Only have one, the case is big and burly. But that is of course necessary for both headphones to fit in. But the fact that the case is not needed to be near you when the headphones are connected make this statement, not really a con. Other than that, I truly do not have any other cons for these headphones! Yes, they are a bit on the pricey end of the spectrum, but I truly believe they are worth it. Very well worth the money.

title: Great headphones, but not for me.
text:
I bought these headphones to replace my Apple Airpods, mainly because the Airpods were having a rough time fitting/staying in my ears. Unfortunately, I was having similar, if not, worse issues with these.

Pros:
- They are Beats by Dre headphones, so they have excellent sound quality and noise cancellation is a plus.
- They have an Apple chip, so for Apple users, it is seamless, simple pairing.
- For Android users, there is a Beats app that is very useful.
- The case is very compact and fits nicely in pockets.
- Extra rubber ear tips are provided for better fit.
- Charged via USB-C cable.
- On a full charge, the headphones can last all day, if you are using one side at a time, and swapping them out, when one dies. But each individual headphone lasts me about 4-5 hours of continuous use, still not bad at all.

Cons:
- The headphones are not a "perfect fit" no matter the rubber tip size. Throughout a day of use, I would constantly have to pick them up as they tend to fall out rather frequently. This was a huge con for me.
- In addition to the previous con, the headphones are very small, so if they fall out, finding them can be annoying too.

Overall, they are a great pair of headphones, and an excellent alternative to Apple Airpod Pros. However, the reason I am not giving them 5 stars, is the fact that they tend to fall out more often than not, despite the "twist and fit" concept.

title: Small in size and volume.  Super comfortable, but best for podcasts and audiobooks.
text:
I bought these on impulse when the price was sale. I own pairs of Tozo T6's, T12's, and NC7's, and didn't NEED these. But I guess I'm turning into a Tozo collector, and after having great experiences in the $50 price range I was curious to see what they could do in the $20 range.

I was really surprised by these. They are by far the smallest and comfortable wireless earbuds I've ever worn, from any brand. Usually I can wear buds for an hour or two before my ears need a break, but I can go with this all day. These have become my go-to daily driver for listening to podcasts and audiobooks.

That's a good thing, because the downside is that they're not the best for music. Their small form factor is matched by having much smaller volume than other Tozo models. With these A1's, you have to crank your device's output up to 100%, to match the same loudness that you get from other models around 40%. The good news is that sound quality is still clear and non-distorted when maxed out. Perhaps this is a good thing, if you like to take care of your ears and don't want the volume too loud. But it should be called out in a review.

Aside from small output, other downsides are lack of noise cancellation and wireless charging. These are no big deal in my opinion, and are more than reflected in the lower price compared to other Tozo models.

However, a more puzzling downside is Tozo choosing non-standard ear tips compared to their other earbud models. Be warned, all of the silicone tips that come with these A1's are TINY. Unless you have very small ear canals, you might not be comfortable with the out of the box tips. They do use the same 3.8mm diameter replacement tips (easy to find on Amazon) as all of the other models. But these A1's expect those 3.8mm stems to be about half to three-quarters the length that they are in all other Tozo models. Otherwise, the earbuds won't fit in their charging case. So I had to take some extra tips from my Tozo T6 box, and trim the stems down with scissors to make them fit these A1's.

So in a nutshell, I'm shaving off one star due to the small sound and wonky ear tip situation. HOWEVER, as long as you understand those caveats going in, I think these are some of the most amazing earbuds I've ever used. Low price, high sound quality, and most comfortable set of earbuds you'll ever wear. Ideal for podcasts and audiobooks, or people who like their music at a more gentle volume.

title: Bad Fit and Too Painful
text:
I decided to get these since the Powerbeats 3 are no longer available, and assumed the fit would be the same. But Powerbeats Pro are pretty painful. At first I thought it was because the arms are too stiff and the size too small, even though it hurts my smaller ear a lot more than my larger one. Then I changed out the ear tips to the small size and it no longer hurts the back portion of my ears where the arms rest. I've never had to change the tips on any other buds before. The standard size was always comfortable. However, the inside parts of my ears still hurt after the change. The tips are pressing on the tragus. Slightly twisting it forward so the tips are more downward facing helps relieve some of the pressure, but not all. Then the tips have this very large base that pushes against the concha and antihelix. Even though the pause button doesn't take much pressure to press, pushing it just gently is enough to make it feel like I'm jamming the base into my sore ear even more than it already is and causes a lot more pain to erupt, so I avoid it. If other wireless buds didn't have such bad reviews on audio quality, and if I wasn't in desperate need of wireless buds, then I would probably return these, and I'm still thinking of doing so. After a few days some parts of my ears are starting to develop callouses, so I'm hoping after more time that will help relieve the pain.

Additionally, the audio drops out all the time. For videos I keep having to exit out and restart. For songs I have to go to another song for audio to come back.

It's now 1 week after I wrote the above. About 1 and a half weeks total wearing these. I thought the rough spots in my ears were callouses, but actually they turned into blisters. 2 of them have popped and are now sores. The back portion of the ear started to hurt again, no matter which way I adjusted. The pain, both inside and back, became greater than the week before and would continue a full day after taking them off. My ears are also swollen pretty much all over. I'm going to try returning.

title: Great sound at a great price
text:
Bought these on Prime day for $100 and so far I am pleased. They sound great and I got about 7 1/2- 8 hours of battery life with ANC off listening at 80% volume while getting about 4 1/2 -5 hours with ANC on. The ANC is average and could be better but is sufficient enough for me. The transparency mode sounds a bit weird but I rarely use that ever. Only gripe is a software glitch I am experiencing with the ANC/transparency method of switching using the iPhone control center by long pressing the volume icon. When you attempt to switch listening modes it immediately takes you back to “off”. The mode does however switch on your buds but just shows incorrectly as “off”. This is apparently an IOS 15 bug and I believe will be fixed with IOS 16 in the Sept release. In the interim you can still switch listening modes using the buds or under Bluetooth settings specifically. I like that you also can change the long press action on the buds to increase/decrease volume now (instead of switching ANC/transparency) with the latest Jan 2022 update via the settings in Bluetooth.
All in all a good pair of earbuds for the price and I’m happy I got them.

title: Battery life and case design issues
text:
I have Apple AirPods but they only had a 3 hour battery life and I needed battery life of 6-7 hours because I am running a marathon.

I got the Beats Studio buds because it claimed to have the battery life I needed. I used them on short runs and they were fine but on a 5 hour long run they ran out of power.

To make things worst I put them in the case during the rest of the run. When I got home I took out the case while walking off the run and dropped the case (waist height of about 32" off the ground).

The next morning I opened the case and saw one bud was missing.

Well it turns out that the case landed flat and the cover opened and launched one of the buds out and closed in an instant. I recreated this by dropping the case with the remaining bud. That lead me to going outside my home and finding the bud in the street. But it was too late the bud has been run over by a car.

Therefore if you are buying these for running both battery life and the case design are going to work against you and I can't recommend these buds for active runners.

I know dropping them was my fault and I accept the fault for their damage but my Apple AirPods have been dropped many times and never flew out of the case due to the extend post that goes into the case.

The overall time I had these buds was 3 weeks.

Therefore, I believe the case design will lead to you losing one of the buds long before you need a need pair.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: Good design let down by poor software execution and reliability. Get prepared to be frustrated.
text:
Pros: fit, sweatproof/water resistance, sound quality, battery life
Cons: terrible connection reliability

Like all Beats products, these headphones over promise and under deliver. The main problem is connection issues. Almost everytime you take these headphones out, you will realize only one side is connecting. After numerous attempts to place both in and out of the case to reconnect multiple times, you realize one headphone did not charge at all for some reason despite being properly in the case. Then you have to wait for it to charge for you to use it.

Then you use it. And it’s fine. Sound quality is decent. No bass but you knew that going in. No noise cancellation or transparent function for traffic but hey, what’s life without a little danger. For running and wearing a bike helmet, these are one of the most comfortable and secure designs out there.

Then you take them off and put them in the case. Then you try to play a youtube video on your phone. And for some stupid reason, despite being in the case, these headphones keep reconnecting to your phone, so that your audio is playing on headphones that you are not wearing. After multiple repeat disconnects…you finally are able to get it to stay disconnected.

For whatever reason, the same team that built the great reliability of airpods did not take over the Beats team. I cannot emphasize how frustrating these electronic connection issues are and I cannot recommend this product.

title: Great earbuds until they aren't – BEWARE devastating battery problems – no resolution
text: I've been using my PowerBeats Pro daily for about 2 years with no problems – I really liked them (used them for phone calls, podcasts, learning foreign language, music). In October 22 I noticed that the right bud died after about 15 minutes (when it got down to exactly 55%) – though both buds were fully charged. THIS IS A THING – it happens to many if not most users (one side or the other). Be aware that your pricey earbuds may not give you anything close to 9 hours of use before battery dies – you may have only 15 minutes or less. This has been a problem for years, and there is no fix. So all the good features don't matter if the buds don't actually work. Note: the battery doesn't actually run out of power at 55%, it just stops working. You can reconnect it briefly in the charging case, and it may work again for another 15 minutes. My pair got very quirky after the 55% problem started – now I think the left bud is beginning to go bad.

title: Just another wireless earbud. Not worth the premium price though AT ALL.
text:
Bought mine in August 2019 so I can give a long term view on this.

Background: I used these initially mainly for running and work because I like to move around and get stuff done around the house while participating in non-crucial Zoom calls (you know the ones), so the wireless aspect + over ear is why I bought them (in-ear buds always fall out my ears due because they are weird shaped, so that ear hook was a selling point for me) + everyone raves about beats so I finally caved into the hype and bought them. I bought them for $250 which I think was MSRP at the time, no discounts or offers.

So when I first bought them and used, they were absolutely amazing...connecting to my android was easy, connecting to my pc easy, then connecting to my work iphone was (admittedly) the easiest for obvious reasons (Beats was purchased by Apple so compatibility will be better with apple products). This honeymoon phase lasted for approximately 6 months. After that it was just downhill from there.

Biggest issues for me:
-They started dropping the connection out of nowehere, even while I was in the middle of a conversation. And even after unpairing from all other devices.
-The charger nodes are finicky. Before I go to bed I would place both earbuds in the charger, the notification would tell me they are charging, but then the next day I find out they have not charged they would be at 10% or 20% despite my charger having enough power to charge them to 100%....cool! Time to use my trusty $10 wired samsung earbuds.
-After 6 months the battery life started decreasing significantly, and not equally on both ear buds, i.e. one ear bud lasts longer despite both getting equal amount of charge (supposedly, see comment on finicky nodes). After 1 year the batteries would last for 3 hours max of zoom calls (not music, god forbid if I play music, 1.5 hours tops). And as of today (2.5 years later), my left earbud goes from 100% -> 0% in 5 minutes or less...while my right earbud lasts for 1 hour. Some would say their useless life is over, I would counter that by saying for $250 I expect them to last longer than some knock off brand that costs $25.

Does the sound quality make up for it?
Nope. Mediocre.

Mic any good?
Not remarkable, but not terrible per se.

Comfy?
They stick to my ears i guess, but not particularly comfy in any sense.

Conclusion:
For the price point of $250 I would expect some quality. Unfortunately they are plagued with so many issues that I don't think you can justify the price. I would have been happy with them if I paid $100 (and there are PLENTY of wireless earbuds at that price point that outshine beats, I won't name here because this isn't an advertising review).

I can see they are now down to $180, in my opinion, STILL NOT WORTH IT. I gave it two stars because the honeymoon phase was good. I'd say their useful life is 1 year, but even then battery life doesn't last as advertised.

TL;DR Connection sometimes drops for no reason. Battery and charging is TERRIBLE. Sound not particularly special. Avoid at any price above $100.

title: Android: no. Sound quaility: so-so. Live Listen: meh.
text:
I got these because they are one of the two wireless earphone types supported by Apple for use with iPhone "Live Listen". Also, many reviewers rave about their sound quality. And supposedly they work with Android. Also they have volume controls on both earbuds. Here's what I found:

Android: I was able to pair them with Android, but not to connect. I tried on three different Android devices. The Powerbeats show up on Android in the list of paired Bluetooth devices, but when you click Connect it just times out. I couldn't find any info anywhere online about what the problem was. Every site said just pair with your Android device and it should work.

iPhone's Live Listen: That app works only with Airpods and Powerbeats, so the only way to try it out is to buy the earphones and give it a whirl. As it turns out, Live Listen doesn't work much better than Google's Android equivalent, Sound Amplifier, except that you don't need hard-wired earphones. The latency is about the same, and creates a reverb/echo effect that makes speech difficult to understand. Also, Live Listen has no audio controls, whereas Sound Amplifier gives you volume and frequency controls for each ear. (However, as with Live Listen, Sound Amplifier's reverb effect produces jumbly speech. I suspect that for either of these apps to be usable you'd have to have massively noise-cancelling headphones so that no outside sound enters your ears.)

Voume control: Yes, Powerbeats Pro has volume controls on each earbud, but they're mirrored. So you can't adjust the volume for uneven hearing, even when using them with the Live Listen hearing assistance app. On the plus side, the volume control rocker switch is easy to use.

Quality: I didn't find the Powerbeats Pro sound to be any better that the $45 Bluetooth earbuds I already have.

Everything else: The case has such a stiff spring that when you open it it's likely to pop right out of your hands. "Hey Siri" works great with Powerbeats Pro. The earbuds pair easily with iPhone, and connect very quickly. But they connect only when in your ears, so when you're trying to reseat one earbud the sound cuts out in the other. And the play/pause/phone button is so huge that it's impossible to adjust an earbud without pressing it and causing all kinds of mayhem. You can use one earbud at a time, just leave the other in the case. The ear wires do fit with glasses, but after a few hours they start to hurt your ears a bit.

title: Schroedinger's wireless buds - Look for something else.
text:
I got these less than a year ago. They worked fine most of the time in the beginning. They have become a complete nightmare.

Buds failing to charge. It began with the left bud not charging after I seated it in the case. There is no way to tell whether both buds are charging or not, unless you open the case near your phone and the phone detects the case and buds. Most of the time for me, it does not. So, often when I go to use the buds, one of them is dead. It has been long been happening to both buds now.

One bud fails to pair. But sometimes it's not a lack of charge. The phone will show both buds fully charged, but one simply won't pair. I can unpair and try re-pairing, use the reset function with the phones in the case, restart my phone and re-pair everything again, and still, the bud still won't work. Then after trying everything a second or third time, something magically gets it to work.

So, Schrodinger's buds. A lot of the time they won't work, even with a charge, and you'll have no idea what will fix the problem or whether it will work even if you try.

When they did work, they sounded fine. But what's the point of having a system you can't count on at all?

Stay away from these. Look for something else. Cheers.

I regularly use wireless headphones for daily workouts 7 days a week and for casual listening when doing other things. My collections of wireless headphones is pretty extensive; sennheiser momentum, jabra elite active 65t, Samsung Icon X, Bose, Jaybird, and AirPods to Name a few. The Powerbeats Pro are the most comfortable, best sounding, and longest lasting of all of my true wireless headphones by a mile. I don’t do tame workouts- every single headphone I’ve ever worn has fallen out during every workout that I do- until I got my Powerbeats pro. These things aren’t going anywhere and are crazy comfortable. They are larger and heavier than my previous favorite, the jabra elite active 65t, but the ear hook makes it where you don’t even feel them in your ears and the 11 hours of continuous playback with ~40% left that I have experienced puts them a mile ahead in the longevity department. At 70% volume they are getting about 1hour and 30 minutes of use per 10% of battery. At that rate they would play for around 15 hours per charge. That’s nuts. I’m getting a full week (7 workouts at 2-2.5 hours each) per full charge and the case still has juice left. The sound has good bass but not overpowering to the point of being muddled like Beats products of old. Good midrange and great soundstage imo. Range is likewise killer, with no dropouts at over 85 feet from the device I am streaming from (Galaxy Note 9 and iPad Pro 2018).

My only complaint is the fact that they charge via lightning instead of USB C. That’s a bummer.

TLDR: THE best truly wireless headphones on the market right now and equally wonderful for both workouts and casual listening. The fit is so secure and comfortable that they’ll not budge in the most rigorous of activities and sound GREAT.

Highly recommended.

text:
I bought this in 2020 and have been using it regularly for the last 2 years. It's ok, but not great.

- Battery life seems very good even after 2 years.
- Microphone seems adequate for conversations.

Cons:
- I cannot get a good ear seal. I've tried no fewer than 7 different sizes and types of ear tips, including two 3rd party manufacturers (Comply and Riyo). Maybe these sound great if you get a good seal, but they are just ok without one. I've not had this problem with prior earpieces, and it is very frustrating.

- I find the charging case frustrating. I have on many occasions found that one earpiece or the other, despite seeming to be firmly placed into the charging case was not, and was dead when I pulled it out. There's no clear indication of this on the case. The case would have been better designed with an LED for each earpiece to indicate charge status and a third for the case itself.

- Batteries are not replaceable. This is an increasing concern, at least to me, in terms of generating electronic waste unnecessarily.

Overall, these are ok. They'd be five star if they sounded good (and perhaps they do with a good seal) and had more reliable charging, as is, I can only rate them 3 stars. Adequate. Good enough not to replace until they fail, but unless you can try them and be sure you get a good ear seal and are ok with the somewhat unreliable charging, I'd probably look elsewhre at this price point.

title: Charging problems are real
text:
After giving up on the product a few years ago due to charging issues, I made the faulty assumption that those problems certainly would be addressed by Apple after they acquired Beats, so I gave it a second shot and bought another pair as my first were out of warranty. After all, I loved the product aside from this glaring nuisance. A love hate relationship was born.

My charging issue on the first pair was that the right earbud would never hold a charge, would discharge even in the case, and was incredibly finicky in getting to a perfect state to take the charge in the case. Imagine my surprise when the 2nd pair I bought had the exact same problems! Only instead of showing up after warranty, they showed up within the first couple months.

So I thought, here's my chance to exercise my warranty, or so I thought. A phone call resulted in a Genius Bar visit where I found out that Apple doesn't do anything in store with the Beats products- they simply ship them away and it would have been easier for me to have just done that from the comfort of my own home. The good thing that came out of that visit though was some additional knowledge. As I took to cleaning the earbuds up a little before my visit, under a magnifying glass I noticed just a bit of build-up, maybe some would call corrosion, on one of the right earbud metal contacts. So I did a little cleaning and noticed an immediate improvement in connection and charging in the case. Upon visiting the Genius Bar I explained that I thought maybe I was onto something and if all they were going to do was ship it away (leaving me without earbuds for an extended period) then maybe I would try it out for a little while longer after a more thorough cleaning of the metal contact. The Genius Bar attendant did make me aware that Apple/Beats will not cover any corrosion issues. In essence I would likely be wasting my time if that's the source of the issue.

Basically I exercise with these buds and I guess sweat may be causing a microscopic amount of corrosion over time. It's no surprise that a person would exercise with them and no surprise that a person might sweat while doing so. The product is advertised as "sweat-resistant". But I liken this to the phone products that are water-resistant and even water-proof, however if that product feature should fail, the company takes no responsibility. In fact in a simple web search you will see that certain states have taken up a class action suit on this product citing this exact problem of sweat causing corrosion. Why the company doesn't improve this with another material, or a huge disclaimer that you must wipe down and clean the earbuds with alcohol on every use if you want them to keep charging, is beyond me.

As a big proponent of Apple products this is one of the aspects that has been a major drag on my image of the company. I had two identical waterproof designed phones exposed to very minimal water around the home button and one survived with no issues as designed and the other had the home button rendered useless and there was no recourse. Not to mention the Apple employees are well trained to pretend as if they never heard of such an issue and are very surprised at the possibility.

I wish I could recommend another product for a runner that already uses the Apple ecosystem but I haven't found one. I wish Apple/Beats would just remedy this problem or make it very clear that a problem could develop and "sweat-resistant" is a generous term. If they would fix that issue they'd have a product that can't be beat (no pun intended).

I also wish I could get my hours spent fiddling with them back. Buyer beware, they're a good product but they need nursed like a baby, so just know that going in. If you never run or sweat, maybe they'd be perfect for you.

text:

title: Great headphones, but a few things to gripe about (stupid case...)
text:
I really like these headphones, and I use them pretty much every day. I’m not an audiophile, but they sound really good for me. I mostly use them to listen to podcasts or watch video on my iPhone or iPad. They don’t have active noise-cancelling, but the ear fit does a pretty good job of blocking things out if you want them to. The Bluetooth connection is usually super fast and it’s very strong. A few times I’ve walked a long way away from my device without knowing it because the connection was perfect. Once I even left my phone in my bag and walked up a flight of stairs and down a hallway at school to print something; the sound was perfect the whole time. Overall, I’m very happy with these headphones and they’ll probably be my primary pair until they die.

Now to my complaints: 1) the charging case is a very attractive design, but the plastic finish is so smooth that there is essentially no friction at all. I drop this thing a few times a week because of it and it’s absolutely frustrating. It also slides out of my jacket pocket pretty easily too, so I have started putting the case in my backpack or zipping up my jacket pocket. I wash my hands all the time and they get very dry in the winter months, so that definitely contributes to the dropping problem some. But I still hate the finish. I also wish the lip to open it was a little deeper too because that is sometimes difficult to grasp as well.
2) the arms that go over your ears are not soft and hurt the back of my ears after a few minutes if I’m not careful about the placement.
3) the Bluetooth connection is sometimes really slow for no apparent reason. I have an iPhone 11 and an iPad Air (3rd gen), so these are all pretty new products. Most of the time, I just open the case and put the headphones in my ears, and they are connected by the time I get the second one in. But every once in a while, it’ll be about 5-10 seconds before I get the little connection chime. I know it’s a minor problem in the grand scheme of things, but when you get used to instant, things like this are annoying.

title: Not bad. Just expected better!!
text:
Once I got the correct rubber ear insert (confess with a few different sizes)the sound was good. Not great. Just good. Volume was on par. Nothing super loud. The bass, once I found the size insert for me, was good.
Comfort is really good. Stay in ear no matter what I'm doing thus far. Working out, washing car, or mowing lawn, they stay put. The sound surprisingly stays consistent throughout moving around. This for me is a plus. Others I have personally tried lost volume pressure as I moved around forcing me to adjust to get better sound. No so with these so far.
They are very comfortable. Had them in for over 3 hours with no soreness.
Battery seems to be really good. Used then for 3 hours straight and still had over 70% left when I put them back.
Connection to phone is not the greatest. Drops more often then other one I used prior.
Ear buds do not like to be away from phone out side more then a few feet. They are fine in the house 15 feet or more away from phone but outside? Nope. I don't walk away to far out buds will completely disconnect and shut down forcing you to go back to the clam shell charging station to reactivate...
These are VERY GOOD ear buds for $75. These are GOOD ear buds for $100. But for nearly$200? Not good at all. Sound quality is not amazing. Build quality is okay. Connection to the phone is not that great. When compared to a $50 pair I picked up very hard to see/feel/hear the difference. They're not bad but for the price I guess you're just paying for the name, disappointed.

title: Charging system barely works. UPDATE: DOES NOT WORK
text:
UPDATE: Drop from 3 starts to 1. A couple of weeks later and the charging system has gone from barely functional to almost completely broken. The left earbud does not charge without major intervention, including wiggling it and pushing it around for multiple minutes, unplugging/plugging in and opening/closing the cases. It registers 1% battery and charging but the % does not increase. After more fiddling it jumps to 45% (presumably it's actual charge). I found a Reddit thread with many other people having the same issue. If this continues, which seems a surety, I will return for a refund and get different earbuds that work properly. I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS PRODUCT.

Sound and noise cancellation are quite good if one of the included earbud sizes fits your ears. In my case, sound was bad with the medium (default) size but quite good with large. It would be nice to have more sizes though because large is a bit too big for my ears (hard to put in).

The main reason I'm giving 3 stars rather than 4 or 5 is that the charging station is bad. I have to fiddle with it for minutes to get charging started, usually can only charge one side at a time because two at a time don't seat properly, and have to check repeatedly to make sure charging hasn't stopped. It also has weird bugs where the detected battery level jumps rapidly between different levels.

Another problem I've had is with connectivity. I've only had them a few weeks and have had to reset them once already to reconnect to my iPhone. Connectivity is also dropped and sometimes requires fiddling to reestablish when an alarm goes off on the phone.

title: Great-sounding small earbuds
text: Tozo makes excellent earbuds. In recent years, I have owned several and I have given others away as gifts because I believe they deliver excellent value. The new Tozo A1 earbuds are no exception. Their sound is rich throughout the range, with plenty of bass punch for those who like it. Their Bluetooth connection is solid, even at distances and around metal objects where my other wireless phones begin to break up. Best of all, the A1s are very small and ultra-lightweight. While they don't offer noise cancellation, their noise isolation eliminates most outside distractions. They are a good buy at any price, but at the discounts now being offered, they are an incredible value. I highly recommend them.

title: Good ear buds, but overpriced.
text: Overall these are good ear buds.  They Meet my purpose for a bud that doesn't fall out when I work out, and the battery life is good with the charging station.  I didn't find the sound quality all that amazing you would expect for a $200 pair of buds.  I have $30 ones that sound just as good if not better.  As far as noise cancellation it doesn't appear to be active.  I don't notice any white noise or anything killing outside sounds.  The buds just provide a really good seal.  there is no on/off button so the buds are supposed to turn on when it senses they are in your ear, which sometimes they do and sometimes they don't.  It's kind of annoying.  The mic clarity is really good for the mic being back at your ear, but I didn't buy workout ear buds to talk.  Like I said overall it is a good product, but I feel priced high because it is an Apple product.  There are definitely cheaper alternatives.  After hearing them if I was going to pull out 200 dollars for a set again I would look towards Bose, Sony, JBL, or someone else known for good sound clarity before I pulled the trigger on these.

text:
I love almost everything about them.

Sound quality is superb: clear vocals, punchy lows/mids, and a crisp highs. The case is TINY and stays closed very securely as well as snugly holding the earbuds in place thanks to some small magnets. They also stay in place really well, which is the main reason I got them. I have a pair of Skullcandy Indys, but they don't stay in place and slowly work their way loose and will fall out if I don't adjust them every so often. The Tozos on the other hand I can pop in and not have to worry about them coming out even when doing something strenuous like mountain biking, or abrupt like crashing to the ground on said bike...😅

The only thing that's somewhat annoying is that you can sometimes have a bit of interference with the bluetooth signal (could have been the area I was in), and there really isn't very much noise cancelation on the microphone when used for calls. Background noise can be picked up more than your voice, so the person on the other end may hear more of what's around you than of your actual voice in a moderately noisy setting.

I have ordered the Fit Beats Pro, only because no version of Apple's Air Pods will stay in my ear and I really want ear buds with the H1 chip to make my Apple devices work together. title: Best headphones are crossfitters
text:
Ok. I've worn these a while now so I can give a good review on them. I workout 6-7 times a week and use these everyday. My workouts are the same: weight lifting, then high intense cardio/circuits (similar to crossfit). Other days I go for 4-5 mile runs. Overall, these are awesome. I use these with my Galaxy S10e, so there are some limitations as they are designed by Apple -_-

Pros:
Amazing fit. They do not move or wiggle out. I have different sized ear canals, so wearing any kind of in-ear buds are hard, especially without the hook that goes behind the ear. These headphones are designed perfectly for fit. Sounds is great and loud. Same controls on BOTH headphones. The headphones I had before only had controls on the right ear bud which was annoying. They do well at noise cancelling, not like over the ear headphones though obviously (so just turn up the music). The charging case they fit in is nice- lots of battery life. I charge them usually only once a week.

Cons:
- Sometimes (once out of 10/15 times) they don't auto connect straight away with my phone. I just dock them in the charging cradle for a second and them pull them back out and they auto-sync. So, it is not that big of a deal. Again, that's because I have a Samsung. On that note, if you have an Apple phone you can adjust the base, treble etc. You can't do that on a Samsung phone. But I don't think I'd mess with all that anyways. The charging cradle doesn't wireless charge, but I ain't that lazy. I'm capable and fine with having to plug in a cable to charge them.

- I've noticed that when the gym gets packed and lots of wireless headphones are out, sometimes the headphones have trouble staying connected. Especially when I walk away a good distance from my phone. I don't have this problem with a few people being in the gym though.

- If you are a heavy sweater, like I am, then you'll want some kind of headband or hat to go with these. The reason is because these headphones have sensors built into each headphone. If you take one of them out of your ear, then the music will pause. This is a feature that can't be turned off. Initially, I thought it was a nice feature, but now I don't like it and wish you could turn it off in the setting menu or something. The reason I'm not a fan of it is because if you sweat alot and the sweat trickles down into your ear, it has the tendency to get between your ear and that sensor. This is enough disruption of contact which causes the unit to think it is out of you ear and pauses your music. Again, this is with heavy sweaters. If you wear a headband or hat that prevents the sweat from getting into your ear then you're fine.

- I do wish the main circular "b" button was harder to push/more tactile. It is pretty easy to push and sometimes accidently gets hit, but that is just being picky now.

Again, overall these are great headphones. They could use some adjustments. But I would highly recommend them.

title: Overpriced and unreliable - Not worth the money
text:
I regret spending money on these, but more than that I regret all of the time spent to deal with all of their myriad problems.

Almost immediately after purchasing these, I noticed the left earbud sometimes would not produce any sound. Sometimes it would just shut off. After spending an hour or so troubleshooting, I disconnected them from my phone, only to learn that they would not reconnect.

I called apple support and explained my issues. After about an hour with them, they agreed to repair them. I went to my local apple store, where I needed to convince the person working there that I had not submerged or otherwise damage them. They were sent out, repaired, and sent back.

Now I would have working earbuds, I thought. No, I would not - after about a week, the left earbud started cutting in and out again. At this point, I can't easily replicate the issue, so I am waiting for it to just die so I can send them off for repairs, again. I wish I could just return them for a refund.

Please, don't make the mistake I did. These are the most exhausting tech purchase I have ever made.

title: It's great but hear me out first.
text:
When I first heard about these I was super excited and pre-purchased it and waited nearly a month for. I was super happy to first get them and try them on. The sound was great and the over the ear design was something I was looking for. I have been using these for about 4-6 hours a day for 2 weeks or so now. I really like the light weight feel. It did take me a bit to figure out how to slide these in and out of my ears but it took almost no time. They have a good sound to them, I have tested them on a few bass heavy songs and it lacks but it was to be expected. Over all I was very pleased with the whole product.

There would be a few changes I would make personally. First would be the case grip, it is slick and nice in and out of a pocket but to open you might slip your hands trying to open. It is a small gripe but should be mentioned. Another thing that I find a real issue with is the comfort in ear. One day I had one unit in and the other in the case. The left ear was in for about 4 hours and now my ear is bruised and very very sore. I cant stand putting it back in longer then a few seconds now. I really am thinking about returning them, the pain is quite bad. I didn't have it lose or bit hit while in my ear just normal walking and sitting.

I will be letting my ear heal fully again before I try and use it again but if it returns I will be asking for a refund. I shouldn't be getting hurt while doing normal activities. The design of the part made in ear is a hard round bit of plastic and that's what caused the issue. I honestly think it should have been rubber or something of the sort to better sound proof your ear and for comfort. The over ear arm should be the one to keep it mostly in place not this huge disk with no give at all.

I may be a special case and the only one this has happened to so far but I think it should be told. Maybe someone else would just read this and make sure this is really the product for them before spending the hefty price tag.

title: Definitely not worth the money.
text:
Not sure how or why these have such great reviews.

The only positive thing I have to say is that I appreciate how quiet these can get (almost whisper quiet), which is quite nice. Unfortunately, if you are listening to something with a very quiet recording, you can only barely get these loud enough to hear, and then only if you are in a quiet setting and have both earbuds in place. Because of this type of situation, I was able to learn these earbuds can produce a bass tone I did not otherwise notice with normal listening settings, which was neat, but otherwise useless.

Unfortunately, these only come with three size earpieces. You would think they would be enough, but they are not. The medium are too big and hard. If I use them for too long my ear begins to hurt. The small are too small and if I use them, the earbuds do not stay in my ear and are constantly falling out. All the earpieces are also short, so none of them really stay in well. I had to use ear pieces from a less expensive brand that came with 6 different sizes (buds that were only 1/5th the price, too).

Because of the twisting motion that is required to put these in your ear properly, I almost always accidentally press the play button before I am ready. Also, even with the more comfortable earpieces I use from another brand, because of the weird footprint these earbuds have, they still do not stay in place well. Also, when repositioning to make sure they don't fall out, I almost always pause what I am listening to by accident. VERY FRUSTRATING.

Only while using the better earpieces from the significantly less expensive brand will these buds stay in place while running, but it sounds like someone is playing a bass drum inside my ear everytime my foot hits the ground (PAINFULLY UNCOMFORTABLE). This does not happen with any of the less expensive brands I have owned.

There is no standby mode with these, so as soon as the earbuds are out of the charger the battery drain time starts ticking and you only get 8 hours or less when fully charged regardless of whether you are listening to anything or not and regardless of whether you are using the noise canceling or transparency modes or not.

The noise canceling function is really not any better with it on or off. The transparency mode is a neat idea, but when there is no sound and nothing is playing it sounds as if you are standing in a wind tunnel (noisy and uncomfortable to listen to). Not worth the loss of battery life to use either function.

There is a Beats app you can install. Other than being able to see what mode your earbuds are in, there is really no benefit to installing it though. I had to uninstall it because it was malfunctioning and causing my earbuds to randomly and repeatedly switch into transparency mode (SUPER ANNOYING).

The only way to see how much charge is left on the docking station is to check your phone while the lid is open. I don't like that I have to look at my phone to see how much charge the docking station has left instead of having a built in meter like many other brands.

There is no effective way to tell if your buds are seated correctly in the docking station and are actually charging.

Major buyer's regret after purchasing these. Definitely NOT WORTH THE MONEY.

title: Don't ignore the lawsuits
text:
Google class action lawsuit against power beats pro. You are very likely to encounter un-charged buds despite putting them in the case and there isn't' any feedback to the user if BOTH are being charged. I'll spend 5minutes+ trying to ensure they are in the case correctly with no luck. About half the time, only a single bud is seated properly.

Another basic product feature its missing is there is no off switch. Once you pull them from the case, the battery life is ticking away.

Another basic product feature its missing is the ability to pair/connect on occasion without the case. Sometimes the buds drop the connection and require to be re-seated in the case and a button pressed on the case to re-pair. This means, if you want to reliably use these, you must bring the bulky case with you anywhere on bike rides or runs.

Pickup a ultra cheap pair of BT buds and you are unlikely to encounter any of these issues.

title: Very good
text:
Out of all the wireless earbuds I’ve used, these have got to be my favorite sound quality wise. The most expensive wireless buds I’ve purchased were the Samsung Galaxy Buds 2 and boy they were terrible. It was when I bought the Beats Studio Buds that I realized that the Buds 2’s sound quality was truly terrible. These beats buds are just very good. Most buds (in order to give the illusion that they’re good quality) typically increase the bass but then the rest of the music sounds terrible. But with these, the bass is increased but the rest of the sound isn’t compromised and is very clear. Very good quality buds. I’m not giving these a 5 stars tho however since there are some issues that I wish would be fixed.
1.) This is very minor, but the earbuds don’t pause the audio once they’re taken out like other earbuds I’ve used (i.e. the Samsung Galaxy Buds 1 and 2). Not a huge problem but sucks having to replay a moment of a song I just missed because I had to take my earbuds out for a sec.
2.) Another small thing, but the audio stops completely when you put in one of the buds which is just a little inconvenience.
3.) This isn’t such a small problem like the last two complaints. Sometimes when I put both buds in the case, one of them doesn’t tend to charge and so then my phone recognizes that the earbuds are out of the case and so then my audio from my phone comes out from the earbud that’s supposed to be charging and disconnected from my phone. This is problematic because sometimes I’ll be trying to use my buds just for one of them to be at 5% since it just wasn’t charging in the case so then I have to wait for it to charge, which isn’t a long time but it’s still very annoying.
4.) The transparency mode kind of sucks. Whilst the Samsung Galaxy Buds 2’s overall audio sucked, it’s transparency mode was much louder which meant I didn’t have to turn down my earbuds just talk still hear whoevers talking to me like I have to do with the Beats Studio Buds. You can barely hear any outside noises with the transparency mode on if the Buds’ volume is somewhere around 50%. The noise cancelling mode is pretty good though.
5.) Finally, the mic doesn’t work that well. From my experience of calling people with the buds on, whilst the sound quality is pretty good compared to other buds, you have to talk kind of loud as the buds don’t pick up much sound. I typically just disconnect my buds when I’m answering a call and just use my phone’s mic because it’s much more convenient than having to yell-talk to my buds just for people to hear me.

Overall these are good buds, especially for 90 bucks (which is what they were when I bought them on sale). If you’re looking for something that’s fairly cheap but still has good quality, then these are the buds for you.

title: Best Bluetooth Headphones. Outstanding Sound Quality.
text:
Bought these for my sons for Christmas, but one of them wanted to exchange for a new monitor. So, I decided to keep these myself. Already had a great pair of Jaybird bluetooth phones for running and for the gym but thought I'd try these out, and I'm so incredibly glad I did. Highly recommend.
Beats are known for excellent bass, and these certainly don't disappoint. It's critical, though, to try out the different earbuds that come with them. I though they sounded great with the medium size that came on them. But they sound phenomenal with the larger size for me.
Sound quality doesn't end there though. Clear, balanced highs (not too bright), solid midrange for voices, great impact, and super fast transients. And detail! I've heard detail in music I haven't heard on a B&W 802/McIntosh 600W Monoblock system before - seriously.
I wouldn't have believed it possible. I'm listening to my favorite audiophile tracks and finding new joy in music I've heard many times on many other high-end systems.
Granted, these don't have active noise cancelling like the AirPods Pro, but with a solid seal they seemed at least as good as the ANC on my Beats Studios on a flight yesterday.
I can't speak to battery life or reliability (will update if needed) because I haven't had them that long. Considering how expensive audiophile gear can be, at this price point these aren't just a recommendation, they're a bargain!
