Way to quiet now for some reason. When I first got these the volume was loud at the high end. Now the high end volume isn’t. I’ve checked all the settings, but there is no obvious reason why these are suddenly quiet. I guess I’ll contact Apple support... again...

For some reason the sound does not seem to be balanced between the two ear pieces at times. This seems to be corrected with a reset. Resetting the earpieces requires holding a button on the charging case for 20 seconds. A control app with info for these earpieces and adjustments would take all the guessing out of the experience.

These are super comfortable and the over ear loop makes them feel secure. Running I can hear wind noise, I’m guessing that would be the case with any device, but there is a wind noise.

They turn on when placed in our ear. No on and off switch and the buttons are simple and easy to use.

I really, really want to like them, but if I can’t get the volume problem sorted out I won’t be able to keep them. I’m already nervous about durability considering they were broken on arrival. I run in the elements everyday of the year and these were marketed as something that was supposed to be able to handle the abuse. We shall see.

title: Meh Audio. Comfy though.
text:
I needed some earbuds quick like after I couldn't find my trusty buds and I had prime, these were the only available ones for one-day same day shipping, and they used USB-C to charge, and my GF needed a pair as well. And when you type ANC into amazon's search these are the only ones that come up. Should've read the specs a bit harder; that isn't TOZO's fault just amazon being unfriendly.

Anyway, onto the buds:

The construction:
They are, the definition of mid, meh, whatever. Okay, fine, these are awful-ish? They are super plasticky feeling, not a slippery plastic feeling but these weren't built with quality in mind. They are fine to be honest. The eartips included are those flimsy plastic ones that are always included in cheap-o buds like these. Maybe they are silicone but I couldn't tell that's for sure. They do the job but it could've been done better. The default tips work fine for me but maybe experimenting with the included ones can get me a better seal. The buds themselves feel fine. They are shockingly light so I could see these being an advantage for fitness people who need earbuds that last two hours max for a gym outing. The charging case is where they really cut back. It's not the best built case. If the buds are waterproof the case most definitely is not. Be careful because if you loose the case you lose the buds anyway. The lid on the case closes with even the slightest of breezes so that WILL annoy you very quickly. See the included video in this review. When you put the earbuds to charge the lights on the case light up once, and that's it. There's no other activity to indicate the earbuds are being charged so you have to open the case and look at the buds themselves. The buds themselves only have a blue light or red light for charging or something. There's no included instructions on the packaging so you'll have to take your best guess on what that means. Luckily most bluetoth hardware should show the charge on the buds.

The sound:
These are not your audiophile phones that's for sure. I've messed around with various EQ settings on my phones, PC, laptop, etc. I just can't quite get them to behave right. That being said after walking around and playing music through them while shopping at Costco and such I've been pleasantly surprised at the ability to damped sound. Way better than I expected.

Fit:
The one part these headphones shine is that they are very comfortable to wear. At no point was I tired of wearing them, they just fit right. They are light and the angle they are built in works for your ear. I've gotta say it's a good design. Wish they had better everything else. If you are the kind that sleeps with earbuds on these may be your ticket.

Pairing:
Worked just like your standard Bluetooth earbuds. Take them out, check your Bluetooth menu, pair them, and you are done. I should point out the announcer voice is hilariously awful. No multi-device pairing so be careful of that one. These connected to my Samsung phone before my Pixel 4XL (my main phone) for some reason and I was lost for a bit wondering why they weren't connecting. Something to watch out for if you have various Bluetooth devices around you and are wondering why they aren't pairing right.

Packaging:
Very eco friendly packaging. Everything was cardboard with some kind of eco-friendly foam thing which felt not unlike a dish scrubber. Included was the eartips, a comically small USB-C cable and the buds and case themselves. I have to say, I approve. The less plastic I have to deal with the better.

Summary:
If I could sum up these earbuds it would be simple:
"Great design, decent implementation"

It would be nice if Tozo could take this same design and make a better high end version of them.

By design, the right ear pod is going to stop charging. At times I didn't think this was going to be the problem when I first had them. However, it started to become more frequent where everytime I put them in the charging case the right side wouldn't charge.

Queue the "you should have made sure they were in there"

I did. Today is when the right side of the charging case actually gave out. You cannot reset the bluetooth unless you have both in the charging case to allow both to connect to a device. Once that goes out you'll never be able to hear the right earpod again.

Don't believe me? Check youtube. Go youtube all the possible fixes for this problem and read all the pissed off customers who cannot fix this problem.

Do yourself a favor. Get a better product. One that actually will last. If you had to pay 200 dollars for a years worth of sound, you'll end up exceeding that price point by the middle of the year since you'll be forced to buy another set of these trash headphones.

text:
I really wanted to like these earbuds because I am a very active runner and weight lifter. Other earbuds kept falling out of my ears when I would start sweating. So, the hear hooks were a big feature in selecting these. I had owned a previous version with the beats that were connected by a cable and loved them but the battery started failing after 4 years and I needed a new set.
Let me start by saying that the design of these earbuds is fantastic. They're sleek and the design allowed the silicon tips to lay in the ear canal comfortably without falling out while working out. Sound was just ok. The bass was not that great and the design, while keeping the tip inserted in the ear canal did not allow for a firm fit so there was a bit of sound leakage.
Over the course of 6 weeks I have had to replace these 3 times. Amazon customer service was great! The first set of buds began to have bluetooth connection issues. The left earbud would disconnect during normal operation and then reconnect after 30 seconds or so. But it would happen in the middle if a workout or worse a phone call and the devices were brand new. After every effort at solving the problem myself, I gave up and assumed that it was a bad unit and asked Amazon to replace them - which they did.
The second set was operating ok for about 6 days. Around the seventh day, the volume and action buttons just stopped working! There was not physical damage or shock or anything that would have caused them to malfunction. So, I asked Amazon to replace these, which they did.
The 3rd set worked fine for about 2 weeks. Then the set started losing the bluetooth connection - again! Let me sat that I have a brand new Samsung S22. The phone has no issues connecting to any other blue tooth device at all. So, I can only conclude that there is an issue with the product itself. I ended up replacing these with the Skokz Open Run Pros and have been have been happy with these so far.

title: Glad I waited for the Powerbeats Pro!
text:
I want to preface this before I say anything about these headphones: I primarily use headphones for music and podcasts while I am cycling, running, or sitting at my desk at work. I use Spotify for music, and I am not an audiophile. I am not comparing these to a pair of Sennheisers with a lossless audio format as my source. I also am using an iPhone 7+ and iPad Air 2 for my devices in this review.

I have been waiting on a getting a pair of truly wireless headphones because none seemed to be worth it to me. The battery life is usually dismal for obvious reasons, and most had complaints of cutouts between the earbuds. Some friends of mine have Air Pods and they all said they didn’t have cutout issues and battery life was pretty good. But, I just didn’t like the design of the Air Pods and they sounded “hollow” to me. But I get their appeal.

I am so glad I waited for the Powerbeats Pro (PBP)! I was using the Jaybird X3 before I got these, and I think the sound is on par with them. One of my main annoyances with the X3’s was that the cord would tug once sweat built up on my neck while exercising, and I couldn’t use the cable shortener they provide because of the way my helmet is. I went for a bike ride yesterday with the PBP’s, and they were fantastic! It was a little windy, so I did get a little wind noise. I am hoping Comply makes some tips for these because I think that would make the noise isolation much better. My ride was around 2 hours and I still had 80% left on the PBP battery.

Cons:

1. The case: it’s actually smaller than I thought, but would still be uncomfortable in a pocket. I think the 9 hour battery life on the actual headphones make this acceptable, but this may be deal breaker for some.

2. Ear fatigue: I didn’t have any fatigue during my ride, but my ears were definitely a little sensitive where the hook was resting after I took the headphones off. I’m hoping this gets better as I wear them.

3. Like the Air Pods, the PBP’s can only be connected to one device at a time. They will pair to all Apple devices on your iCloud account, but if you want to switch between devices, you have to go into your Bluetooth settings and select them. On Android you will need to pair each device separately.

4. I usually listen to a podcast when I go to sleep. These are not comfortable to lay on if you are side sleeper like I am. Also, the button the headphones will get pushed by the pillow. The button doesn’t require much force, which is great because your not shoving the headphones into your ear. Not a huge deal, but just thought I would mention it.

Pros:

1. Great sound for Truly wireless, I think.

2. Great fit for exercise.

3. Pretty good sound isolation, but like I said, I am hoping Comply makes some tips for these.

4. Actual headphones are smaller than I thought they would be, and they don’t look weird on you when you are just walking down the street.

Bottom line, if you use an iOS device and use headphones while exercising, I can’t recommend these enough! In my opinion, the $250 price tag is worth it given where other truly wireless headphones are priced.

title: Almost perfect headphones.
text:
I have had my Powerbeats Pro for about a week now and after a bit of a rocky start and an adjustment period, I find them to be almost perfect headphones. When I first put them on, I was wildly disappointed. They were uncomfortable and sounded tinny with no bass at all. I genuinely believed I would be returning them and getting second gen Air Pods instead. But, given how excited I was for the Powerebeats Pro to come out and the cost, I decided to put in a little effort and give them a chance. It wasn't until about 3 or 4 days in that I decided to keep them.

So, if you are like me and think your new Powerbeats Pro sound like garbage when you first put them on and you wonder if all the positive reviewers are high, experiment with all the tips before dismissing the headphones as crap. In-ear buds need a good seal to sound good. I have freakishly small ears so I always start with the smallest tip available when trying out new headphones which usually works for me. Not this time. It sounded awful and I was briefly outraged that I had paid $250 for garbage. It was counter-intuitive, but I finally tried the biggest tips instead which gave me a good seal and let me wear the headphones without having to go as deep into my ears which made them more comfortable too. Once I found the right fit with a good seal, I discovered that yes, in fact, these things do actually have some nice ear-thumping bass. I think the bass is better than original Air Pods but also not overwhelming as Beats products have a reputation for being. It's satisfyingly skull shaking without being distorted and is balanced out nicely by clear highs. I'm not an audiophile by any means, but I won't listen to any old crap either. I like a little bass and good clarity and the Powerbeats Pro deliver.

My biggest issue with these is comfort. As I mentioned, I have freakishly small ears and while I have been using Air Pods for a couple years, I was doing so with discomfort. I put up with a little paind because of the convenience of function. I love the automatic connection, the ability to use one bud at a time and charging on the go in the case. So, when I first read about the Powerbeats Pro, I was expecting something that would have the convenience of Air Pods with better comfort and something that wouldn't fall out of my ears all the time. Generally, I do okay with headphones that have different sizes of silicone tips so I was expecting the Powerbeats Pro to be a comfort upgrade. Initially, they actually hurt my ears more than Air Pods, especially my right ear. I fully blame this on my freakishly small ears. I'm one of those people who often finds "one size fits all" to be laughably ridiculous. Again, I was determined to love these things so I tinkered a bit to find an acceptable level of discomfort. The largest tip allows me to get a good seal without having to put them in so deep, relieving some pressure and cutting down on pain. When I first tried them, I could only last about 20 minutes before the pain forced me to take them out. After adjusting to find a good angle and replacing the silicone tips with Comply Sport tips, I'm a lot more comfortable and can last 2 or 3 hours before I feel discomfort. Even then, I would call it discomfort and not outright pain. It's discomfort I can live with and not any worse than what I experience with Air Pods. Also, my discomfort is only in my right ear instead of both like I get with Air Pods. Since I go with one bud a lot of the time, I'll just use the left one. No biggie. I can't blame the manufacturer for my tiny ears which is why I'm not taking away a star.

On the plus side, the fit is very secure. I have worked out in them several times and they don't budge. I never could work out in Air Pods because they fell out all the time. I can also wear these while laying down which I couldn't do in Air Pods without them falling out periodically. Also, the connection is great. Original Air Pods used to randomly lose connection or not connect when they were supposed to. The chip upgrade in the Powerbeats Pro seems to have resolved this little annoyance. They connect faster and after a week, I haven't experienced a drop or glitch once.

The Powerbeats Pro do come with a tradeoff when it comes to the size of the case. If you are used to carrying around Air Pods in your pocket in their tiny case, forget about it with Powerbeats Pro. The case is significantly larger. It goes in a bag or purse without taking up a ton of room but it's too big to fit comfortably in a pocket. The extra battery life for Powerbeats is nice though. I frequently use one bud at a time and used to drain an Air Pod and have to switch ears regularly. I'm using the Powerbeats Pro the same way and haven't drained a bud yet. I'm okay with the bigger case since the better battery life makes me feel secure about leaving the case at home when I need to go bagless.

So in summary, these are the best sounding buds I have used. They are super convenient, easy to connect and won't fall out of your ears. If you have normal human sized ears, they will probably be comfortable and the battery life is great. You have to deal with a bigger case but the positive improvements over Air Pods make the size trade-off worth it. If you don't hear the bass, try different tips and twist them around a bit before you give up. Hopefully you won't have to work as hard at it as I did to find your happy place with Powerbeats Pro but the effort has been worth it. These are really great headphones and worth the price.

title: Great truly wireless headphones!
text:
I’ve been waiting for these to get released as soon as I saw the reviews online appraising it. I have a number of wireless/BT headphones already such as the QC35/AirPods/and several cheaper $15-25 BT headphones that I use for various things. If my AirPods didn’t fall out of my ear while running/doing box jumps/ pausing music when benching because it moves a little bit, I probably would not have thought about buying these at all! I really tried to like them but the one issue I’ve had is that my ears are rather large and the hooks put a lot of pressure on the cartilage at the back of my ear. For that fact alone after using for 10-15m at the gym or talking with someone, I may be returning these. But read on why this is the ultimate workout bud if you don’t have large ears like myself.

The beats are as easy to setup as AirPods, as your phone will detect it as soon as you open the case up, and you can put them on and they will immediately and automatically connect to your phone. My first impression from these were that the music quality is actually much better compared to the AirPods. When I first turned them on to listen to music, my first reaction was that I had been introduced to a myriad of sounds I hadn’t noticed before when listening on AirPods! The other great thing is that the mic work well for conference calls on the phone or just when talking to people in general (the main lacking feature in the cheaper BT headphones). Feedback has been that my voice is crystal clear while using these earbuds.

The package also includes 4 ear tips total to help customize the fit and it charges through a lightning cable that’s included in the package. The case is fairly large but easily fits in a gym bag. If you carry these in your pants, there would definitely be a noticeable bulge in the right or left pocket and is not as convenient as AirPods which you can bring everywhere discretely. Definitely one of the best earphones you can buy right now and one that I really wanted to work for me, unfortunately I currently am having slight discomfort.

title: Incredible quality headphones I would buy again, even despite minor drawbacks
text:
These headphones are fantastic and have some neat features!

I'll start with the positives:
They stay on my head and sound great!
Simple stick-in-your-ear style buds always fall out of my ears, but have good sound quality. Headphones that curve over my ear to hold it in place stay put, but have bad sound quality. This is the perfect marriage of those features, which I love. These things stay the heck on my head, which is awesome. The sound is incredibly clear - you can hear everything with these. The built in mics handle Bluetooth phone calls remarkably well. I can hear people, and they seem to be able to hear me well. On the note of the Bluetooth, these things have some serious range. I left my phone in the kitchen and went to the restroom about 25 feet away while listening to music with them, and I had no skips or issues through two walls, a door, and who knows how much piping and wiring in the walls. That alone is freaking awesome. That can vary by house design, but it works great where I am. I can mix and match - I can use both headphones, or just one, and it will cut off the sound in the unused ones automatically. They both have the same buttons, so both are fully functional by themselves. It auto pauses music when I take then out, and starts it back up when I put them back in. For those who don't like that feature, it can be disabled through the Beats app after pairing your headphones to it.

These headphones are also SEXY. Everything about them is sleek from the case to the buds themselves. They keep a low profile in the ear and look remarkably professional if you need to be on the job. They are attractive, sound good, and generally are just excellent.

Here are some personal cons:

The buds are somewhat uncomfortable. There are 4 different sized buds, so that can be mitigated, but none of them seem to fit my ears comfortably. That could just be how my ears are shaped.

I'm a music producer for a hobby, so balanced, true-to-the-audio sound is important to me. These headphones are fairly bass and treble heavy, and have a sort of odd, squashed or "flat" sound in the midrange I don't know how to describe. For me, it is somewhat irritating to have headphones at this price that don't have balanced sound, but that's not what they're made for. They're made for casual listeners who like clear bass and treble headphones while looking good. This in no way detracts from the clarity of the sound - it is PRISTINE despite the boosts to those frequencies - just a personal gripe.

Lastly, these are NOT noise canceling. I frequently have to turn up the volume just to overcome background noise. Also not what they're made for, but it would be a nice feature in future models.

Overall, these things are amazing despite my personal gripes. I would buy them again, largely because I seriously doubt I'll find any other headphones that I'll like that have even half the quality and overall features these have. The over the ear grip combined with the earbud design, plus the Bluetooth range, make for an absolute winner for me.

Edit: I use them so frequently now that the smaller buds cause severe discomfort. Had to put in the largest buds in my small ears just so they don't hurt. I'd still buy again because no other brand of headphone I know of has the earbud/over the ear hook design with this level of sound quality.

title: Good sound. Not the best overall design.
text:
Loving the sound of these. Amazing what they can produce for something small and wireless. I have no complaints with the music they produce. What I do have a problem with is the design of everything.

First is the case. Not sure why they didn't put a lip to grab hold of to open it. It's too slick and if you're trying to open them without looking, it's like that third dimension of opening. So the lack of any type of tactile lid opening is head-scratching.

Then once you get the lid open, you're faced with your second challenge. Getting the buds out of the case. The buds are design so that there's nothing to grab hold of. I've now adapted a method where I push the bud off to the side, and then am able to get out.

Your third challenge comes when you put them in your palm together and need to figure out which one is Left and which one is Right. I have the black pair, and the markings are pretty much invisible. So I've taken a silver oil marker and wrote over the L and R. I can now instantly identify.

Those problems have to be universal for everything. One that's more specifically my problem is that my ear canals are apparently smaller than normal. The small provided tips do not stay in. I can't take a step before they pop out. I was about to return the buds before I did some research. I ended up buying two brands that offer different options. One with foam tips and the other an x-small silicon tip. The foam ones hurt my ears and eventually worked their way back out. So I returned those and kept the silicon ones. WHile better than stock, they're not perfect. Luckily the design of the buds are lightweight, so they stay in somewhat. While working out, I have to keep pushing them in, but they don't shoot out like the OEM buds did.

So overall I like them, but am questioning their design. Small changes could have made a huge difference.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: So glad I went for it!
text:
Several months ago I decided to finally join this decade and buy some Bluetooth headphones. I was mostly focused on the various Airpods options, but I decided to check these out when they came up on Deal of the Day. My main concern was that they fit smaller ears and reviews seemed a bit mixed, but so far I'm extremely happy with these. They come with four different caps - not only different sizes but also different shapes. I had to try a couple to find the best ones for me, but found that the small narrow ones allow me to wear these for hours without any discomfort at all, which has not been my past experience with in-ear headphones.

Pros:
- Sizing and variety of ear caps
- The clip-over-ear design makes them feel very secure. I haven't exercised with them yet but they don't feel like they are going to be constantly at risk of falling out.
- I'm no audiophile, but the sound quality and noise cancellation both seem solid
- Integration with iPhone is awesome and they've worked well with my Windows laptop as well
- Love that they use the same cable as my iPhone so I don't need to keep track of another charger
- Battery life is excellent so far

Cons:
- Periodic issues with connectivity on my laptop where they won't stay connected; this seems to be more of a Windows issue than a headphone issue. Restarting the computer when this happens is an irritating but effective fix.
- The various modes (flashing/solid red and white lights) are a bit confusing but don't generally impede my use of the headphones.
- Super excessive packaging. Obviously this is only a big factor when first receiving, but why on earth do we need 3 different nesting boxes.

title: Android Users Beware
text:
I had an absolutely horribly experience with this product from the get go. However, I guess I'll start off with the good stuff. These things are slick. I think they look super cool and fit really well. I would wear them for hours at work and hardly notice they were there. The sound quality was fantastic and the battery life was insanely good. When they charged (and I will get to this later), they charged insanely fast. Needless to say, I really, really wanted to like these headphones, but I just couldn't deal with the problems I had with them. I will just issue a warning to all Android users, DO NOT BUY THESE. Apple has ruined a once amazing product that was able to be used seamlessly across all devices and now using it to ploy more people to enter into their exclusive ecosystem. The app that beats/apple uses for Android users acts like it's in a constant fight with apples operating system. It will never accurately display the battery life of your headphones. Connectivity was an issue from the start. The moment I walked into a crowded gym where everyone is using some kind of wireless head phone, they cut out constantly. Even after the trouble shooting of restarting the case and turning on location services, it did not fix the problem. This happened whenever I was in a room with more than 3 people using Bluetooth for headphones. Second off, and perhaps the most annoying, the right headphones completely stopped accepting a charge. I really don't know what else to say about that but I just find it unexcuseable. $250 for these? Yeah, I would pick another pair of headphones if you don't have an iPhone. I'm not sure how much better they will be but according to recent Apple forums, the one headphones not charging is starting to become less and less rare.

Luckily amazon let me return them. I purchased the JayBird Versas in place of these and wow am I impressed. Check them out.

I was looking for something to replace my gen 1 airpods (they still work they’re just old) but the airpods definitely are staying because of this and the next point.

Having a physical button instead of touch based controls is increasingly annoying especially when on a phone call because it only takes one accidental push to end the call.

Out of they box they came with and almost full charge which was really nice but after using them for a few days at work it felt like they barely held a charge and I could easily use the earpiece battery and the case battery through a whole day without charging it.

Also the noise cancellation is a great setting and idea, but there’s no signifier letting you know if its on or off. Maybe there should be like an audio signal that says it? It made a noise when changing mode but its the same when you turn it on and off, its really hard to tell when you only use one earbud.

Other than that I have a few picky things like the case being pretty massive, and the fact that it needs a usb c cable to charge and it didn’t even come with one and I didn’t see anything about it needing one when I ordered it, luckily I had one from a magnetic charger I bought.

I’ve already returned this item and got my money back but man I do miss the sound quality of these things but its not worth the above mentions. I’m still using my gen 1 airpods because they have no issues other than they don’t have sound cancellation and that the sound quality just isn’t exactly on par but its not too big of a difference

Someone can be standing right next to me trying to talk to me and I can barely hear that they're making any noise at all, let alone what they're saying. The sound quality is great; storage case is convenient; the earbuds feel very secure in my ears and don't fall out (a problem I've had with multiple other brands of earbuds in the past). I can't recommend these enough.

My only complaint is that the microphone might not be great; I was talking on the phone to someone using these recently and they were having trouble hearing me. But I mostly use them for one-way listening (music, podcasts) rather than two-way conversations, so I haven't tested this at length. (I was in an airport surrounded by ambient noise, so that probably influenced the quality.)

title: Good headphones - should be cheaper
text:
Backstory: I had the beats3 with string and was very happy with their battery life, sound quality, etc, but they started showing wear, and I wanted to upgrade to total wireless same sound quality but with over ear hook without paying arm+leg.

Overall these powerbeats are OKAY:

SOUND - very good. turning up the volume mostly affects treble. Bass is cool but only really really powerful when you shove the ear bud all the close to your ear which leads me to point 2.

COMFORT - after wearing them a while my ears HURT. Doesn't matter what ear bud size I use. Rotating them every so often helps, but someone in the design dept messed up.

BATTERY LIFE - I have an android and needed the app to view battery life etc. its frustrating to have to open the case to get a reading but they keep a good charge. new for me is using one at a time which is cool to conserve battery.

CONTROLS - i dislike that the pause/next/back button is the "b" which is right on the part of your ear that hurts (as mentioned before)

STABILITY - they stay in your ear for walking/running. Very lightweight and not noticable, until they start hurting.

PERKS - love the "find my beats" feature.

I'm hoping I find the right adjustment with them.
Overall I'd buy them again... if they were a lot cheaper.

title: READ BEFORE BUYING (15 Months of Use)
text:
I am not one that usually writes reviews but felt compelled to after the issues I have had with these headphones. I really wanted to love them - the sound quality is good enough for the music that I listen to, the sweat resistance is a must-have, and the stability of them on and in your ears with any kind of exercise is unmatched.

I bought the Powerbeats back in June of 2020 for running and gym use. After four or five uses, there started to be connectivity issues where one headphone wouldn't connect and I'd be stuck with only one functioning ear. I would disconnect and reconnect, even forget the device and re-pair the headphones and only sometimes would that fix the issue. Sometimes one of the buds would be completely dead while other times my phone would show the bud completely charged but with no connection. Maybe its just me but I found it EXTREMELY frustrating to get to the gym or about to head out the door for a run just to spend five to ten minutes dissecting why again the PowerBeats weren't functioning properly. A quick Google search later revealed that unfortunately this is a common issue with these headphones in particular so I put up with them (for $200 I felt like I didn't have much of a choice).

With four days to spare under the one-year warranty, I sent the headphones back to Apple so they could diagnose the issue. Lo and behold they found that the headphones were functioning properly. What the h-e-double-hockey-sticks was going on here? I had looked into everything and figured the issue was a build up of some grime on the metal charging surfaces on the headphones themselves as I wasn't in the habit of routinely cleaning them despite some heavy use. I grabbed some alcohol swabs and went to town removing any grit that may interfere with the headphone's ability to connect to the charging case.

Everything worked great for a few days and then it was back to the same issue. For example, I cleaned them thoroughly yesterday, put them back in the case only to remove them for use today and again only one side was getting sound. I followed my usual steps of disconnecting (in this case to my Peloton) and reconnecting with still the same issue.

Oh and did you also hear about the settlement regarding these headphones that Apple reached? Apparently they sold the headphones knowing that the battery life is far less than advertised. To put it in context, I charge the charging case about every three or four days after about five hours' use out of the headphones.

If I had the option to return these for a full return today, I would gladly do that. I'm currently considering the AirPods Pro ($179 on Amazon) to use in place of my PowerBeats just because I know my wife has never had an issue with her AirPods.

title: WOW!  If you are on the fence...
text:
... Buy these headphones. I was about to type ‘earphones‘, but I think that connotation/ description does this product a disservice. I’ve been buying higher-end quality headphones, earbuds etc. for about 20 years. I should caveat my remarks by saying that I am not an audiophile, but I can tell what sounds really good from good to bad. And these sound amazing! They are simply the best sounding headphones I’ve ever owned.

After reading the reviews, I was on the fence about these for awhile, but decided to make the plunge and so glad I did.

I’m not sure why everyone feels the need to compare these to the AirPods...they aren’t in the same category in my opinion. Certainly from a sound and functionality standpoint, there is no comparison. I think AirPods are quite serviceable, but not in the same league as the PowerBeats Pros.

The only product (that I’ve owned) I can think of that could compare with the Powerbeats Pro are the Bose Quiet Comfort over ear headphones with active noise reduction/ cancellation. However, that was when I was traveling a lot and needed the noise cancellation on flights. AND THEY WERE OVER THE EAR HEADPHONES! The larger size ear tips (provided) do a more than capable job of blocking out external noise in crowds, etc. And I’m sure a third-party will develop some ear tips that will equal the capabilities of earphones with active noise reduction.

title: Defective/Sketchy build quality for the price.
text:
I've had my pair for maybe 6 months or so. They got regular use, but handled with care. For whatever reason though lately I have a hard time triggering the right side to activate when getting pulled from the charger box and placed on my ear, which has become a more frequent issue with time.

Really aggravating when I go out of my way to make sure both sides are on the charger prongs correctly. And often the earbud will be fully charged, but for some reason it simply will not activate on the first attempt out of the box. I don't get it. Pressing the buttons on it won't shock it awake either. Not sure if there's any other way to wake them up besides pulling them from the charger prongs in the charger box, but if that's the case also very annoying.

I haven't even used them to work out with (over the ear is better for the noise), so no issue of sweat build up despite them supposedly being sweat resistant. So there's no way they've been damaged by moisture or really anything else.

A couple of days ago, they simply refused to do their jobs despite the fact that I knew they were fully charged, and I could hear what sounded like faint static in place of where my music was supposed to be coming from my 4 month old iphone.

The sound is just okay. In a lot of noisy environments it feels like it could have more oomph.

I think they're relatively comfortable and sturdy for extended wear over the span of a day. Probably the best aspect along with the battery life, which can probably get the average person through an entire day without a charge. Only all-day/heavy listeners would need a charging break. And they charge at a decent speed, although I've never paid close attention. They just always seem ready to go when I need them (well... the battery anyway).

Overall, for the price (I got mine when they were indeed $250, ugh) I kinda regret the purchase. Could maybe expect these kind of behaviors after a year and a half of frequent, heavy-handed/careless handling or from a sub $100 set, but just half a year handled with care and they're acting like this... either defective or cheap parts. Be warned.

title: Too expensive to have so many problems!
text:
These headphones were great at first but about 6months in started to have issues:
1. Similar to numerous other reviewers (wish I’d seen this issue before I spent way too much $$). One earbud stopped charging entirely, sometimes neither seems to hold a charge.
2. They no longer disconnect from my iPhone when I put it back in the case (inside a bag). I now have to manually disconnect under Bluetooth app and even then it will reconnect while still in the case! This has led to many missed important calls/messages.
3. Inconsistent pairing, despite that they seem to want to stay connected with my phone, often only 1 earbud will connect and you frequently play the game of close/reopen case to try to get both to pair.

**don’t waste your money** I bought these overpriced headphones thinking of it as an investment and wouldn’t need new ones for a long time…I was very wrong.

UPDATE: called the Apple “customer service” line about this, spent 40min+ on the phone for them to say they can’t repair or replace because I’m 12days past the 1yr warranty. Only option was to buy a new left earbud for $100+ shipping. No way I’m giving them another penny & will never buy this brand again.

text: The TOZO A1 true wireless earbuds are simply the finest value in this category that I've ever encountered. title: Powerbeats Pro have a tinny sound and hurt my ears
text:
For the price I paid I expected superior sound but the Powerbeats Pro sound tinny with no Bass. After wearing them to the gym for a couple of hours my ears were sore. Sound was superior and fit more comfortable with my old and less expensive Plantronics earbuds which, unfortunately, are no longer made. They did connect and set up on my iPhone very easily but for the price I expected more. I have debated sending them back but I bought the Apple Care with them and don’t want the hassle involved in returning them. I only wear them cycling, running and at the gym so I will probably just live with them. Tried changing the ear tips but it didn’t help with the Bass or comfort. I wouldn’t recommend these.

Update to my review of Feb 1, 2023. The left ear bud frequently failed to charge and both earbuds had problems connecting forcing me to go to settings Bluetooth and forget the device and reinstall. Now the earbuds in the case will not connect to my iPhone. I did get AppleCare+ with the earbuds and called tech support but nothing we did would get the earbuds to connect. They are sending a replacement and hopefully it will perform better than the original earbuds. I would not consider purchasing these without the AppleCare extended warranty.

Next update: Received my new Powerbeats earbuds and case. At first they charged great, no problem. Now after a month one of earbuds will fail to charge. I have to repeatedly check them to make sure both earbuds are charging. They use magnets to pull the earbuds into place but you still need to push them down to insure the buds are connecting properly to charge. When you close the case often one of the earbuds will lose connection and not charge but will in fact discharge. I constantly get ready to go for a run or to the gym and discover that one esrbud is 100% charged and the other one has no charge or is at 2% or so and will not operate. I then have to try and readjust the discharged earbud in the case and wait for it to charge before going. Annoying to say the least. Also if you sweat while working out, running, etc the contacts will quickly corrode and you have to clean them regularly for them to recharge. Definitely wish I had not purchased these but for the price I paid I can’t afford to just throw them away and buy a different brand. For the next 2 years I guess I will just keep using my AppleCare to return them when they stop working properly.

title: Weak maximum volume and overall midrange biased sound
text: I was overall disappointed and returned the Powerbeats Pro for a refund.  PROS:  they stayed in my ears even during running, they paired very easily with my iPhone without issue, the charging case is great and well constructed, they are sweatproof, the build quality is excellent, Amazon made the return very easy.  CONS:  I am a musician and sound quality is most important to me. As far as sound quality, the Powerbeats Pro have very mediocre clarity of sound and a very midrange biased sound (not good for pop or rock music when you really want to hear the bass and high tones). The headhones themselves do not allow adjustment of  EQ - but you can try several EQ options within your iPhone (none of which really helped the sound quality at all). When I run, I like to hear all the details of the instruments of the song clearly - and I just didn't. As far a maximum volume, these are VERY VERY quiet headphones - even with my iPhone volume maxed out. Loud, clean, detailed sound helps me stay motivated during my runs and makes me run further, and these are just not even close to what I need. I am now looking into the Bose noise-cancelling wireless in ear headphones (waterproof). Bose is more expensive, but....  might be better for me. I will find out soon.

title: Great customer service for tech support!
text:
The left earbud stopped responding to volume control from my phone or from the buds themselves and was at about 15% volume. I contacted Tozo customer support and they told me how to reset the buds. It worked for me and here are the instructions:

1. Remove/forget [TOZO-A1] records on your device, then turn off the bluetooth function.
2. Take out both earbuds from the charging case, then quickly tap the both touch buttons 5 times. Reset is completed when the red light flashes for one second.
3. Put the earbuds back into case first and close the lid. Then take them out again andreconnect to your device.
Note: If your device displays [Connection failed]. Please delete all [TOZO-A1] bluetooth records on all devices before pairing.

After reset, hold and press the right earbud to adjust the volume to the maximum while playing music, then after a few seconds, hold and press the left earbud to adjust the volume back to normal.

First, the good stuff: The sound quality is quite good good. So is the comfort sitting on the ear. The storage case is bulky (esp. if you keep it in your pocket, as I did), but I can live with that.

But from the outset, the product didn't work right. One earbud would regularly and inexplicably go uncharged, or spontaneously stop working. That was annoying, but manageable (I could usually fix things by resetting the storage case). But then, when the earbuds were only 3 months old, they would no longer would connect to my iPhone or computer. I tried everything -- resetting the earbuds multiple times as well as restarting the phone, playing with all the settings I could find -- but nothing worked. I had to discard them.

A deeply disappointing consumer experience. I won't be buying these again.

title: UPDATE: Second pair defective as well. Avoid until they get their act together.
text:
Bought these for use at my gym which inexplicably blasts music throughout the place and I wanted something that might block some of that ambient noise. These help a lot although they aren't noise-cancelling. Also great for outdoor running! Much better to not have a cord although any BT buds can do that.

Fit is pretty good but for me these are a little irritating to wear beyond an hour or so at a time - quite possible I need to try one of the other sizes of baffles that are included or tweak the over-the-ear piece. Sound quality is good but I expected better - my wired Bose earbuds have better sound. Super easy to link to iPhone. Also nice to have Siri integration.

HOWEVER, I experienced un-fixable connectivity issues from day-one when used for phone calls. The call wouldn't drop but the connection to the earbuds would and it's really annoying in a conference call situation to just disappear mid-sentence. Went through many trouble-shooting chats/calls with Apple to no avail and had to send for an exchange. FWIW Apple is experiencing a shortage of return packaging for these. Does this mean they're overwhelmed with returns? Certainly sounds that way but who knows? I wound up returning them to Amazon for an exchange.

The new pair arrived and I was surprised to see the box sealed in plastic wrapper. The first ones sent to me by Amazon were unsealed which I thought strange. I now understand that they were likely returned by someone and then sold to me as if new. These weren't from a third party merchant, they were from Amazon.com so buyer beware on that.

UPDATED on 10/25/19
Had to send the new pair to Apple for repair - same connectivity problem as the first pair. Was actually at the gym when it happened and on a chat with Apple the tech said I need to re-sync them, however you can't do that without the case. He said I should take the case with me when I work out or go for a run. So yeah, that's a great solution. No wires but a large case stuck in your pocket. Great idea. Thanks Apple. If I could do this again I'd wait a year for them to figure out how to actually make these correctly, assuming that ever happens.

text:
What I liked: The battery life is better than my phone. They are amazing in regards to how long they last. Its been about 8 months I have owned them, and not one single time have they died. I have listened to music for at least 8 hours straight. The sound quality is top-notch for them being an inner-ear design. I charge the station maybe once or twice a week and again, have never had neither the case or headphone die. They are comfortable, have never fallen out, and take calls like a dream.
Dislikes: They are minor...But for me personally there are two specific setbacks. I do home repair and refurbishment for a living; sometimes that means working outside and using tools that require safety glasses. with safety glasses, the comfort level *slightly goes down, but they still obviously work fine. With earmuffs and other warming materials that cover the ears, the earphones will continually play and pause the music as it is an actual push button. So the pressure from the fabric clicks it on and off. so you decide to either go cold ears or music. It's irritating but I don't presume to know how many people this would actually affect. Also the carrying case is too large to really carry in your pocket. So when you are in the middle of working and have to take them out for a few minutes, you end up just setting them down which increases the likelihood of losing them. (I have had 3 close-calls). So greatest earphones ever, I just hope in the future the case is smaller and I can wear them with earmuffs.

title: Do not buy if using the microphone is important to you
text:
I bought these to wear for my remote job, as there are a lot of zoom meetings and I need a pair of headphones with a quality microphone that are comfortable.

My standard headset Jabra Evolve has excellent sound quality but they hurt my ears after one hour use. Over-the-ear headphones are the most comfortable, so I wanted to try PowerBeats, as it is known as the premium version.

However, out of all the over-the-ear headphones I've tried...Powerbeats is the worst. 3 reasons:

-You must have them in the case to pair to a device. All the cheaper versions you just hold down the power button on the earpiece itself.

-They fit awkwardly into the case compared to cheaper headphones I've tried.

-The microphone quality is just as bad as the cheaper headphones.

-You must use an apple charging cord. Most other devices require USB-C now, so it is inconvenient to have to setup a new type of charging cord for just one device.

If you are just looking for premium over-the-ear wireless headphones with good music sound quality and noise-canceling, as well as someone with multiple apple products that would make sense to have them already handy, these are for you.

NOT for people who need to use the microphone or prefer USB-C cords, as well as the inconvenience of needing the case to pair the bluetooth.

title: Very musical. I'm impressed!
text:
I have never owned a pair of Beats headphones before and have always assumed that even though they sound decent, they are nothing special, and simply have a boosted low end to appeal to a particular type of person who has a lot of money to drop on a pair of headphones.

I HAVE owned a number of good in-ear monitors/ear buds, including expensive models by Bose, Shure, and several models by Westone. All of those cost more than these Powerbeats.

But I am absolutely DELIGHTED by these ear buds. The sound is wonderful and balance. And there is no lack of low end, as I suspected for a product by Beats, but the low end is beautifully defined and clear. Today (third day of ownership) I took them running and listened to 90125 by the group Yes. This is an album I listen to quite often while working out, but this is the first time I have actually heard, not just "bass," but the BASSIST, and the BASS he was playing. I heard the instrument.

I gave a lesser rating for noise cancellation because I don't really know how well they do that, and that's really not a concern of mine. On the other side of that coin, I actually prefer an ear bud that sits more ON the ear than IN the ear because with ear buds that seal my ears, I have to listen to all of the internal sounds of my body while I'm running or jumping rope or whatnot. So the form factor of this pair of ear buds is very appealing to me.

I also did not give a high rating for battery life because I don't yet know what my rating would be.

All told: This is an amazing product. I highly recommend it.

title: Works great WHEN you can actually get them to charge
text: I bought these only for workouts.  I needed something with good sound quality (good bass) that wouldn't fall out of my ears when running/jumping.  These do it.  They do sound great, and I never have to worry about them falling out or shifting during exercise.  My only issue (and it's a big one) is that they will not charge on a consistent basis.  I've read other reviews stating the same thing, so it looks like it's a manufacturing issue.  If the headphones are off the charging pins by like a tenth of a millimeter, they won't charge and you have no way of knowing that until you put the earbuds in and realize they're dead.  I've had mine for only one year, and I have to manually hold the right earbud in place the entire time it's charging, because as soon as I let go it stops.  So I have to give myself an extra 20 minutes before my workouts to make sure I have enough of a charge to get me through that one hour.  If I could find something similar to these that would actually charge the way they're supposed to, I would get those in a heartbeat.  For the price tag, I would expect more out of these.

title: After a year of ownership…the good and the bad
text:
There are things I like and things I don’t.

Good - I generally wear one in my ear at a time so I have one ear unobstructed to hear my kids. I like that it can function on just one bud.
Bad - It’s good that I can switch the buds in my ears
during the day because after a few hours, the buds begin to hurt my ears and I have to give the ear a rest. The hard plastic ball that the ear bud attaches too presses on the cartilage and makes it start aching. I suspect it this piece had a foam layer around it, it would be more gentle on the ear.

Good - I like the over-the-ear clip which holds the bud in my ear. I’ve struggled to keep other brands buds in my ears in the past. I also use it to hang on front of my shirt when I remove it from my ear. Keeps me from losing it or breaking it in my pocket.
Bad - the clip is molded a bit too compactly for my ear shape and after a few hours of it pressing on the back of my ear, it aches terribly and I have to remove it and switch ears.

Good - it has a long battery life. I can listen to many hours of an audiobook each day. I charge them at night.
Bad - the sound quality is not as good as the much cheaper, Bluetooth, wired earphones that I have. But since I listen to audiobooks mostly, that’s not a big deal for me. It’s not bad, but not great.

Good - I haven’t had connection issues to my iPhone or my car Bluetooth player. I’ve used them heavily for a year and they are stilling going strong.

I’ve read reviews of others who say the earphones are comfortable and I can admit I may have a different ear shape than most and that’s why they are less comfortable for me. That said, I like them enough to wear them daily but when it comes time to replace them, I will shop other brands to see if I can find a brand with a better fit.

title: Solid gym headphones for iPhone users
text: I use these headphones exclusively for exercise and have them paired with an iPhone 12.  For my use, they're close to perfect.  I sweat a lot when doing cardio, and these have stayed securely in place and haven't had any issues with the moisture.  The default ear tips sit inside my ears completely, which can lead to a slight feeling of pressure inside the ear but they are acceptably comfortable.  Sound quality is fine for a gym-oriented headphone, although you won't mistake them for real audiophile grade gear.  The sound is a bit lean with an obvious base boost.  These do not have active noise cancellation but do offer good isolation because of the in-ear fit.  It's nice to have the integrated volume control so that I don't have to fumble with handling my phone or getting to the right screen on my watch.  Battery life isn't a big concern for me since it's much longer than my workouts.  As would be expected, Apple compatibility has been excellent.  Overall, a perfect set of earbuds for Apple users at the gym.  YMMV with other use cases.

title: New Powerbeats Pros Are A Pleasant Surprise!
text:
OK, so let's be honest, beats headphones have always been really stylish - good looking devices, but the sound tended to be an acquired taste. Or, so has been my experience. So I when I started to read about the introduction of the new Powerbeats Pro I was both excited and skeptical. But the stylish design really caught my eyes and based on most reviews where users commented on the balanced sound I decided to take a chance and invest in a pair. I was not disappointed!

First of all, and as is typically the case, these little gems are well built and really gorgeous! The style is very sleek and form fitting for a very comfortable fit in and around the ear. The control on each ear is easy to access and operates smoothly without a hitch. The selection of 4 different ear pieces means you'll probably find the right fit for your own ears. And while I have not tested their moisture wicking ability, by everything I have read, they should exceed in that regard as well.

But where these babies really shine is in the sound quality they deliver. I've owned several iterations of beat's ear buds over the years and while most have been pretty decent these new Powerbeats Pro's really blew me away. They do have the solid bass reproduction that beats have always been known for, but now with a much smoother overall tonal balance. The mids shine through as vocals are forward and clear and the high frequency reproduction is less harsh than in beats I have owned in the past. All-in-all the new Powerbeats Pro really delivers on sound and it does it in about as stylish a package as you could ask for.

The charging box, that doubles as storage for your Powerbeats Pro, is a nice and simple design. And while a bit bulky by other brand's standards I found it to be quite comfortable to work with. And the buds seat nicely into the magnetic charging ports for a simple and secure fit.

All-in-all I was extremely pleased and maybe even a bit surprised by the well balanced sound of my new Powerbeats Pro. And while not a surprise, the new Pro's stylish looks are second to none. These little titans will no doubt impress. And judging by early sales numbers the message has gotten out!

Highly recommended!

Also, my left ear bud isn't working anymore. I've try charging the left ear bud over and over; it's still not working. I thought it was just a connectivity issue, but my right ear bud is working perfectly fine.

Honest review on each:

Sound: 5/5.
I loved it when it was working . Awesome bass. Loud loud loud (what I like).

Connectivity:1/5
there will be days when I can't get one of the ear bud to get sound. This was a problem right when I got thee ear buds. There is a connection issue with the ear buds and sometimes I just end up using one of them for hours or sitting for about 10-30 (varies) minutes disconnecting/reconnecting the earbuds until it connects.

Especially with the problem I am having right now. I wouldn't recommend getting these.

Battery: 2/5
The battery life was awesome in the beginning. Until I realize that if the BOX is dead then you can't even connect to your phone. You have to carry the box everywhere with the earbuds and if it's dead then the earbuds won't be able to connect via bluetooth.

Aesthetic/looks: 5/5
These looks awesome! You'll feel like a boss in the gym with these on! lol. anywho, awesome look and good fit around the ear.

Comfort: 3/5
It feels good for about the first hour or two, but then you will start to feel a bit of pain within your earhole. Might be the material causing this etc. Not too sure, but i endured it through my workouts.

title: Very Uncomfortable. Not Very Loud.
text:
I was very excited for these headphones. At $250 and from a brand name I always hear about I figured this would be the best pair of headphones that have ever been in my ears. The last pair of headphones I purchased were about $70 and that was the most I'd ever spent on headphones at the time. When I got these I noticed immediately that even turned up to full volume they were not very loud. About as loud as those $70 pair of headphones I mentioned when they are only at 70% volume. They felt like they would not fall out while running or exercising though so I was eager to give them a try. However after having them in my ears for about 30mins my ears began to ache. Literally sore to the touch. I tried every different rubber piece size that came with the headphones over the course of several days but still had the same issue, after a little bit of time of them being in my ears they made my ears hurt pretty bad. I switched back to my old headphones and immediately noticed the difference in volume and comfort. I even tried taking the rubber pieces off those old headphone and trying them on these beats but that did not help. Something about the design was extremely irritating to my ears. Easily the most uncomfortable pair of headphones I've ever had in my ears. Absolutely ridiculous that my $70, 5-year old pair of some random chinese brand headphones were more comfortable and louder than these that were more than 3 times the price.

The only good thing I can say about them was the sound quality was clear. They sounded nice ever if they weren't loud. The buttons on the side that give you complete track and volume control were great too. It was also cool that as soon as you put them in your ears they start playing, and as soon as you pull them out they stop. The charging case that magnetically locks the headphones in and charges them when you place them in the case was cool too. Honestly the charging case was the coolest aspect of these headphones which is really sad to say for a top of the line pair of headphones.

I would not recommend these to anyone after this experience. I researched reviews of headphones to settle on these too so now I am reluctant to purchase another pair based on critic reviews. I guess the pair I have now as still pretty solid despite their age and lack of cool new features.

title: Horrible battery life makes them useless
text:
I have an iPhone. I bought these because I thought Siri would work super-fast compared to the $50 Aukey headphones I had been using. Plus I was looking forward to converting to "true wireless" Bluetooth headphones, without an annoying cord pulling on the back my neck.

Yeah, no, I returned these. Problems:

* Siri really didn't work that much faster. "Hey Siri" with headphones on worked, but if I have to wait several seconds just to get the voice prompt, I'm not going to use it.
* No good seal in my ears, no matter which tips I tried.
* The battery case is RIDICULOUSLY LARGE. Compare with something like the Jabra Elite Active 75t charging case, which I can carry in my pocket.
* Here's the real kicker: When I'm not using these, I put them down on the desk. Surprise! The battery drains surprisingly fast when you just leave them idle, sitting on a table! And they don't turn off!

Let me reiterate: I'm listening to podcasts or whatever throughout the day. I'm constantly taking the headphones off and putting them back on. Since the battery case is too big, I don't have it on me most of the time. Since they drain while they're idle and not in the case, the battery doesn't nearly last me the full day.

At this price, and given the competition, I consider this just laughably bad.

It's not all bad. The comfort of the over-the-ear design is good, and my ears are very sensitive to poor fit or pressure in the wrong places. The pairing process was really cool and effortless. (Too bad you (hopefully) only do that once or twice.) It's cool that it automatically shares them to all your Apple devices via iCloud. They sounded fine.

But when the battery dies—which it did—they're just an overpriced fashion accessory.

title: Dr. Dre:  Hands down, the best!
text:
I have five pair of "true wireless" earbuds that have turned out to be less than expected; from bass response, mid ranges and treble, they all lack in one way or another which is very annoying when you expect clear, pure and leveled sound according to the advertiser claims. I have Sony, TreLab, Cowan, G9, and a pair I got from Walmart for $9.99 that sounds better than the rest! Sony is the worst, especially when riding a bike. The air whistles in the little holes that are supposed to be for isolating sound instead of actuating it - whistling to the point that I had to remove them. They were $300.00, yet I was tempted to step the mess out of them! Which, after the bike incident, I promptly returned to Amazon.

I've had this model of Dr. Dre before, but I left the right earphone at someone's house which they can't find (total bummer). So, in the meantime, I used the devices listed above until I couldn't stand it any longer. I pulled out my wired Eptomotics Research earphones, and my Bang & Olufsen, but the wire kept getting the way. And, still, these lacked the smooth, mellow sound in all ranges that Dr. Dre provides to my ears. The difference in sound quality with Dr. Dre is amazing and above the others which can't compare and are not even close to being in the same class.

I have an Android Samsung Galaxy S10 with Dolby Atmos, and it really kicks with Dr. Dre. I hope I never have to use another pair of earbuds, wired or not. If you don't trust my review, then try them out yourselves. If you don't like them, return them. It's that easy. Amazon is very willing to make things right and will refund your money.

So, this is my second pair of Dr. Dre which I received today, same day shipping, and they are heaven.

I don't often write reviews, but after using the other crap earbuds, I felt compelled to write this review. Amazon has about a billion different "truly" wireless earbuds, but I have no doubt they are all junk. You get what you pay for, except with Sony...which is crap, too.

title: Great headphones with solid sound, battery life, and interchangeable tips for comfortable fit.
text:
I don't usually write reviews, but I like these headphones so much that I had to share. I had AirPods before these ones and I left them in my pockets and ran them thru the wash :( I ordered these headphones to just switch it up and I have zero regrets. Though the case is equivalent to 4 airpod cases and they are pricey, they are worth the gamble in my opinion. Battery life is great, sound is clear and loud with great bass and the interchangeable tips allow for a comfortable fit for long periods of time and better noise cancellation compared to AirPods. They also will NEVER fall out. They come with 5 total ear tips (including the ones that are on the headphones in the case) allowing for a secure fit and thus a better/louder sound. Took them on a 18 hour trip and only had to charge once the entire trip (driving there, while there, and driving back) and they were comfortable in my ears for extended periods of time (word of advice, bring the interchangeable tips with you on trips as they really do help for comfort and sound). Great microphone for talking on phone and for Siri. Down part is the size of the case and price. Other than that, great headphones. Hip-hop, EDM, pop, alternative +.

Update: After having these for a while I’ve realized that though they are great for workouts and sound great, but I’m really getting tired of them having problems with connecting and charging. Sometimes I’ll have to put them in my ears, back into the case, and then back into my ears again for them to connect. Other times I put them in and only one headphone is charged. I’ve also realized that the bigger case is slick and falls out of shorts easily. Got so tired of these factors that I just ordered the AirPods Pro. Unfortunate cause they are good headphones, but the flaws were deal breakers for me.

title: Best Beats Yet
text:
I have most of the Beats catalog by now and I have to say the sound quality of these earphones is at least two cuts above their other offerings -- they're even better than their over-the-ear headphones.

Listening to Dire Straits "On Every Street" I was mesmerized by the clean upper register of these phones. The snap of the snares and brush of cymbals were rendered perfectly and the bass was solid and punchy without being overbearing (which is more common for Beats products). I am truly surprised by how balanced these little earphones are.

That's not to say they are perfect in every way. The initial fitting was a little problematic -- I tried all four eartips before settling on the largest size. Getting a proper seal is vital to appreciate the solid bass. If there is any gap, the bass declines to thin and reedy. The noise isolation is also compromised by a poor fit. I eventually modeled the wire ear loops to help keep a good seal on the phones.

The Bluetooth features are as good as expected from using the Apple chips. Pairing is dead simple for Apple products. I've slowly gotten rid of other brands so I couldn't comment about pairing with other brands.

All in all, these are the best sounding Beats yet -- and I've listened to them all. These sound as good as my Etymotics ER-3s, which are wired. Highly recommended.

title: Do not last
text:
When I first got these headphones I was ecstatic. They were easy to use, great sound and the battery life was long enough for me. They were also comfortable. 2 years and a few months later they are nothing more than a reminder not to get sucked in by a brand. About 6 months ago the left headphone stopped holding a charge. It would only work for a bot 10 minutes no matter how long a charged it. My iphone would show 100% charge at start, then I would begin listening to music 10 minutes later it was dead. The right headphone has now followed suit. Maybe I am naive to believe something is supposed to last more than a couple of years, but my old crappy, heavy, uncomfortable, off brand, wrap around bluetooth headphones from 8 years ago still work . Very disappointed in beats longevity. Never trying them again.

If you are one of those people that replace your electronics every 1 or 2 years these are fine. Everyone else stay a way they do not stand the test of time.

title: You will love these
text: I waited about 6 months before writing a review on these just to make sure I had enough time using them.  If you ever owned Powerbeats and like them, you will absolutely love the Pro's.  I can't believe the difference of being completely wireless.  The overall sound quality is improved but, the bass has been toned down and they don't block ambient noise as well.  I miss those two things but I suppose it's safer being able to hear your surroundings.  The battery life is crazy long.  Whereas the Powerbeats died on my periodically, I would have to be stupid to let the Pro's die.  I did experience a problem with the left side failing on me about a month after receiving them but I sent it to Apple who repaired it for me in less than a week.  The only knock I have is the price.  They should cost no more than $200.  However, I would definitely buy them again for $250.

title: The worst

Even without moving, I’d be really careful to ensure they’re connected to the charger (verified on my phone) and then come back to a dead pod. I dug out my husband’s PowerBeats Pro that he never uses, charged them up only to find that if you close the case, the right one won’t charge so I have to leave the case open 24/7. Worst Apple purchase ever. Total crap. Don’t buy.

title: Really, really good for this side sleeper
text:
I like to listen to podcasts while I fall asleep. I've tried the wireless headband ones previously, but taking it apart to clean was a pain. These are perfect for my budget. The sound quality isn't the best but it's fine for my needs. On a full charge, one bud lasts about more than half of the night. If I need to I can swap it out for the other ear bud.

The voice that says "low battery" is soothing and not abrasive. (My previous sleep headset would give a loud beep when it was about to die...) These don't interrupt me in the night.

I sleep on my left and usually use the right earbud. I can gently place the left earbud in my right ear if I need to swap them out, for me it isn't noticeably uncomfortable.

I use them with my Nintendo Switch too. When they're both in my ears it seems to cancel out noise pretty well.

The case is sleek and small and could fit in my pocket if need be. I've had them for a week. I'm a little worried about the sturdiness of the top but it's ok for now. I'm so thankful I have them - it's exactly what I needed!

title: Lasted Eight Months
text:
I bought these in November 2020.

I used them for eight months, at which time the right ear bud started leaking green stuff (from the battery).

I called Apple support since I was sure they would be covered under warranty. After all, this was clearly a defect.

After chatting with one rep I was then referred to another who told me the issue was that they were damaged by water (my sweat) and they were not covered under warranty. So much for being "sweat resistant".

However they would arrange to repair them for $99 for the right ear bud and $99 for the case for a total of $214 after tax. FYI, I bought these for $199.

So, let me tell you: these probably won't last. If they don't, they probably won't be covered by Apple. And if they are "nice" enough to offer to repair them, a partial repair will cost more than you paid for them in the first place.

Bottom line: won't last and not supported by Apple. Buy something else.

text: I am hearing impaired, but not deaf. So I started using the earbuds that plug into the bottom of your phone instead of my hearing aides and they work well at blocking all noise except the conversation. The problem is  they are cumbersome and I always have to ask my caller to hold while I get them situated.  The cords always got tangled and it was frustrating to get them in quickly. Plus you can’t really wear them all the time.  So I tried the Powerbeats Pro Wireless Earphones. I wear one and it stays secure and I can answer my phone and maintain a conversation as I put in the other one. In fact they work so well I had to turn down the volume in my phone because it was too loud. AND they block out the background noise so I am able to hear everything the caller says. title: Make sure they're actually in the ear!
text:
I love these, but like another reviewer, I thought the sound was TERRIBLE at first. Turns out, I just hadn't pressed them into my ears, and thus could not hear any of the bass. The big thing that distinguishes these from Airpods is that low-end response, and you lose it if you don't actually have these in your ears. The box comes with additional ear tips in case you need them.

For me, I had to use the largest ear tips in the box in order to ensure a good fit. It's not that the whole unit fell off my head without the big ear tips -- but the ear tips themselves popped out a bit, killing the sound. When I fixed this with the included ear tips, all problems solved. Note that you can get replacement ear tips as well.

Once properly fitted in my ears, which now takes 2-3 seconds, these sound roughly on par with my Beats Solo 3's, which I also love. I am going to keep my Solo 3's for running, and use these for activities that involve being on an incline, like weight lifting. I love the charge case but it's a bit big. I think these sound a touch better than the Solo 3's since the bass is a little less overpowering, but I think both are great exercise headphones -- they get you in the mood to work out. These are just a bit more versatile because of the in-ear design.

What is the advantage of the Solo 3's? Well, this is kind of gross, but earwax can really mess up these powerbeats and block the sound (ew). That is a bit of a hassle that is just not there with the Solo 3's, which are on-ear instead of in-ear. However, this will vary person to person.

text:
So, I purchased these wireless headphones in august of 2019, and although I dont know the lifespan of this product, I can tell you that in march of 2021, these headphones are really starting to fail.

The left side is constantly losing connection and it is absolutely the most frustrating thing in the world.

The solution generally revolves around stopping what youre doing, putting both headphones in the case, opening up the app on your phone, waiting for the app and headphones to connect, and finagling it until both headphones are actually working and playing sound.

I'm going to try to do a deep clean of both headphones and the case, but for the last 6 months or so, it's been really tiring of the worseing quality of the connection of these wireless headphones. Like I said, I dont know the "lifespan" of these headphones, but for 200$ usd, I expect a lot more than a year and a half.

More to follow.

title: Good, but nowhere near $249 good
text:
I really wanted to like these since they are apparently perfect for what I would use them for, indoor cycling training and outdoor mountain biking on rough trails where retention is key. I borrowed a coworkers pair for a while to test and as much as I wanted to like them, I was left underwhelmed. For reference my personal buds are Soundpeats Q30 which cost $30

Firstly the Powerbeats are not that loud, they are on par with or slightly quieter than the Q30, I don’t listen to my stuff loud but some do. I found myself having to turn the volume up, at which point the high notes were piercing and if I turned it down the bass was lackluster

The sound quality is undeniably better on the Powerbeats, but it still doesn’t sound great. Maybe my expectations for earbuds are not realistic, but when I used them I was not wowed into thinking “these are definitely worth $200+ more than mine”. The vocal clarity is better for sure, and generally everything is more clear, but the bass is kind of weak for my taste, I imagine workout buds would have a big more thump to them. Overall it’s a bit disappointing for the cost but like I said maybe I’m expecting to hear something that can’t happen

Comfort is ok, they are bulky in or outside of the case and get in the way of glasses, and the hoops irritate my ears. They definitely stay in place but I prefer the retention setup of the Soundpeats or the Bose Soundsport which has a soft rubber hook inside the ear and not wrapped around

The sound isolation is also surprisingly poor. They use rubber tips like my Soundpeats but let in more ambient noise. Some consider this good, some consider this bad. They don’t seem to let in enough to make it seem like a safety benefit while running etc, but you can hear just enough to make it annoying to listen to music unless you crank the volume and have piercing high notes bleed your ears

Obviously a lot of people are happy with theirs, but I didn’t think they were that special. They would have to cost under $100 for me to consider them, maybe I’m not putting any value on the H1 chip or the other benefits but I used them strictly for working out, not wearing them for phone use etc. hopefully the next version is better
