title: Works great with multiple devices
text:
I’m giving 5 stars because I think these are the best on the market for ME currently, but they are not perfect and other people might not like them.

Pros:
* Clear audio from phone calls, watching TV, and listening to music.
* Pairs easily with multiple devices. I have this paired with my wife’s iPhone, my iPhone, my work iphone, our iPad, and our Fire TV cube. I can leave my earbuds in and then just click “connect” on whatever device I switch to.
* blocks out some background noise
* excellent battery life on the buds and the charging case
* won’t fall out of your ears while you exercise
* volume and call/pause buttons work well

Cons:
* my wife said that they hurt her ears (so I kept them for myself. Her loss is my gain.)
* I have a hard time hearing other people if I have my buds in; i have to take at least one out to hear people nearby
* I’ve read that in-ear earbuds cause hearing loss over time, but that’s probably true for any earbud.
* you can’t lay the side of your head on a pillow with these in; doing so would be uncomfortable and would press the pause/call button on the “b”

title: The best totally wireless in-ear buds.....almost!!!
text:
Probably one of the best purchases I’ve made in terms of in-ear buds.

Pros: Syncing is a breeze (if you are pairing them to any Apple product). Connection strength and quality are as good as it can get, with no discernible audio lag (a must if you are watching videos on your phone, tablet or laptop). They haven’t ever fallen out of my ears even during vigorous gym sessions. They fit perfectly even with glasses on. Most importantly they have amazing battery life and they sound absolutely brilliant. They still retain that thumping low-end that Beats earphones are known for, but have significantly improved the delivery of the mid and high frequencies. I’ve never been a fan of Beats audio gear but these are something special.

Cons: The charging case is clunky and isn’t pocket-able (not an issue if you plan to carry a backpack around). My biggest issue is the way the case charges the earbuds. Despite there being magnets to guide the buds to their charging pins, the buds don’t dock unless you push them down firmly. There have been times when one of the buds hasn’t docked properly and hence hasn’t charged at all while the other has. Also, if you have any sweat on the metal pins on your buds, they won’t charge so don’t forget to wipe them before you place them in the case.

I wasn't looking for a tectonic nosebleed, just *something* down there below the midrange. Unfortunately, there's just...nothing. Nothing but tin and disappointment.

The earbuds ran fine for a couple weeks connected to my Galaxy S10 and home desktop. For calls, voice quality was very good, appreciably better than the cheap MPOW X5 wireless earbuds I also have. Score one for the Pros, but whereas the MPOWs pair easily and rarely IF EVER disconnect, the Pros no longer stay connected to my phone or PC at all. They're charged, they connect, but they always disconnect within 3 - 30 seconds. Hey what - I paid extra for this!?? Unimpressed.

Naturally, this only started happening when I was a couple weeks outside the return window. So, now I get to decide how much of my life I want to dedicate to figuring out to make these expensive duds work. Meanwhile, the MPOW X5s just keep working like they should.

These inexpensive little buds absolutely put my pricey Jabra Elite Active 75t and Jabra Elite 7 pro buds to shame! Those are so bad on voice calls that I'd given up on using earbuds for calls, assuming that in order to get clear calls I'd need to buy even more experience earbuds. Not true, it's just that the $200 Jabras cannot compete with these $20 Tozos. It's quite laughable to be honest.

The controls are tap based and extremely accurate. A light touch is all you need to register a tap, and it works every time, so easy and natural.

title: Powerbeats Pro v’s AirPods and others
text:
Having bought almost a dozen pairs of Bluetooth earbuds over the last 2 years I feel I’ve got a reasonable perspective.
No one seems to have got it quite right and so here is my relative comparison. I value sound quality but am not an audiophile by any means...

The win for Powerbeats Pro over AirPods is straight forward- they are louder (read that I don’t have to have them cranked all the way up on planes or in noisy environments lie downtown LA). They stay in place no matter what, while the AirPods for me fell out fairly easily. If neither of these are issues for you, go with the AirPods because....

The downside of the Powerbeats Pro for me is also simple- the case is big. Not big like can headphones but big if you want to put in your pocket while the AirPods is less than a quarter the size. Now that may be a downside as the AirPods case is really easy to lose! The Powerbeats are sturdy and with their long battery life I’ve carried them around in my pocket for the day but you can’t turn them off (I don’t believe) so your phone defaults to the ear buds.

Comfort wise, likely very personal but I find them as comfortable as anything else I have worn and not having to regularly make sure they are secure make them a win on comfort.

I also have B&O and Bose Bluetooth ear buds. The number one shortfall for these are the slower connectivity versus the instant connectivity of the AirPods and PowerBeats. Maybe not an issue for some but tends to be annoying delay (and sometimes i find i have to go to Bluetooth settings) but I’m also impatient.

The B&O may have slightly better sound and for me are more stable than AirPods but nothing like as stable as Powerbeats. Bose fall between B&O and Powerbeats on secure fit.

If you fly or are in a noisy environment, I would go with Powerbeats for their volume and some noise cancellation (due to fit not active technology). If volume and fit are not an issue, go with the cheaper and easy to carry AirPods. B&O and Bose are not really competitors to Powerbeats Pro unless you really love the sound which I cannot really tell a difference, personally.
4/5 stars just because I think they could have made the case more ergonomic for pockets, otherwise 5 stars.

title: Not for gym/exercise!
text:
Let me start by telling that I own dozens of in ear and over the ear headphones. The closest these come are the Apple AirPods Pro, which IMO remain the best. If you like bass, then you will definitely like the Beats Studio over AirPods Pro. The noise cancelling is nowhere close to AirPods Pro. Battery is decent. Case is ok.

Now for the dealbreaker … seems like they really wanted the Beats logo to be prominent and sacrificed an important design to achieve this prominence — weight distribution. These buds are very back heavy. No matter how secure of a seal you achieve with these, the heavier weight on the back (away from ear canal) will always cause these to slip out. It’s basic physics. As you move (exercise), the acting force on these buds will push these out of your ears. It’s a terrible design because it’s completely predictable. All of this so that others can see the B logo! I will guarantee you that anyone using these in any sort of rigorous exercise will find the Beats Studio painfully annoying as they will slip out. To make matters worse, as you fiddle to get these back in, you will inevitably press one of the buttons to cause the music to stop or advance or Siri to kick in. Absolutely awful if you plan to use these at the gym.

It will take 2-3 connection attempts before it will work as it should. It has been like this from day 1 and my gf who has a pair too, says she has the exact same issue. text:
O.K. I never thought I'd own a pair of beats earbuds, bud I do. And I have to stay, they're not bad. There's a (alright, there's a few) caveats, but not enough for me to return them. The build is the typically spun hardened plastic, of a oddly shaped buds that interestingly fit near perfectly. The buds are tiny, compared to many other brands. As mentioned they're oddly shaped, by two (also an oval shaped flat surfaced which is used to control the buds) angular sides and a round ball in front, where the canal protrudes that you attach your tips. The fit isn't bad, and once sealed it doesn't move around, or fall out whilst doing certain activities. I use XL sized silicone tips. I find they work best for me, for almost every bud I've owned or tested over the years.

If the fit is too short, you can always use double, or even triple flange tips. Which I use on occasion. Depends on the buds I'm fitting in question. That extra length can help get the seal you need for the most optimal sound reproduction. Throughout this year I have tried a plethora of buds. From Sony's XM3, to Audio Technica CKS5TW And Nuarl (I plan to get them again, when funds permit) N6Pro's , which I actually (they have a really good sound, rich luscious bass, sweet and engaging mids, and to top it off, a sparkling treble, not over the top, mind you) liked, but the buttons were a little finicky. As to why I returned them.
The biggest, most prevalent issue I came across was that most of them didn't fit properly, at all. I could barely get the XM3's in, and keep them in. As with Shures Aionic, another I liked and wanted desperately
them to work out. Because they sounded great. The Studio buds are not a problem. It takes me seconds to insert and position them in my ears. The only (again, there's more than one) detraction I have, is that the buds are easy activate whilst attempting to insert them into your ears. For me it's not a deal breaker. Oh, I almost forgot an important issue. And that is with the battery life. They average a minimum three plus hours. Which is not that long. Then again, who spends more than three hours listening to stuff ? Well, I do. These are for nighttime use mostly. I use them when my roomy has gone to bed. So I need to get an average fours plus. One night I got close to 5 hours. Guess it depends on usage. What else can I say, other to try for yourself. . At the least, you can return them if you're not happy, right. I'm using them now, as I do at nights.

I'm going to buy the Philips Fidelio T1's. I bought and had to return for a replacement. But the delivery person did not deliver them, when they came. Why, I don't.. title: Pretty good. Not GREAT, but not bad.
text:
Whenever I see something with a 4-star review, it usually means it’s a solid product but there’s something (or somethings) keeping it out of 5-star range.

For me, these are a perfect example of that. They’re small (good), not terribly obtrusive (only some out-of-ear-stick-out, tho your experience may vary), the sound has some solid bass which is helpful for the gym (where I tested these out), the sound overall is clear (download some equalizer apps to play with the sound itself), and they stayed in my ear well. I don’t know much about soundstage or whatever, but the sound itself is clear, bass is nice and strong, and you can hear even the subtle nuances like the shifting of a hand on guitar strings clearly enough without being disturbed. That, to me, is the sign of a good earbud.

The transparency mode and noise canceling modes were alright. But that’s just it, they’re alright. Granted, the AirPod Pros have a higher price tag, so they do the ANC and Transparency mode much better. So it’s understandable that these would do the same, but on just the slightest bit of a lower level.

I’m also spoiled bc the Airpod Pros have wireless charging. These DO have USB C, but the lack of wireless charging is a small thing, really. There’s something about being able to toss these on a charging pad and leaving them there to charge that’s just so satisfying. Also, was not a fan of how the case just doesn’t have that “premium” feel. The matte finish is nice, tho I would have liked a little more weight in the case lid, but at this point, these are such little (and I mean LITTLE) things that really, it’s not a dealbreaker.

My only thing is the amount they stick out. I’m sorry, but they do look a little…funny, the way they sort of stick out just a bit so that the “b” logo is upright. They don’t stick out a LOT, but juuuuust enough that when you look in the mirror, you’ll see a vertical line where the physical button (which I have managed to press on accident a couple of times while adjusting the bud) sticks out. Also, I had a little difficulty getting them to stay in, but that’s beyond pretty much anyone’s control.

These get that 4th star because of just how they are a solid enough product worth the purchase. They don’t do any one thing particularly well, but there are just enough teeny things for me that I wouldn’t say these are the best I’ve ever used. (For comparison, the Jabra 75t gets the equivalent of a 4.3 rating…the hear-through is amazing and their app really helps boost functionality).

For me, these are SOLID gym earbuds. They play music loudly, clearly enough, and the bass is strong enough for me that I can drown out whatever annoying other music is playing outside. They fit and stay relatively well. For the price tag, you get some good bang for the buck. You could do worse, but at this range, depending on if you want to pitch in a few more, you could also do better.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: The best Earphones you will ever buy...
text: These are probably the best Bluetooth earbuds I have ever bought. There is one bug, but it is very easy to fix and it rarely happens. Occasionally (I am saying like once every 3 months), the earbuds will disconnect from my device and stop playing sound. The easy fix is to turn off Bluetooth and turn it back on. I have read reviews of similar occurrences and people are thinking it is Bluetooth interference. I do not think that is what it is. Just happens randomly. I use them every day and sometimes I lose connection with no other Bluetooth devices around. But other than one small bug, these earbuds rock! I will use one earbud at a time and rotate them when one earbud is low. Each earbud lasts about 9 hours and the base charges an additional 24 hours, which means I make my earbuds last about 42 hours. Bluetooth range is excellent. Sound quality is excellent. Does get loud but it does not completely cancel out sound (like a vacuum running). Earbuds are very relaxing on the ears and I wear them all day. Works with my 2 computers, Windows and Chromebook. Works with my Samsung S8 and my Samsung tablet. I do have an old iPod touch (gen 2) and it did not support it. But these are made for apple so you will get the most of it using an iPhone. Did some research and with the iPhone, you can use Siri by holding down the button on the earbud and you can get a battery status of the powerbeats on the phone. Android, Windows, and Chromebook do not support these features. Unless there was an update recently and they fixed it. I tested all of this out months ago when I first got my powerbeats. What I love the most about these powerbeats is the security of the earbuds. To sync to new devices, the user must hold down the sync button, then connect. Once connected, the user can connect to the earbuds when they are not connected to another device. Let me give you an example. I have these connected to my laptop, phone, tablet, etc. I can take one earbud with me and put in my pocket. The charging base is at home and I am out doing errands. I can turn on my Bluetooth on my phone, find the powerbeats under Paired Devices, and it connects. I then can disconnect from my phone and connect to my tablet. Once they are connected, they remain connected. It will never switch devices. The earbuds are never in discoverable mode unless you sync them. So, someone else that has Bluetooth on and is searching for a device will not even see it, even though it is not connected to anything. With most Bluetooth devices, if it is on and disconnected, people can see the device. The last thing I will talk about is the sensor in the earbud. So far it works with all my devices. If I take out my earbud, the music or movie that is playing will stop and once I put the earbud back on, it resumes on its own. I guess one thing I do not like is that there is no battery indicator on the charging base. I will use them every day and forget to check the battery life on the charging base. Usually every 2 or 3 days I will charge the base to make sure it is always charged. Whenever the Powerbeats Pro 2 come out, hopefully they add this feature.  Like 4 lights on the bottom, indicating 25, 50, 75, and 100%. The 25 should blink when almost dead. But other than that, I love my powerbeats pro!

title: I can hear clearly now, the rain is gone!
text:
I was super excited to get these since they came out, but decided to wait since Apple was releasing the new AirPods Pro. Even before trying the new AirPods, I made up my mind to get these since I’ve had the Beats 3 previously.

I love these! They do everything an AirPod can, but so much more. The volume controls are on both ears, and so useful! Buttons on both sides are also helpful for answering calls, repeating, and skipping tracks. All useful components that AirPods do not have! AND of course they work singly if you only want to wear one (either side)!

I never get ear aches from keeping them in, and I’ve been on phone calls that have lasted over two hours. The sound quality is nice, the bass has been upgraded from the 3s. There’s a volume limit to these, probably to prevent deafening heights, but they can get loud enough to block the world out. I enjoy the security of having these wrap around my ear, as well! There are so many stories of people always losing their AirPods, and these never just fall out of your ear.

The Bluetooth distance on these are phenomenal (I’ve been told by friends with other earphones.). I’ll pop them in, leave my phone in my in room, and walk all around my house and the perimeter outside without having any connection issues. Don’t expect to go running without carrying your phone, but it is nice to not be so dependent on having it in your pocket while using a Bluetooth device.

They do stop working when you pull them out of your ear, but as soon as you put them back in, it’s right back to work for these babies. Don’t worry about having to turn them on and off every time you take them out. Your sound will pause.

The only issue I have with these (not a real problem) is the bulkiness of the case. There aren’t a lot of covers for the case (again, comparing to the abundance of AirPod case covers), but was able to find a good silicone one on Amazon, too! The case battery lasts days, and does recharge your earphone every time you put them back. I don’t think these completely shut off unless you put them back in your case, so don’t leave them lying on your desk, table, or counter for hours thinking they’ve turned off without draining the battery.

text:
I had read that these had poor sound quality and range but wanted to give them a try because I spend a lot of time working out and otherwise being active so I thought these might be a good upgrade from my Bose soundsport mainly because I didn't like the wire that would eventually get sticky on my neck and I had to pull my phone out to change tracks ect.
Right off the bat these felt loose in my ear canal and I could easily hear ambient noise even with trying all the different tips included. Other reviews I read stated that the big plastic piece caused pain or discomfort on their ear was something I experienced and only after wearing them for 30 minutes while cycling through music gave me lasting discomfort after taking them off.
Other reviewers stated as them being very secure and I know we are all built a bit differently but they felt less secure than my soundsports.
The next shortcoming was the sound quality. As stated by many reviewers and people with professions in music, they lack range, mids are off, there is distortion, hiss(although slight) and an imbalance in the equalization that you are unable to adjust. I compared these to my several other headphones ( corded buds, studio headphones, previous wireless headphones even 2 Bluetooth jam boxes) all outperformed these for sound quality over several genres of music ranging from black metal to pop music. The only thing similar was my cheap gaming headset that actually had better directional sound than these. I know they're popular and expensive but I'm kicking myself for trying Beats products again as they always seem to fall short and cost way too much. You can get better sound from reputable companies for nearly quarter the cost, but I know these are fashionable. If you care/know about music and sound quality as well as your money, do not buy these. My old skullcandy earbuds that I bought at a gasstation in an emergency (currently falling apart) have better sound, comfort and you can adjust the levels!!
I returned the sesame day I got them and picked up a pair of Bose soundsport free (built in controls and no cord). Much better and.....cheaper!!
Fit and comfort is subjective but the sound is awful. I suppose anything is worth a try but personally I felt like a jersey for wasting my time and Amazon's. The return was simple and easy as with everything with Amazon but the product really fell short, I almost want to say its insulting for the price....but hey... they look cool....😒😒

title: Nice earbuds, lousy case/charging design
text:
The earbuds themselves are quite nice and sounds as good as any that I have used before. Where the product falls down is the design of the case and charging system.

Once the ear supports are bent into shape to fit your ear well (as described in the instructions) they can fail to hit the two small bumps built into the top of the clamshell. These protrusions are there to keep the earbuds secure against the charging contacts.

Which means that most of the time the earbuds in their case, rather than charging, are draining; that they can jar loose if the case is moved, and that they will opportunistically reconnect with iDevices and rather than listening to what is being played, the sound is coming out if the (supposedly) charging earbuds in the other room.

*Every* time I put these into charge, I have to check the charging status on my phone to make sure that they are both properly connected. It's a PITA and I cannot count the number of times I've got them out in the morning only to find that one or both are below 10% charge.

Sound good, not necessarily worth the frustration. Expected much better design than this.

title: The Case Makes This a No-Go For Me
text:
I paid the $250 price tag. I’ve had a few issues more related to the charging case than anything else. The charging case makes or brakes whether one should buy this device.

My own experience, it is the most challenging case to get my ear pieces back in place to charge. If you do it enough times, it gets easier, but your brain has to think of it like a puzzle each time you put them back into the charger.

I then have to wait and make sure they are truly secure or they won’t charger properly. I’ve had one charge more than the other because one wasn’t quite snug in the case.

The case is so bulky, I cannot travel in my minimalist way of life I’m used to these days. I can fit them in a backpack, but my minimalist briefcase makes it bulge. I can fit them in my jeans, but it isn’t comfortable. So basically, these are not the best for working out in or travel unless you have a good place to store the case. If you go to the gym and have a locker, these are perfect. Leave them there!

Unless there is a function I haven’t tried, the earpieces burn down the battery when I take them out of my ear and leave them, let’s say in my car, desk or dresser. So they have to be put back in the charger when done.

Getting them in my ear isn’t to difficult, but I’ve found the Apple AirPods are easier.

The sound quality is good, not great. I’ve tried them on an airplane, and they are NOTHING compared to the Beats Studio 3. I know those are over the ear and more expensive. But man...huge difference.

I have owned 2-3 best in-ear pieces and still have the over the ear Beat Studio 3. I plan to stick with the Apple AirPod Pro and Beats Studio 3 for my 2 earpiece choices.

The case makes it a deal breaker for me, since I’m always on the go. I feel the price is too much!

title: Time to return this mess.  The case won't charge, but the buds do.  Go figure.
text:
This is so disappointing. When the buds arrived, the case had enough charge to allow me to pair them with my phone. In order to do any Bluetooth pairings, you have to have the buds in the case with the lid open, and the case has to have a charge. The case has a built-in battery that you can use to recharge the buds several times before the whole setup has to be recharged. In this case, the charge on the case gradually drained and I have never been able to get it to recharge. The odd thing is that the buds will charge in the case when it's plugged in, but the case itself will not take a charge. As you can see in the photo, the buds are at 100% charge while the case is at 0% charge.

The buds come with a really short (think six inches) charging cord with USB-C on each end, but no power adapter. I tried multiple USB-C power adapters that I already had, and even bought a new one (ensuring I got a 30W model), but the case will not take any charge whatsoever. So, now I have to return the whole mess.

Other than that, the sound is pretty good, the ear fit is mediocre and they WILL fall out if you're moving around, and the app is a joke. The app has no equalizer or sound shaping, and the micro-function buttons on the pods themselves let you play/pause, skip forward, or skip back. Press and HOLD the button? That turns noise cancellation on/off/transparent. Or, you can use the app to reprogram the buttons so that, instead of manipulating the noise cancellation, they activate the "Voice Assistant."

Phone calls are difficult and the mic quality is very poor, but I bought these mostly for playing music so I quit screwing around with the phone call abilities as soon as I discovered that nobody could hear me clearly. UGH - so disappointing.

title: Best earbods I've ever owned
text:
So I've had these earbuds for over 6 months and they are literally the best I've ever had. I was a little hesitant to get these due to the price. The advantage I had is that my wife recently got a pair and i was able to try them out before actually buying a pair.

My issue with earbuds has always been that they fall out of my ears, as I use them for high intensity uses such as mountain biking and road biking. I've lost more earbuds than I care to count. The ear hooks take care of that definitively. I have hundreds of biking miles with them, and they've never so much as even came a little loose.

The sound is awesome. The advice I can give is to make sure you actually try every size of inset to really test them out. I thought i had large ear holes, but it turns out the second smallest size insert was what fit me perfectly. I typically ride with only one earbud to keep tabs on ambient sounds for safety, and the sound level is perfect. Battery life is more than I have ever needed for event my longest rides. I recently did a 65 mile road ride and still had 30% left on the battery.

Pairing is super easy. I use a Google Pixel 6, didn't need to download or use the app. An interesting side note is that range is substantially better with my Pixel than either my 2121 MacBook pro or iPad. Odd considering Beats is an Apple product.

text:
The Good: The charge lasts more than enough time for me and the charging case avoids having to recharge them all the time. The sound quality is very good. That's clearly a selling point and it definitely delivers. What's not a main selling point is the microphone however it's actually pretty solid and more than enough to use for phone calls.

The Bad: They do move a little here and there during physical activity. This isn't enough to be concerned about them falling out entirely, but I do have adjust them now and then while I run (which is annoying). Previous versions of Beats you could adjust the ear flap a little to get it to hold in place, but for whatever reason they did away with that here. The other minor issue is durability. They are water resistant, but not water proof. With as much as I sweat this makes me concerned about their durability as well as being able to clean them off. Also the case has zero water resistance so I can't put them away right after a workout which is a bit annoying.

Overall these are not perfect but still the best running headphones I've found. I've tried a number of the other major players out there (AfterShokz, Jaybird, etc) and these are my clear go-to. If they were a moderate price point I would give them 5 stars, but with the premium price I would like to have seen them a bit better with the minor issues noted.

title: Bad connectivity
text:
I've had way cheaper pods with much better connectivity:
1) I have both apple and android devices, every time I want to switch devices I have to reset the pods. Sometimes I need several tries.
2) Sound breaks due to connectivity issues. This doesn't happen too often but still is annoying.
3) Sometimes, one of the pods would not connect (even at 100% battery) so again I have to reset and reconnect.

Noise cancelation (passive) is ok but it fails when moving fast (e.g biking) and the friction with the wind generates vibration and noise. Still is not as bad as my previous pods.

title: Great sound, not bad NC, bad fit for me personally.
text:
I got these as a test to see if the expensive side of earbuds work, I’ve tried cheap, to up to $80 ear buds. These are the first I’ve ever spent more then $100 on earbuds.
I have sensory issues and loud noises make my social battery drain quickly, I have a pair of Skullcandy HASH ANC headphones but I wanted something discrete for work (I clean houses) and big headphones seem rude for every day wear.
I’ve seen lots of reviews say these (beats studio pros) are best for noice cancellation and people with sensory.
Problems for me:
1. They fall out, the small ear plugs fit perfect they don’t hurt and they’re snug, but I bend, move around, work a sweat and the fall out. I’ve tried the medium size and they give me a headache an hour in.
2. Battery life, 4 hours in after fully charged and the earbuds are a 3/4 dead, a full day cleaning can take 2-6 hours so these wouldn’t make the full 6 if I used them constantly.
Good things:
1. Great for on the go, the case is smooth and small easy to put in a pocket for traveling.
2. Earbuds stay in even if lid is open and shook, it was one of the first things I tried and I was very surprised by the strong magnetic connection.
3. Beside the short battery life it charges pretty quickly, it’s an awesome quality.
Again this is just me and my sensory problems make me a little picky if you don’t sweat a lot and use them for short periods these would be great but personally not for long periods and working.
If I can’t find someone to take them and like them I will be returning them, it was a great experiment but not personally fit for me :)

title: Great headphones, infuriating charging case
text:
The case is a HORRIBLE design on these. If you bump the case they'll stop charging, but there's no way for you to know until you're ready to workout and put them on and one of them is dead.

You can't tell if it's charging both sides because it only has one LED on the case. It should have another LED or turn a different color when both sides are charging.

I can check with an iPhone or iPad to see if both sides are charging. You open the case up and hold the phone next to it. You'll see if it's only charging one side, then you can jiggle it until both sides are charging. But it doesn't really matter, because closing the case might break the connection and cause it to stop charging.

I guess I have weird shaped ears, because these (and the previous Powerbeats 2s) are the only thing that really work for my ears. And the sound quality is decent. It has good bass. But it's really frustrating how bad the charging case is.

I got these when they were released in 2019. I lost them and got another pair in 2020. I kinda thought they would improve the charging connection since it's such a bad design, but they didn't. And I guess I'm ridiculous because I just lost another pair in 2021, and I guess I'll buy a 3rd pair now.

I'm still giving them a 3-star review. Obviously I like them enough to keep buying them. The Spirit X2s are just too ugly (and look like they wouldn't fit as well). I should probably get the Trelab X3s instead. But... reviews say the Powerbeats have better/louder sound, and I probably have these turned up to about 75% when I'm running to get enough bass. So I'm just going to get a 3rd pair of the Powerbeats Pros. At least the price came down $80!

title: Very good for the price!
text:
I got these for Christmas and have been using them for about a month now. I am a mobile dog groomer so I am all alone in a trailer for long 8+ hour shifts. Wrestling with bouncy happy dogs doesn't knock these out if you have the right fit end on the buds. The dogs shake water from the bath drenching me and the earbuds, but they so far keep on running. They get coated in dog hair pieces, but have been easy to clean and the noise canceling feature works AMAZING to tune out those barking dogs or muffle the obnoxiously loud air dryer that usually requires gun range earmuffs. (Dont worry I have earplugs for the dogs) I tested out phone calls and my husband was able to hear me in a phone call clearly and without it being too annoying with my hair dryer on at low speed. High level was a little too loud he said. The sound quality is great. It's not like my car where I have a subwoofer to make my music slap, but it is better than most.

The battery life is good enough for me. By time I finish a dog 1-3 hours typically, I pack them away and drive to my next house which by that point they have enough power to go the entire next chunk of time. On long shifts 9+ hours I am able to go without stopping to recharge the case. I will charge it when I get home though. I do feel the fact I have lots of breaks helps me keep the buds charged, but others might run into an issue.

title: Amazing headphones! Update..beware
text:
I am very particular when it comes to headphones. My ears cannot hold any type of bud. I have tried over 8 different pairs of wired headphones, 4 different pairs of buds, 3 different over the ear hooks, and 2 different completely wireless headphones. It’s like I’m obsessed with finding the right fit, sound quality, (I’m not a sticker for sound but some headphones have a tinny or just bad sound) and connectivity.

I can say with certainty these headphones are the best at fitting in my ear, sound quality, and synching with my iPhone...hands down.

Fit.... they ain’t going nowhere. Once in my ear they don’t move a millimeter. I’ve done jumps, handstands, runs, bikes, played tennis with them. They simply don’t move. Huge win.

Synching...They forced my phone to synchronize with it...whoa. As soon as I put them in my ear, they turn on like magic; no buttons no dial, nothing...they just turn on. When I put them in the case, they automatically turn off. With my old Bluetooth headphones, often I would not get sound from the phone after I was done only to realize the headphones were still connected. The same applies when you only put one in as well.

Sound. Sound quality is fantastic...loud, crisp, and easy to hear...even with one in.

Overall, these headphones are a complete game changer. If you have the funds these are well worth the money.

UPDATE... huge paring problem with my new iPhone 12. Headphones have a difficult time paring for some unknown reason. I have reset Bluetooth, reset the headphones and still I have a problem automatically connecting. I often need to put them back in the case and them take them out to work. I even brought them into apple store, and after a week, they sent them back claiming nothing was wrong with them.

title: Better alternative, but still not the best.
text:
LOOK
If you’ve ever had the Powerbeats, you’ll notice the look is similar. The body on each side is slanted this time around, which gives them a more comfortable feel. They have a behind-the-ear loop that goes, well, behind the ear. It holds the earpiece firmly in place. I am a very active person and they have yet to fall out of my ear. The Beats logo is an actual button used for accepting and ending calls, playing music, skipping tracks, and accessing Siri. The volume button is at the top of the earpiece body. The great thing is both earpieces have both buttons. There’s nothing you cant do with one that you can’t do with the other. The Powerbeats Pro (PBP) are made that way so you can use only one earpiece if you’d like.

BATTERY LIFE
The battery life is ok. They aren’t as good as the 12 hour Powerbeats3. They do included a portable charging case. This is absolutely my favorite part. I use my PBP for literally 9-10 hours a day. When I ran out of juice on my previous ones, I’d have to hunt down a charger. Then an outlet. Then dedicate an hour of my time. Not the case anymore (no pun intended). If I need a charge, I put them back in their case, slide them in my pocket, and continue with my day. Then I take them out when they’re ready. No more tethered to a wall. The case fits in a front pocket, but it definitely feels bulky. Keep in mind, the earpieces cannot be charged without the case (more on this later).

RELIABILITY
I wish I had all good things to say, but alas I do not. My Powerbeats3 kept a strong connection with my iPhone. The PBP seem to struggle at times. I would try playing music or watch YouTube only to have to reconnect the Bluetooth. Fortunately, that didn’t happen enough to cause me stress. The real issue is “Hey Siri”. It’s more of an annoyance than a feature. For those that do not know what that is, it’s when you can activate Siri hands-free by saying “Hey Siri”. The problem is if I’m having a conversation with someone, Siri would start talking in my ear because she thought I was calling for her. Then when I would actually call for her, she would only respond half the times. It’s a joke of a feature. I turned it off altogether.

SOUND
So they sound pretty good for what they are. Keep in mind, they are not large studio headphones. For the size of them, the audio quality is good. Volume is loud. Base is decent. The sound on both earpieces stayed in sync with one another about 99% of the times. Phone calls sound clear as well. The other end seems to hear me loud. Are they the best in their class? Probably not. Are they the worst? Not by a long shot.

FEATURES
As I said before, my favorite feature is the portable charging case. Just like the Powerbeats3, you can get about an hour’s worth of playback by charging it for only 5 minutes. The case also does well as a protectant for when they’re not in use. The “Hey Siri” feature sucks, but we went over that. Another handy feature are the sensors on each earpiece. If you are listening to music, Pandora, YouTube, etc, the track will pause itself if you remove one or both earpiece. Then it will resume playback once you put the earpiece back in your ear. This worked every time. Although they cannot be charged without the case, there is a reason for that. Beats eliminated the port on the earpieces to give them more water resistance than the older models. Up until now, none of the previous models have been given an IP rating. The PBP have been granted a rating of IPX4, which translates to being able to withstand splashes of water, not submerging. One feature that I appreciate (which is not an actual feature) is the PBP main button is a soft touch. So if I’m carrying a baby and I receive a call, I can tap the button with my shoulder to answer. Very convenient!

RESULTS
These are a great option for those who want a true wireless earpiece. The sound quality is good. Battery life is decent. The connection fails occasionally, but nothing crazy. “Hey Siri” is frustrating. The charging case keeps them charged and protected. The automatic pause/resume feature works beautifully. The behind the ear loop keeps them secure in your ear no matter what you’re doing. If you’re hesitant, I’d say wait for the next iteration of the PBP so Apple could clean out some bugs, but it might be a while since these were just released. If the wire on the Powerbeats 3 doesn’t bother you, I’d say stick with those. If you want 100% wire free, I’d recommend these over the AirPods.

title: Expensive, But ABSOLUTELY worth it!
text:
I'm one of those people who never leave reviews but was going to buy them as a gift and stumbled across the reviews. I've owned these since they launched and I am here to say--DO NOT LISTEN TO ANY REVIEW THAT HAS LESS THAN 4 STARS. I don't give 5 stars because nothing is perfect. These are expensive af so that's why they get 4 stars.

As far as sound quality? They suck on airplanes. You really need some over the ear headphones if you want to drown out the engine of a 747 or any plane for that matter. In any other instance, these are great. If someone starts talking to you, you will not hear a word they say. They have great bass and true Beats quality and I've owned many Beats products. They all end up on the Facebook marketplace whenever I feel like being the Oprah of gently used items. But I'm also an audiophile. 4/5

Battery life? They get pretty decent battery life on their own. I can usually go an entire day with them in my ear. I listen to music or podcast at work and on breaks I watch TV shows and they don't die on me until I'm about to go to bed. They are great for the gym--even in sweaty workouts. Now I wouldn't submerge them, but if you forget about them when you hop in the shower--don't fret, these can take a beating. The case holds severals days of charges without needing to be recharged itself. And if you're in a pinch, 5 mins in the case will usually get you about 80% battery life. After over two years, these are still holding up pretty well. 4/5

Comfort? I've seen some pretty nasty reviews of people saying "they pinch my ears" well, news flash not all ears are created equal. In addition to all the things I am, I am also one of those people who can't ear regular ear buds because they just fall out. I would have loved to be able to wear Air Pods, but alas, that's not in the cards for me and that's okay. So I have always been an ear hook guy. These are AWESOME! For the people who own them and have hurting ears who haven't returned them yet--you can bend the hook in almost any direction to suit your needs. There is no need to be in pain, these are great. 4/5

That being said, I highly recommend them. I don't go anywhere without them, they have become a staple to my life.

text:
Just got these at the $99 price and sooo worth it! I bought the Echo Buds 2 for around the same price about 9 months ago and they are fine, but could never get a good, comfortable fit. Grabbed these at the low price and liking them much more. Super light weight and comfortable and strong bass as mentioned many times which is a staple for Beats (and for me!).

One minor issue using on Android. At first, the volume was pretty low even when maxed out on the phone and the Beats app is pretty much useless (no volume or EQ controls). Solution is to max the volume on the device, then go to the developer settings and turn off "Disable absolute volume", turn off bluetooth, then turn back on to reconnect the buds. Volume can now go way high. May need to toggle the "Disable absolute volume" thing on/off cuz turning it back on didnt affect the volume after for me so your device may vary.

Very happy so far. Will report back if anything changes with more use.

FYI: ANC is not a huge selling factor for me so nothing to really share there. But anything is better than the Echo Buds ANC. That is a joke as far as I can tell.

title: If you sweat a lot, look out for this problem (on occasion)
text:
These work very well. There are occasional dropouts of one or the other earbud, but they are generally very reliable. Plus, with the earhooks they definitely stay in place.

One thing to look out for however, is the following:

On the underside of each bud there are 2 very small concave electrodes which fit the convex outputs in the containing (charging) box. If you sweat a lot it seems as though this can cause a build up of sediment/brine which can interfere with this electrical connection. If this happens, one can no longer connect the earbud (with the buildup) to one's device.

This is solvable simply by cleaning the connectors. It took me a little while to notice this phenomenon and figure out the problem, so this is just an FYI for others.

I heard mostly great reviews about the Beats Powerbeats Pro, and despite my reluctance to spend nearly $200, plus the $30 2 year extended warranty, I purchased them with fingers crossed. The sound is ok, but not near as good as I expected from a Beats/Apple product. Noise cancelling is pretty good, and battery life along with it's storage/charging is a definite positive. I've also had connection and disconnecting issues. Which honestly are very disappointing from a premium brand(s). I'd give them a C to C+ for Overall quality, sound, features, and H2O resistance. Next time I will save myself $100 and go back to JBL.

title: I highly recommend these, especially for the price, but your needs and usage may vary
text:
TL:DR is that I recommend these, especially for the price, but your needs and usage may vary.

I don't really need or use the ANC or Transparency mode right now as I primarily use these around the house when I want to listen to some tunes without disturbing the fam, and while on my Peloton bike, so I'm not going to review that.

For me, they are more comfortable than my AirPods and AirPod Pros, and they don't constantly fall out of my ears. The sound quality is on par with my Powerbeats Pros and they are lighter, more comfortable, and less obtrusive.

The small case and overall smaller size of the buds is also quite nice. Did I mention how comfortable they are? And good looking?

Let's be honest, Bluetooth is an inherently flawed system that affects all earbuds and BT speakers, but these are doing an excellent job for me for what I need them to do, and they are reasonably priced (I got mine the day they were released, as I had a coupon from a chain store that will remain unnamed, although it rhymes with Rest Guy).

Give them a shot.

These are a near perfect fit. I only have to adjust them every 30 minutes to an hour, which I assume is normal.. They are light and go deep in my ears. They are comfortable.

Now I used to rip on Beats all the time for they high price and bassy muffled sound quality, but these are different. Yes they are on the bassier side, but not in a bad way. It doesn't boost the 200Hz hum bass, its more of the low 20-60 Hz umph of kick drums and Guitar picks. It makes for a "powerful" feeling listening experience, even at high volumes. I am on iPhone and use the Rock EQ setting for apple music, this creates a very good "V" EQ and makes these headphones shine.

Build quality is fine, not crazy. The case is slightly larger than the AirPods Pro case and feels a little cheaper, but not by much.

title: High price point, but high quality
text:
Didn't buy these from amazon but I figured I'd write a review since I'm bored during lockdown. These are indeed expensive however so are the airpods so if you are looking for wire-free earbuds then consider this one of your choices.

Pros:
- Excellent quality audio consists of very crisp bass that almost compares to car subs with the right settings. High end frequency is good and does not get drowned out by bass. Mid frequencies are ok but the clarity makes up for it

- Comfortable at least for my ears. Of course this changes depending on you however one advantage I can say for sure is that at least the rubber part can be changed out.

- This goes for if you normally have earbuds fall out of place. The part that goes around your ear is snug allowing you to exercise without worry.

- Buttons on either side allows for easy pausing and playing as well as volume control.

- Good battery life. Charging it is quick while the life of the case can last for a while without charging.

Cons:

- Sometimes the earbuds don't sit well in the case which may cause charging issues. Make sure it is snapped in place before you close it up

- There is an issue where one of the earbuds will not work unless you place it back in the case and re try. It probably has to do with what I wrote above.

- Bulky case. This is a big one for me. The airpod case is very compact and doesn't take much space. Understandable given the size difference.

That's pretty much it. Take note I am an iPhone user so Android users may have a different experience with these in terms of connectivity and other things. In Conclusion, I'm happy with these things and will continue using them for whenever I get on the punching bag.

title: Good sound, awful case and experience
text:
I would highly discourage anyone from ordering these. I've looked high and low for a good pair of sport headphones with good sound, and these are close — with a glaring exception. First, the good: Good sound, good fit, good integration with my iPhone. The bad: It's down to the case. Not only is it big and bulky, but it's also poorly designed and a constant nightmare.

The contact points to charge the earbuds are very small and susceptible to water (or most accurately, sweat) damage. Not only is it extremely hard to get the buds to connect to the case when putting them back in after use, it's also very easy to jostle the buds loose in the case when they're inside. What happens more often than not: One bud stops charging, connects to my phone and drains the battery. When I pick up the buds to go work out sometimes, the earbud dies within minutes. There's no way to manually turn the buds on or off, and it's a consistent pain to make sure that the buds are housed within the case.

I asked Apple for a service, and they replaced a bud (with a completely different model). That didn't last long so I went back for more service and they determined that the case had water damage. I paid an additional $99 for service, and it appears they completely replaced the lot — case and two buds. Now with a new case, same issues. What's more, I never dropped the case in water or anything of the like. What it was was sweat on the earbuds (which is common for "sport" earphones), which the case didn't like. Now, when I work out, I lay the headphones out to dry, put them back in the case VERY CAREFULLY and cross my fingers that it doesn't happen again.

The short of the long? Great sound. Awful design. Pass. I would get a refund if I could.

text:
Honestly so annoyed and disappointed in this product. It wasnt a small amount of cash for me and I really wanted to invest in a decent pair but stick within my budget. I should have just saved more and spent the extra to be honest. The sound is great and noise cancelling is fair BUT I can't use them at all because they will not stay in my ear at all, what the heck! That's the least I would ask for at this price point! Did this product not get tested for that!? I have tried every different ear pad they gave and it makes no difference. Even sitting still they kept coming out and then you are constantly pushing them back in which is just irritating and defeats the whole point. I stupidly did not listen to the reviews and should have as it seems many have this issue. I also tried to give them more time to work so now can't return them and are stuck with a useless pair of earbuds I will can never use.

*** UPDATE: Hoping others find this tip useful, so I experiemented and had some extra eartips left over from another pair of headphones (a chorded cheap pair) and decided to try them on these to see if it would be better. And guess what, they are far better! So has very much improved the ability for them to actually stay in my ear. Now it's not one hundred percent, they still slip out a little occassionally, but still much better than with the ones beats provided to the point I can actually use them now without 100 percent annoyance. So my suggestion is if stuck these like I am now, try to put other brand eartips on to see if it helps! You can buy a pack super cheap on amazon of various ones.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

The Beats case will lose battery life even if it’s not charging any ear buds…and earbuds can get maybe 2 full charges from case without needing to recharge. Earbuds last 2-3 hrs, and lose battery life even if they aren’t being used. Fell asleep with ear buds in at full charge and woke up to them dead and there wasn’t anything playing. I guess the one plus side is I’m having to charge or switch ear buds (I often use one at a time) so often I don’t have time to lose them like I would with the Tozo ear buds.

title: Great for the price
text:
After losing my apple AirPods I was very disheartened to have to spend 300 bucks on another pair. That’s when I went out and searched for something comparable and found these. After using them for several month I have overall positive feelings about them however their is many things the future consumers of this product should know.

Pros:
To start the price point on these is much more affordable than the airpod pros. The wireless works well and I have not had any range issues with them or issues with them randomly cutting off or disconnecting. The noise cancellation is solid but not perfect. It does it job but it does give me a fish bowl feeling when NC is turned on. The battery life is also amazing. I believe they are rated for 8 hours and I can say I can get around 6 hours out of them before the low power beep comes on.

Cons:
With the benefit of its low price point, some corners were definitely cut. Let’s start with the spacial audio. It’s not vary clear and when turned on it fails to compare to the air pods pro, where you can literally forget you have headphones in. Secondly the microphone on these is very bad. It sounds like you’re talking through a two way radio. And finally my biggest gripe with these is that in certain situations they emit a very loud high pitched squeal. If I am holding one headphone in my hand, and close my hand, the headphone almost sounds like it has feedback and this isn’t a little it’s loud. Loud enough to hear across the room. I can also recreate this when closing the lid to my case. If I close it to slowly the feedback screech happens almost every time. I worry that this is causing damage to my headphones but I don’t know.

Overall I think these are great for the price but have issues and if you have the funds, go buy a pair of galaxy buds or air pod pros.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: What an utter embarrassment...
text:
This is the first time in 30 years of life I have been so disappointed that I went back to review a product.

Allow me to preface with the fact that I have used every single generation of Beats since they have been coming out and have never had an ill word to say towards them.

You may have noticed a terrible overall review (DO NOT BUY THESE) but great reviews for features such as sound quality, noise cancellation and battery life. The reason is this:

These headphones WILL NOT CONNECT. Every single time you wish to use these you must manually go into your phone's bluetooth settings, delete or "forget" the device and then redetect it as if it is your first time ever using them and even then it may not work. Imagine you have a 30 minute break and wish to listen to something: these headphones will take 10 of those minutes simply to detect if you're lucky it may even detect both.

What an incredible waste.

title: Buyer beware! Check your warranty coverage date for “new” products
text:
ATTENTION: My 1 star review is only to call attention to the selling condition and warranty of the product.

I purchased a pair of these Wed 11/2/22 (received Thu 11/3/22) and I paired them and looked at the settings and product numbers. I noticed that the warranty coverage did not cover the full year; in fact 4 months of coverage was missing. So I contacted Apple Support and Amazon Support and both agreed that it was unusual for a “new” product and that it should be a year from purchase.

As Apple wasn’t able to do much on their end regarding coverage on an already active product. The end result was to send the earbuds back for a ‘new’-“new” pair. They arrived today (11/4/22) and I repeated the process of pairing and looking everything over. There is still an issue with the coverage; it’s missing 9 days. That’s unacceptable for a product that is being sold and shipped by Amazon listed as ‘new’ yet having evidence of previous activity. That is not a new product by that definition, it is technically refurbished.

While I have chosen not to repeat the process a 3rd time as 9 days is much less missing time then 4 months. I am not entirely satisfied because no time should be missing and a product listed and sold as new should be just that in its entirety. I am extremely disappointed with Amazon over the lack of transparency and honesty. So to any people who have purchased this product ‘new’ from Amazon recently, make sure you check the warranty coverage.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: You get what you pay for..
text:
These headphones are mediocre at best. I am an avid music listener of all genres, and believe I know good balance, bass, highs and lows, and overall sharpness when it comes to trying out headphones. I am not a consumer goods professional, but certainly a worthwhile critic. When it comes to headphones and wireless earbuds, I have bought and used a number of brands from skullcandy, jaybird, bose, and of course apple. That being said, here is my review:

Noise quality: 3/5 - I was expecting a bigger "punch" being that the brand (even though its now owned by apple) was developed by Dr. Dre and Jimmy Lovine, and geared towards the rap and hip hop industries. The bass and overall output of these headphones is quite indistinguishable. There is no "wow" factor.

ANC/Transparency mode: 2/5 - The ANC mode is BARELY noticeable. If Apple's airpod pros were given a 8 on a scale of 1-10 in the quality of this feature (10 being superior), these would rate a 2 or 3. My only reaction upon receiving and using these headphones and this feature is "Seriously?" Absolutely piss poor and a genuinely deceiving selling point. It simply is not a feature.

Comfort: Out of 5 starts, I'd give there a 3.7-4. They fit snug and are comfortable for long periods of wear. Without a stem like the airpods pro, they are less noticeable in your ear. Sweat resistant, sure. But by no means superior. A cheap pair of skull candy headphones seem to stay in the ear better when sweating. One drip, and they will slip. However I will say that the sound quality is not as affected as some other competitor headphones when exposed to sweat.

Functionality: 2/5 - Who is the genius that decided to make the front of the earbud the source of the controls? It is the only exposed surface of the earbud. If the earbud is slipping out of your ear, you cannot simply push it back in as this generates a "tap" and will pause/stop music. Most annoyingly this will end a call. It is ever more frustrating if lying down with your earbuds in. Again, any pressure on the face of the earbud (the only exposed surface), will generate a tap. This feature needs to be GREATLY re-engineered! A big, hard slap on the back of the head to the six figure paid design team.

When I bought these headphones on prime day, I paid $100. I took the risk of trying something different, hoping for a good competitor to the airpod pros I was using at the time. I am quite disappointed. I would not recommend these to anyone, and would encourage consumers to buyer cheaper headphones, or spend the extra $70 for the airpod pros or beat fits pro.

SEVERLY DISAPPPOINTED IN YOU apple, beats, and the designers and engineers of these headphones. You certainly underdelivered! And well, we get what we paid for...
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

I rarely spend hundreds of dollars on big brand items, but these were 40% off, so I thought I would give it a try. They were great...for 2 months. Now they have a very loud buzzing in both buds and she doesn't want to wear them. She's gone back to her old Tozos, which are starting to not hold their charge very well. I'm going to try and get a hold of customer support. I didn't keep the box or the warranty card and I can't find a serial number anywhere on the case, so I'm not sure if they will give me a replacement. I'm tempted to just buy a new pair of Tozos for her. Her old pair lasted over 2 years before they started having issues, and that is with pretty heavy, constant use. Sound quality of the Tozos are pretty decent too, especially for the price. I think I only paid $30 or $40 for them. All in all, I'm much more impressed with Tozos and quite disappointed with the Beats. Guess I need to stick to the "bargain" items I usually buy.

title: Annoying bug for iPhone users
text:
Just got a pair of these and there's a bug with iOS devices. When they're connected to my iPhone if I try to change the noise settings between Active Noise Canceling (ANC), Transparency mode, and "off" in the control panel, it doesn't work. Sometimes the earbuds do actually change, sometimes they don't, but in both cases the control panel's UI doesn't change. Googling around it sounds like a lot of people have faced this issue* and that it might have been introduced in iOS 15, which might explain why earlier reviews didn't mention it. The earbuds themselves might be fine, but until Apple fixes this software bug I wouldn't say they're worth the price.

Update: Similar problem on my Mac (MacOS 12.4) - now it doesn't look like you can switch modes on the Mac at all, I need to disconnect them from the Mac and connect them to my iPhone in order to change modes. I can long-press the button on the buds of course, but this doesn't allow for turning ANC/Transparency mode "off" only for toggling between them.

*Google: "beats studio buds iOS transparency reddit" and check out the first two results, I can't post a link here.

Workaround: It is still possible for me to toggle between the different modes, I just need to use the bluetooth settings on the phone or press and hold the buttons on the buds.

title: Don't believe the hype
text:
Don't believe the hype over these things. I've had my pair for over a year so I'm not speaking as some excited fanboy. Among the many different ear pieces I've owned over the years by far, these are the worst (adjusting for money spent).

Cons:

Noise cancellation doesn't work; not for you or the person on the other line. People rating the noise cancellation favorably simply haven't experienced what true noise cancellation is like.

Call quality: total garbage and it gets even worse with time When I first got the ear piece, people had slight trouble hearing me. A year later and I will no longer use my Beats for phone calls.

Random settings: the settings randomly change to transparency mode, something I absolutely abhor.

Unstable fit: do not use these if you're doing cardio or need to move your head around. Your buds will pop right out.

Pros:

Long battery life: Credit where it's due, Beats have a great battery life and if you're on the go, the carrying case acts as a charging station. I've gone several days without needing to charge the carrying case.

Sound quality: the sound quality is great for listening to music or podcasts. NOT FOR PHONE CALLS.

Bottom line:

these earbuds are only good if you're sitting or walking around. If you want to workout in your earbuds or if you want to make phone calls with them, get something else!

title: good starter earbuds, but a terrible replacement
text:
i bought these while they were on sale because my airpod pros seemed to be on their last leg. while i loved my airpods, i didn’t want to spend that kind of money on earbuds that would only last about 2 years. i decided to give these a go as beats are known for their sound quality. within a few days of receiving them, i had to order a replacement for connectivity and playback issues. when my replacement came, i released these connectivity issues were just poor product quality and the headphones inability to connect when your phone is in a pocket or not in clear shot of you. i took too long to return them for a full refund so i’m stuck with these, but i’ve just resorted to dealing with my static filled airpods as they still sound and feel much better.

pros:
- snug in ear fit that creates a seal for audio to be heard without distortion
- clear and good bass
- easy to pair and use
- anc is not nearly the best among its class but the noise cancellation is good

cons:
- despite having a snug fit, the shape is very odd and makes it difficult to adjust the earphone without pressing the buttons
- transparency mode is non existent. you cannot hear ANYTHING when these earphones are in
- the sound is overall muffled and muddy with only bass and some treble being clear
- no wireless charging case

overall, if you’re in dire need of affordable earphones then this might be the choice for you. if you’re an audiophile or you’ve experienced a more premium earbud, you’ll have some gripes with this product and it’s likely best to look elsewhere.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: good quality earbuds - just a couple of things I didn't like
text:
Bought these as Christmas present as I was looking to move on from another brand that had let me down on two occasions. Went with Beats because I have their over-the-ear headphones and LOVE them!

Sound quality is good. I wish there was the ability to adjust the sound via EQ levels. The option to have noise cancelling or transparency mode is awesome. I feel like I can lost in the sound of whatever I'm listening to while on either mode.

They feel good in the ear but because of their shape design and the sensitivity of the buttons, I find they can get caught on my winter hats...meaning I can from play mode to pause or vice versa because the material of my hat will rub up against the earbud. I also cannot use them while I'm laying down because rolling over on my side causes too much pressure and thus pauses whatever I'm listening to. Other earbuds I have used have a more sleek design which doesn't cause this (slight) issue.

Had to buy a silicone pouch for it because of the slippery nature of the box it comes in...which I may or may not have dropped on the first day! Overall a good product.

title: First impressions after 10 mins.
text:
I wanted to write a review that was as non biased as possible. I own a pair of AirPods Pro’s. I bought these beats for my job, where it can be it very loud. I didn’t want to run the risk of losing my AirPods. I saw the beats were on sale.

I like them a lot, for it to be a cheaper alternative for AirPod pros. The noise cancellation isn’t as good as the AirPod pros. In my opinion it’s not that much of a difference between the two. It’s noticeable difference but not an inconvenience either.

With either ANC or Transparency mood is on. The beats sacrifice some of the audio performance for either one. Sounds the same in either mood. When you turn noise control off, the bass, treble, and etc are amplified. For the AirPod pros it’s the complete opposite from the beats in terms of noise control. The bass is amplified in ANC or transparency mood; and sacrifices the audio performance with noise control off. Make sure to figure out what ear tips fit best in your ear to get the best quality.

To me they’re worth 89-110 dollars, I wouldn’t pay anything over it. Especially not at 150, but it’s a great quality for that price range I set if you can find it on sale. Whereas I’d pay full price for the Pros, and did.

All in all they’re a good quality pair of ear buds to get the job done. They’re a good cheaper alternative to AirPod pros. Would still serve as a great gift or to satisfy the average everydays needs.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: Left side often doesn't charge (even if you make sure it is...)
text:
I don't often leave reviews on things, but I felt the need to for these headphones. The sound quality is great, noise cancellation is great, features are good. Overall, I genuinely do enjoy them...when they charge, anyways.

I've read troubleshooting, and, yeah, you could go through the pain of resetting them everytime you want to charge them, but that's really not ideal, right? That's not how they are supposed to behave, is it? Or, am I to believe that these were released with the intent that we go through several troubleshooting steps everytime we want the left bud charged?

When they first arrived they were great, but the left side slowly became less and less likely to charge. It has gotten to the point that I do enusre that it is charging when I put them away. I press down firmly, I make sure it's clean, I go through the process and make sure that they are both charging. I close the case, leave it be, and when I go to listen to music again I find the left bud completely dead while the right is fully charged.

Every. Single. Time. Without fail!

So, if you can handle the frustration of having to wait an extra 20 minutes before you can go on a walk or listen to music with both of your ears, then go ahead and buy these. Otherwise, maybe invest in a product that isn't so horribly flawed. And it's not just me! Googling that the left side doesn't charge brings up a managerie of different folks looking to complain, and all the answers are always the same ol' troubleshooting. Well, guess what? That's unacceptable.

Fix the product.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: Good headphones for a discount
text:
Honestly, I really wanted to like these earbuds. I purchased these for a 30$ discount but just missed the 40$ discount. Unfortunately, I ended up returning them as they just didn't cut it.

1. Sound
I was really underwhelmed with the sound of these earbuds. Upon receiving them, I immediately wanted to see what the sounded like. To my surprise, the sounded shallow, and not immersive at all. I have a pair of fake air pod pros and even they sounded better than these. Now, I'm not one to require an insane amount of base, but this was ridiculous, these earbuds had horrible sounding low base. It relied too much on higher frequency sounds. This make the sound seem like it was coming through a filter or like you were listening through a wall. This is especially disappointing as Beats are supposed to be catered to base-junkies. I was also surprised when I found out that these earbuds cannot get very loud. I don't think these earbuds ever touched 90 decibels for me. Even though I try not to listen to music too loud, I would like the option to turn up my music for a little bit.

2. Fit
Overall the fit was ok. The instructions to properly insert the earbuds were a bit difficult to adjust to but I got the hang of it eventually as once they are in your ear, you are supposed to twist them down into your ear. The issue with this was that after a period of time, the earbud would untwist on their own requiring you to readjust them. This also happens if you make any kind of face movement aside from talking or eating such as smiling. This might not be a problem except the noise control ability of the earbud is completely dependent on the seal it has on your ear. This is easily disrupted when it moves out of place. Aside from that, the earbuds did not fall out of my ears easily.

3. Noise control
One of the aspects of these earbuds I was excited for was the noise control. According to some reviews, it was just shy of Air pod pro level. Especially since I got it for 120$ less than half the price of airpod pros, I was excited to see their noise control ability. I was again disappointed. As mentioned above, the seal of the earbuds on your ear is easily broken therefore making noise control pretty much useless. Aside from that, it does a pretty decent job at blocking out VOICES when there is music playing at a medium volume. BUT it does NOT block out low frequency sounds well such as that of a car engine.

4. Appearance/case
These earbuds look decent enough, if you dislike having stems like from air pods you will like these. They are pretty discrete but not as discrete as the beats fit pro. The ends of the earbuds still come out a little bit of your ears. The case is slightly larger than that of the air pods pros and slightly thicker. It has a matte finish as opposed to the glossy finish of the air pods. I actually prefer the matte finish but that is my preference. One gripe I have is the fact that you are provided with a charger but it is usb-c to usb-c as well as being about 2 inches in length. Aside from the ridiculously short length, not having a cable have a usb side is extremely annoying.

Summary:
If you can get these earbuds for a discounted price, they are an absolute steal, for being only very slightly more expensive than regular airpods, they are a big step up. For 150$ I really don't think they are worth it. I decided to return mine and pay the extra 50$ for the Beat fit pros.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: Good but...
text:
Bought these as a replacement for my dying airpod pros. I'd bought a few cheapo airbus in the past that were ok but super glitchy and decided to invest in a better pair. I finally decided to purchase these because 1) they seemed to be good for people with small ears unlike a lot of earbuds out there and 2) they were on sale (they always seem to be on sale at least 20%).

Pros:
-More comfortable than airpod pros when wearing for long periods of time.
-Sound is good as far as I can tell
-available in different colors. I got the moon grey ones and love it.

Cons:
-the buttons. They're super sensitive, they'll get pressed by any slight pressure (fixing your hair, leaning your head on something, etc.) It's IMPOSSIBLE to use these laying on your side with your head against a pillow. I usually end up taking one out because whatever your watching/listening too will constantly pause over and over again while your laying on it.
-battery life. The earbuds themselves are ok, comparable to airpod pros if slightly shorter. The case though has terrible battery life. If you're using them a lot it will need to be charged every other day or so, while my airpods could go for like a week.
-noise canceling is only ok
- transparency mode is super staticy, basically rendering that mode useless. You're better off just taking the earbuds out.
-they switch to transparency mode when only one earbud is in. That might be ok for some people but I don't like it at all, especially since there is so much static with that mode. And when you have to take out one earbud when laying down it's just an annoying routine.

Overall they feel like one of the cheapo earbuds I've previously purchased, just with less connectivity issues and a bigger price tag. I'm not an apple person at all but I think I'll just end up getting another pair of airpod pros when these eventually start dying (or if I get fed up with them).

Overall rating: Meh.

title: When they connect they're great, but iPhone connectivity is incredibly frustrating
text:
The overall quality of these is solid. About what I expected, really good noise cancellation (although one of the buds the noise cancelling effect is sometimes louder than the other, but usually they're good). The issue that I've had is one I've googled and found has been going on for awhile and it's that they have an issue connecting to iPhones, which... that's a pretty big issue to have. What this results in is a super frustrating case of typically needing to put in and take out my earbuds sometimes 3-4 separate times before they automatically connect to my phone. It might not sound like a big deal but when you're on the go and they have a magnetic case having to take them both out of the case and insert them, and then put them back, and then insert again etc. is very tedious. It's particularly frustrating because I've found that the issue is wildly inconsistent. Sometimes they connect perfectly, other times I have to repeatedly insert them and put them back in the case, and on a few occasions I've had issues where only one will connect at a time and I need to reset the earbuds.

I've done research into the connectivity issues too and some of the contributing factors seem pretty ridiculous. One reported cause is if your phone has bluetooth enabled for awhile but isn't connected to anything it will have issues connecting. Another suggests that low battery for either the phone or earbuds impacts connectivity. I've had much cheaper buds in the past and never experienced these issues with other brands.

Another issue I have with them is the battery display. The battery life is really good, but the on-screen indicator that pops up when the case is open seems to pop up at random for me. I've had like $30 wireless buds before that show the battery in the top right corner of your iphone next to the phone battery so long as they're turned on, and I'd honestly prefer that to this fancier feature that doesn't work all the time.

The bottom line is if you don't experience the connectivity issues then these are high quality earbuds. If you do, the issue is so frustrating and frequent that you're better off looking elsewhere. I often find myself walking my dog, or to the bus for work and thinking that I'd rather just have wired earbuds that I know will never have any issues connecting than go through the steps of trying to get these to connect.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: Too Big
text: I want to like these, but there’s a really bad design flaw. They don’t fit in my ears and if they slip even a little and I try to gently push them back in, the “b” is trigger happy and hangs up on my phone calls or stops my music. There is no way to go back a song unless you have access to the device playing music. Not user friendly. I can’t move when I’m wearing these or they will fall out, so forget about working out or running or even gentle walking really. Sitting on a plane perfectly still, they fell out of my ears 15+ times in less than 2 hours. It’s incredibly frustrating and beats doesn’t seem to have any solution other than to say that my ear canals must just be too small, despite the fact other in ear buds fit fine and are much more comfortable. Even if I jam these in my ears, they’re uncomfortable and cumbersome. They’re heavy, not light like you would expect. The correct way to wear them to show the logo doesn’t make sense with the shape of the ear. Switching back to another brand. The noise cancellation is a nifty idea, but the quality is not comparable to over the ear headphones. The transparency setting is not much better and it’s complicated to switch between the two. I’m tired of not hearing well and the buds falling out and trying to hold them in causing me to accidentally hang up over and over and over again on work calls and video calls.
