title: These Cause Contact Dermatitis
text: I have owned several sets of earbuds and have never had the problems that these Powerbeats Pro earbuds cause for my ears.  The problems began when I started wearing them for more than an hour.  My ear canals became very itchy and I had severe discharge of clear liquid from both ears afterwards.  This eventually occurred every time that I would wear them for more than just a few minutes.  My ears became less tolerant of me wearing the Powerbeats Pro earbuds as time went on.  Always, the same symptoms after using them - itchy ear canals followed by two to three days of severe clear liquid discharge from within the ear canals and then crusty, dry, parched skin in and around my ears.  One time, these symptoms led to a severe ear infection that put me on steroids for almost a month!  The severe skin cracking due to the dermatitis became infected and caused the wholesale ear infection that I experienced.  I would say from reading several related posts that this has been reported by many, many people to Apple. In my case, my doctor diagnosed me with contact dermatitis and told me not to wear these earbuds anymore.  Again, I have never experienced this type of problem with any other earbuds that I have owned.  So, it took me several bouts with the resulting contact dermatitis to finally convince me not to wear them again.  It's a shame due to the amount that I paid for these and I thought that they produced great sound.  If you experience contact dermatitis after wearing these Powerbeats Pro earbuds, you will probably develop the same condition again with less wearing time in the future.  It takes about a week to alleviate the symptoms.  The key to recovery is to keep the affected areas of the ears lubricated several times a day with a good moisturizing lotion and NEVER use them again.

Then shortly after, the problems started. If I ever tilted my head down for ANY reason, I lose connection. So don't tie your shoes, pick anything up, or sometimes even turn your head too fast if you want to hear your music or be able to talk with a friend.
Then after placing the earbuds into the charger, for God know whatever reason, sometimes it fails to recognize that it is charging. This happens even if I ensure that all the contacts are clean
I don't know if this is user error or whatever but I swear, sometimes I need to resync them with the app or they won't work.
Now, my biggest issue with them is battery life. I can charge them all night but they die in less than two hours.
All these problems are completely unacceptable from a multibillion dollar company, that is content charging me $200 for a piece of junk.

let me first start off by saying I own AirPods 2 and AirPods Pro .Reading reviews I don't think people understand this product before they purchase it.

The bass is their but if you owned older beats product the bass in these is not as upfront as the older models even ones that acme out 2 years ago. Putting then in your ear and putting them in the case takes some practice. Battery life is good the beats get around 5 hour without noise cancellation on and 4 with it on. I usually charge the case before work and use the beats through my 8hr shift, if one battery goes low switch to the other ear and then im back n business. I usually get about two maybe three days of use before I have to charge the case. Theres no equalizer so you can't tweak anything so if that's important look elsewhere.

title: Surprisingly great earbuds!
text:
This is the most important review for the Tozo A1's you'll ever read:
These are probably thee best earbuds I've ever heard at this price point!
I have incredibly nice and expensive, name brand, over the ear headphones- and I use them all the time for a multitude of projects, both work and fun. However I've needed some cheap earbuds for doing ranch work, since my over the ear headphones are like wearing earmuffs, sweaty!

I saw some reviews and decided to pick up these A1's, and I have to say, I'm impressed. These are not the best thing you've ever heard before in your life. BUT- these are $20 earbuds that sound like $90+ earbuds. My wife has a pair of Samsung galaxy buds+ and I would say that these A1's are 70% the sound quality. That's a big deal considering these are only $20. Stop scrolling, you don't need anymore reviews, buy them, depending on where you live they're $20 after tax. Buy them, the sound is great, my brain is no longer over heating from the sweaty earmuffs, the call quality is good enough. And these feel like they have noise canceling. If you get the right tips on them and if they're in your ear the right way, they sound fantastic. Let's face it, nothing sounds better than looking at your kids 3 ft away as they're trying to talk to you and you can't hear them because your Tozo A1's are in your ears just right and the sultry sounds of the band 'Lettuce' is blocking out their 'DaAaAaD, I'm hungry. Or Daaad! There's a fire!' It doesn't matter- you're jamming out in peace. Not to mention this peace only set you back $20. Go get you some.

title: Great earphones... no regrets!
text: Having a very well tuned ear that picks up lots of instruments and vocals that others don't hear, I had high hopes for these earphones and they don't disappoint.  Little history... I had been watching and wanting a pair of Powerbeats Pro Wireless Earphones for quite a while.  Finally found them at a price point I appreciated, pulled the trigger and bought them.  They arrived in great condition.  The navy blue is a great color.  Set them to charge and when that was done put them to the test listening to classical, rock, jazz, and several other genres.  The sound was clear crisp, had bass, volume was fantastic.  I worked out with them, they never lost connection with my phone, a Motorola.  The battery life is great lasting all day and then some.  Longer than what they are rated.  It may have to do with the way that they have been charged.  If you are looking for a great set of earphones, look no further.  They hold onto your ear, are very comfortable (they don't fatigue my ear like others).  When you remove them it feels like you hadn't had anything on unlike a tight pair of shoes or tight belt.  The controls on the earphone are simple, rocker switch for volume, press once for pause or to answer the phone, press twice to go to the next song, and three times to replay the song.  Listening to audio books is super simple and clear.  The stereo sound is amazing.  Any hesitation because not enough bass, no way.  They have to be seated right in your ear to get the quality of sound that is without a doubt great.  If you have any question about getting these, don't hesitate.  Oh, one last thing... when you use them for phone calls, crystal clear!

title: Really wanted to like these for running
text:
I have owned Powerbeats Pro since it was first produced. It has all of the features I had been waiting for in a music solution for my outdoor running. The sound is excellent, but unfortunately there are several design problems that prospective buyers should be aware of.
1. The well-documented battery contact problem is real. There is no guarantee that storing the device in the case will charge the battery or for that matter, turn the units off from being connected and active with your phone. Regularly the buds are without power right when you want to use them and your choice is to try to get these to quick charge or go about your run without them. My sending these back to the manufacturer resulted in them reporting that there was nothing wrong with the unit so apparently this known problem has been acknowledged with no solution.
2. In cold weather the temperamental buttons stop working all together. Even in warm weather the buttons can be infuriating but when the units get below 30 degrees F the buttons stop working all together.

These problems make this a bad choice for runners looking for a no-hassle solution.

text: I got these because I’m a runner and wanted securely fitted earbuds. While these are quite secure, the sound quality was disappointing. The mids are muddy, the bass bumps (which some people may like), the highs are shrill (when I was running, I couldn’t have my volume that high because the top end hurt my ears— it sounded sharp— not like tuning sharp/ flat— more-so sharp in the painful way). I listened to rock, pop, classical, piano, and live music on these— pop is by far the best genre, but still lacks overall balance. The sound was not crisp in any genre I listened to. These are my second purchase of Beats (I bought a wired earbud set in the past), and I will not be purchasing from this brand again.

title: Way over rated, I don't get it
text:
What am I missing because these things are so overrated, they would be great at $49.

I've been wearing cheap Senso bluetooth earphones for years and the only complaint I have is they have a wire between them that gets in the way sometime, but for less than $50 they're awesome!

I need the wrap around ear type because I do a lot of jumping, burpees, box jumps, SkiErg, etc and I strain while I workout which distorts my ear during a workout so wrap around earbuds is a must. I was excited when I saw the Powerbeats Pro was $100 off so I bought two pair. I thought I'd get at least as good sound quality and announcement features as my cheap Senso's but that's not the case and I'll probably be returning both pairs if I don't figure this out by the end of the weekend.

Here are the issues I can't seem to find answers to;

1: While listening to Apple Podcasts or Spotify music it sounds great but when the podcast/music is interrupted with a call announcement I can't hear Siri because it's so low compared to the music volume so I have no idea who is calling. This feature is critical for me because I will only answer important calls during a workout. Why is Siri volume so low compared to music volume? My inexpensive Senso ActiveBuds S-250 earbuds announce clearly and if I ignore the call the music automatically continues.

With the Powerbeats, when I ignore a call the music doesn't automatically continue, I have to tap the earbuds again, that really sucks if you're in the middle of a workout where you can't tap your ears, you end up working out without music.

2. Every time I turn them on or pause them or do anything, the volume lowers a few notches. This sucks because these earbuds aren't very loud to begin with, nowhere near as loud as my Senso earbuds.

3. On a few occasions I couldn't tap to restart music and had to play via my iPhone because the screen was locked out, again something I never have to do with my Senso.

If someone has answers to these issues I'll gladly keep them and delete this, but finding answers or support is a pain in the ass so far, another issue I'm not happy with, solutions should be readily available.

The Pros pair super quickly and reliably to devices; The Studio Buds have a lot of hiccups any time I try to use them with a previously paired device. The battery life of the case is a lot lower than the Pros. Then this gets to the worst design feature: USB C instead of lightening charging. Probably done to accommodate both Apple and non Apple users but it’s sort of painful.

Overall, earbuds were designed perfect, but the charging/pairing case is not very good. 3/5 stars.

title: Best balance of audio quality and convenience features in the True Wireless category
text:
The best sounding headphones in Apple’s (and Beat’s) entire product lineup, handsdown. Effortless pairing, comfortable, and decent sound isolation, especially when compared to Apple AirPods.

These things rarely ever need to be charged, seriously, they absolutely sip power and last all day without the charging case. The ability to have all day music without charging is good because the case is pretty bulky, one of the few marks against these buds.

I generally don’t like this trend in modern head phones of a bass forward EQ, and prefer a flatter EQ. But these things sound really good, full rich bass without being fatiguing, and clear mid range and high end. Classical music sounds great on these, which I wasn’t expecting.

If you have the extra cash I think these are worth the premium over AirPods. Better sound, better battery, better seal, water resistant and all the new tech of the AirPods (H1 Chip, Bluetooth 5.0).

title: These are for the audiophile wanting wireless earbuds that stay in comfortably.
text:
I'm an audiophile. I finally found what I've been searching for...wireless earbuds that deliver a good sound, stay in and don't get in the way whenever I move or put on a jacket. A friend suggested these Powerbeats Pro Wireless earbuds after my exhaustive efforts searching for good, affordable sound. I've had four or five other earbuds in the last couple years but if I include all the wired headphones and the over ear earphones I've had in the past two decades it is probably close to 20 headphones...always looking for good sound quality and almost always falling short. I found two out of all my purchases that actually sounded good, but they were wired and eventually they wore out and I couldn't find an affordable replacement. I'm not usually the one to review something right away but I felt this deserved it. I’ll update this if any changes merit.
Tips: if you don't want to seal out the outside world you can rotate them forward and kind of break the seal on your ear--which lets you hear past them AND THEY STILL STAY ON GREAT!
Pros:
-Sound quality: I'm in my 50's, so I acknowledge that my hearing is probably not as crisp as it used to be. But that said, I'd rate these at 9.5 for sound quality. I'm able to get a buzz listening to my favorite songs. Goose bumps, euphoria, uncontrollable smile...call it what you want. The music from these earbuds are fulfilling. I wish I had an app with equalizer adjustment, but I'll discuss that below.
-Fit: First thing I did was to put them on straight out of the box and shake my head like a Polaroid picture. To my surprise and delight they stayed on. My glasses have a silicone around-the-ear grip or they would have come off. These earbuds even stay on when they're on loosely. Even trying the different ear tips I was pleasantly surprised to find that the tips it came with fit best. That is rare for me.
-Button controls: Easy to understand and easy to use. I like that they actually have a ‘click’. The volume button is easy to use.
-Automatic Ear Detection: It can be turned off but I really like that if I take it off it will pause what is playing. Then it resumes when I put it back in, like magic.
-Ear hooks: I can’t believe I lived this long without a comfortable ear hook like this. I’ve tried a few ear wings and a couple of others with awkward ear hooks but these are comfortable and work very well. Easy on and easy off with only two fingers. I’ve read that they are adjustable however I don’t know if that is really true. They are flexible and they seem to naturally fit well, and around my glasses, with or without a hat or a hood.
Neutral:
-Cost: I think these are more expensive than they really need to be, but I'm sure there are many out there now that would like to lecture me about quality and how it doesn't come cheap. I feel it is a good investment but if I didn't have a good friend repeatedly recommend them so highly I would typically not have been willing to spend so much for ear candy.
-Battery: I've only drained them a couple times and have never timed to see how long it takes to drain them completely, so I don't know if I can give you an accurate assessment, but they are more than adequate for me. If they need a quick charge mid-day I find that acceptable. I’m a couple hours in right now with music cranked and they are still at 85%.
-Noise cancelling: I thought I read somewhere that they had ANC, but they do not. The fact that the ear hooks keep them against your ear orifice will cause outside noises to be greatly reduced, to the point that I can't hear things outside my earbuds when I have them on listening to music, unless I loosen them by twisting them forward. I like that they seal out the world without using extra battery power to cancel out the noise. I can still hear people speaking or noises when I wear them if I rotate them to the front to break the seal a little bit.
Size: The case is a little clunky but it also holds the ear hooks and a 700 MAH battery...so I think that is to be expected. The earbuds are not cumbersome and don't stick out as much as many others to. Also, when wearing a knit hat they don't push hard into my ear like others.
-Siri: Siri is a nice feature to have but it seems to adjust it up a lot with the command to turn it up and down a lot with the command to turn down. It IS possible though to tell Siri to put the volume at any level: “Hey Siri, adjust the volume to 72%” for example. I'm new to Siri but I think this will really grow on me.
Cons:
-Equalizer or customization: I’m surprised to find that there is none. I hope that they come out with an update to allow us to crank the bass or treble more and adjust it to our personal preferences. Don't get me wrong, it's great sound, however I'd like just a little more treble and a little less bass. Like I said before, it's 95% perfect but I don't mind dreaming of 100% perfection.
-Wireless charging: I’m surprised to find that this does not exist.
-Button controls: Until you get used to the main button they are a little awkward. The manual click is nice but it’s very soft and easy to click more times than you want.
Powerbeats Pro, thank you for the great tunes.

title: Slick But Sound Quality Is Mediocre, And Many Have Trouble Pairing Both Sides
text:
At $199, I really wanted to like these, and they were backed by Apple. Well, my $39 TAOTRONICS ear buds sounded much better. One problem that I had, and that clearly impacted sound quality was the fact that with the ear hooks (a must for me since the ear buds fall out while riding my bike), the Beats just didn't sit firmly in my ears. If I pushed them into my ear canals, the sound was better and the bass was much better, but they would never stay that way, leaving me with mediocre sound with little bass. Maybe it's just the shape of my ears but as I said, the $39 Taotronics were much better SQ. I would have been able to live with that, since I really only use them for riding, but mine (and apparently many others) constantly dropped one side or the other

First, one side wasn't charging and I had to be extra-careful that they were both seated into the case well. They always looked and felt like they were, but I can't say how many times I would put them in my ears and leave for a bike ride only to discover that one side or the other wasn't charged at all. the next problem and really a significant PITA, was that even when both were charged fully, one side or the other (usually the left) would not pair with the iPhone. I would try disconnecting and reconnecting, using "forget this device" and then re-pairing with the iPhone 14 Pro Max to no avail. Google this problem and you will see it happens to a lot of people. Sent them in for service. Same problem. Now Apple is telling me "too bad, by another pair." Good suggestion, Apple. I am going to by a $39 pair and I can afford to throw 5 pairs away before I get to the expense of the Beats. Bottom line, the Beats are all brand and no delivery. The sound quality sucks unless they fit firmly in your ear with the ear hooks, which I don't think is even possible, and the reliability blows.

title: Best Comfort Ever
text:
I can't wear earbuds. I bought a set of Beats ear buds that sound great. But my ears hurt within less than 15 minutes, and they keep falling out. And who wants to carry a device around all the time?

I've beem looking at PowerBeats for quite some time. But they cost a lot for something you can't try out. Yesterday I got an email with a $50 price reduction, so I jumped the gun, so to speak.

I still can't believe it took me only 15 seconds to pair with my Android phone. Then I put them on and brought up some music - Woah Boy! They sound every bit as good as the wired Beats earbuds, but have more volume and bass.

I've been wearing them for 52 minutes, and my ears feel good. I can shake and bob my head, they won't come out. Some reviewers said there are better sounding ones for a good bit more money, but my 72 year old ears wouldn't tell the difference. I can't ever remember listening to music for more than 9 hours at a time. My house is 60 feet long. I lose connection toward the end, through four walls.

I can quickly think of one con, I can't connect to the aircraft movie screen. But my Galaxy Note 9 holds a lot of music and movies.

It's been a long time since I fell in love with a $199 device so quickly. I almost never say this, but I REALLY love my PowerBeats.

title: Only Earbud I'd Ever Buy Again
text:
I bought these primarily for using while running or biking. It's just hard to get out sometimes without the extra motivation of being able to listen to a podcast or something. My only fear was that I've never had an earbud that actually stayed in my ear while living a normal life—much less while running or biking. I saw these earbuds one morning and decided to give them a try.

5 stars overall. They don't come out, and I've gone on 12+ mile runs inn blowing wind, and ridden my bike in wind with them as well. They're exactly what I wanted. They don't bug me or hurt my ears, and a friend of mine who came by and tried them on remarked how much more comfortable they were than his airpods pro.

I didn't know noise cancellation was a thing on these. There really isn't any ANC to speak of, but it's fairly difficult to hear any ambient noise, even heavy traffic, when I have both in. I usually only bike with one in because of this.

Battery life is pretty good. I've never had a problem on an almost 2-hour run with them. They work perfectly well to suit my needs.

I'd buy them again in a heartbeat. Only pair of earbuds or headphones I can say that about.

title: Good not great (for any bouncy activities).
text:
I’ve been on a constant search for active headphones for all the misc activities I do - rock climbing, weight lifting, boxing.

Utility: 3/5
These do not hold in place for very bouncy activities. For me when I jump rope, and box, these headphones tend to easily come loose and fly off. I do not recommend them for that. For climbing and lifting and other activities where you’re moving slowly, they hold in place just fine.

Comfort: 3.5/5
The loop around the ears and mostly hold in place. The tips that go into your ears are hard, and not very comfortable compared to other silicone based ear tips (Bose active sport are very comfortable).

Aesthetic: 4.5/5
These look beautiful. Nice materials, minimal, and look great on me.

Battery: 4.5/5
Holds a very long charge and when dead it only takes 5 min to get over an hour of charge. I will say, the case is kind of annoying. I’ve had it for 3 months now, and I can never sit the headphones perfectly in them on the first try. It’s not very intuitive how they sit in the case. My only gripe on this aspect, otherwise I would’ve gave this a 5 in Thai category.

Sound: 3/5
These sound a little flat for my taste. I like things clear, but with a lot of bass (for workout music). This is more my expectations of it, so if you enjoy a flat/clear sound profile, this is perfect for you.

title: I don't write product reviews, but these earbuds are GREAT!
text: I've owned literally dozens of earbuds over the years, including Tozo T10s that I use in the shower (to not disturb my sleeping partner). But the T10s, while waterproof, are uncomfortable in my ears and fall out pretty easily. So when the Toza A1s were described as low-profile and better fitting, I decided to try them. Wow! These things fit perfectly along the BACK of the ear, whereas other earbuds try to just push deep inside and hang on. But the A1s just stay in, you don't have to repeatedly adjust their position, you can run or shake your head or do anything -- and they stay comfortably in place. Very, very nice. The sound is great, the comfort is superb, and they don't fall out. What could be better in an earbud? And they don't protrude much from the ear, like the (oh, I won't mention the competition, you know how ridiculous those long things can look hanging down from your ears). Now if Tozo could only make them as waterproof as the T10s, I'd have only one set of earbuds and be all the happier for it. So if you're not listening in the shower or dunking your head in the tub, the A1s are the best you can get.

title: Headphones don't work with Macbook Pro - Apple refuses to replace them!
text: I bought these Powerbeats Pro headphones in November of 2021 as a Black Friday sale. They worked great for a month or two, but then started to have intermittent issues with sound quality while using them on my Windows PC or my Macbook Pro. I contacted Apple support and they had me remove them from the bluetooth settings and pair them from scratch again. They told me to try them for another week but the issue persisted. I called again and they sent me a box to FedEx them back. Apple Support just sent the same headphones back to me the next week. The issue does not occur when connected to an iPhone but on any computer they are unusable. Apple keeps saying they can't reproduce the issue and won't take my word for it so they said there is no way for them to replace them. I called Apple again and spoke to a support manager, who assured me that she would do a "forced replacement." This was last week and today I got THE SAME EXACT HEADPHONES sent back to. Except this time they were covered in dust! Now today on the phone with a manager they said they were sorry but that they could not replace them. This is so frustrating since I have gone back and forth with Apple support since March and they assured me they would do a "forced replacement." I guess Apple just does not have the same support that made them the company they are, and does not stand behind their products anymore. I expected more from a pair of $199 headphones and I expected more from Apple. Amazon customer support offered to give a full refund for the headphones and I will go and buy a different non-Apple headphones now. It is a shame because I really liked the headphones but they are too expensive for such horrible customer service and support. Apple just lost a long time customer for life! After this horrible experience I won't be buying the next iPhone or another Macbook Pro in the future. Apple products are garbage now and their customer service is worse than many much smaller companies.

title: Good inexpensive earbuds
text:
I had purchased a set of TOZO T10 a couple of weeks before buying these. I liked them so well that, when the A1s because available for nearly half the price, I decided to buy a set of them. It's always nice to have a backup and, while I'm currently using the earbuds for working out, I plan to use one set while mowing my lawn and it will be nice to not remember to put them back in my gym bag.

As far as quality is concerned, the sound from these seem just as good as the T10s (which I described as very good in my review of them). They are labeled as 'mini' but they really don't seem much smaller than the T10s. The charging case is significantly smaller, about an inch shorter than the T10s which might make a difference if you are carrying the case in your pocket. One of the biggest differences between the A1s and T10s is that the case on the A1s have very strong magnets that hold the earbuds in. Since the surface of the earbuds are very smooth, it can actually be quite difficult to take them out of the case. This was pointed out in other reviews for this product. My solution was to add a thin (~1mm) strip of a thick tape (like duct tape) to the earbud to make it easier to grip (see arrow in attached image). With this minor modification, the annoyance of it being difficult to remove the earbuds from the case becomes a non issue.

Overall, I find these earbuds an excellent buy.

title: Poor Noise Isolation
text:
I really wanted to love these headphones, They're comfortable, fit securely and totally stylish.

Unfortunately, while they sound great, they don't sit inside the ear canal properly and fail to seal out any outside noise. If you're sitting in a quiet office, or in a library, that's great, but if you're walking down a city street, the only way to actually hear anything is to blast the volume really high and trashing your hearing. Even then, it's really easily overwhelmed by passing traffic or an open shop door with music inside. Don't even think of trying to hear anything if you're on public transit. None of the provided ear-tips make any different and I even got some aftermarket squishy foam one's too.

On the plus side, when you are in a place where you can hear them, they sound fantastic. They sit over your ears securely and won't fall off no matter what you do, and again, are pretty darn stylish. I only wish that Apple would have invested more time on the in-ear fitting and would add in some of the active noise cancelling they have in their over the ear cans. I'd happily pay a bit more and give up a bit of battery life for those features.

text:
I have used the Powerbeat Pros since September of 2019. I wore them 4 to 5 times a week for approximately one hour each use. I continued this use until the end of February of 2020. Early on, I noticed that my ears (in ear canal and around the back of the ear) were itchy. I never associated it with the use of the Powerbeats, as it was Winter and I attributed it to dry skin. That said, with continued use, my ears began to get worse. My ears began to leak clear fluid around the clock. The back of my ears became raw and would drip clear liquid. The issue became so bad that I had to go to the doctor to get it checked out. The first time, I was put on a steroid cream and eardrops. After 10 days of use, the medications did nothing. I returned to the doctor and was placed on an antibiotic. That too had no benefit. At the end of February, I went on a two week business trip and did not use the Powerbeat Pros. My rash and associated issues all cleared up...…. Still I never put it together. When I returned home, I began using the Powerbeat Pros again. The rash quickly returned. I went online and looked up if anyone else had the same issues. I found out that this is something that happens to people who use the Powerbeat Pros. I saw posted photos and they matched my symptoms. I have stopped using them at this point.
I have been a long time user of Apple/Beats products and never had issues. I cant believe that a $250 item uses cheap and essentially poisonous rubbers. I am disappointed that it took so long to associate the medical issues with the Powerbeat Pros, as I can no longer return them. APPLE needs to recall these and fix the issues.
The sound is good.

- They remain on when I don't expect them to, and steal the bluetooth connection from my car, forcing me to dangerously reconnect my phone to my car to take phone calls
- Upon reconnecting, one headphone playing sound but not the other
- Frequently don't click into the charger securely, thus failing to charge by the morning
- 0 means of diagnosing connectivity problems via an app or UI

They look great, and when they work they work well, but they're just not dependable. If I had to choose again I would not buy these.

------

Edit for iPhone experience, which I'm happy to report is much, much better. Deep Siri integration makes voice-based commands a breeze, and generally speaking the bluetooth connectivity seems a lot better.

Also, my iPhone tells me exactly how charged the headphones are which is something you don't get with Android phones.

Highly recommend for iPhone users.

title: Unfinished, buggy product
text:
The good:

These look great, feel sturdy, and are much more comfortable to me than my older Powerbeats 3s. The sound quality is ok, and they were easy to setup with my iPhone.

The bad:

These feel like an incomplete product, I’m constantly running into issues and bugs, many of which other users are also reporting. When they work they’re great, but constant issues, even after multiple repairs and firmware updates, makes for an awful experience. I’m not a novice with BT and wireless tech, in fact I work around it on a daily basis as an iOS developer, and all the issues I’m running into points to a product that is rushed and unfinished.

The first pair I received would drain incredibly fast, even when they were not being used. After two trips to the Apple Store and a 2 week wait for repair later, I got them back, only to find that they would fail to reconnect after being idle for a few hours. I was then instructed by support to perform a firmware update, which seemed to fix the connection issue, but also caused the battery drain issue to return for the right earbud. Now Apple support is asking me to return them for yet another repair, which will be another 2 week wait.

At this point, I will have been without use of these earbuds for 1 out of the 4 months since I’ve bought them, that is ridiculous. This is very atypical for Apple, but given how the original release date was delayed, and how after many months issues still persist, I’m not confident they’ll ever be resolved.

Since I’m outside of Amazon’s return window, I’m stuck with these. I can’t recommend these given all the issues, especially with so many other competing products out there, guess I’ll just have the write the $250 price tag off as a loss.

Sound is ok/good. I have no problem hearing the bass and the highs are ok but for the music I listen too they are not bad and are better than most cheapo earbuds out there (there are some much cheaper ones that do have better sound).

Noise cancellation is mediocre at best. It’s there and you can tell it’s supposed to do something but if I’m in a crowded place this does nothing compared to it’s competitors.

My real gripe though is the battery life. I have had cheapo brands that cost half the price outperform the batteries on these on their worst days. I have used AirPods Pro’s, Powerbeats, and any number of cheaper stuff 80$ and under. All of them do better than these. Unless I leave the case plugged in at all times it maybe holds a recharge per one headphone and then is gone again. The hands down WORST battery life.

For bein on sale they still really aren’t worth the price. I might pay 60$ but even then there’s plenty out there that would do better than these. If these are something you are considering I would highly recommend to keep looking because these will be fun at first but be irritating and disappointing after the 2nd week.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

Fit: Walking around with these is a pain (I can't imagine how these would be if someone took them to the gym). They are constantly falling out, irrespective of the tip or combination of tips being used (Beats provides 3 pairs).

title: Better than PowerBeats3?
text:
Before buying these, I had used the Powerbeats3 for several years and really liked them. The only thing that bothered me about them was the small wire connecting the two buds. It would always get stuck on my shirt and tug the buds out of my ears. Other than that, they were great.
But recently, that wire started to get more annoying and I decided it was time to try fully wireless earbuds (which was a big leap because I really did like the Powerbeats3). This was about a month ago and the Powerbeats pro still hadn’t come out. I really don’t like the look of AirPods, so I got on Amazon and purchased one of their best fully wireless pairs. It had great reviews, was a decent price, and looked solid. However, after using them for a week, I HATED them. The sound quality was awful compared to the powerbeats3 and they just wouldn’t stay in my ears. I returned them so fast and went back to the powerbeats3.
About a week later, I saw and ad for the Powerbeats Pro. I knew I had to give it a shot because it was everything I loved minus the one thing I hated (the wire). I wasn’t sure if they would fit the same or sound the same, and I was hesitant to try it given the price point, but I knew I needed to.
After using for a few weeks, I can honestly say these are the best earphones I’ve ever had - by far. The sound and fit is just as good as PB3. I wasn’t sure if I would like the look of them, but I actually do. I love using them. They’re great in the gym, making calls, at work, etc. highly recommend!

title: Upgraded to 4 start
text:
Update January 2023: Spent an hour online and then on the phone with Apple Support. They said my beats were out of warranty even after I sent them a copy of my receipt showing they were purchased new 6 months ago. A manager actually called me , I reexplained what was going on and she said that Apple was showing the warranty expired less than a month ago so she was going to over ride it and issue an RMA. The return box showed up the next day and I had a new set of ear buds in 4 days. Now let's see how long these last. I'm not an audiophile I just need noise in my ears to distract me while I run, so I don't really care how they sound, I just need them to connect and stay in my ears. I have never had an with them staying in my ears just the charging and connecting.

Update December 2022: Six months in and now only one of two buds is charging. This seems like a common occurrence from all the posts I have seen online.

I have had these for a month and so far they are great. I have small ears and I sweat a lot when I workout. I live in Florida, run, cycle and workout outdoors almost daily, even with the heat and humidity I have not had any issues with these headphones coming loose or falling out. I have taken them into the surf without issue as well. I am not an audiophile so as long as I'm hearing music I am satisfied. I previously had a pair of Jaybird Vista ear buds and I had nothing but problems with them staying in my ears, filling with sweat and losing audio and disconnecting from my Garmin 945. I have taken a few calls and have not had any complaints from the people on the other end of the call. Battery life works for my needs as I haven't had a workout longer than 2.5 hours yet.

title: You get what you pay for
text:
Bought to replace my TOZO T6s that I lost, wanted to try some of the company's other products cause I did generally like those for the price. My experience with earbuds is a number of brands up to $80 per set over the last 20+ years. I prefer a slight V shaped response for listening to a large variety of music and prioritize clarity and separation. I'm a big fan of balanced armature drivers but will give anything a chance, just as long as it doesn't sound muddy.

Pros:
• Price
• Bluetooth that works

Cons:
• Sound quality - 6mm driver sounds small and muddy, other cheap TOZO models offer up to 10mm, bigger is definitely better
• Volume - does not go as high as competitors, not enough in loud environments without degrading sound even further
• Voice responses - another reviewer put it perfectly when they said this headphone sounds like a robot that's been enslaved. They are horrifically bad and you're stuck with them. This is puzzling because T6 voice is completely fine. Most TOZOs have unique voices and the quality is all over the place
• No wireless charging - almost all other TOZO buds do have this
• Not really that small - yes, smaller than some other TOZOs but I have owned plenty of other smaller buds
• Case is bulky too - significantly thicker than the T6 case, making it less pocket friendly

title: Huge Disappointment
text:
I finally decided to make the switch to wireless headphones and searched aggressively for the best earbuds that would not fall out while running. That was my number one priority. I was hopeful for these after comparing to several other brands.
I ended up purchasing from Target and ended up returning them two days later.

The main thing I was looking for was to actually stay in my ears while running, which has always been an issue for me.
The pros: these earbuds are fantastic at staying in your ears, no matter how hard you run or work out. I loved that!!

But that was it for the pros. These advertise as having great sound quality. I greatly disagree. I use an iPhone 11 and the volume has to be all the way on max to hear it at a good level. And even then, I still hear all the road traffic or gym clanging and it’s hard even to distinguish the music. The sound is also very flat. I don’t hear any bass at all. It’s similar to your car battery dying and then turning the stereo on once the battery is replaced. The sound settings reset and everything is just flat. I was seriously disappointed in the sound quality.

I noticed a lot of complaints about charging of the ear pieces themselves. Brand new, out of the box, the right ear piece would not fully charge, held only at 71%, but the left one did reach 100%. It never would go about the 71. This was brand new, unopened. I can only imagine when they become older and used on a daily basis, how they match other folks negative reviews.

I also had great pain in my left ear after about 30 mins of use. The cartilage of my ear felt bruised from wearing for just a short time. When I switched to my old wired headphones, that pressure almost instantly went away. Something about these just increases the pressure on the inner ears.

I really wanted these earbuds to be my use for the future. To top it off, after spending $200 on them, showing a $250 normal price, they went on sale further to $170 the next day.

One pro, which was my ultimate must, however followed by all cons, I had to return my purchase and I will continue my search.

Hope this helps someone in a similar situation.

title: Wanted these to work out so badly, but I'm giving up on Bluetooth
text:
First, I must mention that I am using these with a Samsung S9. I don't know enough about BT technology to know if there is a difference between the way they work with Android and Apple.

I'll start off with the positives:

- Super Super comfortable
- Pairs very easy
- Button controls have a great feel
- Case was very easy to work with and made good contact for charging.
- Battery life is excellent, can use them all week without charging ~ ten hours and they were still going.

Negatives:

- Constantly dropped out in my gym which normally has about 30 - 50 people in it. This would happen approx. 3-5 times per song and dropouts were 1-2 seconds. This is super annoying and it was my ultimate deal breaker.

- Poor sound quality... I understand these are Bluetooth earbuds and the resolution is limited, but I know they can sound better than this because I have listened to other wireless earbuds. Sound is very thin and hollow-like. Mids are recessed to the point that I can barely stand it. I mean, certain instruments and details I couldn't even hear in some of my songs. I thought something was wrong at first and tried different sized buds and all that. I looked deeper into the reviews and saw that many others have complained about the same thing. Maybe an EQ app would fix some of this to get an acceptable sound, but honestly for $200 they should be reasonably balanced out of the box.

I would have probably been able to overlook the poor sound problem because I love the comfort and convenience of these so much. Unfortunately, with the dropouts I am just going to go back to good old wired earbuds until the BT technology advances enough to prevent dropouts in crowded areas.

title: Could be great, but they aren't
text:
The sound is great. No doubt about that. They are a little difficult to get fitted into your ears at first, but the process becomes second nature within a month. Once they are in, they stay in place great. The charging case looks nice and feels sturdy.

Now for the deal breaking issues. They don't connect well. Sometimes they connect as expected. Many times only one of the two will connect. When this happens, the only way to get them to both connect is to take them off and put them back in their charging case and try again. This process may need to be repeated multiple times to get both connected. Could take you 20 plus minutes to get them working. Then there is charging. You'd think that is you put them in the charging case and they magnetically locked in place, they'd charge as expected, but that's not the case. If you do that you have a 50/50 shot at them charging. You need to put them in their case, get them to magnetically lock into place and then check your phone to see if they have the charging symbol. If not you have to wiggle them around until they do. To make things worse, if they aren't seated properly they will drain all of their remaining power more quickly, usually in one night. This charging issue only amplifies the frustration of them not connecting because sometimes only one connects and it's because the other wasn't seated 100% correctly and fully drained it's power while the other was charging.

My suggestion is to get something else until these are fully redesigned.

Three months after purchasing them, one stopped playing any sound. Volume controls still work on it, so I know it's connected but no sound comes out. Hopefully Apple will toss this design in the trash and start from scratch on the redesign.

title: Terrible User Interface
text:
They sound OK and are comfortable for me but the overall usability is terrible.
Once the very simple initial pairing is done, they are supposed to sense when they are in the ear and connect to the phone and play music. When they are returned to the case, they disconnect and start charging. There is no on/off switch or any manual control over the earbuds.
When it works, it's fine but it often doesn't.
If I put them on and one doesn't connect I have to take them completely off, return them to the case and try again.
Frequently, one will not be charging in the case and I've had them be completely dead numerous times when I go to use them. Unless they are placed very carefully in the case they don't touch the charging contacts and when they do they are very susceptible to minor bumps. Impossible to rely on them in a backpack.
When they aren't charging in the case, they connect to the phone. When receiving a call I'll frequently find the headset in the case has taken over the speaker/microphone. It takes a while to figure out what's going on and try to get them to let go of the signal.
I can see now they are $30 less than what I paid but I expected a lot more for this level of expense. I would not buy these again.

My first pair of Powerbeats Pro were defective and stopped working within a few weeks. I exchanged for a new pair, and these are hardly better.

Many times when listening, one or both earbuds disconnect randomly. The headphones also often reconnect without me opening the case, so the battery gets drained even when it's supposed to be charging. The headphones themselves have very unreliable charging. I place them in the case carefully and frequently clean the charging port, but they usually just refuse to charge.

I've still given two stars instead of one because the sound quality and battery life are excellent, and noise cancellation is pretty good, but the inconsistency with charging and connectivity make them almost unusable.

I can't believe such an expensive product from a reputable brand is so unreliable. This is clearly not a finished product, and it shouldn't have passed testing.

title: Great headphones with one issue
text:
For the most part, I love these headphones. They connect easily. They are comfortable to wear for less than 4 hours. After a while, they start to hurt your ears. You can use one earpiece at a time or use both at the same time. The only thing that really irritates me is there is no way to power them off. When I am at work or the gym I use these all the time. When I am in my vehicle I prefer to use my vehicles BlueTooth over the headphones. Because you cannot turn the headphones off my phone is confused when it comes to connecting to my vehicles BlueTooth or the headphones. I can be driving in my vehicle talking on the phone on my vehicles Bluetooth and out of nowhere, I can no longer hear the person through my vehicle speakers. Instead my phone is trying to connect to the headphones. So the whole time while I am driving I have to constantly choose my vehicles BlueTooth or the headphones. Even when I select my vehicles BlueTooth it disconnects and connects to the Beats headphones. I even put the headphones in the case and CLOSE the case and I still have the same issue. Apple made a great pair of headphones but why in the world would they not allow you to turn them off and avoid this issue? When they are in the case and the case is closed they need to turn off or not be able to pair with any devices. I do not know what the hell they were thinking when they came up with that but hopefully, they will solve this issue with the next generation.

I am giving four stars because of the issue with not being able to turn off or in the alternative prevent my phone from connecting them. I do not want to unpair my phone from the headphones just to go through the whole process of pairing them again.

title: Athletic Airpods Pro with a lacking sound signature
text:
When initially receiving the earbuds they were nicely packaged(Apple-like of course). The charging case was a little bit larger than expected but they hold the buds in nicely with magnets and charge the buds quickly in a pinch. I was hopeful these would be end-game workout earbuds.

The box includes 5 different tip sizes so that a good fit is ensured. Battery life is quite good with 9 hours of playtime and 15 hours left in the charging case. Understandably a lightning cable is included as this is essentially an Apple product with Beats marketing, but USB type-c needs to be an Apple standard someday as well.

Pairing was super simple; open Bluetooth settings on your Android and open the case to pair. With an iPhone this process is even more simple with the H1 chip inside.

Now to the part that brings these down to 3 stars...the sound. I was expecting these to sound very similar to AirPods Pro given that this is an Apple product but I was completely wrong. When comparing the Powerbeats Pro to the Airpods Pro, the Powerbeats have a large emphasis on low end with a huge lack of mid range. This leads to them sounding muddy, muffled, and with a narrow sound stage. It's possible to have bass with mid range punch; Apple dropped the ball on this.

In summary if this product were half the price I wouldn't have much to complain about, but even at a discounted price of $175 this is a lackluster product in the market. Sony, Bose, and Jaybird all offer better options at a lower price.

title: Causes Chemical Burns or Allergic Reactions
text:
I bought this product a few months ago and used them to take long walks. I had no issues the first few months I used them. I'd even wear them to work.

Then about a month and a half ago, blistering and itching would occur in and behind my ear where the rubber made contact with my skin. On top of that, my ears would drain horribly – so bad I'd have to lightly plug them with sterile cotton.

I'm not allergic to anything except poison sumac, much less to silicon, latex, or any other kind of rubber material. I clean my earbuds and my ears regularly, so it couldn't have been dirt.

I did some research and found this reaction has happened to a lot of people. Apparently Apple is treating this as if it isn't an issue? The reactions these earbuds caused have landed people in hospitals. The pain and itching was so excruciating that I felt I'd been shot in both sides of my head. Antibiotic treatment did little to nothing. My doctor even said it looked like I had chemical burns in and on my ears and couldn't explain what exactly was wrong.

I wear latex gloves at work, and my phone case is made of silicon. Nothing has ever caused me so much issues before. I don't even have sensitive skin and these gave me blisters. All I can do is warn people that these can cause skin issues in and on the ear.

I've disinfected the headphones because I initially thought it was a bacterial or fungal infection since gyms are gross. This had no effect. My symptoms cleared up after a week of no use but after resuming my gym sessions the issue returned.

Then I found a thread on the Powerbeats Pro sub Reddit where dozens of others are having the same issue. As of now there are over 80 comments and the symptoms we are experiencing are uniform.

Some chemical used in Apple's silicone is causing contact dermatitis. They know about it and they are still selling them. I love these headphones, but apple would rather use known irritants in their manufacturing than produce a safe product.

title: The Best For Me, But Not Transcendent
text:
I work out 5 days a week: 3 days lifting and 2 days cardio. I’ve used cheaper buds and replaced them ~biyearly in the past, but I got these on sale when my last pair of cheap ones started to fade in the fall. The sound quality isn’t much different, but the build quality was much better. The hooks allow for slight adjustability so they don’t break, and the tips sizes cover everything you could want. Battery life is incredible and doesn’t seem to be dropping off. The Airpod-like IOS integration is really nice. The physical button for play/pause/skip works perfectly, and the volume rockers are so much better than gesture based nonsense.

Unfortunately, these “top class” fitness buds do have similar problems to their cheaper cousins. First, the mesh at the eartips fell off while I was cleaning earwax off of the buds. I expected this when I used cheaper products, but a luxury item allegedly built for wear like this shouldn’t be damaged by a little brushing. Additionally, the buds sometimes don’t charge/disconnect while in the case. Thankfully, this problem is somewhat cancelled out by the IOS integration, as I can see when the charging is unbalanced.

If you can get them on sale and use an iPhone, they’re worth it. Otherwise, there are cheaper options that fill the same niche with regular replacement.

title: Awesome quality for the price, and I've bought 3 pairs now. PERFECT FOR SMALL EAR CANALS.
text:
I originally bought these because I needed something cheap and small and was expecting to have to replace them pretty quickly just based on the price, but I seriously love these things.

Compared to my Bose QuietComforts (over-ear):

1) Usability: Bluetooth is DEFINITELY easier to connect to my work computer, Nintendo Switch, phone, and iPad since you don't have to have an app or login on each device to connect and the tap features are simple and minimalistic (which is why I quickly bought my mom a pair to replaced her corded earbuds).

2) Microphone/Noise-Cancellation: My job is half Teams meetings, and the microphone functionality is definitely comparable. The noise-cancellation is even better, though. (I have really good hearing and don't like playing things too loudly, so I can easily carry on basic conversations from across the room with music playing with my Boses, but I literally have to pause whatever's playing when someone is 3' away with these, and even then it's hard to hear until I take them out.

Lastly, the selection of different sized tips is great because I have small ear canals and had never found a pair of buds that I could wear without them falling out every 20 seconds, which honestly may play a big part in how good the noise-cancellation is. I use the smallest tips in the square-ish shape and easily wear them 6-8 hours/day without issue.

title: Dang, I really wanted to love these.
text: Maaaaaaaan!!! I wanted to love these bad boys, because they really are legit. My issue isn’t so much with beats, but how they fit overall and what they say about them being tailored for everyone. This was a breakup I didn’t even want. I naturally have small ears, not baby ears and probably not that noticeable, but trust me... ear buds definitely notice. I received these and immediately put them in, battery life is legit as all hell and both sound quality/noise cancellation are close in their running. I believe the reason they weren’t 100% for me was because of how they fit. (Womp womp) Any who, I’ve been searching for some good earbud for a while... lo and behold, These babies fell into my possession. Here is the part that makes me sad... after wearing them for about 30 minutes my ears became extremely fatigued and they started to ache... I instantly knew that this meant, they were like the rest. Now, before putting them on, they came out of the box with the largest rubber buds... (you have a few to choose from). I instantly though that that could be my issue, and hoping it was not the issue of having small ears. I decided to give them a rest for the rest of the day because my ears were seriously aching. The next day I changed out the rubber buds for the smallest in the pack.... all was going well, 30 minutes later.. ears became fatigued and started aching... since I wore the smaller buds, the sound quality was funky... they plugged my ears with suction... y’all, it was super weird. I again gave them a rest and tried again... I mean I watch my family members put theirs in with ease, meanwhile every time I put mine in, it took me a while to “adjust them”... I then discovered that the band that goes over your ear had such a large gap, and that if you ears aren’t large enough to hold it, they’ll shift. Literally the earbud is almost if not larger than my ear. This clearly has nothing to do with Beats, but more so for those who have been gifted small ear such as myself. I thought maybe it was just me, but after I researched Powerbeats Pro and small ears, it made sense. I added pictures for reference which shows how loose they look at the top where the band is, a gap where the rubber buds sits, how small my ear is compared to the actual earphone lol, the different size rubber earbuds, and overall how they look on me . These are some amazing amazing amazing earphones. I wish it worked out for me, but the ear fatigue is something I wish to live without. On to the next I guess. I hope this was helpful for someone .

text:

Their sound quality is wonderful, when they are able to stay connected.
The overall connection issues with them are atrocious, they don't stay connected or connect properly when you want them to; one of them, usually the left one, fails to function properly. And then they will regularly reconnect automatically when you are not using them, and they are snug in their charging case.
This causes them to kick off other bluetooth devices that are connected, and it also causes them to drain out the battery overnight, even when plugged in and "charging".
There is no way to effectively stop this activity without turning off the bluetooth on the phone.

title: Decent sound for the price
text:
Ordered the Tozo A1, but with my luck, I received a pair with issues.

Pros :
Really liked the design of the earbuds and the presentation of the package & contents.
Good response right out of the box and over half battery, paired right up.
Fit well in my ear with no comfortability issues. (big thumbs up)
Bluetooth range was impressive, was able to walk away from my phone up to 25 feet without any signal issues.
Sound from call test and music play was clear, crisp, and solid.
Noise cancellation was good.
First use stress test - Battery lasted over a full 5 hours with constant use during my work day, but cons may have contributed to that.

Cons :
First use I noticed that the left side had great range and volume control, but a slight delay in signal. Attempted to re-pair with the other earbud, but no change.
Right side had some concerns though.....
- Up to half volume, it sounded great, good response during calls, caller said the mic sounded good too. However, anything above 50% and the volume didn't change or increase at all, and the earbud audio began clipping out like I was out of range or something.

Overall, it appeared to be a really good set of earbuds... if they worked as intended.
I gave the 3 stars as a middle ground to potential sound & call quality (very good), I think I just got a defective pair (volume & power handling).
I hope they are good for everyone else, I just wish mine worked enough to enjoy. I didn't order a replacement, as my wife has a set that impressed her so much, that I am going to try that brand instead.

text:
The main reason I submit this review is the charging issue. To charge, you place the earbuds into the case, making sure they are correctly seated on the charging terminals. The process is aided by magnets that are supposed to pull them into the correct position. That is the critical part. More than once, I have put them in the case to charge overnight, only to find out in the morning that one of them got 100% charged but the other one is only 40% charged! That one must not have gotten seated properly when I put them in the case the previous night. But I find it is possible to get them both 100% charged if I place them properly. It's just a little tricky.

Otherwise I love them. They are not going to fall out of your ear because they hook around it securely (therefore they are not going to be unnoticeable when you wear them, if that matters to you). The sound quality is great. They sinc up immediately with whatever you have paired them with. I use them with an iPhone SE 2020, a 5 year old Samsung smart TV, and a 6 year old Lenovo laptop. On the laptop I use them with voice recognition software and a language-learning program that listens to you talk. These two things plus the telephone calls indicate that the microphone and noise cancellation work fine.

Just be careful about that charging issue.

I stopped using them because they would sometimes have connection issues with the case after several months of use. I thought buying some nicer ones would do the trick and they would be replaced under warranty. I was wrong.

My right bud stopped charging 3 months after purchase. I had to send them to the apple store where they offered apple care which I have to pay for that service and then pay again everytime the phones malfunction. Or pay 100 to replace one bud if it is broken or malfunctions.

Do yourselves a favor, just buy the cheaper over ear headphones on the market. The sound quality is the same, they are easier to pair (you have to download an app for the beats and have the phones physically in the case everytime you want to pair them) and If they crap out on you, you can just buy a brand new set for 30 bucks on Amazon.

More expensive does not mean better quality and durability. I Learned my lesson the hard way.... recommend occiam or Tozo available on Amazon for 30-40 bucks.

text:

It’s annoying and wastes my time when I just want to get going.

I've had these a week, added to my collection of over 30 different headphones. I needed something for the Gym that met the criteria of easy to use, great sound, great sound rejection and comfortable.

Pros:

- Very good sound, not mind blowing. I didn't get a 'wow!' experience, but they do sound great on all types of music.
- Very comfortable. The default in ear pads were a little rough, switched to the multi tiered of similar size and they fit perfectly.
- Very light
- Very long battery life

Cons

- The charging case is bulky, it's nicely designed but it's not what I'd call pocket friendly. A bit taller than the height of a bar of Irish Spring,
- Due to the size of the charging case, I leave it in the car when I head into the gym. However something occasionally goes wrong - the right headphone seems to lose sync with the left and the only way I've found to resync it is to drop it in the charging case. Which means I have to head back out to the car or drag the case around with me. Didn't have to disconnect/reconnect, it just started working after that. Note, it was fully charged so not a battery life issue. Wish it had a resync option that worked without the case.

Summary - These are the absolute best sports earbuds you can buy. Gym compatible, sweat and water resistant, comfortable, easy to run with and mostly hassle free.

title: An honest review
text:
Update on my initial review:
Tozo customer manager reached out to me personally and apologized for the inconvenience. Stellar customer service. She offered a new 3 different earbuds to choose from for free. I chose the Tozo T6 the earbuds are amazingly awesome! T6 have noise cancelation, they are loud even at a mid volume on my phone. They hear super clear, the bass is real deep. My daughter has airpods pods pro2 that I paid $250 for. I did a side by side comparison and the Tozo T6 were louder! I would suggest the T6 you will not regret it!

I bought these Tozo ear buds. I was using them in mid volume, the battery went from 100 to 90 in 10 minutes. Then 20 minutes later the battery went down to 70 percent. I left them on for 30 more
minutes and the battery went down to 40 percent. I thought I had a faulty earbuds so I exchanged them. The 2nd pair same thing. I reached out to Tozo and the person from Tozo told me that battery life is 2-3 hours which is not correct based upon my experience. I explained that the specs say 6 hours she said that's based on tech lab result which didn't make any sense. I returned them and got my refund. The sound quality is good and they are loud with noise cancelation but that's about it. I purchased JLab ear buds what a difference. Jlab is good quality for a reasonable price. There are way better earbuds in the market. Do not purchase these you will end up returning them.

title: Compact with surprisingly good sound
text:
They are light and very comfortable. The inserts fitted to them out of the box are the largest size, and I initially thought I would need something bigger. They are a really good fit though.

As far as sound quality, I saw some reviews that killed them. I will say that the max-volume is lower than expected and thought "that's it?" (even though it was, for me, plenty loud) when I topped it out.

I will say, however, that they make the most of the digital processing that my phone is capable of compared to other headphones I have - including my mixing monitors. The compression and 3D effect is more rich with these (so maybe that is what most reviewers who give such high marks have going when they judge the quality?). They're mediocre without any effects set, but they are quite good with all of that turned on. Combine that with the convenience and comfort, and it makes them a win.

title: Great sound. . .when it works
text:
I bought some Powerbeats pro headphones to work out with at the gym as they looked like they'd stay put no matter how active I was. All was good for about three months, until one earbud or the other suddenly just wouldn't connect. This was odd. I checked that they were both seated in the case, but nope, one earbud (usually the right one) wouldn't connect.

So I developed a routine which would sometimes fix it. Connect and re-connect, unpair and re-pair, reboot the phone (a Galaxy S21). The problem got steadily worse, so I took it to the Apple store and they said they'd repair it. I got the earphones back a week later and the problem wasn't fixed. I mailed it into Apple after talking with their tech support people, and they returned them to me saying there was nothing wrong.

I saw Apple put out a firmware release and I was excited as I figured they're finally figured out the problem and had a fix. So got that installed. . .and nothing. Still usually only the left earbud is recognized.

It's incredibly frustrating. The sound is great, but 80% of the time the right earbud isn't recognized. I have three other types of wireless earbuds, all of which pair quickly and firmly as soon as they're out of the case.

So when I go to them gym now I bring my Powerbeats, in case they're in the mood to be recognized by my phone, and a backup pair of earbuds (Plantronics or the new Monster Fit ones) which always work.

Really crummy that Apple can't fix this. Not recommended.

title: Needs a Software or Firmware Update due to a Connectivity Issue
text:
The Powerbeats Pro are an exceptional product, but they have a connectivity issue that needs to be addressed urgently.

Pros: have great sound, fit my ear perfectly, snug fit and have never fallen out of my ear, and my sunglasses go right over the top of them comfortably.

Cons: Biggest issue is the connectivity. I have automatic ear detection set to off and have taken the automatic microphone selection from automatic to left ear. I set these setting this way because I was experiencing my right earphone constantly disconnecting. This helped the issue a lot but did not solve it completely. Even with these two setting disabled I will still have an earphone (right or left) disconnect from bluetooth while listening or not connect at all. It has never happened to both earphones at the same time but there is no rime or reason as to which earphone will not connect or disconnect. It happens to both of them. Another big disadvantage is that the case is fairly large and unfortunately I have to carry it with me while I wear them because you need the case to correct this issue. When an earphone disconnects, I have to take both earphones out of my ear, put them back in the case, close the lid for 10 seconds, open the case back up, put them back in my ear, and this USUALLY corrects the issue on the first try. However, I have had to repeat this procedure several times before it works. This can happen several times within the scope of an hour workout. Sometimes it doesn't happen at all. Like I said there is no rime or reason as to when this happens. Having this connectivity issue happen and carrying the large case with you is a big disadvantage. For the money these cost, this is really kind of a big deal. I think a software or firmware update is in order and is way overdue. I am hoping one comes out soon to correct this issue. If they could correct this issue, I would definitely give these earphones 5 stars.

Second Con: not that big of deal really. They stick out of your ear a bit more than most other earphones and I ride a bike on a daily basis and due to this the wind noise is a little distracting. Because of the speed you are going on a bike, the wind wraps around these earphones in such a way that if causes moderate wind noise. More so than I have experienced with other earphones. Again, not a huge deal for me, but it might be for some. If you are at a running speed or slower this would not be an issue.

title: Apple AirPod Pros Slipping Out? THIS is it.
text:
I’m writing this review for the people who were looking for this review. I like my Apple AirPod Pros, but I couldn’t stand the fact that it always slipped out of one ear constantly. Drove me absolutely nuts.

These Beats Studio Earbuds are what you’re looking for. Just like the AirPod Pros, they have three different sizes and the mediums seem to fit me perfectly from the beginning. There is absolutely NO slip whatsoever and the way the earbud is designed it kind of fits snug in the little (I don’t know the damn ear term) area around the ear canal so it it’s more than just your ear canal holding it in. It’s like your whole ear is holding it in place. I’m absolutely happy that I can walk around with it looking stylish with this red color. Looks great.

Now for everything else (I’ll be brief):

Music Quality - Vs the AirPod Pros, there’s really only a SMIDGEN of a difference and the beats have like… a 5% increase in bass. It’s incredibly small but it’s noticeable if you go back and forth like I did for ten minutes testing it. Sound quality is great though. Nice and clear.

Comfort - Does not move in my ear. Thank god. All good here

Active Noise Cancellation - I think the AirPod Pros has some slightly better ANC/Transparency modes. It’s not a huge gap but it’s more noticeable than that bass increase I was talking about previously. The AirPod Pros noise cancellation cancels maybe 20% more background noise and the transparency let’s you hear like 10% more than the Beats (I’m using percentages to give you guys a better feel of the gap).

Battery Life - I mean they last a LONG ass time and charge mad fast so it shouldn’t be a problem.

Look/Feel - Case and earbuds feel solidly made. I love the magnets when you put the air buds into the case it kind of gives me confirmation that it’s the right slot and that it’s in place correctly.

Voice — Tested this too, my voice sounds like slightly deeper on the phone. That’s it.

5 stars for sure, again the only thing the AirPods have over this one is that their ANC/Transparency is better.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: Not even worth the $20; Great customer service. See Update
text:
TLDR; If you want to have issues every time you try to use these, then buy these headphones, otherwise, spend a little more money for something better.

Okay, I just had to leave this review. This product is too much trouble even for the $20 price tag, I got it yesterday and I have been having all sorts of weird issues since.

Firstly, opened up the package, took out the buds, and connected it to my phone, the left side refused to play. The manual said to turn it off and back, I did that, it started playing, a little weird but not a deal breaker.

So now I start to listen to music on my computer, although it said 6 hours playtime, the battery dies in 2 hours of listening going from 77% but I still don't pay it any mind because of how cheap the product is.

Now fully charged, I connect it to the computer again, I start listening to music again, but this time, the audio keeps going in and out on each side(even though I'm sitting right in front of the computer). I turn it off and back on about 3 times, still the same issue. I then connect it to my phone, the audio plays without cutting out, I then reconnect it to the computer and surprise surprise, the audio now plays without cutting in and out.

Now I lay on my bed listening to music before sleep, everything goes well, I put the buds back in the case and go to sleep. I wake up this morning to continue where I left off, but all the audio from the computer keeps playing at a super low tone. I play the audio through my wired headphones, and sure enough, it sounds fine.

The one redeeming quality is that, when it actually works the way it's supposed to, the sound quality really isn't that bad, but as far as I'm concerned, just because a headset is $20, that doesn't mean that every single time I go to use it, that I have to jump through a bunch of hoops just to get it to work properly. Would NOT recommend these.

Update 14/March/2023
I had a rep reach out to me after posting my initial review, they have sent me a brand new pair of earbuds free of charge, and the new set is a more advanced and expensive set(Toze NC2). So far it the new set is working perfectly on both my computer and phone, it also has a killer noise cancellation.

I have decided to upgrade the review to a 5 star because although the first earbuds was not up to my standard, the customer service was great and I ended up with an even better pair of earbuds free of charge.
