title: Solid Choice of Earbuds for Daily Use
text:
Really happy with these compared to my AirPods. I have initial release AirPods and the batteries are quite worn out so I was looking for a solid replacement. After scouring multiple online shops for them, I finally secured a pair from Walmart. The sound quality compared to AirPods is undeniably better, with actual bass thump. Being a bass lover, these are quite great while not being as aggressive as other Beats models. Definitely wish the price point was a bit lower, maybe around $200, but then that cuts into the Powerbeats3 and AirPods 2, which Apple without doubt is trying to sell without competing with itself at price points.

Just some things that I noticed to keep in mind:

1. WIND NOISE! I haven't seen anyone else mention it but when walking outdoors in a breeze, the microphone or the bass exhaust port lets wind in and plays it into your ear, basically covering up anything you're playing. Not sure if this is just me or if it's other people too. A bit annoying.

2. Not sure if this is iOS or the earbuds fault but I've had a couple times when the earbuds disconnect while at over 50% battery life and won't reconnect unless you put them back in the charging case. Hasn't happened for a little bit but I'll update again if it continues.

3. The charging case is huge compared to the AirPods and also matte black, so oil shows up really well on it. I'd recommend keeping the case in a bag or in your car and just wearing the earbuds around.

4. The sensors seem to be a little sensitive, triggering the in-ear detection when it was in my hand.

5. The eartips might be an awkward size. My ear size was in between the one that comes on it by default and the smaller one, so I either had an improper seal on the earbuds or pressure on my ear. The pressure can combine with the size of the driver housing, which is quite large, and can start to hurt your ears. Definitely recommend buying aftermarket eartips to use on them.

6. The earbuds fit fine with glasses. You just need to be sure to use the correct eartips for yourself so the pressure doesn't hurt your ears.

7. Battery life listed is pretty conservative. Beats lists it as 9 hours but I've worked 11 hour shifts with them in the whole time and they don't die.

8. The button to play/pause sometimes doesn't work. I have to manually pull out my phone and hit play again. Seems like it happens when you pause for a while. Other times, it takes a second or two for the music to get going again.

A lot of these are just me nit-picking everything. Overall, I love these earbuds, they're a solid replacement for my daily drivers over my full size headphones (Bose QC35 ii) and my AirPods.

title: Good but not Great.........
text:
I have had these for a couple of months now. I bought them because I was updating my cellphone and my new cell was not going to have a headset jack. Also I have had the Beats Studio Over the Ear phones before and was impressed with that product. Since I workout and walk/jog frequently I was intriqued and interested in the true wireless nature ( no cord connecting the two earpieces ) and the hook that would keep secure on my ear during activity. I previously had Bose Soundsport and they would fall out often while on treadmill.
Pros: Easy to pair with phone ( i have an android ). I had no problems here. Works great playing music and for phone calls. Works great for workouts, stays in place. Stylish and looks good. Love the true wireless nature of these headphones. Charges quick.
Cons: Only charges if you set them in the case. You cannot turn these off, there is no power button to turn off and conserve charge. If they are NOT in the case, they are losing charge. Consequently I find I need to charge them everyday. In comparison, my previous Bose soundsport would last weeks on one charge because when not in use you could turn them off. Although the PowerBeats look small, they are actually bulkier and larger than you would think and in my opinion a bit too much. The ear hook can be uncomfortable when used with sunglasses. One last thing I have noticed....... when updating the firmware ( only done through beats app ), if I receive a text while it is updating it interrupts the update and you much start the update over. Seems odd because I can download a new app from the app store while at same time having a text conversation with a buddy and it does not interrupt the app download.
Overall: Good pair of wireless headphones, with really good sound quality both for phone calls and music but there are some flaws and you are certainly paying for the name.

text: These earphones are a great upgrade from the Powerbeats3 headphones. I didn't realize how great it would be to not have the wire that went behind the ears until I upgraded to the Powerbeats Pro. For anyone who goes to the gym, these headphones make it way more comfortable while squatting or benching since there is no wire getting in the way behind your neck. The design of these earphones has also been a noticeable upgrade as they fit more naturally around the ear, feel much lighter, and are overall more secure while in the ear. The recharging case is also an amazing plus with these earphones as I did not have this prior. It is also far more convenient if you have an iPhone as the charging cord for the case happens to be the same lightening adapter that is used for iPhones so you don't have to worry about having an additional universal USB cord with you (unless you don't have an iPhone). The sound quality is a little better with these than the previous Powerbeats but there isn't too much of a difference. However, I have tried the AirPods (not the AirPods Pro) and these headphones have far superior sound quality. Overall, I would highly recommend these!

title: I wanted to like them more. I really did.
text:
After losing my 1st Gen AirPods Pro to my son, I needed some wireless headphones, preferably with decent noise cancellation since the guy who sits next to me at work likes to eat ice for no particular reason. I went with some Beats buds - these and a pair of Beats Fit Pro. The Fit Pros had some better features but I wasn’t sure about the fit and the price, as the Studio Buds had a better look to me, a better price point, and looked as comfortable as my previous AirPods Pro. Figured I’d try them both and report back. My notes on the Studio Buds below:

The good:

Feel: the Studio Buds sort of twist into the ear canal, and surprisingly stay in place pretty well. I used the smallest of the three supplied ends and they still stayed in better than my AirPods Pro ever used to. I had them in for over an hour straight with no discomfort.

Case: the oval case was secure and the buds locked in tight with the internal magnet. The smaller case fit into my pocket well.

Look: the color options stood out. Honestly, the red color of these made me want to keep them over my grey Beats Fit Pros. There’s something about “Beats” and that red color.

The bad:

The sound: I mean that’s what we’re here for, right? I take teleconference calls with these and that’s fine, but if I play music - especially something bass heavy - and the difference between something like this and the Fit Pros comes in. It doesn’t sound that bad on its own, but carrying the Beats name and a three figure list price you expect something more.

Noise cancellation: again, this is a case of “it’s fine, but you expect more.” This doesn’t reach the ability that the Fit Pros or AirPod Pros did. Maybe I’m asking too much for something not labeled “pros,” but again - for the price, you expect more.

Battery charge: these seemed to drain pretty fast. Even with limited usage I was down to 70% before lunch if I wasn’t putting them into the case to charge during any downtime.

VERDICT:

Like I said in the title - I wanted to like these, I really did. But I really can’t justify paying full retail price for these. They’re an Apple product so they pair with iPhones and other iOS devices pretty easily, but they lack the H1 chip so they lack certain features that AirPods and other Beats earbuds have. If you’re spending this much, you might as well spend a little more and get the Fits Pro or AirPods Pro and get better quality. If you don’t need the high end sound quality, look for something from a third party like Anker for half the price.

title: Love them but.....
text:
I got these as a gift in 2019. I hadn't used them much the first year that I had them as I wasn't really working out much. I started using them more within the last year, mostly while I run or lift at the gym. The point being they weren't used a ton in the two-ish years I've had them, so I was quite surprised when I went to take them out of the charging case to go for a run a couple days ago, that the left one was at 0%.

I fiddled with it for a while and couldn't get a charge. I went online to find that this isn't uncommon, although many people could wiggle the earbud around on the docking station to produce a charge, I cannot. I tried updating the firmware, which also worked for some people, but still no charge from me. I contacted Apple support and did everything they suggested, different cable, cleaning the connection leads, and resetting the earbuds.

I couldn't get them to reset, as holding the button didn't produce the red/white flashing light, it just wanted to keep pairing, though I'm not sure if this is a separate issue, or related to not being able to connect the left earbud. I then brought them to the nearest certified repair location and was told that they were out of warranty, and sending them in for repairs would cost nearly as much as buying a brand new set. Obviously I'm quite upset about it and plan to write Apple a separate email. $200 dollar headphones should not last less than a couple dozen uses, especially when my research discovered it's a common issue related to a design flaw in the docking mechanism.

I loved these so much and would have been a beats lifer, but I cannot in good faith recommend a product that costs this much and is this unreliable. I took good care of them, they just stopped working far too soon. I will be doing extensive research when I buy my next pair, and depending on Apple's response to my email, I can almost assure they will not be beats.

title: Not worth the asking price.
text:
These wireless ear buds are sold for a premium price, and so must be judged as a premium product. Sadly, in my experience, this has been far from the case. For starters, the design of the wireless charging case is just bad. If they are not seated absolutely perfectly into the case, and if they case is jostled for any reason, one or both ear buds will not charge and you will have one dead ear bud next time you go for a run which is fairly infuriating.

Also, connectivity is a problem. Often times, only one bud will connect, or neither, and will require you to re-seat them in the case and try to reconnect, or turn off/on bluetooth settings on your phone until they re-register with your phone. It's extremely annoying, and I've had much better connectivity from $50 dollar wireless ear buds.

Lastly, the sound quality is just so/so. I was never fooled by the fact that I was wearing anything other than a tiny ear bud in terms of quality. I guess sometimes there really isn't a replacement for displacement. However, even worse is the fact that the volume of these buds is low and are rapidly drown out by traffic and surrounding noise. Again, my $50 back-up pay had a much louder overall volume.

On a positive note, I'm pretty sure you could crash an airplane with these on, and they would still find them attached to your ears when they sift through the wreckage. They fit that well.

title: [UPDATED: +1 Star for Good Customer Service] Good for the Price, but Noticeable Audio Delay
text:
--UPDATED FOR CUSTOMER SERVICE EXPERIENCE--
While I would still rate the product I received 3 stars for its defects, I would like to mention that TOZO customer service reached out to me via e-mail and offered me a brand new set of ear buds completely free to compensate me. VERY nice of them! I've decided to up my rating to 4 stars to reflect the overall experience that I had with TOZO as a brand.

They actually sent me the TOZO T6 model earbuds too (which is a step above the TOZO A1 in quality), and so far I haven't had any issues with them thankfully. While the original issues I had in my defective product are still present, I believe buyers can feel slightly more reassured knowing that customer service can help them out if something similar happens.
--
I have only seen a handful of reviews mention the audio delay in these headphones, so I don't know if it's just the pair I received, but the audio lags about 0.2-0.4 seconds behind the video playing on my screen. I have tried these on multiple devices (phone, tablet, desktop PC and Nintendo Switch) and there's a delay across all of them, unfortunately.

This makes watching TV shows and YouTube vids pretty off-putting, as the lips won't match the words quite right and sound effects come in late and ruin the impact of some jokes/scenes a lot of the time. The same goes for playing video games, as many gaming experiences will be hampered by even a slight delay in audio.

I personally would not use these for playing games or while watching something that requires a lot of attention on the screen, which is disappointing. Music, podcasts, audiobooks, and any other kind of media where sound delay doesn't matter much will work fine though, of course.

As for the earbuds themselves, the audio quality is alright — it's not terrible but I do notice some songs/videos have a slight tinny sound to them, which is the only time I found them jarring to listen to. I wasn't looking high-quality, just something functional, and these get the job done.

I like the charging case — it's compact and shuts firm with a magnet, so it feels nice and secure. The earbuds fit in my ear pretty well, and feel comfortable for about an hour before they start to hurt a little. This could just be me having small ears or not being used to wearing earbuds much, but I don't mind since my listening sessions usually don't go past an hour anyway.

One last thing — some reviews mention one earbud dying or the whole pair not working anymore after a couple months or even weeks. After about a month of use, one of my earbuds sometimes does not connect right away when I take it out of the case. One earbud will sync and play audio, while the other will be completely silent or even cut in and out of playing audio. This has only happened a couple times, and popping the earbud back into the case usually fixes it for me, but I think this is lines up with some products being faulty or failing in a short time. This type of risk/gamble isn't uncommon with items of this price point and I was willing to take my chances with it, but keep that in mind if you're considering a cheaper option or possibly saving up for a better and more consistent product.

title: Buyer Beware. This is below trash.
text:
It works well--when it works. I bought this to lift, and I was really impressed with the sound quality, comfortability, and duration of the battery. A few weeks in, however, and it stopped working at all (connecting to neither my computer nor phone).

Oh, just a bad apple. That's fine. They were really nice and sent me a replacement, which worked great again. Amazing! Well, a month in and this one disconnects randomly after 20 minutes. I can reconnect to it eventually, but it always disconnects after a bit.

title: Not worth the heartache, good sound only when they work
text:
These headphones are great...when they work. I have had these for a few months now and I can’t even count the amount of times I have had some sort of issue with them (paired with an iPhone 8 Plus then 11).

Yes the battery life is decent, but the catch there is they actually have to charge. Because of how the magnet pulls them in the case, you have to make an effort to ensure the tiny two prongs are successfully connected. If they are off by the tiniest bit (or get shifted ever so slightly when you close the case) not only will they not charge, but the one headphone will continuously try to connect to your phone and massively drain its battery. There have been so many times now that I show up to the gym, pop the headphones in, and one of the buds is fully charged and the other has less than 10%.

Which leads to my next issue, even when both are charged, quite often only one will connect. I’ve yet to figure out if I’m removing one too fast/slow, but then I have to go through this troubleshooting phase of putting both back in the case, closing it, opening it and leaving the headphones in, pushing the buttons to try and get the connection screen to come up on my phone, then take the headphones back out and hoping I see them both connect (rinse and repeat for when it inevitably doesn’t work).

Now you may think I just have a faulty set. But according to apple (who has now processed them in their help/repair shop twice) they first didn’t have any issue and then the issue was repaired. So apparently these problems are just features of the beats.

My experience with these has made me consider just buying from a different brand, but I have to suffer a little longer cause I spent so freaking much on these.

Buyer beware.

title: Not ready for public use.  Quality control issues
text:
I’m an everyday runner, wearing headphones every morning for my daily jog. I’ve spent years buying cheap headphones every six months until they die. I decided to finally invest in some good headphones. I’ve just returned my second pair of these Beats Pro Wireless headphones in three months. Both pairs I’ve used have similar problems. Don’t get me wrong, day 1 these headphones are great. They stay on my ears during a run when apple air pods do not. They sound great. They’re comfortable. They seem like a great product. Then after a couple weeks and a couple of charge cycles, things stop working. Both pairs I’ve had have started with one of the ear buds not fully charging. Imagine charging the ear buds overnight and waking up in the morning to see the head phone case at %100, the right ear bud at %100, but the left ear bud at %34. Seems weird, but technically they’ll still work for a 1 hour run or workout. I think maybe that %34 ear bud wasn’t set right in the case overnight. Each night I diligently ensure the ear buds are set just right on the charge pins for fear that I’ll wake up with another %34 ear bud. This only gets worse over time, with a single ear bud randomly getting worse and worse, showing %17 battery after a full charge, then %4 battery after a full charge, until finally it just doesn’t turn on or connect or charge at all. Keep in mind, the charging case and the other ear bud still charge %100.

So this morning my second out of beats pro wireless have a totally dead ear bud. I’m returning, and Amazon is sending me yet another pair. I really hope Beats fixes whatever quality control issues they, cause I do really like these headphones. I just wished they worked. The only thing that bumps this review from 1 star to 2 stars is amazon’s great customer service and easy returns. Everyone cross your fingers for the third pair I try.

title: Does not turn off, does NOT work with Android (even though Apple's marketing says so)
text:
Apple is falsy marketing these headphones as "For Apple and Android". They absolutely are not! Detailed problems listed below.

I love premium electronics! so it's very annoying when basic functionality is horrible.

I've tested this product on multiple Android devices, including Sony, OnePlus and Xiaomi the latest Samsung S20. The same Android devices have been tested to pair and play with similar Bluetooth headphones from brands like Sony, Samsung, Plantronics and JBL. This was done to make sure that the phones are functioning well, which they all did. The Powerbeat Pro does NOT work with Android, and testing them with multiple devices clearly shows that it’s not a ”quirk” limited to a specific Android product or Android version (the samson S20 was the only that had Android 10).

The following are the problems:

- Pairing fails in 80-90% of the times. If they pair, the pairing is extremely slow. It’s almost as it’s intentional. (Pairing with both iPhone and iPad works perfectly.) I visited Apple Store twice about this and they were unable to fix this, shrugging their shoulders saying ”Well, it’s not Apple so we don’t know” while pushing me and my spouse to sign a receipt that they ”fixed” my issue. Apple Store were able to pair ONCE with my Android phone after about 5-10 minutes of trying, meanwhile they also tried multiple times with their Apple devices that worked perfectly.

- Trying to use the headphones multiple times often means having to re-pair with the problems.

- Due to the issues above, these headphones are essentially useless.

But there’s more:

- Apple claim that in order to turn the headphones off, you must put them in the included case (which also acts as a charger.) The right headphone never shuts off (I can verify that because I can hear the music coming from it).

At the time of purchase, the seller could not get the right ear bud to work, so they charged it and it worked. Initially it was thought that there was simply no power in the battery in the right bud.

After a few days the right bud stopped working. The case has only one light that will indicate if charging is done, but you don't know if both earbuds are charging.

I visited Apple and requested repair, which they claimed they did after I got it back a few weeks later. (These are the same visits as described above.) Once I got them back the right ear bud stopped working again.

Later via experimentation I realized that the problem is simply because they don’t shout off properly.
The way the case work is that it has an internal powerbank. But since one of the buds never shuts off it will drain itself of power, if I put in in the case it will drain the powerbank too. So, the ONLY way to be able to use the headphones is to CONSTANTLY keep them in the case, with the case CONSTANTLY plugged in to a USB socket. … Not very ”wireless”.

And to be clear, if I keep the headphones in the case and carry the case with me, the battery will drain.

- Apple Store claims that various problems can be fixed with Bluetooth settings, which ONLY exist in Apple devices.

- Apple Store refuse to claim responsibility, almost surprised why I try to use the headphones with an Android even though they are marketed EXACTLY as both for Apple and Android. The shop that sold the headphones said that functionality issues I must talk to Apple, the shop was clear about this when I bought it.

Meanwhile Apple kept wiggling out of it suggesting that if there is a problem with using it with Android they are not really interested to take the issue seriously. Apple don’t see there are any issues as it work for them with their Apple devices.

The Apple Store visit after the claimed fix (now with battery in both buds charged, but me still not being aware that the right bud never turns off) was a bit bizarre, I kept showing them my issue with pairing and they kept “demonstrating” to me that it worked with their Apple. This went forth and back maybe 4-5 times. And after each time they were able to pair and use the headphones with THEIR Apple devices they kept pressing me to sign a form that the issue was fixed.

Eventually, I was able to pair with my phone so I signed the form. At that time I thought it was an issue with my phone.

I see online that multiple people have the exact same problem with these headphones. And, from what I understand, exactly when using Android.
I’m a big gym junkie and have had no problems with the buds. High recommendation. Sound cancellation is great just gotta rotate the different type of bud pieces for optimal performance.

So long as you plan to exclusively use these in your home or when working out, and you'll have a gym bag or somewhere handy to put the big, fat, case, you're fine, and these are pretty good. If you wanted to wear them on the subway, you'd better have a bag for the big fat case, or you can't turn off the headphones when you take them out.
The problem is that these headphones try to be too smart, and end up pretty dumb. I get that they have sensors to tell when they're removed from your ear, and this works, sometimes, but most times the audio won't properly route if I've taken the headphones out, even if I've put them back into my ears.
Unless I am missing something, you can't actually turn them off unless you let the batteries die or put them back in the case. The case is huge, which will make taking these with you anywhere somewhat problematic. I have to run back to where I have the case plugged in and charging whenever I want to stop using these headphones.
Another problem is that it uses a lightning cable instead of USB C. This is the only device in my home that uses this particular proprietary cable, and I'm honestly not sure whether I would rather spend $10 on a replacement cable or use it as an excuse to buy a more practical pair of headphones if I ever misplaced this cable.
So, if you plan on using these exclusively at home or when working out, you'll be fine. That way you can't misplace the magical glory that is the lightning cable, the only cable majestic enough to provide premium electricity to these elite headphones. And this way you won't have to go too far to place the headphones back into their glorious throne to allow them to go to sleep in the only place that they deign to rest, enabling your phone to go back to playing audio through more mundane means.

title: Not worth the price
text:
I truly wanted to like this product. As someone who lifts regularly, it was important to find head phones that didnt intervene with my workouts.

Positives:
Fit of the head phones were spot on. Very secure. Through heavy compound lifts and cardio, the head phones stayed snug and secure.

I enjoyed the ease of charging the case which contained the head phones rather than the head phones themselves.

Headphones were only paired to my phone once, no issues with pairing.

Negatives:
The music would cut out regularly when performing basic movements. The irritation of spotty music inevitably led me to return the product.

Head phones have to settle into metal prongs within their charging case to enable charging. I didn't experience an issue with this, but as someone who tries to plan ahead, I can see the prongs inevitably being damaged at some point in time, causing the co sumer to shell out additional cash.

Head phones are difficult to quickly take out of ears. If you need to talk with someone at the gym.

The overall price point simply isn't worth it. Buy the previous version of the headphones at a third of the cost and save yourself the irritation of having to return the headphones.

title: Wings for Marie/10000 Days never sounded so beautiful!
text:
I upgraded to these from being a longtime user of BeatsX. I have owned three pairs of the BeatsX due to the sound quality and longevity of the device. Every other brand Bluetooth headset I have owned has taken out every 6 months on average. The little things I didn't care for on the X are all addressed in this beautiful model headset.
1. Sound quality- As you may already be aware, us Tool fans are extremely arrogant and prefer speakers that will enable us to hear all the slightes changes an inflexes in the music and this product definitely delivers, and then some.
2. The fit- Never ever have I owned a pair of earphones that stayed in place so well that I didn't have to adjust every 5 mins even while not working out, as I suppose I must have the most oddly shaped ear holes in the wide world. As soon as I put these in place, there is no readjusting, not even once.
3. Battery life- This is one of the two issues I took with the BeatsX model. The battery life on all those pairs of the X I had seemed to only last me an average of 4 hours of continuous use, which definitely does not seem to be the issue with these at all. I wore them 9 hours for work and workout with some of the battery life still intact before charging them again when my day was over.
4. Range- The second minor complaint on the X model. The X seemed to have very limited range when I would set my phone down to busy myself with workouts or other tasks about the home. PowerBeats Pro allows me to set my phone down to work out and walk all around my home without the signal dropping off.
Call Quality- Crisp, clean, and clear, just as to be expected with the Beats line.

title: Domination of JBL by cheap Chinese company.
text:
I have had several pairs of JBL ear buds. Live 300 and and Tune 130. They break constantly!! So I said screw it I'm going to try an ultra cheap option. To my surprise the sound quality of the TOZO pair isn't as good as the Live300TWS but it's pretty darn close, it's on par with the Tune130s (TOZO having higher volume).. Noise Cancelation is better then the Tune 130s not as good as the Live300 but pretty close.

I just got them so I can't speak for build quality, but at the price point these sell for as long as they're close to on par with JBl (which are terrible build quality) it will be worth it just to buy another pair of these instead of having to buy a pair of Live300s every 2 months, and are 5x the price!

Another factor is the physical size. The TOZO pair are a bit smaller then the Tune130s and about half the size of the Live300s, and fit perfectly in my ear right out of the box.

As for battery life the TOZO pair isn't as good as either of the JBL buds. However unlike the Live300 pair you can wear the TOZO buds independently of each other. So you can wear the left one till it dies then swap it out for the right one and continue listening. This is great in my use case because I wear them at work and can only have one in at a time..

title: The design is the only good thing about it.
text:
Edit (11/3/2021):
Changing from 3 star to 1. The number of times one of the ear buds doesn't turn on is close to 50/50. Sometimes both or one ear bud won't charge properly in the case. I'll take them out and within 5 minutes one of them will do the beep noise and turn off. They are so inconsistently reliable that every single time I pull them out, I anticipate something not working properly. Whether it failed to charge, one ear bud doesn't turn on, or the pairing is broken. The automated controls are straight garbage to detect power/charge. On top of the fact that as everyone else already points out, the sound quality is actually worse than (in my case) my $20 corded ear buds. And noticeably worse too. When a $20 product is better quality then you know you fudged up. The only reason to buy these is if you want something that will stay in your ear pretty well while running/jogging/hiking hard. My guess is that you can find a cheaper/better product in that case. Not worth even worth $50 imo.
-Also, I've been using them daily. This isn't about random 1-offs. They are F'ed quite literally almost once every single day I try to use them. The rarity is that I can go the entire day with no issue.

*Review before I lost my patience*
Average/Expected:
- Sound quality
- Battery life
- Charging time
- Connection distance

Cons:
- Connection reliability is really bad. When you get temporary interference and the connection gets "choppy", it will sometimes turn off and not automatically turn back on until you take them off and put them back on. Kind of weird since it "turns on/off" based on detecting your ear so you don't have direct power control of them.
- More connection reliability. This is the biggest complaint I have about them. Sometimes they just don't connect. Even if you've just used them an hour before, it will randomly still show as paired to your device, but it won't connect when you try. Unpairing and pairing doesn't fix it either. You have to unpair them, and do the reset function where you hold the volume and box button. then pair again. It's annoying enough that I actively avoid using them all together sometimes and just use my corded earbuds.

Pros:
- An awesome fit. Being able to adjust the ear hooks makes it great for perfect seating so that my ears don't start to hurt after longer use. Comes with a good selection different inner ear piece sizes. Mine can stay in snug for several hours without any pain/irritation and without coming loose during moderate to difficult activity. In my case that's several hours going 8 miles and 2600ft elevation up and down a mountain.

Personally I wouldn't recommend them unless you're specifically looking for workout/running earbuds. I've never had issues while I was actively using them and stayed within arms reach of the connected device. For use other than needing a good solid fit, get a cheaper product. The cost isn't worth to me since it doesn't seem like you're getting anything else. For sound quality, you can just compare the technical specifications with another product.

title: One of the few that I find comfortable
text:
Short version: Small and comfortable with the case being a weak spot with it's flimsy lid and lack of way to open it with any sort of 'notch'. Just 'push around the lid'. The app is okay, but has very few options.

I'm not an audiophile by a long shot,

Comfort: I own plenty of true wireless earbuds, but most just aren't comfortable for long term use (by that I mean for over an hour). I generally find most earbuds to be uncomfortable after 30 minutes or so, but these stay fairly comfortable for longer. Perhaps due to their very small size?

Sound: The transparency mode is decently loud if you have the music turned down (you do need to have it turned down to hear voices), and the ANC is in the mid-range of effectiveness. I'd probably give it a 6/10 if I were to compare it to the other brands I have. It definitely 'takes the edge' off noise, though you can still tell there's noise nearby.

Case: The weak point in my opinion. The lid feels flimsy and has no place to really apply leverage to open it. You just sorta push on the entire top part of the case. I feel like over time this might affect the hinge but we'll see.

Software: The app is so-so. It's very simple in terms of both ease of use, but also in what you're allowed to do. I'd like to customize the 'cycle' of normal->ANC->transparency you get when long-pressing the button on the buds, as some other brands allow, but that's not an option. Really, the only option at all is switching between that loop on long-press, or activating voice assistant. And doing firmware updates, which seemed to work fine.

title: Very meh for anything other than using 2 at a time in the gym
text:
As plain basic headphones for just audio out, pretty good sound. EQ doesn’t do much mid but it’s beats so yeah, expected, delivered.
Honestly can’t hear ANY audible difference between the “noise cancelling mode”, and just the passive noice cancelling of having a rubber ball in stuffed into your ear.
But some major problems:
Trying to answer a phone call? Mic sounds like you’re in the other room. In a tunnel. And underwater sometimes.

Trying to use one ear while leaving the other in the case so it won’t get lost? Not gonna happen.

Connecting to a PC? The Bluetooth is and outdated spec that doesn’t support simultaneous headset and headphone mode. So if you open anything that wants to use the mic, windows will shift them to the headset driver and you’ll go to “tape recorder” quality. Not making that up^, that’s the audio quality setting that windows will pump to it

Very disappointed in these all around. Other than explicitly as “Headphones”. But if that’s the only thing they do, 150 is about 5x what you should pay.

title: Unless you only listen to hip hop, these headphones aren’t for you.
text:
Oh my god bass. That’s all these headphones do. Apple engineers just scooped the hell out of the mids to get that Beats signature punchy bass.

I really wanted to like these headphones. The compatibility with my phone, compact design, and use of actual buttons instead of touch sensitive controls brought me towards these. All of those features worked great, except the whole headphone part.

Great voices like Aretha Franklin, Luke Combs, and Freddie Mercury sound dull and are washed out by instrumentals. If you like great vocalists, these are not the headphones for you.

On a positive note, I was blown away by the bass these buds deliver. If Beats could’ve delivered 50% of that punch with a more balanced sound, I would’ve been floored and kept these buds.

I replaced a pair of Jaybird Vista’s with these (one bud went through the washer), now that I’m returning them I’m probably going to splurge for the Vista 2’s. I chose the Beats to save $50, that was a mistake.

The previous generation Jaybird product delivered a far superior listening experience at the expense of both money and convenience. Based on reviews, it seems they’ve only improved with its successor.

Really disappointing experience, I expected more. Especially from an Apple backed brand.

title: Wish I had bought them sooner!!
text:
I listen to music 8+ hours a day. I’ve tried several small size wireless headphones that said the lasted 8 or more hours. Some did, but only for awhile. All of them were uncomfortable. All of them were connected to each other by a cord, which dangled & got in my way. Plus I always have to remove the cap that goes in my ear (which makes them more uncomfortable) because I’m allergic & it causes issues for me.

When I saw these I read that they lasted 9 hrs. They were pretty pricey, but I thought I would try them. I’M GLAD I DID!!!

They last as long as & often more than 9 hrs. There’s no wire.
The distance from device is as advertised, but if there are no walls / obstacles, I have gotten them to go a bit further.
They are VERY comfortable! I don’t even have to remove the little cap (I’ve had no issues with being allergic to them.)
They work the very well with the old cheap LG phone that I use as a media player & even with a Bluetooth converter I use with my old stereo.
They sound fabulous! Deep, rich sound that feels immersive. (BTW I’m also a musician, so I know quality sound when I hear it.)
The controls are easy to use & when you set them down they automatically pause your player! I love that!
Each one works independently. I can only wear 1 at work because I have to be able to hear what is going on around me. So, when I work overtime and the 1 I’m wearing runs down, it is super easy to pick up the other half & start listening again!
They also charge quickly, both the case & the earbuds. Since I only use 1 half, I usually get 3-4 days of recharging from the case. My regular phone (not the cheap, old LG) is new enough that I was able to download their app, which enables me to see how much juice is left in them (case & earbuds).

Detractors:
The case only comes in black (so it doesn’t match the color of my earbuds).
There’s no handle or clip on the case. I ended up purchasing a silicone cover that has a clip on it, which I switched out for a sturdy metal keychain with leather strap. I also found some hard cases & zip around cases, but the slip cover was best for my use.

I highly recommend that you get these!! I really wish I had I known about them sooner.

title: Inexcusably inconsistent for the price.
text:
I've had these for a little over a year now, and while I use them almost every day, it is with contempt.

TL;DR - These headphones don't work 50% or more of the time (connection issues making you unable to hear anything). Even if they consistently worked, the mediocre sound quality and terrible microphone don't warrant $250.

When they work, they are only fair.

CONS

- CONNECTION ISSUES.
This is ultimately why I would not recommend this product to anyone. I bought one pair, and they would consistently cut out on me, so I assumed they were defective. A few weeks after I returned those and got a second pair, they started to do the same thing. "Maybe this is just something that only happens every now and then," I thought. No. It happens all the time. Sometimes the audio will just cut out for no reason and you have disconnect it from your device then reconnect it to work again. Even that is just a band-aid, though, because there is no telling how soon the same thing will happen again. Yesterday I was trying to watch a show on Netflix on my laptop with the Powerbeats connected and I had to reconnect them ~every minute about 10 times in a row until I decided that I'm just done trying to use them for that purpose. I'm honestly still salty about the fact that I spent $200 on these a year ago because they just straight up don't work.

- Mediocre sound quality for $250 and not even full of bass like I thought they would be.

- Garbage tier built in microphone.
My friends/family can tell when I'm using these and hate it because they can always barely hear me.

- Pause/play button does not work well with YouTube.
If you pause a YouTube video then try to play it, often times it won't work until you press it a few more times. Sometimes it doesn't work at all and you are forced to do it on whatever device you're connected to.

PROS

+ Secure on the ear due to the hooks.

+ Built in volume controls are convenient and work well.

title: Good quality but not at the $250 price
text:
I use these to work out.

Pros:
-The durability and sweat/water resistance work great. I sweat a lot, have dropped them in the sink, and they are in very hot saunas with me for 15-20 minutes a day! No issues whatsoever with that.
-The battery life is more than enough.
-They stay in my ear nice and snug and have never fallen out.
-They are comfortable.

Cons:
-The sound quality is (to me) literally paralleled by the $25.00 Apple wired headphones that I used for the years prior to buying these. Also, I wish they would get a bit louder, but I suppose it's for the best because I listen to way too much loud music as it is.
-Sometimes pairing is weird, often I'll take them out of the case and only one will pair and I have to mess with putting them back in the case, re-pairing them, etc. to get both headphones to play music. Also, once in a while the music will cut out (while my phone is in my pocket) and cut back in 1-2 seconds later. $250 headphones shouldn't do that.
-Price is too much. I'd value headphones like this at $100-$150 max! The remaining $100+ I feel like you're paying for the little red b on the side of the headphones so everyone else in the gym knows you're a big baller. If I didn't buy these off a Christmas gift card I feel like I'd be pissed that I dropped this much on headphones.

title: Not satisfied with connection Issues
text:
I am not pleased with the Beats PowerbeatsPro True Wireless Earbuds. The Psedo-luxory label applied to them by Apple is not worth the $249 pricetag. Great sound quality. Music is perfectly centered and you can hear and differentiate specific musical parts. The bass is phenomenal. Whaddya expect, Beats??

However, the supreme sound quality is not even close to an excuse for the list of other issues I have experienced in the 4 short days I have owned them. Chief of these are the frequent connection dropouts and random music stoppages while music is playing on device and bluetooth is still paired. It does this with both my mac and nonmac devices. Also it charges unevenly. Sometimes, one headphone will not fit just absolutely perfect into the case and it will cause it to go dead while the other one fully charges. Also one heaphone, the left in my case, drains much faster than the other side. Talking 23% vs 78% after only two hours of listening time.

In the end I am very disappointed in purchasing these headphones for $249 when they might be worth maybe sparingly $99.

title: Good sound, garbage product for the price.
text:
I've had 2 sets of these now. The first set died in less than 6 months, and the second pair has had constant battery issues due to the horribly designed automatic on/off since day 1. Honestly, I don't CARE how good your sound is, if the product never works, it doesn't matter. For a $200 pair of ear buds, I expect it to work almost flawlessly, for at least 2 years at absolute minimum.

Seriously, who's brain child was it to not include a physical on/off? That would be LOADS better than the current idiotic design where the only way to turn them on is putting them in your ears, and the only way to turn them off is putting them in the case. Both which fail to work on a regular basis. To make it worse, even when they do turn off in the case, they'll randomly decide reconnect to my phone, seemingly just to spite me, and run their battery dead.

I don't care if it's long pressing the button on the side of them, or a separate switch, give me full control to turn them on and off. I'm tired of this automatic garbage that tries, and miserably fails to work under the guise of trying to be "user friendly", while actually doing nothing other than causing endless headaches because it almost always fails to work properly.

Even worse, when the DO turn off when I put them in the case, and they don't decide randomly to wake up, connect to my phone, and run their battery dead on a whim... even then, half the time things don't work properly. There's been many times where I've taken them out of the case, fully charged, put them in my ears, and they don't turn on. The only way to make them work is put them back in the case, close the lid, take them back out, and try again. That's frustratingly annoying.

Then there's the many other times where I'll take them out, put them in my ears, and only ONE turns on. To which I need to take the one that isn't working, put it in the case, close it, take it back out, and put it in my ear to make it work. Seeing a pattern here?

The automatic sensor stuff is just bad design. I don't even care if it's included, as long as I still have the ability to physically turn them off, and ensure they stay off until I need to turn them on again.

text:
First the good - The quality of sound is excellent, they are comfortable to wear and I love how they are able to sync either to my phone or my ipad automatically. two thumbs up!

The bad - When you put the earpieces into the charging case they do not seat properly and do not give you any indication that they are not seated properly. This results in either one or both of my earpieces being completely dead at least 50% of the time I go to use them. I have complained to Apple and even sent them in for repair as they are only 4 months old, but Apple will not do anything about it. I have tried to be very careful about seating the earpieces properly and then will close the case and having the case closed seems to unseat the connection and result in dead earpieces. The odd thing is that even if I put them in with 50% charge, if they are not seated properly they will deplete the charge to 0%

This does not seem to be a repair issue, this a design issue. The earpieces will charge when I leave the case open and I press down on them to ensure a solid connection. But they are not reliable and for the price they are a complete disappointment.

title: What you need to know
text:
I've had my PowerBeats Pro for about eight months. Full disclosure, I did not buy these from Amazon but rather directly from Apple.

First, the good: they stay in place. So, from a workout perspective, they're great. The sound is also not bad, though, for most audiophiles, they will be less than stellar. For phone calls, they're great, and as someone who works from home and has an obscenely inhumane amount of conference calls, they do the trick.

The so-so: while the battery life is good, it's not as great as advertised. Certainly, for the case itself, it's fair at best. Now, that said, it's better than most in this device category, but you should know you will not get the full amount advertised, either for the buds or the case.

The terrible: the connectivity. If/when you get them connected, no problems. No significant issues with dropouts. However, the biggest issue is the fact that sometimes one bud won't charge, thus leaving you without a bud. Other times, one won't connect, and it's never consistent. Sometimes it's the right one, sometimes its the left. And, just for fun, sometimes it's both of them! For this, and this alone, I would recommend avoiding this set like a child avoids homework. Of course, if you only use them occasionally, you likely won't be as annoyed. However, if you use them with any sort of frequency, this issue is likely to drive you so far up the wall that you'll finally get that spider that's been camping out in the corner. Oh, and even better: good luck getting Apple to do anything about it. I finally got fed up with these issues, invoked my warranty, and then just sent them right back. A cursory search of reviews, both here and elsewhere, will net you similar stories. This means Apple knows there's an issue and, as is the case with many large companies, they don't really care.

So, to summarize: good for working on, good for phone calls, meh on battery life, terrible for your patience while you play the will-it-or-won't-it-connect game.

title: Best earbuds for distance running - by far.
text:
I’m a distance runner and have been searching for a while for a pair of Bluetooth earbuds that meet the following criteria.

1) They must fit securely enough not to dislodge or fall out during a long run in warm weather when my head will get sweaty
2) I wear glasses, and the earbuds must be able to accommodate the arms of my frames where they go behind my ears.
3) I must be able to hear approaching cars or dogs while listening to music.
4) The controls must be easily accessed and intuitive.
5) They must hold enough charge for a 4 or 5 hour run and not suffer any Bluetooth dropouts.
6) Finally, I am also a bit of an audiophile, so they need to sound good. In particular, they should overcome the #1 audible weakness of all sports-oriented Bluetooth earbuds – a weak and muddled bass.

In my quest for these all these features, I’ve tried three different versions of Bose earbuds, the Jabra Elite 75T’s, and multiple generations of Apple earbuds. The Powerbeats Pro buds come the closest by far for meeting all my criteria. They have a moldable loop that fits snugly around the back of the ear and is thin enough to accommodate wearing my glasses at the same time (a failing of the corresponding Bose product). They have the best overall sound of any sports-oriented earbuds I've heard - especially at the low end. However, to get that great bass response it is crucial to choose the correct size rubber tips. You will lose all the bass if the ones you use are too small. I did an 11 mile run yesterday (about 2 hours at my pace) and they stayed snug in my ears the whole time, even with sweat. There were no Bluetooth dropouts at any time. I had no sore spots on my ears after the run and my glasses stayed in place just fine. A great feature is that they have a full set of controls mirrored on each bud - no need to remember which side does what. A superb product and great value.

title: Don’t buy this product
text:
One of the worst purchases I’ve ever had, especially when you consider I had a prior version for over 10 years that had no problems.

First, they constantly connect to my iPhone regardless of whether I’m using them, and there’s no option for manual connection. This consistently drives the battery down to nothing in at least one ear, leaving me working out with only one headphone. This is a regular occurrence, and now I bring old school wired headphones since I’d rather deal with a cord than not listen to anything.

Second, like the AirPods Pro, the charging station is incredibly finicky, meaning that even if they’re seated well, they still might not charge without shifting them around manually and seeing if they connect. (Others have noted as I have that they can start charging when the case is open but then stop when it’s shut. Someone posted this issue online, but of course no response).

Finally, the sound quality kind of sucks, especially on the low end, and in comparison with other headphones like the AirPods. I’ve tried adjusting the equalizer, but really doesn’t help much when using with Spotify.

Overall, my advice would be to just buy two sets of AirPods if you want something for working out, or consider a wired version if you want to avoid getting to the gym and having no headphones to listen to.

text:

I could only find one review relating to that, so I took it as a fringe feeling that everyone else didn't notice. Once I got them, however, I quickly noticed what that person was talking about. The black ball that's behind the rubber end is essentially an ear sensor (and ONLY an ear sensor) and it really sticks into my ear and I can't where the buds for any more than an hour at best. Taking them out and massaging my ear helps, but if I want to wear them to bed I have to find the exact position that those sensors won't stab into my ear.
Other than that, the sound quality is good. The battery life is surprisingly high (9 hrs, which can make the comfort problem worse). I'm not gonna recommend them, but I'm not at all going to discourage buying them. If you're buying them to wear for a short period of time like working out or walking, go for it. title: Don't buy these - they do not work
text:
I'm writing my first Amazon review to warn people not to buy these headphones. They actually sound great and are great for working out because they stay in your ears even with a lot of sweat. The problem is they do not work. I've had mine for less than a year and there have been NUMEROUS technical issues making these things essentially useless. Problems include: only one bud pairing, only one bud charging, one bud not automatically disconnecting when case is closed so battery drains, firmware not automatically updating, "hard" reset does not work, neither bud pairing at all, buds charging only when case is open, buds not charging at all - you get the idea. I'm actually taking mine in to the Apple store today for the second time in less than a year. They currently won't pair with my iphone and won't reset.

I've looked at the Apple support website and Redditt and these issues (and others) are not at all unique to my headphones. These things have a ton of technical issues and bugs and chances are pretty high you're going to have to deal with them. So probably best if you buy some different headphones. title: Beats me why I bought these
text:
For a $200 pair of headphones, my expectations were much higher. Had I known there would be so many nuances and issues, I would not have purchased, and am already thinking of returning them.

Pros:
-Not sure about Android, but initially connects pretty easily and seamlessly to an iPhone via Bluetooth
-Sound quality is decent
-The hook makes them stay in your ear

Cons:
-On multiple occasions, the headphones have just arbitrarily disconnected from my laptop (during work calls at times), and from my iphone
-There were times when one ear would just randomly disconnect during a workout session and I'd have to stop, disconnect the entire device, and reconnect
-Sound quality is good, but nowhere near loud enough for a decent workout
-Earbuds can be uncomfortable, and when adjusting them, it's easy to accidentally press the "b" Beats button on the side which can either disconnect your call, or pause your music
-Annoying to initially get in your ear with the hook, I have to like spiral and slide it over my ear to initially get it on
-Took a few tries to get it connected to my laptop, and had to fiddle with that extremely small button in the case, which is hard to tell if you're actually pressing it because the headphones in the case get in the way
-Instructions were extremely basic and simple, too much so that they're useless. They tried being "modern" and keeping things short and chic in the instructions but they failed
-Biggest annoyance to me - I find it near impossible to tell the battery level. To get battery info for both the headphones and case, you have to hold your phone near the case, and there's a 50/50 shot the little battery status screen will pop up. You also really have to press the headphones in the case to make sure they're making a connection to the case and actually charging. On a few occasions one headphone was fully charged and one was dead, I can only guess that's (maybe) because one wasn't fully pressed in and connected in the case. You then basically have to wait for one to charge or charge both again
-Are you supposed to store the earbuds in the case when not in use? There's no way to turn off the headphones (to my knowledge), so if you leave them out, the next time you use them the battery will be dead, but if you leave them in the case until the next time you use them, if that's a day or two away, I worry about overcharging them in the long run. There's no guidance in the instructions on best practice for storing them when not in use

All in all, to me this is an overpriced Apple product that is riding on hype. The things I described above I'd expect from a $30 pair of headphones, not a $200 pair.

title: Amazing Wireless Earbuds
text:
These are really amazing wireless earbuds. I'm gonna do pros and cons along with some other thoughts about this product. This review is written 4 months after using this product.

Pros:
1. Battery life. The battery life is amazing. I never had these die on me except when I play video games all night. They also have fast charging which is very useful if you need to charge them real quick.
2. Fit. The fit is really perfect. They feel comfortable and they stay in my ears perfectly. I exercise a lot and these earbuds always stay in my ears when I'm at the gym and when I'm running. If you are looking for some workout earbuds, then these will give you reliable and beautiful performance.
3. Sound quality. The sound quality is amazing. Nice, clear and crisp.
4. The Apple features. The extra features that the Powerbeats have when using with apple devices are nice but don't let those features discourage you android users from buying the Powerbeats. The features aren't important enough for you to decide not to buy them (Not gonna list out the features in order to make this review shorter)
5. Range. The range is amazing. I can be listening to music on my phone and leave my phone in my room and walk anywhere in the house and still be able to listen to the music. The music starts cutting out depending on the amount of objects blocking the signal.
6. Ability to wear with glasses. I can wear these with my glasses with no problem at all. I can take my glasses on and off and have no trouble.
7. Good microphone. I use these earbuds for phone calls and video calls and the person can hear me pretty good. I can hear them perfectly fine. My brother tells me that I sound muffled but he can still hear me good.

Cons:
1. Pain. After wearing them for a couple of hours, I start to feel slight discomfort. This only happens after many hours so it isn't something i'm complaining about. Just felt like I should mention it so everyone is aware. The pain that is the problem is the major pain that comes after weeks of regular use. I'm not sure what is happening but it's like the Powerbeats is making the skin inside my ear peel off. I think this is happening because they are too tight in my ears. This has happened I believe 3 times and the goes away after I left my ears heal. As i'm writing this review, I am experiencing the major pain and I adjusted the left earhook so it's not as tight in my ear as before (Problem is currently only in my left ear). I'm not sure if I'm the only one who experiences this but if you can deal with this then don't let that discourage you from buying the Powerbeats (It isn't that big of a problem for me).
2. Bluetooth connection on Windows 10 computers. I'm not sure if this also happens on other versions of Windows and android devices but sometimes there would randomly be a 1-2 second cut in the sound about every two minutes. This doesn't happen at all on my iPhone. I would also experience random disconnections on my laptop. Another thing about the connection is that it is weaker on my laptop than on my phone. Not sure why.
3. Bulky case. This doesn't matter to me at all because I usually have a bag that I carry with me when I go to places that I can slip the case into. I'm just mentioning it so people can be aware. You can put it in your pocket if you want but it will look weird because there will be a giant bulge in your pants.

That's it about the pros and cons. Now it's time to talk about the problems I had with the Powerbeats. I'm having flashbacks of the problems I encountered while typing this part of the review. Problem 1. This only happened once but I will still talk about it. I was connecting the Powerbeats to my iPhone and forgetting them in the bluetooth settings because I was enjoying the animation that pops up when you pair them with your iPhone. Then all of a sudden they would not pair again. Man I thought they were already broken and it was the day I got them. I thought my $200 dollars went down the drain. But luckily I managed to get them to pair again after a long time of research and trying different things. What fixed the problem was charging the case because apparently since it was at I believe 30 something percent, it couldn't pair. Problem 2. This was the worst problem. I've had this problem happen twice in the last month and a half. One of the earbuds would not pair and sound would only come out of the earbud that was paired. I had to switch back to my other pair of wireless earbuds that I previously had until I figured out how to solve this problem. It took days of extensive research and multiple solution attempts before I finally managed to fix the problem. I was about to return them but luckily I solved the problem before I did.

Final thoughts: Despite the cons and problems I encountered, I would still recommend these earbuds to anyone. If you encounter any of the problems I did, I hope you can easily solve them and if you don't, you can reply to my comment and ask me for my solution. Hopefully Amazon has a feature where you get notifications when someone replies to your review. If you read this whole thing, thank you and I appreciate it. If you didn't then thanks for taking a look at it.
Update: I no longer experience the major pain in my ears and the skin peeling off after I adjusted the earhooks to get the right fit (Update written on 8/18/21).

title: Longevity is non-existent
text:
I'll start by saying the Powerbeats Pro are great earbuds... when they work. The sound quality is pretty solid if you like bass (by earbud standards), and the wrap-around design ensures they stay in place during workouts.

The biggest caveat is that these earbuds are not as durable as they should be, given the activity they should endure. My wife and I have both separately owned a pair of these earbuds, and both pairs stopped charging / syncing almost exactly a year after we received them (conveniently, just outside of the covered warranty period).

My wife's experience is especially concerning because she had only actually used them for a few months before COVID hit and gyms closed. The earbuds then sat unused for ~9 months, and were broken when she got them back out on vacation.

I've used mine quite a bit, but am now having issues getting one side to charge / sync. I regularly open the case to one dead earbud (the right one), super frustrating. Appears to be an issue with how specific the seating position has to be in the case for the earbud to charge properly.

Neither of us will be replacing our earbuds with another pair of Powerbeats; 0/2 is not a particularly encouraging record.

title: Some issues, but for the most part better than AirPods
text:
Although the sound was good, I hated my AirPod pros because they would fall out of my ears after a while, and it was happening with all the adjustments I made. I resorted to using my old original AirPods, which I still like a lot, but the sound on those things are not great. I wanted to find something which took the best qualities between the AirPods and airpod pros, and I came across the Powerbeats. After using them at the gym today, I can confidently say these headphones are fantastic. Here are some pros and cons
PROS:
-Killer sound. Bass on these things is amazing, a whole lot better than the normal AirPods and better sound than the pros as well
-Great fit. Big hesitation was whether or not it would fit well, and if they would fall out or not, I had these headphones on for about one and half to two hours and they didn’t move at all. They also didn’t get uncomfortable after a while which was something I felt with the AirPod pros. I also really like how there’s a band around your ear, just makes it feel much more secure.
-Look dope. Love the color design of these things. Always hated how AirPods don’t come in black, but I’m glad I finally have some great in ear buds that are my preferred color of choice.

CONS:
-Carrying case. This thing is big. Something I love about AirPods is that I can just carry them around in my pocket and it’s not noticeable at all. These however you can’t really do the same thing with. They’d fit best in a jacket pocket or bag.
-Not as versatile in some aspects. AirPods are really simple to put on which I really like. Powerbeats takes some getting used to, and even then they still are not as easy to put on.
-No sound transparency. One of the best features of the pros is the transparency mode which makes surrounding noises more clear. However, with the Powerbeats it doesn’t have this feature which I think was a huge mistake. It’s impossible to hear surroundings when ur playing music, and even when u pause it’s still a little muffled.

The cons are important to keep in mind, but i would say buy it if you hate the sound of regular AirPods and the AirPod pros don’t fit your ears well. These are perfect for gym use. The great sound makes songs a whole lot better, and the fact that the bass punches made my workout much better.

title: Other person says you sound like you’re talking thru a mask
text:
I really like the the receive audio (the sound that you hear in your ears). It has good tonal quality and sufficient bass. Each ear bud has a button to pause music or answer calls The button on the right doesn’t have enough tactile feedback (you can hardly tell whether you pressed it) so I use the one on the left most of the time.

In general, I don’t think these are worth the full price but if you can get them on sale (like $75 off that I did) then I think they’re ok.

I’m somewhat of an audiophile so the way the transmit audio sounds on a phone call (described above) is disappointing. I do want to mention that I’m running an iPhone 6 so maybe the newer Bluetooth chipset in the newer iPhones will render better mic audio. There’s a mic in each earbud and in the iPhone settings I’ve switched from default (automatic selection) to left preferred then right making sure it just wasn’t one mic that was bad or sub-par.

Also, these are fairly tightly integrated for the Apple products (iPhone, iPad) so that’s another plus. For example, when you open the case the iPhone displays both the battery level for the earpieces as well as the case battery which charges them. Pairing is extremely easy — there’s a tiny button in the charging case (they should have made it raised or a different color since it wasn’t that obvious when the pairing instructions said to press the button in the case, I’m like what button?

Also, so far I’ve paired three devices so there’s no issue with keeping the other devices in memory, so to speak. It’ll power up paired to the last device.

I see third party so called “cases” for this but I wouldn’t waste your money on the one I bought advertised as a case ($10). When I got it, it was only two silicone shells with double sided sticky tape so you can overlay them onto the Powerbeats case. The upside was if you need a hole to sling a carabiner through, then it’ll do that.

I actually didn’t realize these come with a case so there’s no reason to buy a “case” (really a shell) unless you want to change the outside color of the case to find it easier in your gym bag.

title: Don't waste your time or money
text:
The design, fit, sound etc. are all fine.
The problem with these is 2 fold: the charging and the connecting.

Countless times I've put them back in the case (very carefully I may add) only to come back to use them however long later to find that one or both earbuds didn't charge. On the off chance that they do successfully charge, there's connection problems constantly. You're supposed to be able to just open the case, put them in and they connect immediately no problems. In reality however, one or both earbuds wont connect. Then you play this little game where you put them back in the case, close it, take them out of the case and put them in your ears, over and over, back and forth. Then after about 5 minutes they connect the way they're supposed to as advertised (honestly I consider this false advertisement and blatant lying).

90% of the time I have one or both of these problems. Literally 10% of the time (or less) do they work as advertised where you open the case, they're both fully charged, you pop them in, they connect automatically and you go about your workout. And I know I'm not alone in this, look online and there's numerous youtube videos, reviews, forums etc. about people having the same issues. Completely unacceptable for a name brand and especially for the price. After the train wreck that was the Power Beats 3 I thought I'd give Beats another chance. Last Beats product I will ever waste my money on.

text:
I just got these and I was a little bit skeptical after reading some of these people's reviews. I am not disappointed whatsoever. Let me address the main complaints I saw:
"These Hurt My Ears" - I have extremely small ears and these do not hurt me whatsoever. If I use EarPods for a super long time they hurt, and I at worst can expect that from these, but that is after a super long time.
"The Bass Isn't Good" - FALSE. The bass in these is amazing. I was very surprised being that they are earbuds and not headphones. I was not expecting anything crazy good or bad, but the bass is very good and very noticeable. This is without any adjustments to the sound.
"They Aren't Noise Isolating" - WRONG. These are very good at isolating what you are listening to. People don't realize that if you have bigger or smaller ears, you need to change the tips of the earbuds to the correct size. Luckily for me I didn't even need to change them because they already fit perfectly fine.

So far I have no complaints, but if I ever do I will update it.

title: Frequently Do Not Work
text:
These headphones are great when they work. They do not work most of the time. Frequently, just when I'm getting ready to listen, they completely brick themselves. Each time seems to happen in a unique and exciting way. Sometimes only one side works, sometimes neither. Sometimes I get a delightful electrical buzzing noise, other times just silence. Occasionally resetting them (yes, I know, hold the button for 15 seconds until it blinks red) works, other times it just seems to make them angry. Sometimes when they're bricked they show up as connected, other times just nothing.

At first I thought it was faulty hardware, so I had Amazon replace them. Twice. Now I'm convinced most people have this happen to them all the time and just deal with it because they love Apple. Not me.

When they brick, it rarely makes a difference whether I'm connecting from my own android phone, my wife's iPhone, or my own MacBook Pro. I'm sure some will read this and assume I'm too dumb to work them. If that's you, by all means go ahead and find out for yourself. If not, then please save yourself some money and buy the Jabra Elite instead.

text:

I'll get ready to do yard work, or go on a run, and as I'm ready to begin whatever it is, I press play and only sound comes out of the right ear bud. I kid you not this happens 60% of the time. I then I have to go put them back in the case, try and reconnect (the process which is not efficient at all) and hope they then work. Even after doing that, I find that once connected and the pop up of battery life comes up, my right ear bud is fully charged and the left one is dead. The case is so poorly designed with the charging ports so tiny that you have to place the left ear bud just right in order to make a connection to charge. I've literally never had this issue with the right ear bud, only the left.

So between not being able to connect, to having it not be charged after being on the charger or in the chargeable case for several hours, I pick up my old trusted $30 sony extra bass wired headphones and get going with whatever it is I was doing.

Not to mention... the sound is not good at all. I have to have the volume up near 80% to even try and block out some noise around me or to have a volume which I like while at the gym. For reference, those same sony headphones would give me the same output at just 40-50% volume. While not the best for my hearing, I wear headphones while cutting the grass, even at absolute full volume these $200 headphones are barely loud enough to hear the music, again my sony headphones are at 75% volume when cutting grass.

title: Do Not Buy These Buggy Headphones
text:
I purchased the Powerbeats Pro over a year ago after having gone through several other headphones that Wirecutter recommended and failed to survive my extreme sweat from my runs. While the Powerbeats Pro do survive the sweat, they are a pain to use with my Apple Watch Series 3.

My first largest complaint is they tend to fail to connect and charge in their case. I frequently have to jiggle, re-orient, and apply pressure to the headphones in their charge case before I get a successful connection and even then they can jiggle loose from minimal movement. This means sometimes I go to start my run and have one or two dead earbuds.

Second even when they seem to have charged they do not effectively auto-connect out of the case. I often find myself taking the earbud out of the case, hearing nothing in my ear, and then having to place it back in the case and take it out again before it turns on.

Third the wireless connectivity with the Apple Watch Series 3 is poor. Using WatchOS 8.3 I will directly connect the headphones to listen to my music on my run. It often takes multiple attempts for Apple Watch to successfully connect to the headphones. When it does succeed it will work while in my home, but then lose the connection again as I start my run once I'm out of range of my home WiFi and iPhone. I have to then fiddle with the watch to reconnect them. It will then lose the connection when I return and am back in range of my iPhone. I am not sure if this is the fault of the watch, the headphones, or Apple, but it sure fails to live up to my expectations.

Overall if you're willing to tolerate these annoyances they are great when they work. But I would not recommend them with all these annoyances. Save yourself the pain and get AirPods Pro or something.

title: Don't buy...not worth it
text:
Top dollar means there shouldn't be ANY ISSUES right? Well, that wasn't the case. Nothing like getting ready for a good run or a good workout after a long day of work to find out one of your earphones is at 0% battery life while the other one is at nearly 100%.

In summary, DO NOT BUY THESE THINGS! They are extremely expensive, and you deserve so much more for such a steep price. I exchanged them at an electronic store, and the tech support member said that he has these earphones as well, and he has the same problems. He agreed with my position that they simply aren't worth it.

You'll get a phone call, and the earphones will randomly connect to your phone call when they're no where near your resting in the dock case, They won't charge correctly, and the dock seems to be faulty as it doesn't always connect with your phone. They're crap. Get the previous model beats that have the cord ear to ear. Those are great. I exchanged them.

title: Cannot get it repaired at an Apple Store!
text:
The most important thing that no one tells you (or told me) is that Powerbeats Pro, while having excellent connectivity with Apple devices just like Airpods, cannot be repaired at an Apple store. You have to wait for it to be shipped to an Apple/Beats repair center, get fixed, and shipped back to you, and mostly they just get replaced not repaired. If you're having an issue in the first year, it will get replaced for free. If it's the second year and you had money to splurge to buy Apple Care after spending $250 on freaking earphones, then it will cost you an additional $29 for the replacement. If they do decide to fix them instead of replacing them, you are looking at $99 for fixing EACH earpiece. NO THANK YOU.

I have been using apple products for years without ever needing Apple Care because I am careful with them and trust the quality of Apple. Not this time. Apple has GOT TO improve their customer service and not drain the life out of their loyal customers.
This is strike 1.

Oh, and the connection is spotty with no voice cancellation. Maybe it's just a "Beats" thing. Apple should ditch pairing with them asap.

title: Minor nitpicks on ear fit and Bluetooth connectivity
text:
I really enjoy these earphones. They have a solid amount of battery, the case is sleek and I've enjoyed running with them a lot, whether I'm listening to podcasts or music, it does the job. On calls, people hear me just fine and have not had any difficulties.

Here are my nitpicks: ear fitting and Bluetooth connectivity

My right earpiece fits differently than my left, so I had to change the earbud size. I guess my right ear is just shaped differently and had discomfort with all of the earbud sizes that they offer. It's not terribly sore, but enough that on runs longer than 45min, I can feel it.

Bluetooth connectivity sometimes fails and I have to reset it by putting it back in to the case, holding down the case button for 5 seconds, and then reconnecting. This doesn't happen too often, and it's the fault more so on BT technology than the earphones themselves. It's just an inconvenience, but they still work perfectly fine.

text: These are epically bad, unfortunately.  Sound great - and I really wanted them to work - but I've given up. The tiny prongs that charge these things are so sensitive that the MAJORITY of the time you go on your workout or activity and get sound on one side.  They are that sensitive, that maybe they appear to be charging and then they stop at some point and one side is dead.  The interface to the phone that allows you to check battery life isn't right either- it will show both at full green when one side is dead.  Sometimes the simplest method is best- could have solved this with a simple micro USB plugin or 3.5mm to charge instead of trying to be fancy.  Don't believe me?
