title: Well polished product that works just fine
text:
A few weeks ago my original BackBeat FIT started failing when charging, so I decided to get a new pair of earbuds.

I've tried purchasing a couple of other wireless earbuds before getting the Powerbeats Pro, but the other ones were not to my satisfaction. There were multiple reasons, but the main ones that made me return them were:

1) Not being able to easily switch connection between previously paired devices. My original BackBeat FIT was great in this regard because I could just go to the Bluetooth menu of a previously paired device, click on the earbud device's name, and voila, the connection would switch from whatever other device the earbuds were connected to. I was surprised to see that other expensive and well renouned modern earbuds couldn't do this at all! Some of them let you do that through their app, but that's cumbersome and also the app itself might not work very well.
2) App integration felt subpar. I had never used earbud apps to be frank, so when I used them for these two earbuds that I ended up returning I was surprised to see how bad the apps worked. Things like misreporting the status of the earbuds or not being able to find them would happen all the time. Also the fact that I have an Android phone and an iPad seemed to have thrown a bit of extra confusion in for these apps.

The Powerbeats Pro earbuds, on the contrary, work just fine. I own an Android phone (Pixel XL 2) as well as an iPad, and I was afraid I'd have connection or integration issues on Android, since I had heard mixed reviews on this regard. But that's not what I'm experiencing. I can easily switch my connection between my phone and my tablet and the Powerbeats Pro app works perfectly.

title: Extreme disappointment
text:
These headphones under perform and under deliver for their price tag.

Frustration #1 - Connectivity
I connected the head phones to several devices, placed the device in my pocket, and started my workout. With every device they would cut in and out several times during my workout, like I was tuning an AM radio. This happened with all my devices and they are Apple products which should pair and connect seamlessly.

Frustration #2 - Charging
The charging case has a long battery life and a cool design. The flaw is that the earbuds are difficult to get into the perfect spot to charge them. Once you do get them in the right spot do not jar the case around in any way. On several occasions I would pull them out and one of the buds would be dead. I could never throw them in a bag without worry of them popping out of their charging station.

Frustration #3 - Volume
The sound and bass are great, but the volume level lacks. I put in a $50.00 pair of Bose wired headphones and I get more volume from them. These headphones are great in an empty room, but put them in on a subway or gym setting with ambient noise and good luck hearing your music.

Frustration #4 - The amount of refurbished and refreshed Powerbeat Pros on the market. Simply Google - Powerbeats Pro Refurbished and you will see every major supplier with thousands of these waiting for a sucker to buy. I bought a brand new pair that I am hoping are a lemon, but I am sending them into Apple for them to "repair". I will now get a refreshed pair of headphones that I paid full price for. There is a reason there are so many refurbished pairs of these on the market....They just are not made well and have tons of issues.

Frustration #5 - The volume rocker is nice, but the stupid pause/play and change song button is annoying. It is a cheap button and if you change songs you push the earbud deeper into your ear and moving the earpiece off your head. Again, unless you are sitting in an empty room not moving...but I think these are marketed for people on the move.

Pro #1 - They do sit in and around your ear nicely. I haven't found a better pair yet that does this, but if they don't stay connected, don't stay charged, don't have enough volume...It doesn't matter.

I recommend purchasing a refurbished pair because there are thousands of them on the market, for a good price, and if you buy a new pair there is a good chance they will be sending you a refurbished pair after your new ones don't work properly. Happy Shopping!

title: The last Powerbeats headphones I will ever buy
text:
I bought the Powerbeats Pro, directly from Apple, on February 24, 2020.

After less than 2 month, the right earbud stopped charging, therefore working. After calling Apple's support number, I was directed to their authorized service center, where I was informed that the reason why the earbud stopped charging is that there is corrosion on the contacts. Corrosion isn't covered by their warranty, therefore the only option left would be to repair it at my own expense, for a price that is about 45% of the cost of buying a new set.

I tried to call Apple again as, in my opinion, this is clearly a case that should be covered by warranty. I bought these earbuds for running since they are advertised as "Sweat & water resistant earphones" on their official web site. I have used these headphones approximately 10 times, never in the rain, and always placed them back in their carrying case once I reached home. I never dunked them or exposed them to water, never used any detergent or chemicals to clean them. The Apple representative claimed that it is likely that my sweat was the cause for the corrosion on the contacts. Yet, in spite of the fact that they are advertised as "sweat resistant", they claim that I am responsible for the "damage". Anybody who has ever dealt with Apple and their bullying will be aware of how pointless it is to argue with them, regardless of how unreasonable their claims are.

The earbuds were actually ok for the extremely short amount of time they worked. The sound was decent, the pairing with an iPhone was effortless, the signal strong. Do you ever plan on using them for running, or in an environment where they might be exposed to humidity? Then don't bother, because they will stop working very quickly and Apple won't really give a damn.

title: Tedious and finicky devices.
text:
The best thing about these ear buds is the fact that they stay in your ear extremely well. That’s it. That’s the best thing. Everything else is not so great. They don’t really sound that good. They don’t really cancel noise beyond the effects of having little pieces of rubber stuck in your ear. But the most annoying problem with this product is the way that it charges.

The connection between the earbuds and the charging dock are these tiny little metal contacts, and they have to be aligned precisely in order for them to charge. If it’s off by a little bit it won’t charge, and there isn’t really any way to let you know that you’ve done it properly. There is know click, or any other physical sensation that would let you know it’s seated properly. The buds just sit inside the dock. I will say that it does work most of the time, like 8 or 9 times out of ten. But often I’ll get up in the morning to go for a run and I’ll put them in my ear after they’ve been sitting in the charger overnight only to discover one wasn’t seated properly and is now dead.

Another thing that I’ve had to work around is when I first got them, I would grab the buds from the charging dock, put them in my ear, then drive to a park or somewhere to go for a run and then try and play something from my phone only to discover that only one ear bud was connected. The only way to reconnect was to place the earbuds back in the charging dock (which was back at home), close the lid on the dock, then open it and grab the buds and put them back in my ears. So I know have to double check they are connected to my device before each time I go anywhere with them.

For what they cost and the brand that they are, I’m pretty disappointed with how they perform. I feel like they shouldn’t be so hard and tedious of a thing to use.

title: unreliable and frustrating
text:
The Powerbeats Pro sound fine - you'll need to use one of the EQ settings your phone to overcome the tinniness of the highs on this set, but that's not that big of a deal. they are quite secure when running.

The real issues lie with reliability. They will often charge when you place them in the charging case. Even if you carefully and methodically place them in the case and make sure that they are charging....and then do not move them at all, you can return the next morning to a completely uncharged ear pod. The charge display on the phone is also unreliable, so you often need to spend several minutes to make sure that the charging is actually in process (again, that often doesn't matter). The design of the charging box seems to be a fault: the connecting points on the case are not precisely enough designed to accommodate the headphones. I mean, I guess that's what's going on? As I have typed this review I have watched the charge start and stop three times. I reset it and then it stops again.

Also, even when charged it is often the case that only one headphone will sync to your phone. When that happens, it seems that the only way forward it to entirely re-pair your set. That isn't that difficult, but you need to have the charging case with you to accomplish that. If you put them on and start a run without music only to turn it on a bit later and have only one headphone working, then, well....you're out of luck.

These are issues you get with poorly constructed electronics regardless of how much they are sold for.

text:

title: Very disappointing, unintuitive, and not nearly worth the price
text:
These earbuds sound pretty decent when they work, which they rarely do. Half of the time sound will only come out of one, other times they won't connect at all. This is only fixed by putting them back in the box and holding down the pairing button for 15 seconds (why you need to hold it down for this long I do not know). That's right. If you want to pair or reset these things you better hope you have your box close to you because the only functionality they have without the box is play/pause and volume up/down. There is also no way to know if the earbuds are "on" or "off", or the battery left on them (unless you download the iOS app, which I can't because they don't have an Android version for whatever reason).

Odds are I just got a faulty pair, but even when they are working they are not nearly worth the price tag. They are frustrating to put on due to the clip and awkward angle of the earbuds, difficult to understand due to lack of controls or led lights, and the sound quality is average to slightly above average. Save yourself money along with headache and frustration and buy a different pair of wireless earbuds.

title: Generally happy with a couple issues
text:
TL;DR: Great fit, great sound but the charging can be touchy - and given the high price there really should be absolutely no issues.

About a year ago I took up running. At first I was using the standard apple wired headphones - but I found that due to the shape of my ears and the weight of the cord they kept falling out of my ears as I ran. The wire was also getting annoying.

I upgraded to a pair of cheap bluetooth headphones (wire connected) with an over-ear hook. They worked well - the earphone itself kept popping out of my ear but at least the hook kept them on my head. These lasted about a year before dying.

I was worried about the Powerbeats Pro earbuds - they're pretty expensive but I use headphones every day.

I've now had them for about a month and am really happy with a couple caveats.

The fit is great - they sit perfectly above and in the ear and don't "slide" out of the ear canal the way my previous headphones (both wired and wireless) do.

The sound is great - I'm not an audiophile but to me these sound as good as or better than any other headphones I've owned. When it's windy you can definitely hear the wind but it's not too bad and the volume gets as loud as I need.

The volume rocker is good - easy to use on either headphone - but the placement of the "play" button is exactly where I want to push to set the headphone into my ear. It's not a big deal because you can push them in by setting your fingers on the edge and pushing that way.

The headphones work great with my iPhone. Setup was trivial and the iPhone has extra features to make them more user friendly (for example battery level checking is real easy).

The one biggest downside is charging (there are a lot of complains online about this as well) - they come in a nice charging case and you pop them into the case to charge - but if you're not careful the contacts don't quite click and one or both of the headphones won't charge. The case will indicate if they're charging but there's no difference in indication between one or both charging - so if only one headphone didn't click in then you end up with an uncharged headphone the next day.

On my first set of these the left headphone was REALLY hard to get to charge - it had to be fiddled with VERY carefully while watching the phone to see that both headphones were actually charging - and if you closed the case it would pop out of the charging pads and stop charging (again with no indication). Also the left headphone drained twice as fast as the right one indicating that maybe it was just defective. I exchanged it and the new set (4 days in) seems to not be as finicky. I would write it off as a singular problem but looking online many people seem to have similar issues.

title: Purchased new but it was sold previously and dead on arrival
text:
Purchased a new powerbeats pro. Was having trouble syncing it to my phone, laptop, and a different phone. Called Amazon support which forwarded me to Apple support. When we checked on the serial number, the product was sold / registered over 9 months ago. Product is being sent back to Amazon for a replacement. Will update on a resolution / when new product arrives.

Update (July 2021): received the new set and have been using them for about a month now.

1) decent sound but it's only noise isolating and not noise canceling. Sound quality is not significantly superior vs much cheaper headsets.
2) on calls, I have been told that I sound like I was in a tunnel or far away from the mic
3) the earpiece has more of a 4 hr battery life vs the 9 hrs claimed.
4) the app requires for you to disclose your location : what for? Does it help someone locate me if I was in danger?
5) the case is bulky and there is no strap to it. The case is smooth (good and bad) as it is decent to the touch but can lose grip and slide out / drop the case easily.
6) no other way to secure / clip / strap the case, so it's very pocket dependent
7) lose connectivity to paired device pretty often. Although the re-pairing process is not tedious, it's not convenient either
8) the app doesn't give you a warning of low battery level (i.e give you a message once it's at 25%)
9) headset doesn't beep when it's low on battery so all you get is a surprise dead headset you have attached on your ear.

Overall : Meh

title: Awesome earbuds except for a serious flaw
text:
I want to love these headphones so much. For its first year, I did, and they really were perfect. 5 stars. The best form factor and fit - they’re great for working out, running, as well as taking long calls for work or play. I really do love this design. They fit so much better than other copycat over-the-ear designs. Simple, well-thought-out UI. Aficionados may nitpick about the sound, but I think it’s fine. Great battery life.

The serious flaw is there’s something wrong with the silicone material. Perhaps the sweat-resistant coating breaks down over time. I’m not sure. But after a year, I started getting really itchy ears. It was nasty, as my ear canals “crusted” up. Initially, it was only inside my ear. So I tried foam earbuds, and that helped for a while. But then the itch spread to other parts of my ear that was in contact with the headphones, where the hooks touched.

It’s really unfortunate as I think these are great headphones otherwise. I’m not alone - there’s a whole Reddit with others discussing the same issue. Unfortunate for me. Maybe others are luckier with less sensitive skin.

title: A short review, if you're trying to decide on buying this...
text:
I've been a music junkie for decades and have had many headphones/earbuds.
I'd give these a "4 1/2 stars out of five"

On the good side:

1) I use Tidal with Boom on my iPhone and I have over 200 GB of music on my phone. I had to tweak the sound settings on the Boom equalizer to get sound setting I want. Out of the box, I'd say the sound quality is good but not necessarily exceptional. But if you have an equalizer, odds are higher you'll be satisfied.

2) I've found that the battery life is indeed about 9 hours and the charging time is about what they advertise.

3) As for the fit: these are not going to fall out or slip (unless someone walks up to you and physically tries to pull them out). The fit is perfect. (See my notes further down for the "comfort")

4) I've rarely had problems pairing. I've used these nearly every day for a year and a half and have rarely had pairing issues with the iPhone. I can't speak for Android, as I don't use it.

OK, the "not so good" side:

1) The charging case does not support wireless charging.

2) The charging case is a tad large (in fairness, these buds are larger, hence the better battery life). You "can" put it in your pockets (pants) but you'll notice it.

3) OK, on the comfort: the human ear isn't designed to have something stuck into it for hours at a time without feeling the pressure. Yes, there are some buds that fit in a way that you won't feel the pressure, though I have to wonder what the downside is, as far as secure fit and seal.

Having said that, if I have these in my ears for more than 90 minutes, I sometimes need to take them out for a few minutes, just to let my ears "breathe".

Overall, give this 4.5 stars out of 5. The three things I mentioned are not "deal breakers" for me, but they might be if you are looking for something that will feel comfortable for hours. As much as I love these (and I do love them), I do need to pull them out for a few minutes.

Also, there is no ANC. Yes, there's "noise reduction" but not cancellation. I'm mainly in the suburbs and really don't have the need for ANC. However, it's always a personal choice, and if you spend a great deal of time in a noisy city/transportation system, you might want to look at the newest Bose.

So - these are not perfect. but they are very good and I'm happy with them. I love the battery life, the secure fit, and overall sound quality (after some tweaking). I listen to tons of jazz and classical and 70's rock and am happy with these.

I had a few wireless buds before these, and was always wondering if "the grass is greener" with another set. I have to be honest, after buying these, my interest in finding better ones down the road is much lower.

Most reviews I've read are positive on this product. Yes, a few negative ones, but mostly positive. I bought these when they were a bit pricier, and even though they've dropped the price a bit, I'm not angry - I really like them a lot.

It's really frustrating, the ear buds are pretty durable and I haven't had any sound issues through some ridiculous gym use. I requested a return once and the shipping box never showed up. The fix action from Apple is they have you send it in and then they send it right back to you without doing anything; again lots of folks having these issues from what I'm reading online. The Bluetooth connection for these is just miserable....spend your money elsewhere.

They are great headphones when they work. I don’t know how many times I’ve woke up in the morning to get in the gym just to discover that the left ear piece has decided not to charge and is inexplicably at zero percent. I use them almost
exclusively for the gym and they spend more time in the charger then they do on my head and miraculously they are constantly never charged despite carefully seating the ear pieces in the charging cradle. Connection issues are constant, but usually easy to fix...reconnecting these using the button on the charging case usually eliminates the problem when one ear bud decides it doesn’t want to hook up. I like the ruggedness of these ear buds and the sound is good all things considered, but I’m getting frustrated with how finicky these are to charge and connect. For the price I expected better performance in that area. Support for these is a bit lackluster...I initially experienced issues and was told to upgrade the firmware which I did using a website but was still having issues and ordered a return from the provider which never arrived. I’ve more or less just worked around the issues I am having to get use out of this product. I’d recommend waiting for a rework or the next iteration of this product before purchasing.

title: Pain, swelling, and oozing.  Product defective.
text:
The headphones worked as expected, for the first 2 months. Then, I developed a pretty severe allergic reaction to them. It took me a couple months to figure out what was causing the reaction, because I wear the earbuds so sporadically, and the reaction was not initially so severe but would last for days after wearing them. (Typically, for me, allergic reactions calm down after removing the allergen pretty quickly -- but not this time! So I thought it must be something environmental.)
These headphones caused contact dermatitis in my ear canal and the outside of my ear where the hook wraps around. On the same day as wearing the headphones my ear canals will swell nearly shut, then the itching and oozing starts. My ears leak liquid like crazy for a few DAYS, then it calms down but crusty irritated skin remains. It takes about a week to recover from wearing these.
The most frustrating thing is that Apple does NOT stand behind this product. They said that since I did not buy it directly from them I could not get a refund. Clearly, to me, since such a large number of customers are having reactions that make it unusable, the product is defective! I spoke on the phone to Apple for nearly an hour, and after giving them all these details including symptoms and serial number, they were like "Sorry, but there is nothing we can do, call Amazon." Then amazon puts me on hold for a half hour, and are like "sorry, return window closed."
This is COMMON reaction. Just google it. Don't risk your ears or your money.

title: If you like the PowerBeats line, you'll probably like this iteration
text:
Have owned the 2nd and 3rd iteration of this product and somehow always ended up in the lucky category. My PowerBeats 2 set lasted something like 3 years of daily, sweaty, abuse before I threw in the towel and got the 3s. The 3s lasted just a little over two years with the same kind of abuse and really had no problems at all until one day the over the ear piece just broke off (from the inside) of one of them. I had been sticking it back in to get some workouts in but one day it fell out without me noticing so they were officially unwearable.

Being a creature of habit, I just bought these. Yeah, they don't have noise cancelling capabilities. Yeah, sound wise they are a little subpar. That's always been the case for this line, in my opinion. For $200+ you could do better if that's what you're primarily concerned with. I think they sound fine for working out/walking through a city.

As for how these compare to the previous iteration: Totally wireless is nice. Forgot I had them on for awhile, at least until it got a little uncomfortable. These seem to be a tighter fit than the previous headsets, but maybe I just need to break them in and bend the over the ear piece a bit. I'm not a fan of the multi-touch button's placement at all. It's right over the ear canal, and pressing it presses the headset _further_ into my ear. I think they tried to offset this by making it light touch, but there have been some times where I can't tell if I pressed it or not.

Update 12/4:
So I swapped out the tips from the pointed/arrow-looking tips for the medium size ball and the multi-touch button problem has been fixed. I had used the arrow-tips on my last two pairs, maybe I've just been using the wrong ear piece this whole time.

I did run into an unexpected problem though. I assumed, wrongfully, that the auto-detect sensors would put the headset into a lower power/idle mode when I removed the earpieces. I left them on the table overnight and grabbed them on my way out to a two hour car appointment to find out that, nope, they don't turn off, and they had died overnight. They only turn off when they're in that rather bulky case. So that's not great.

title: Great True Wireless Earbuds
text:
Powerbeats Pro's are great products. They have good sound, great functions, and portability at an fair price tag.

Sound: The sound is great. but mainly because the fit and seal are good and because they have upgraded their hardware... (Powerbeats Pro use a 12mm rigid aluminum linear piston driver).

Tip: To get a good sound, make sure to use the correct tip size and the loops are adjustable to create better alignment into your ears.

Form and Function: I do like the sportier function as well as the look of these earbuds. These are thin and comfortable in the ear. I do like that they have 3 buttons on each earbud that works the same no matter which one you choose. They will also work independently of each other so if you need to have one ear in, you can choose which side to use. Most true wireless earbuds require the right side to be in if you want to use only one, or both.

Buttons: BEATS Logo
One click to play pause.
Two clicks to fast forward
Three clicks to go backwards.
Hold to invoke Siri

Volume Rocker
Volume up and volume down... simple

Price: there isnt much to say. It's in the upper price range of true wireless earbud prices, but for the company that makes them, the price seems fair.

Other notes: The case is gigantic. The case will still fit in your pocket, just not without looking obvious. The earbuds last 9 hours and the case will charge it to a total 24 hours of use. 5 minutes of charge in the case adds an additional 1.5 hours. The case does not have wireless charging. it will come with a black lightning cable.

Do your own test with songs you recognize, not just what other people say.

Enjoy!

title: Best multi-use headphones I’ve bought
text:
I bought my navy Powerbeats pro about 16 months ago, and they’re still my favorite headphones I’ve ever had. I will often use one at a time when I’m out walking or doing household chores so that I can still hear my surroundings through the other ear. They also auto-pause music when taken out of your ear (ex. To talk to someone).

I read reviews before purchasing that recommended swapping out the earbud size for the smallest one (provided in package). I did, and that helped tremendously with ear fatigue. I can regularly go 5-6 hours before my ears start to feel uncomfortable. The over-the-ear section has never once been uncomfortable, even while eating glasses. I’ve also never had them fall out of my ear, no matter what I was doing. My mask sometimes gets caught in the ear-loop section when I try to take it off, but that’s not an issue most the time I’m wearing them.

Battery life is great as well, and I have only had them die on me when I have used them for 5-6 hours straight. When they start to get low (they beep at you), I’ll take one out and start charging it in the case. By the time the first one dies, I’ll have another couple hours of battery in the charging one.

As for sound, I’ll be honest I’m not super picky, but it sounds great to me! When I have used them on phone calls, I have never gotten complaints about nearby noise, and people have always been able to hear me well. While these block out some sound by the nature of having headphones in, there is no active noise cancellation like in the AirPods Pro.

Another thing to note is that the charging case is not compatible with wireless charging devices, so you will need to plug it in to charge it. The case is usually good for 2-3 full charges of the headphones before it also needs to be recharged. The case is also larger than AirPods cases (about the size of my palm), so I don’t usually bring it with me when using the Powerbeats pro.

TLDR; great headphones, even a year in. Would recommend to anyone wanting a nice pair of wireless headphones and are worried about them falling out of their ear.

Pros: convenience, comfort, durability, battery life, stays in ear
Cons: no wireless charging, case is large, no active noise cancellation

title: Great budget Bluetooth earbuds.
text:
I work in a greenhouse. I wanted a Bluetooth earbud that sounded great, didn't completely block out sound (as i still talk to customers/coworkers) and was on the cheap. (In case I dropped or lost an earbud.) These are great! They come with 3 different sizes of earbuds tips (the middle size worked best for me ) the earbuds/case and a type C charge cord. After about 2 weeks of use, these are my findings.

Pros:
Great price $15-$20. The price fluctuates regularly.
Easy to connect. The second you pull an earbud out of it's case it automatically goes into pairing mode and connects to my phone.
All touch based, no buttons.
Easy to charge. If your case is charged, just toss your ear buds in and they'll charge. You'll know an earbud is charged if the little light is blue. I get about a weeks worth of use (alternating earbuds (left today, right tomorrow, etc) about 4 days a week for about 4-6 hours) before I need to charge the case.
Compact/small case.
Good sound. 4/5 Treble is good and the bass is deep.
Durable. I dropped an earbud from about 6-7 feet and watched it bounce a couple times. (Yes I totally freaked out lol) I picked it up, turned it on and it worked just fine. No visible scratches/dents either. 👍

Cons:
Battery life. Battery life for 1 bud ranges from 5-6 hours. That's with the bud connected to my phone listening to Pandora. Pausing occasionally to talk to other people. No skipping songs. You get a warning that the battery is low. Sometimes 1 warning, sometimes more. But once you get that warning, you've got less than 5 minutes before it turns off.
Fit. Sometimes when you turn your head, the sound drops out as a result of the shape of the earbud. The earbud tends to move from that perfect position and you have to adjust them a couple times an hour. (Obviously I have stretched ears, but that fact does not come into play in regards to the fit of this particular earbud.) I would wear these while working out in a gym setting, but I would not take them while running on the trail, bag work (boxing, etc) or anything rigorous. (I've yet to have an earbud fall out.)

All and all, I rate them a 4 out of 5. They serve their purpose as great budget Bluetooth earbuds that sound great and don't break the bank. Would definitely buy again. 🤘

title: Excellent fit, sound, and convenience... the mic? Not so much...
text:
[[VIDEOID:c34c9b94b53a62fb85a3c698e3f73a50]] Update: Added con for crackling at higher volumes.

I'll preface this by saying I've owned AirPods for two years now. I'm making that statement because I believe that, for 80% of consumers, these are an AirPods replacement or competing for the purchase decision. I'll list some basic pros and cons and try to keep it short.

- Cons:

CRACKLING
The sound quality is great when you’re in a quiet environment and can listen at medium volumes, but the second you step into a crowded coffee shop and need to pump it up to 75%, expect some crackling. I limit my phone’s max volume to 75%, and even at 90% of THAT I was hearing crackling while listening to... wait for it... classical piano -_-

THE MIC
The microphone on these is abysmal. I did a few side-by-side tests with these and the AirPods and the difference is immense. When talking with my family on the phone they continuously complain about the sound quality, being used to the AirPods up until now. While walking down the street, every little noise gets registered; cars, people, dogs, etc. Living in Seattle and using these at any capacity just doesn't work (especially in the heart of the city).

THE FIT
This one is probably subjective, but I did experience a bit of ear soreness (in the cartilage, not my inner ear canal) after extended use. I use my AirPods almost all day and never experience soreness. I will say, though, that they are wonderful for running. I went on three 4-mile runs using these and never had any issues with the seal coming loose.

- Pros:

THE SOUND / NOISE ISOLATION
The sound quality here is well above what the AirPods can produce. This can mostly be attributed to the full seal that the silicon buds create in your ear canal. All things considered, I enjoyed my music quite a bit more, as well as the isolation from ambient noise outside, than the AirPods.

THE BATTERY
Holy moly these things last forever. 9 hours is the rated lifespan on one charge, and I can attest to that. I went through a whole day at work without placing them back in the case.

THE CONVENIENCE
They function identically to the AirPods in terms of usage with Apple devices. They pair almost instantly (faster than my AirPods in most cases), and have an extremely long bluetooth range... However, that's where the convenience ends. To pair them with anything other than an Apple device can be a nightmare. Instructions say to hold the button inside the case, with the Beats seated, until it pulses white. I did this and my computer would not recognize them. It wasn't until I took the Beats OUT of the case while the light was pulsing that I got a connection. Good thing almost everything I have is an Apple device.

Conclusion:
These are great headphones. There's a reason they are rated higher than almost all other truly-wireless earbuds on the market. However, due to the nature of my work and the frequency that I am on the phone with other people, I cannot justify using this product over the AirPods. They're fantastic for exercise and music, and the convenience of them working with Apple products, including Apple TV, is incredible. I think I'll just stick to my little white bulbs.

text: I'm sad to say that I am disappointed with these earbuds. I was excited based on reviews and will say that when they first arrived, my immediate impression was very favorable. They were super comfortable when I first put them in, and the noise cancelling quality is pretty high. Then I took them out for a spin, and my impression significantly changed. They didn't stay in as well as I'd initially thought they would. The last fifteen minutes of my hour-long walk, I was constantly pushing them back in and one even fell out entirely. They are difficult to work, with the touch points being very finicky. I found myself answering calls I didn't want to, unable to answer calls, and had a difficult time controlling the volume. Perhaps most annoying, is that they pick up a ton of background noise for the person on the other end of the call. There's was a very VERY mild breeze, and I was told it sounded like I was in a wind tunnel. They could also hear all the conversations and noises going on around me, making for very difficult and frustrating conversations. I'm sorry to say that I am extremely disappointed and will be returning these asap.

title: Connectivity experience is really bad and buggy
text:
I bought them as they were very well reviewed and needed some earphones with hang-thingies.

That is the only pro of these earphones. Sounds quality is good enough for me, not for others.
Connecting via bluetooth is a serious nightmare.
Out of nowhere they will stop playing my Spotify music while still connected. Getting them to play again requires me to turn them off and on again.
Discord and normal calls get very buggy (input and output devices switch every time!).
None of these points happened with my old 20$ earphones I bought a few years ago.

For the price specially, I was not expecting them to be this bad.

Update: They turn themselves on after removing them from the box. Problem is, the connectivity from earbud-box is really bad, so there are times where I take them off and one of the buds did not even turn on, so I have to either go back to the box to turn them on (!!!!!!!) or just not use them. This problems also affects charging, as there are days where I leave them to charge but I forget to check if they are really charging, because the connectivity is stunningly bad.

Anyway, after just a few months, one of the earbuds just gave up, no longer working. Part of me is happy because I will be moving on from these, but man were they expensive.

title: Sound quality better than expected
text: The earbuds are a little smaller than most other models I tried and these fit my ear well.  This is very important because I listen to audio books and classical music a lot and tightly fitted earbuds would be uncomfortable after a while.  I wasn't looking for noise canceling feature in my earbuds because I also need to hear some level of the sound around me while I enjoy my audio books and music.  The battery life is as described, not particularly long as some other models, but it's adequate for my usage since I would be putting them back in the charging case after 5-6 hours of usage in a day in general (other activities occupy my time and I need my focus), and they get charged up again.  These are cheap enough that you can get multiple ones for different rooms (family room, bed room, kitchen).  When paired with TV, however, there is noticeable latency even when it said "low latency" in the description.  So I use a different headphone that works with RF signals (not bluetooth signals) which doesn't have any latency issues.  The sound quality is very good and the price makes it a great value.

text:
These headphones were "okay." For 20 dollars, these are not worth purchasing, however.
Over the course of one month, the batter life has noticeably shortened from it's initial advertised time.
It's audio quality isn't great, but it's not bad.
It's feel in my ear was bad. I would change out the earbud tip but the spare tips were leagues too small for these buds, not to mention that the buds themselves are tiny compared to most I've owned.
Even further, the tips that do fit have left small marks on the insides of my ears.

In addition, the "controls" on the sides of the buds make little sense. They use touch sensors, yet use that for increasing/decreasing volume, pausing and powering on or off. And, because they're so small, my already thin fingers can't use the volume control and pause features without triggering the other a quarter of the time.

The cherry on top is that these headphones have what I assume is a Chinese accent.

Overall terrible headphones for long term use.

title: Disappointed: Not working with Windows 11(Updated: Problem Fixed)
text:
I got these mini earbuds yesterday and was so excited. It worked well with my android phone. I've never imagined the incompatibility of this Bluetooth with Windows 11. Windows is the most commonly used OS. How come this Bluetooth device doesn't work with it? I googled this issue and found that many people have been complaining about the incompatibility of these earbuds. If you're looking for earbuds working with a laptop/desktop Windows11, you should find something else.
(10/19/2022)
------------------------------------
Update (10/21/2022): I did research more about this issue after writing my first review. I've even thought about downgrading from Windows 11 to Windows 10. I'm glad I didn't do it because I didn't want to get any troubleshooting of not pairing these earbuds with Windows 10 either.

The issue was simply solved. When I first tried to pair them with a laptop, I was using earbuds with my phone. Even though I disconnected Bluetooth in my phone to pair them with Windows 11, it didn't work.
However, today I took the earbuds out of the case and automatically powered them on. Windows 11 could find this device. Successfully paired!

title: Decent, cheap, and portable earbuds
text:
For context, I already own a pair of Sony XM4s, which I use the most around the house and for listening to music. However, even though they come with a travel case, I did not feel comfortable lugging them around everywhere, especially since they are so expensive. So, I was in the market for some cheap and portable earbuds I could carry anywhere and not worry about losing them.

The earbuds have a fairly small case, which is nice, although the hinge is a bit cheap and might break after some use. The actual shape of the earbuds is comfortable and stays in the ear, probably even when running (although I haven't checked). There is no active noise canceling, and the sound quality is aggressively mediocre. They are suitable for watching youtube, etc., and sound better than cheap wired headphones, but I still wouldn't listen to music for extended periods with them.

For my use case (mostly just listening to videos on my phone), they work pretty well, especially for the price. However, if you're looking for a "daily driver" pair of headphones that you wear all the time, I would spend some more money, especially if you listen to a lot of music. You really can hear the difference.

Then again, for 17 bucks, there really is not that much to lose. I honestly couldn't care less if these break in a year anyway. They work, they're cheap, and they're small, so they fit the bill.

title: The KBEAR KS1 of bluetooth earbuds, pleasantly surprised!
text:
Keep in mind, these are <$20 wireless earbuds (when purchased in Jan 2023)...
The earbuds are a reasonable size, have reasonable battery life, and reasonable sound quality. As you'd expect, these can't compete with more premium offerings, but for the price, these can't be beat!
It was not long ago that I remember paying <$25 would get me a pair of massive, bulky earbuds that hurt to wear (both from poor sound quality and fit in ears), which would mysteriously stop working a week later. The Tozo earbuds prove that this is no longer true.
Pairing on the buds is seamless, and the touch sensors work well and are much better than tactile buttons. Amazon seems to want to rate these based on noise canceling, but these have no ANC, so the minimal noise cancelation comes from the physical fit, which will depend on your ear shape. The case charges via a USB C port, which is always a welcome addition. If you aren't after high end sound quality or just want a backup pair of earbuds, I highly recommend these, they are the KBEAR KS1 of bluetooth earbuds!

title: Best “boom” for your buck.
text: I own the A1’s, T6’s, and T12’s and Tozo’s wireless charging pad. The T12 buds are pretty large for earbuds, but has the best sound quality of the 3 and excellent bass. Largest case. The T6 is right in the middle of the 3 for size, sound quality and case size. It actually may be smaller than the A1 case, and is the easiest to open especially in a pitch black room. The A1 is my favorite because the sound quality is still very good, most compact buds, and the case is a nice design. However it doesnt seem to work on the tozo wireless charging pad like the T6 and T12 case. I will try again, it might have been fully charged when i tried. A little “lip” tab would be nice to pry the lid open easier. The A1’s are the easiest to lay on your side in bed with while watching youtube or listening to music trying not to wake a loved one. I DO NOT like the particular voices used that say “power on, connected” etc. They all have different voices with different accents, almost as if english is a second language for the narrator. Still, 5 stars from me, Tozo is one of the best bang for your buck for earbuds. Also, I should add that the T6’s survived and trip through the clothes wash machine not in the case..

title: Very fussy and aggravating product
text:
Yes it is a cheap alternative to airpods, but there are a lot of aspects to this product that are very annoying:

-Adjusting the earbuds in your ear, or even so much as grazing them with your finger, will prompt them to pause your music. This is especially obnoxious when the design so easily slips out of your ear and uses a practically worthless suction thing that doesn't keep the product in place.

-Whose bright idea at the company was it to program a loud voice to tell you "MAX VOLUME" every time you turn the volume up on your phone to the top. This is no unnecessary. Obviously it is at max volume if you aren't hearing it get louder. Not only does it disrupt the music you're listening, it doesn't even pause the track while interrupting. Usually I turn up the volume on a song because I'm really vibing to it and the last thing I want to is hear this lady's voice telling me "MAX VOLUME" and breaking the track's magic.

-Connecting the earbuds to your bluetooth will often only connect to one ear and not the other. And then trying to get the other bud to work requires some sort of trickery with an invisible button on the product that doesn't always work, and also apparently just turns it off?

title: Lasted only 63 hours
text:
I bought this item LITERALLY 35 days ago, on 8/18, to use while on the bus going to work and back home. I’m not a teenager who lives connected to the phone via earbuds day in and out. I ONLY used them while on the bus – I put them on once I sat down and always removed them before getting off because I liked them so much that I was terrified one would fall while getting off the bus or when crossing the street and a car would run over it.

NOTE: You have 30 days to return or exchange and the first day starts on order date. I requested these on Thursday Aug 18th , they arrived Friday Aug 19th, I set them up on Sunday Aug 21st, and officially began using them on Monday Aug 22nd – 1.5 hours in the morning, going to work, and 1.5 hours in the pm, going home. So… 5 workdays a week, 21 workweek days from when I officially began using them to when the left earbud died this past Monday (9/19) is a total of 63 hours. That is how long these lasted. And I’m being generous with giving them 1.5 extra hours of life.

At first, they were AWESOME. Wow! They worked amazing. The depth of sound was lovely. No cheap sound at all! Now, I am so so SO disappointed - because I can't have them exchanged (I did want the same item, just in proper working condition), and because they were so awesome in the beginning and ended up being junk in such a short time. Should have stuck to my usual, old fashion, $9 JVC Gumy wired earbud headphones - inexpensive, reliable, decent sound, and long lasting.

Many people have had a good experience. I was one of the unlucky ones. If you decide to buy these, keep in mind the return period, and really, really use them to make sure you didn’t get a lemon.

title: Samsung Buds Alternative for Great Price
text:
Coming from a pair of Samsung Galaxy Buds (original) that I got for $10 and lost, it's hard to spend $60 on a replacement. I will say, I think these are an excellent alternative for the price. There are some feature losses and oddly enough one major bug fix.

For starters, these have great sound so far. If you're looking for a song to stress test these with and you're not an audiophile (I am not), "I'm So Sorry" by Imagine Dragons is an excellent start. It picks up the bass drops and doesn't tear, but the lyrics are also nice and clear. It's a pair of $20 wireless earbuds, so don't expect something amazing, but compared to Samsung's AKG offering, it's on par if not better. They're still brand new though. The distance seems to be on par with the Samsung Buds too.

You will lose the Buds app, so you can't change the sound equalization (unless you use TOZO's very poorly rated app) or disable noise cancellation or locate your earbud. Honestly, disabling noise cancellation kinda defeats the point, so it's not really something that I ever used. I also installed a frequency generator app that can play sufficiently loud tones to locate an earbud, even better than Samsung's locator. The sound is actually pretty good for all scenarios in my opinion. If you really need equalization, there are other ways to do that from the Android side.

These actually fixed a major bug with the original Samsung Buds. The Buds or Android updated in a way to make the audio drop when using HD audio, which is enabled by default every time a bud is connected. These earbuds do not have that flaw, which has made me very happy.

These have two flaws in my opinion. They do not have proximity sensing to pause when removing from your ear (and can be activated in the pocket). They also require you to wear both buds to use all of the touch features. If you only use one at a time, you're limited when it comes to prev/next as they're bud-dependent. Having no app, you have no way to reconfigure that. I should note that I have not tried their app because I don't want to risk breaking the buds. They're working just fine as is with expected flaws for the price. These are not deal breakers in any way.

I will say, they are fairly small and very smooth. If you have small hands, you may have issues with them. I even have some issues, but I wouldn't say that's necessarily a flaw. They are pretty cool to feel because they're really smooth, but it isn't necessarily the best design choice for something so small and intended to be handled. They don't have that annoying rubber ring that the Samsung Buds do.

One other point that may irk people that I don't really care about is wireless charging. I don't use the flat wireless chargers, so I always have to find a prop for a case like this to hit the charge point. I don't really care enough to be annoyed that I can't wirelessly charge these. It's a nice feature, but if it increases the price, I don't think it's worth it. They charge fast enough and last long enough that worrying with wireless charging isn't really a huge concern to me.

Overall, they seem like an excellent alternative to the original Samsung Buds and probably ever iteration of every big name brand wireless earbud with charging case. Hopefully I won't have to contact customer support, but I hear they're lovely, so that might not be too bad.

With the design of the how the earbuds fit in the charging case, I found myself fumbling the earbuds in my fingers more often than not, as I removed them from the charging ports --- I would take extra precaution where you are when trying to remove them (i.e. are you near a vent, sewer, at a high elevation, etc?). That said, they are very light weight which is a plus. The charging case itself is good and closes securely. In addition, they earbuds themselves fit snuggly in the ears.

title: Great product that actually stays in your ear
text:
This is a wonderful set of earbuds. Here's my breakdown:
-Size - for really small ears like mine, where not a single other earbud I tried stays in my ear, these earbuds are amazing. They really stay in, no matter what! And they come with 4 different size tips (the 1 that's on the earbud and 3 other sets) to fit anyone. I needed the smallest size for it to comfortably fit.
-Comfort - They are really quite comfortable and very small and non-intrusive. I wouldn't say they are perfectly comfortable and I can't wear them for hours, but honestly I don't expect that anything in my ear would feel perfectly comfortable. I just wore them for a 35 minute phone conversation and my ears felt fine during and afterwards. Any other earbud I tried hurt my ears.
-Sound quality and volume - When I wear both earbuds it's great. When I wear 1 earbud (which I do most of the time because I need to hear what's going on around me and it's more comfortable for me), it's very good but a little lower and slightly less quality. There are probably earbuds out there with better quality but I don't feel like I'm compromising much (especially for the price). Also the smallest earbud tips don't fully block out outside noise, which for me I'm happy with - makes it more comfortable too and not like I'm underwater- but others might not like that. When I tried 1 size up it did block out the noise better, which likely means it fits my ear more fully, but I chose to go smaller for comfort. (Yes, my ears are pretty sensitive.) Another thing to mention is that often when I hang up from a phone call, the earbuds often stay on "playing" mode and make a tinny noise repeatedly until I "pause" it manually from my phone. I'm not sure how to resolve that issue, it could be the earbuds need to be reset.
-Microphone - for me this was most important because I mainly need earbuds for phone calls. So far everyone has been hearing me just fine, with only occasional requests to repeat myself. And this is with me walking around and doing alot of housework and other things while talking. The only complaint I got from 1 person on the other end was that they heard all the noise from what I was doing as well. Meaning, the mic picked up loud rustling, talking from others, etc. Quiet noises were not picked up.
-Ease of bluetooth connection - very easy. There's literally nothing to it once you connect the first time.
-Using the touch area for functions - firstly, I love that it's not too sensitive to touch - ie. you can't accidentally hang up on someone or mistakenly switch songs. It's also bulky enough around the sides that it's easy to take out of your ear or adjust it without touching the touch area. That being said, you have to really touch the whole touch area to do different functions so it might take an extra try. It takes a bit of practice to get the hang of using the touch area - like knowing when to tap once, twice, 3 times, or tap and hold, and for which function. I am also a bit limited because I use 1 earbud (ex. for volume you tap and hold the L earbud to lower it and do the same for the R earbud to raise it). So far it's working to use 1 or 2 functions and do the rest from my phone, and I'll add more as I get used to it.
-Instructions - the instructions are not fully inclusive and clear but they are clear enough for you to get the hang of using the earbuds. They also have good instructions with pictures of the correct way to position them in your ear, which I found helpful.
-So far I've not had to charge the earbuds at all, but I only had them for a few days and didn't use them too much so it's hard to know what the battery life is.
Overall, a great buy and I look forward to using these buds for awhile.

title: Good Headphones. Great Customer service
text:
I like the Tozo A1s, they are small, very portable, with good sound quality, and noise cancellation. The bass leaves a bit to be desired but is expected from such a small device. The battery lasts very long on a single charge. I fell asleep with them in once, and when I woke up the next morning, they were still at half charge. The charging case itself charges very quickly about 20 minutes or so and lasts about a week without needing to be charged.

As for customer service, the set of Tozo A1s I received worked great for a few weeks but then all of a sudden cut out in the right ear. I messaged customer service and a nice and helpful person named Nicole took me through steps to attempt to rectify the issue. Each time a workaround failed she responded promptly with a new attempted fix. When all else failed, they sent me a new set, free of charge and shipped immediately even though it was the holidays. All in all, a great company I would purchase from again.

text:
For the price these seemed like they were worth taking a chance on and for the initial pair I had, and the subsequent replacements, they were great...for less than a week.

First off the praise. Both pairs of these I had sounded great but I guess it's a case of you get what you pay for. So yeah, the price is great and they sound really good, when they work, but they have to continue to work to be useful.

For the initial pair, after one day of use the left earpiece began to drop audio and then eventually wouldn't work at all. I unpaired and reconnected the earpieces with multiple devices and made certain there was enough battery charge but nothing would fix the left earpiece.

I ordered a return and decided on an exact replacement figuring the audio issue was a one off but unfortunately not. Within a few days/less than a week of use of the replacement, the right earpiece started having the same problem. I used the same steps as before to try and fix the issue but nope, so these are going back and I will absolutely not be getting a replacement, nor will I buy another product from TOZO.

Perhaps it was just bad luck with the two pair I had but when considering it was the same overall issue that happened within days of use...nah, guess I'll spend a few dollars more and hopefully get something that continually works.

title: These earbuds are hurting my ears
text:
I got the tozo a1 as a cheaper alternative of earbuds since I always lose an earbud. I usually get the tribit flybuds 3. Although the tozo a1 is a good purchase for the price, I have a few complaints about them.
The sound quality on the tozo a1 is clean and doesn't have static which is pretty good for the price. The sound sometimes sounds low or flat but that that could be only me because I like booming sound and bass. The a1s have a annoying loud voice that tells the user low battery, power on off, etc. I personally hate the voices in earbuds and prefer beeps. On the a1s, you touch the earphones once (not twice which would be better) to play and pause songs which is annoying when you accidentally touch them. The a1s takes a few seconds to connect to your phone and doesnt connect as fast as other earbuds. The ear buds are small enough for people who have small ears like me. I was very happy with the small size but these earbuds are causing blisters and irration in my ears. I think its due to the angle of the ear tip and the stiff plastic eartips. I usually keep an earbud in my ear for long periods of time but other earbuds I have owned haven't caused blisters in my ears.
These earbuds are a great cheap option for people who aren't picky about earbuds and don't need to use the headphones for long times. But if you have a earbud popped in like me, you will get sore and blistered ears.

In fact, they are so great that I can’t hear my co-workers when they try to communicate with me. LOL (hidden benefit!) The only thing I cannot review is the battery life at this point since I just got them, but I like the charging case that came with them. They were incredibly easy to pair with my phone and immediately start listening. They automatically start playing music when I fit the right one into my ear which was a nice treat. It is also very easy to utilize the pause and volume buttons. I like that both ear pieces have the same controls.

Back to the case—I read some reviews that the case was too large, but I disagree. I could easily carry this case with me in a pocket... maybe I just buy clothes that have normal sized pockets though? Maybe trendier clothes have smaller pockets.

The last comment is about the design...I love how secure they are! I’ve never found ear buds that would actually stay in place. I have smaller ear canals, so apple air pods would never work, nor would any normal pair of ear buds stay in, especially when working out. title: Long Term Results Powerbeats Pro
text:
For 250 USD, Apple is making a killer profit on these ear buds while the customer is getting minimal value. The craftsmanship is no where near the Apple buds. I have had the opportunity to use the Powerbeats for a year during workouts (HIIT, Run, Bike, Free weights) and general use and the below are the positives and negatives.
Postitives: 1) Good sound quality 2) They fit securely in ear (especially during workouts).
Negatives: 1) Cheap plastic feel 2) Loose fit inside case - the buds don't always make contact with the charging connector. Thus, when you are ready to work out; one or both buds have no charge. 3) On occasion, one or both buds fail to connect bluetooth. You have to reconnect to your buds to your phone to resolve. 4) High Price.
For the above negative reasons, I can only give 2 stars - and that is being generous.

title: An awful experience with my iphone
text:
Good lord where do I begin. First off the way they fit in your ear is just bad, they fall out within 5 minutes of use even when sitting still not doing anything, if you want these to stay in your ear you HAVE to buy silicone guards that have an ear hook. Second off the software integration with iPhone is terrible, 90% of the time when I pull the earbud out to listen to something it just won’t connect, you have to manually go into Bluetooth and connect it and even then sometimes it won’t connect. Half the time it won’t give you an actual cue or noise that the battery is going to die, it’ll just randomly die without any noise or anything making you think the video just stopped. Speaking of low battery holy crap these headphones have the most annoying use of low battery banners when using the your iPhone with these. You’ll be watching a video and every 2 seconds a banner covering the top portion of your screen will come up showing “% of battery left” from 19% to when they die. And when you look at the battery percentage in settings it constantly switches from 100% to whatever the actual percentage it is over and over causing the banners to pop up which gets very annoying if you want to see what other notifications you have and then you can’t even pull the banner bar down because it blocks your ability too. Also another note on battery life, these headphones only last a max of 4 hours per bud on medium volume without using any pass through or noise cancelling. My AirPod pros would last almost all day but these just have awful battery life for the price. And the sound quality isn’t amazing, it’s passable but nothing incredible. Even if they do use the same drivers and speakers from the AirPod pros, the pros sounded wayyy better than these.
In my opinion, don’t buy these. They’re a waste of money, a very infuriating experience and just uncomfortable in your ear even with covers with ear hooks. Just buy the AirPod pros or anything else

title: Would recommend for $50 or less
text:
As the title states, these headphones would be a pretty good value for about $50, however for $150 they can only be described as hot garbage.

The sound quality is really bad. Like realllllyyyyy bad, and I'm not even a stickler for that usually. But upon my first time using them, I immediately noticed how awful all of my music sounded. The highs are extremely harsh, the mids are non existent and the bass is loud and absolutely hollow. Seriously, these things are barely a step up from the headphones they give out on airplanes. Really bad. Noticeably terrible to the average listener.

Other cons:
No EQ options within the app so you can't even make attempts to correct the awful sound they give.

The case is used to connect to your phone, and not the headphones. So your buds might have full battery, but if your case is dead they will not connect to anything. Such a stupid feature.

It's been stated before that they're not for working out, which is no doubt true, but they're really not meant for any movement.
When I walk to work I'm preventing them from falling out at least once per block if not more.

They're also buggy. Now a lot of modern wireless headphones can be buggy so I'm not even that upset, but what happens with mine is they will randomly "pop", which is disorienting as hell and extremely loud when it happens.

Long story short, I genuinely could not recommend these headphones less. I'd be shocked if any other headphones at this price point sounded or performed half as bad as these. All i have experience with is jaybird vistas, which sound and operate like $500 headphones compared to the beats.

After using them, I now finally understand why they are on sale for half the year. They really do suck.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: Much more compact than previous generations and don't fall out now
text:
Full disclosure: I got these for free as part of a promotion but tried to write my review from the perspective of someone paying $20 for them. This is my fourth set of TOZO earbuds and the sound quality has always been very good (I'm no audio expert but sounds great to me). I've had two sets of T6, one T10 and now the A1s. Broke one T6 (my fault) and lost one of the T10s. Other set of T6 still working fine.

The T6 and T10 both protrude out of my ear about 3/8" and I look a little funny with something hanging out of my ear, though not as dorky as the Airpod 1/2 a Q-tip people. T6 and T10s both have round cushions and 1-3 times per day, will fall out of your ear, often at an inconvenient time when I don't have a free hand to catch them. The A1s seem to have fixed both of these problems and sit flat in my ear and have a cone- shaped cushion that grips your ear hole when pulled by head movements, chewing, etc and keeps them from falling out. Tip: try out all the tip sizes, even if you don't think they will work and you will probably find one that you prefer better than the pre-installed one

Because these fit snugger in your ear, unlike the T6 and T10, you need to put them in the Right or Left ear they were made for, not interchangeable. I only use one at a time while charging the other all day long so I can't change ears without changing earbuds if one ear gets tired now. That's an ok sacrifice when you consider you get a snugger fit that does't let go.

Warranty: TOZO seems to care greatly about their reputation. When I repeatedly dropped my first pair of T6s out of my ear onto the hard floor over and over and over until one stopped working, they simply sent me another pair for free when I asked if that was covered under warranty (knowing it probably wasn't). Nice!

Case: The A1 case is pretty compact but not as flat as the T6 case for going in your pocket if you have tight pants. Kinda like a large walnut size. As others have said, it is a little difficult to extract the earbuds from it but not too hard once you learn the right place to hook your fingernail under.

One funny choice TOZO made from the T6 and T10s was changing the voice for the earbuds that tells you they are connected from a clear British female accent to a very thick Chinese female accent. Once again, not really a problem, just a funny design choice that makes me chuckle when I hear it.

Tip for keeping them connected when switching out one for the other: As soon as you hear "Lo Battowee", take second one out of the case, wait for a beep signaling they paired with eachother, then put the first one back in the case. Then no need to reconnect bluetooth.

Keep the manual in case you need to reset them as startup pairing problems do happen occasionally with the T6 and T10s (maybe once every 2-4 weeks) though I haven't had the A1s long enough to have this problem or say if it's been resolved with the A1s. Simple reset gets them working fine again with older models.

Battery life seems to be good as rated in description.

Bottom line: Are these earbuds worth $20? Definitely. Who wants to pay $250 for some overpriced Apple Q-tips that have the exact same sound quality and do the same thing?

text:
Short answer - I just didn't find the perks to justify spending $200 on these earbuds. I was attempting to upgrade from JBL Reflects.

Longer answer - I was excited to get these. Nice/beautiful design, Beats brand (I have some studio headphones) and ready for the truly wireless setup, and the $50 drop in price. In reality, didn't find that much of a boost in the sound quality (I had one of each in my ears - and I do realize there are limitations to an ear bud from an audio perspective). The over/around the ear was always there/present - I ran with them a few times and the gym a few times - they were stable over my ear, but felt the arm on my ear, not pinching, but too much pressure for me to forget they were there. The controls, mic and call quality was good. Set up was "kessel run" speed... :15 seconds tops with my iphone. title: Just wasn't the perfect fit for me
text:
I'll start by saying I don't have a educated ear, so pristine, flawless sound vs average sound is beyond my knowledge. However I'll say that these headphones weren't the magic fit for me.

I have odd ears, so not every earbud fits/stays in. For example airpods and airpods pro don't fit at all and constantly fall out. So I needed to find a earbud with the over the ear loop and these had good general reviews.

PROS:
1. These stay in my ears, likely due to the over the ear loop, and memory foam-ish earbud tip, very important as I use them exclusively for the gym.
2. Sound is decent, doesn't seem like anything to write home about though
3. Have never had battery issue, but never tested the limits, I plug and charge them after every use.
4. Stylish and good looking, I got the navy matte looking finish.

Cons:
1. Really awful bluetooth range. Granted, I'm using them at the gym, and I'm sure they are fighting against other people's Bluetooth connections all over... However, when I start to get music cutting out walking 20 ft away from my phone... It's disappointing. Sometimes just one headphone cuts out, sometimes both. then it won't re-sync until I get right next to my phone in my bag again. Perhaps I was spoiled by my last headphones, Plantronics backbeat fit bought in 2016 or 2017 which had unbelievable Bluetooth range of like 100 ft.
2. No noise canceling, granted I knew this going in, but for $150 it would have been nice to have.
3. Sound is nothing exciting, although like I said above... I don't have a experienced ear to differentiate unbelievably good sound from regular.
4. Volume scale seems rather low. Again with my prior headphones... Being at 75% volume was always more than enough, with these, I have to go up to 90% or so sometimes. Not sure if this is a phone or headphone issue but thought I'd mention it.
5. Case is a little large, which isn't really an issue for me... But some people might not be a fan. About two and a half times the size of AirPods case.
6. Expensive. I decided to go the 'pay for what you get' route, and try to get something really good, and these are pretty underwhelming for $150. I feel like I could get something very similar for $50

title: Wireless Earbuds not Ideal for Cyclists
text:
TL;DR:
The Beats Powerbeats Pro wireless earbuds have limitations when it comes to certain activities. They can be affected by unwanted noise caused by helmet straps while cycling, and their size and bulkiness may not be ideal for everyone.

Review:

I tried out the Beats Powerbeats Pro wireless earbuds during my cycling sessions, but unfortunately, they didn't live up to my expectations. While they offer impressive sound quality and features, I encountered some limitations that affected my overall experience.

One of the issues I faced was unwanted noise caused by the earbuds coming into contact with my helmet straps. This created an annoying rubbing sound that detracted from the music or podcast I was listening to. Additionally, the wind noise during cycling was more noticeable compared to other earbuds I've used.

Another aspect that didn't quite work for me was the size and bulkiness of the Powerbeats Pro. They felt slightly larger and more cumbersome compared to other wireless earbuds on the market. This made them less comfortable for longer periods of wear, especially during intense physical activities.

However, it's important to note that the Powerbeats Pro still offer impressive sound quality, with punchy bass and clear audio. The battery life is also commendable, providing several hours of playtime on a single charge. The secure fit is beneficial for activities that don't involve helmet straps, ensuring that the earbuds stay in place during workouts.

In summary, while the Beats Powerbeats Pro wireless earbuds offer good sound quality and a secure fit, they have limitations that may impact the user experience in certain situations. The unwanted noise caused by helmet straps during cycling and their larger, bulkier design may be drawbacks for some users. Consider these factors and your specific needs before making a purchase decision.

Pros:
- Impressive sound quality with punchy bass
- Secure fit for active use
- Good battery life

Cons:
- Unwanted noise caused by helmet straps during certain activities
- Larger and bulkier design may be less comfortable for some users

title: Not Worth the Price
text: This product has a lot of problems. I was looking for a good pair of earbuds that also had noise cancelation. What I got was definitely a mixed bag. The first complaint I have is that the earbud sizes are much too large. I know that might not be the case for some people, but I just can't imagine them fitting anyone as all three sizes provided are large, with each larger than the next. This became even more of a problem when the noise cancelation just stopped working. There doesn't seem to be a difference between transparency mode and turning the modes off, and since the noise cancelation doesn't work anymore, I have modes turned off. That really devalues the app itself. The noise cancelation worked great when it did work, even with the earbuds themselves not completely fitting. I got these on sale around Christmas time 2022 and that is one of three things that keeps this review from being two stars.  The second thing is that the sound is good. It would be even better if there had been some smaller sizes available. The third thing is that the battery life is exceptionally good. The product is still useful, albeit at a diminished capacity, so I feel like this product should be in-between two and a half stars and three, but that's not possible. I've bought a lot of cheap earbuds and it's sad to say that their features lasted longer than these. Except Raycons. These are still better than Raycons.

title: Charging, Connection, and Sound Issues
text:
When these ear buds work, they're great & they sound fantastic. However, both my fiance and I have had numerous instances where we thought both earbuds were sleeping soundly in the case and recharging for our next use, only to find that one was dead the next time we went to use them! That can be kind of annoying after a while. We've also both had issues with opening the case up with our phone right in our hand, pocket, etc., and putting the earbuds in our ears, putting the case away in our gym bag, only to find that they haven't automatically paired with our phone. Once again, not a super big deal the first time or two, but gets annoying when it happens frequently. We've also found that when this happens it usually takes multiple attempts of putting the earbuds back in the case, closing the case, reopening the case, taking the earbuds back out, putting them back in, closing the case, rinse & repeat, etc.
Finally, my fiance also found that one of his earbuds has reduced to being at approximately 50% of the loudness of the other. When we took them to the Apple store, we found that despite having purchased them less than a year ago, they were already at the end (like within days) of the warranty. So be aware that the warranty is based on when they're released from the factory, and not from date of purchase. To make the situation even worse, it was determined that the price to repair the issue would be $99 because it is "a hardware issue." So to make a long story short, the warranty seems to be effectively useless if you have a real issue with the earbuds.

title: Overhyped
text:
First, I'll say that the best thing about these headphones is that they do not fall off. I've had many wireless headphones in the past that do not stay on my ears which lead me to purchasing these. The sound is also decent compared to other wireless headphones.

Now to the reason I gave these 2 stars.
Charging- For the first month I had no problem with charging. I would simply place the headphones in the container, comeback the next day and they would be charged. Now that is not the case, I have had a lot of difficulty charging these headphones. I place them in the container, making sure they are attached correctly, then go to put them on 24 hours later and they are dead. This happens a good 3 out of 4 times I put them on. I'm not sure if the connection is bad or what it is. But for this price, I should not have to deal with this problem a few months in.
Battery life- Definitely does not last as long as it says. Also takes much longer to get a full charge than advertised.
power button- The only way I have found to turn these headphones on is pulling them from the container. There's no power button on the wireless headphones themselves (not sure who thought siri was more important than an power button).
In conclusion- save your money. There are plenty headphones out there for much less that will provide you with the best quality in wireless headphones.

title: Such a let down for the brand name
text: For being Beats and the price that they are, almost everything about them is horrible. Unfortunately, they sound thin and airy. Usually Beats have pretty decent bass but these lack them almost completely. Even using bass boosted audio and an equalizer, the bass only just comes through. They come with an extremely short power cable that can really only be hooked up to a computer and they take a couple hours to charge. They claim that 5 minutes of charge will last for an hour but that couldn’t be further from the truth. If you charge them for 15 minutes, you’ll get 30 minutes of listening at the most. Additionally, the charger charges slow and unevenly, causing the two earbuds to have different charges at any given time; which makes it so one earbud works great but the other sounds even worse or just doesn’t work. Pairing it to my phone is a nightmare. Even though I have the latest updates on my phone, they take a couple minutes to pair, don’t pair at all, or will randomly connect and/or disconnect at random times throughout the day. These also come with three different sizes of earpieces to fit your ear but no matter which size I choose, the shape of the earbud isn’t great and even after following fitting and placement directions, still chafe and dig into the the sides of my ears which hurt after about 10 minutes of use. The only thing going for these headphones is the active noise cancellation, which I will admit, is pretty nice when it works. Unfortunately, about a third of the time I turn active noise cancelling on, they instead play a very shrill and high pitched noise which won’t stop until you turn them off. As I said earlier, for being a name brand like Beats and charging $100 for these earbuds, it’s really disappointing to see such a poorly thought out and executed product like these. Especially considering I can get a pair of off-brand, 20-30sec dollar earbuds that will perform better. In short- don’t waste your money on these. They are not worth it and you will end up wanting to return them. I have nothing against the company, just the product
