title: 100% Would Recommend
text:
Ok, to start I am writing this review on day 1 of owning these earbuds. On that note, let's begin.
Pros:
The audio quality is absolutely amazing. No matter what song I put on, I can hear all of the highs, the lows, the in-betweens without any static or interference.
There is incredibly low latency between media controls and the actual feedback on the earbuds. When you press play or pause (on the buds themselves or on your device), there is a very minimal delay until the function actually happens.
Having entirely mirrored button design is a highly overlooked feature for most truly wireless earbuds, but these work flawlessly. Both sides having full control of overall volume and media control is super helpful because you can use whichever hand is free instead of freeing up the proper hand for media controls/volume.
I'm a "basshead" and when I was shopping for earbuds, these were at the top of every list and I have to absolutely agree. With the proper settings set, I can actually feel the bass vibrating in my skull and down my spine. It might seem like overkill, but that's why I spent the money on these.

Cons:
The only thing that I can come up with for a con is that my husband complained that he could clearly hear what I was listening to, but I expected that since they were all the way up.

As I said earlier in the review, I'm still in day 1 of owning these so there are some things that I can't comment on because I haven't gotten that far yet (specifically call quality and battery), but overall I absolutely love these earbuds.

title: Love everything - but not great for side sleepers
text:
I got these earbuds instead of the new airpods when my old ones died because I wanted to try something new, and they have the noise canceling feature for a fraction of the cost of the airpods pro. I have been very happy with them. I have tiny ears and while they definitely stick out, they stay in place well. The sound quality is terrific, exactly what I would expect from Beats, they pair easily to my phone and my computer and switch between the two with no trouble, and the battery life is fantastic. I can generally go a week between charges but I usually only use them for a couple of hours a few days a week.

However, I do have one complaint. One of the main things that I use earbuds for is to listen to music or brown noise in bed at night. While the beats provide great quality sound, the play/pause button is a click button on the side of each earbud and I am a side sleeper, so it is almost impossible to use them in bed without accidentally pausing what I am listening to. If you are a side sleeper and want an earbud that you can fall asleep using, I would recommend trying something else. But if that is not a need for you, then I highly recommend the studio buds!
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: Lives up to the price tag and brand name
text:
These Beats are amazing. After having these for over a month and a half I can give my honest pros and cons list for this product.

Pros:
-Completely wireless
-Amazing bass and sound quality
-Fits comfortable in pockets
-Amazing fit and hold while running
-Extremely easy to pair and use

Cons:
-They’re a but heavy but you get used to the little extra weight fast
-Pricy but again worth the price

All the “cons” are negated by the performance and overall worth of the headphones. They’re worth the price tag. You get what you pay for and what you’re getting is an amazing headphone that feels great and performs just as well. Pairs well with a smart watch for absolute empty pockets while running and exercising. I wanted headphones and a smart watch to go for runs and play basketball without being weighed down by my phone or wires and this was the perfect fit with my watch. Great sound quality with calls and a great mic too. Music sounds crisp and clear. Overall a great experience again with the Beats brand.

title: Comparison of Tozo A1 mini and T6
text:

title: Genuinely the worst headphones i’ve ever had.
text:
I got these as a gift for my birthday in May, and today i’ve officially just thrown them in the trash (literally, they’re sitting at the bottom of my trash can). If sound quality is the sole thing you care about in headphones then sure, pick up a pair and have *decent* sound quality. If you, like me, also appreciate usability, connectivity, and headphones that work properly, then I would steer clear of these. Here’s some highlights:

Pros:
- They have better sound quality than Skullcandy
- Cool colors
- You look like a person who can afford Beats

Cons:
- About 50% of the time they refuse to connect to your phone
- Awful battery life
- Microphone quality is abysmal
- Can’t use headphones if case is dead, despite buds themselves being charged
- Once every two weeks or so you have to do a “full reset” on the case because it refuses to connect and then further refuses to charge.
- You apparently have to use the USB-C cable that comes with it, no other cable will work to charge it (even though this one barely works anyway)

My review? Just buy Airpods or Raykon, don’t make the mistake we made by wasting money on the absolute worst “big name” earbuds that have ever existed. The fact that these are still being sold should be considered a crime against humanity, no one should ever have to go through the absolute frustration and anger of owning these headphones.
product_name: Beats Studio Buds True Wireless Earbuds

title: OK to use in dry sauna. Try large ear tips
text:
Overall great product. Like a few others, I had to switch to the large sized ear tips to obtain better quality sound. I use these during my workouts and they do stay on when in a dry sauna, which was one of the things I really wanted because I also own the Bose SS Free and those shut off within a couple of minutes in the dry sauna. The battery life is outstanding. I turned off the feature that pauses the music when you remove a bud from the ear. I feel like the volume is a little low though, I have the volume up higher than normal when using these. Also, double check the EQ settings of the phone, that helped with the sound quality.

For those undecided on these or the Bose, if you’re ever going to go in a dry sauna, then go with these. If you’re on the go and have to carry these in your pocket, the case for these is a bit bulky and square vs the Bose which is more compact and cylindrical. Battery life is much better on the PBP and you can use either left or right while keeping the other in the case vs the Bose where the right is the main bud and the left will not work if the right is docked. If you just want the better sounding pair, I would say go with the Bose.

Disclaimer: I have the “1st gen” Bose SoundSport Free so some of the features may have changed from the first release 2 years ago.

The earbuds also came with changeable gummies with different sizes just in case the ones it came with didn’t fit your ear hole size. After 2 months I started to notice that charging became an issue . The left one would charge perfect but I always had trouble getting the right one to charge . I would have to wiggle it around or put some pressure on the bud in order for it to charge . After 6 months the right one stopped charging overall. I feel like they should have a better charging design or maybe even a port on the actual buds to charge them manually instead of using the charging case because the charging case is not reliable at all . Since the right bud doesn’t charge at all i no longer use these earbuds , which upsets me a lot because of the amount of money I spent on them . I would give it one star but the charging situation is my only complaint as well as the cost .

title: Worst Charging System I have ever seen.
text: I really like the fit of these ear phones and that they don't fall off when exercising.  The sound quality on them is excellent and even the microphone when taking phone calls does well.  Now for the bad!  To charge them they have two contact points that are suppose to mate up with the help of magnets when placed in the charging case.  This works poorly to say the least, some times they make good contact sometimes they don't even pushing them to try to force contact does not insure they will be charged.  Now, they have a single light on the front of that case that is the charging indicator but as a single light you don't know if one is charging or if both are charging.  There is zero ability to see if both are in good contact and being charged.  I would honestly say that even being extremely diligent in trying to make sure they are aligned properly about 25% of the time I pull them out of the case the next day and one is dead and the other is fully charged.  It is so frustrating and an extremely poor design.  The least they could have done is put two lights on there so you would know that both have made good contact and are being charged.  I want to love them but I can't due to the poor charging design.
